**D-IMPL-62 — Experience-surface HITL authority composition (HTTP/CLI action door).** RESOLVED — **option (a), submit-only with honest-contract hardening. 2026-07-30. Approver: Dave.** The HTTP/CLI HITL channels keep submit-to-transport semantics — this survives cross-process deployment, and the MCP channel's in-process resolve-wiring is a ruled asymmetry, not a defect. Required hardening, in-phase (Phase I.4): the HTTP response (and the CLI output over it) for HITL action submission must state `submitted` — never imply `resolved` — and must include enough execution/queue state for the caller to see the action's disposition honestly. Auth remains tied to T-07-24's residual-risk entry; no new auth surface is forked from this ruling. Surfacing context, preserved: surfaced by the Phase I.4 gate review (Cursor finding X-1, Codex finding C-2). As shipped, `POST /hitl/actions` (and the `ccf hitl decide` verb over it) enqueues a fully-bound `HitlActionSubmission` on the typed transport and **does not itself drive a primitive's `resolve` or land a dim-2 replay record** — no state transition and no authority effect occur from the submit alone; the composition root must pull submissions and drive the owning primitive, as the MCP HITL server demonstrably does (`tests/crossproc/servers/mcp_hitl_child.py`: gate resolve + replay write). Question for Dave: is the v0 HTTP/CLI action door (a) submit-only by design, with authority reserved to primitive-wired surfaces (the MCP channel being D-IMPL-20's primary) — in which case the route's naming/docs state it and D-IMPL-23's "HITL actions" reads as submissions; or (b) required to compose a primitive `resolve` per event class server-side — which needs a ruling on how one generic endpoint maps onto the four primitives' distinct resolution surfaces? Adjacent divergence folded in here rather than a fifth entry: D-IMPL-23 rules the API "adds … auth hooks"; the shipped v0 surface performs no authentication (T-07-24 accepted residual, posture sentence served and test-asserted), and treats future auth as a new contract. Also records the D-IMPL-20 sentence "serves … the `ccf hitl` CLI" (via MCP) vs the shipped CLI's HTTP-thin-client layering (D-IMPL-22/23) — resolved by the same ruling: the CLI's action door is a submission surface. Originates: CLAUDE.md §8.2/§8.3; D-IMPL-20/22/23; `docs/PHASE_I4_GATE.md` §7. *Verb status (2026-07-31, plan 08-04, D-14 obligation):* the v0 HITL CLI surface ships exactly one decision verb, `submit` — `decide` removed tree-wide per D-15 (see the D-15 Phase 8 context ruling, executed in plan 08-02 with an absence test).

Approver: Dave.** The two D-IMPL-21 reference identity-binding implementations (auth-context-derived principal; JWS-signed binding reusing D-IMPL-15) move to **explicit follow-up-phase scope** — a named deferral, not an indefinite posture. Caller-supplied principal fields are the recorded v0 posture, consistent with the unauthenticated v0 HTTP surface (T-07-24 accepted residual). Neither shipped in I.4: `HumanPrincipalBinding` is required by type everywhere (the type-unrepresentable leg holds), but its fields are **caller-supplied** — the MCP server's verified token identity is not bound to the submission's `subject_id`, and the HTTP surface has no auth context to derive from (see D-IMPL-62). Question for Dave: defer both reference impls to a named phase (with the caller-supplied posture stated as the v0 scope of the D-IMPL-21 claim), or pull one (the MCP-auth-context derivation is the smaller) into a Phase 8 plan? — ruled: defer both, with the caller-supplied posture stated as the v0 scope of the D-IMPL-21 claim. **D-IMPL-64 — Webhook notify-only reference transport: v0 disposition.** RESOLVED — **deferral REJECTED; build it this phase. 2026-07-30. Approver: Dave.** The ruled notify-only webhook HITL transport (D-IMPL-20) ships in v0, implemented in Phase I.4. Notify-only means exactly what D-IMPL-20 said: authority never flows through the webhook — it notifies external systems of HITL events, and every human action returns through the typed `HITLTransportProtocol` queue. Implementation discipline matches the other transports: injected dependencies, typed refusals, `mypy --strict`, no inline prompts or domain values. Surfacing context, preserved: ratification ask. D-IMPL-20 rules two reference transports; the notify-only webhook emitter was **deferred from v0** by plan 07-08 (single-owner rationale in its SUMMARY: authority never flowed through the webhook leg, a notify-only emitter is a pure observer implementable by any deployment against `HITLTransportProtocol` with zero SDK change, and shipping one would encode notification-infrastructure choices the SDK has no business making). Both gate reviewers flagged that this narrows a ruled deliverable without a decision-log entry — this entry is that surfacing, per the new-number-not-amend discipline (D-IMPL-20's text stands as approved). Question for Dave: ratify the v0 deferral (naming a receiving phase or "post-v0"), or require the emitter in v0 — ruled: require it in v0, this phase. Originates: D-IMPL-20; `07-08-SUMMARY.md`; `docs/PHASE_I4_GATE.md` §4.2/§7.

**D-IMPL-67 — 7.1 review findings N1/N2/HIGH: wire the identity mechanisms into the HITL doors before merge.** RESOLVED — **2026-07-30. Approver: Dave.** The 7.1 re-review's top three findings (Codex HIGH; Cursor N1; Cursor+Ollama N2) are ruled fixable-now, in a thin 7.2 wave on `phase-i4.1` before the cycle merges: (1) **HTTP door composition** — when an auth hook is bound to `create_app`, `POST /hitl/actions` derives the submission principal from the verified `request.state.token_grant` via `principal_from_token_grant`; a body principal conflicting with the verified identity is a typed 4xx refusal, not an accepted claim. When no auth hook is bound, behavior is unchanged (T-07-24 posture stands as ruled — D-IMPL-62's auth linkage is not reopened). (2) **MCP door composition** — `submit_hitl_action` binds the submission's `subject_id` to the MCP server's verified token identity instead of accepting a caller-typed value; conflicting claims are typed refusals. (3) **Hardened-surface demonstrability (N2's SDK-side half)** — the composed hardened path is itself test-asserted (auth bound ⇒ principal derived ⇒ audited action carries the verified subject end-to-end), so Phase 8 examples have a proven composition to demonstrate rather than unused helpers; the examples-must-bind-auth obligation itself remains Phase 8 scope. Not reopened: default unauthenticated posture, `AUTH_POSTURE_SENTENCE`, signed-binding optionality (N5), FORCED_LLM pass-through (N3). **D-15 (Phase 8 context ruling) — `ccf hitl decide` removed; v0 ships one verb: `submit`.** RESOLVED — **2026-07-30. Approver: Dave.** Executes the `decide`-alias removal-or-keep policy carried out of D-GATE-I.4.1: the deprecated `decide` alias (introduced under D-IMPL-66(d)) is removed entirely in Phase 8 per 08-CONTEXT D-15 — `ccf hitl decide` no longer parses; the parser rejects it as an unknown choice, and no deprecation path remains. `ccf hitl submit` is the single HITL action verb, unchanged in behavior (D-IMPL-62 submit-only semantics and the `HitlActionReceipt` contract stand as ruled).
