The fourth correction finally pinned the gate's rule surface by digest to the append-only decision log — using a bound the third correction had just created — and the pin was independently reproduced firing on a silently-raised budget while every other check, including the budget check itself, passed. **Two falsification results, both independently reproduced at the gate.** With `FlureeGraphReader._translate_query` neutered to return `None`, **all seven differential tests stay GREEN** while both telemetry tests go **RED** — `GQ-34` makes the degraded posture byte-identical *by design*, so byte-identity to the fallback is a conformance bar and provably **not** a pushdown bar. Any adapter claiming pushdown on corpus-green alone claims something its evidence cannot distinguish from an absent translation. **Probes before code, and they earned it.** F-A6 established that `c[$key]` dynamic property access parses, returns HTTP 200, and evaluates to **null** — porting `_ENTITY_POLICY` verbatim would have shipped a stage-1 policy family that silently excludes every claim. F-A3(e) returned `[{"props": [null, null]}]`, confirming Fluree relationships over plain RDF triples carry no properties, which is why the Neo4j walk was replaced by the interposed `CcfEdge` node (BF-1) rather than copied. Both were caught before a line of adapter code existed. **Code review: 1 Critical, 10 Warning, 3 Info; eight closed in-phase.** **CR-01** was real and is the phase's most instructive defect: `policy_key` gated two of its three components, because the docstring asserted *"The class name is safe by construction"* one line above an argument that was otherwise valid — so a claim the audited fallback **excluded** was returned by the pushed path (T-15.2-03 over-disclosure). Reproduced end-to-end before acceptance and re-verified fixed after merge. Four mechanisms were structurally blind to it, including the unit test, which repeated the guard's own two-of-three gap because it was written from the same false premise; the regression test that now protects it needs **no server and runs in ~20ms**. Also closed: WR-02/WR-03 (a credentialed Fluree URL **connected anonymously** — `httpx` derives no header from `base_url` userinfo, and `bearer_token` was reachable from no supported path), WR-07, WR-08, WR-09, WR-10, IN-01. **Six remain open as recorded debt:** WR-01, WR-04, WR-05, WR-06, IN-02, IN-03. **Rulings issued during the phase:** F-A4(a) `approved` (the ground `delete`+`insert` body holds, so `D-02`'s letter is unchanged); Q1/Q2 extend the proxy to match the normative rule, never loosen the rule; Q3 `docs/DECISIONS.md` joins Tier C bounded **append-only**, with `docs/**` explicitly rejected because it would free the frozen `GRAPH_QUERY_SEMANTICS.md`; keep the weekly `fluree-drift` cadence; fix CR-01, WR-02/03, WR-07, WR-08, WR-09/10, IN-01 in-phase. **Residual, non-blocking:** `15.3-HUMAN-UAT.md` carries two GitHub-Actions observations (the fluree leg green on `main`; the drift job's first firing) that cannot be established from the working tree. **Substrate #7 warning, carried forward:** `manifest.py` is at 24 of 25 and `artifacts.py` at 9 of 10 — **tied**, not tiered — so a seventh substrate breaches both on arrival, and `D-IMPL-92` forbids raising either. `D-IMPL-93` commissions the remedy. **D-GATE-15.4** — Phase 15.4 (Backend Registration Seam — The Substrate Stops Naming Its Adapters, INSERTED) approved. Date: 2026-08-09. The invariant test that mirrors the lint carried the *same* blind spot in its own regex, so it structurally could not have caught what the lint was missing; both are fixed, including `from ccf.graph import reader, _writer`, the same import wearing a comma. **CR-03**: duplicate discovery compared distribution *name* only, so the ordinary failed-uninstall state (two dist-info directories, one name, different versions, different modules) was accepted and one silently chosen — and the winner's version then landed in replay dimension 2 as fact. **One finding was checked and REJECTED: WR-05** ("neither new checker has a test of any kind") is false — 41 test functions exist in `tools/lints/tests/`, created in plan 15.4-01. Its grep searched `tests/` and `examples/`. The underlying condition is real and is now recorded in the gate package: `ci-core` never reaches the checker suite, so a local sweep alone supports exactly that false inference. **Four rulings taken at this gate.** **(1) The `tools/gates/gate_15_3.py` deletion is accepted.** The ROADMAP says twice that `D-IMPL-92`'s gate is "superseded by the structural check, **not deleted**", and plan 15.4-07 deleted the script and its whole package. It is recoverable at `d364b65^`** (`git show d364b65^:tools/gates/gate_15_3.py`), and that SHA is recorded here so the executable record of Phase 15.3's claim — the artifact `D-GATE-15.3` calls that phase's strongest output, watched to fail eight times on eight distinct violations before being believed once — is retrievable rather than merely gone. **(2) The HTTP error code is hyphenated, at this gate, while it is still free.** `backend_registry_conflict` became `backend-registry-conflict`, matching all seven values in the API's shared vocabulary. and `15.3-HUMAN-UAT.md`'s two GitHub-Actions observations remain non-blocking. **Two planning-template defects worth fixing before the next phase, both repeated rather than isolated:** five consecutive plans listed a surface-change *fragment* in `files_modified` but not the assembled `docs/SURFACE-CHANGES.md` it regenerates, and four plans hit the same self-referential trap where a docstring, comment or Makefile note explaining why a token is absent fails the grep asserting that absence — resolved the same way each time, describe the token rather than spell it. **D-GATE-15.4 (addendum, 2026-08-09) — the close-time cross-AI panel, and two structural invariants it found unenforced.** Recorded because the entry above describes a state that has since changed, and because `docs/DECISIONS.md` is the canonical phase record: a reader of it alone would not otherwise learn that the panel ran, that it found more than the single-agent review did, or that what it found was not a Phase 15.4 defect. **What happened.** `D-GATE-15.4` was approved on a self-review that consisted of the single-agent `gsd-code-reviewer` pass (`15.4-REVIEW.md`, 3 blockers, all fixed in-phase). CLAUDE.md §3.1 step 1 required `/gsd-review --phase 15.4 --all` — the cross-AI panel — and the single-agent review was substituted for it. Dave directed the panel be run afterwards and that all defects close before Phase 16. **What the panel found.** Four reviewers (Gemini, Codex, Cursor, Ollama; Claude excluded for independence) over ~50k tokens of *shipped* code, given the three already-fixed blockers with an instruction not to re-derive them but to search their neighbourhoods: **six further findings, every one verified against the tree before being acted on, and one rejected on verification** — recorded at `15.4-CLOSE-REVIEWS.md`. **The serious one is not a Phase 15.4 defect and predates it.** The harness-neutrality lint did not see `from google import adk`: `HARNESS_DENY` holds dotted entries and the deny loop still called `imported_module_names`, which reports only `google` for that spelling, while line 227 of the same file already used the CR-02-corrected `reached_module_names`. Phase 15.4 fixed that exact defect one file over and stopped twenty-seven lines short. Reproduced by execution, not argued. **And it was worse than the panel reported.** The panel named one blind checker and guessed at two more; all three were blind, and the two it could not prove were blind in every direction. The sharpest instance is the algorithmic seam rather than the harness one: `from ccf import llm` inside a module tagged `__ccf_mode__ = "algorithmic"` produced no finding, so **CCF's own LLM seam could enter the algorithmic path unremarked** (CLAUDE.md §11's Algorithmic ⇄ Semantic Alternation) — by a spelling a CCF developer is *more* likely to write than the covered one. Two structural invariants with CI enforcement that an idiomatic import form walked past. **The diagnosis, which is the part that generalizes: only *dotted* deny entries were ever blind.** `langgraph`, `claude_agent_sdk`, `anthropic` and `openai` have no parent package to be named by, so every spelling a test author would naturally write already worked for them. The blind spot existed only for `google.adk`, `ccf.llm` and `ccf_runtime.adapters`. That asymmetry is why a 141-test checker suite stayed green over two invariants — the tests were written against the entries that could not fail. The replacement suite derives its cases from the deny constants rather than from a spelling list, so a new harness arrives covered in every form; it is now 400 tests. **All six findings closed** (`15.4-CLOSE-FIXES-A-SUMMARY.md` for F0/F3/F6, `-B-` for F1/F4/F5), each with a regression test that fails without its fix, F0/F1/F6 mutation-checked. F6 shipped *both* candidate fixes rather than choosing: the public `GraphWriter` protocol gains `close()` (the declaration — without it an adapter author reading `protocols.py` cannot learn the requirement) and `adopt_writer` refuses a non-`BaseGraphWriter` (the enforcement), by `isinstance` rather than `hasattr`, because a `close` that does not release the mint is the same defect with one more step in it. F1's fix was mutation-checked in both directions: reinstating the echo fails with a DSN visible in the refusal, and *over*-redacting fails three tests including two pre-existing, so neither half passes for the wrong reason. **One finding carried, deliberately: F2** — `substrate_vocabulary` derives from in-tree adapters only, so `cinv04-substrate-name` enforces "no *built-in* substrate name in core". Codex's framing is recorded verbatim because it is the accurate one: this makes the third-party zero-cost claim *"partly true by construction of the measurement."* It is not a defect but a bound on what the measurement proves, and the obvious remedy — deriving the vocabulary from installed entry points — would make a structural invariant environment-dependent, green or red by virtualenv. Carried to a design cycle with `DI-15.4-05`. **Sweep after the fixes:** `make ci` exit 0, **2457 passed / 81 skipped** (from 2450 at the gate), checker suite **400 passed** (from 141), both invariant holes re-verified by execution on merged `main`. **Nothing here reopens this gate or falsifies the phase's headline claim** — the out-of-tree adapter did arrive at zero substrate cost. What the panel established is narrower and worth stating precisely: *the enforcement was weaker than the achievement.* **Process consequence, applied.** CLAUDE.md §3.1 step 1 now states that the panel *is* the step and a single-agent review is additive and never substitutive; that at close the panel reviews shipped code rather than plans, to a distinct `<phase>-CLOSE-REVIEWS.md`; that the panel is handed known findings with instructions not to re-derive them; that every finding is verified against the tree before being acted on and rejections are recorded as rejections; and that the ordering is execute → panel → single-agent → verify → fix blocking in-phase → present. Directive from Dave, 2026-08-09.

**D-GATE-15.4 (addendum correction, 2026-08-09) — finding F2 is `DI-15.4-06`, not `DI-15.4-05`.** Appended rather than edited, per the Tier C append-only rule the `D-IMPL-92` corrections established. The addendum above closes by saying finding F2 — `substrate_vocabulary` deriving only from in-tree adapters, so `cinv04-substrate-name` enforces "no *built-in* substrate name in core" — is "carried to a design cycle with `DI-15.4-05`". That cross-reference is wrong, and the phase security audit caught it as unregistered flag UF-4. **`DI-15.4-05` is the private-surface gap: which names an adapter *author* must reach for** (`materialize_view`, `_ordered_view`, `_entity_records`, `_relationship_records`, `_LineageRowsFor`, `_GraphTxn`). **F2 is the lint-vocabulary gap: which names the *rule* can see.** Both are questions about the same seam and neither is the other; conflating them left F2 tracked nowhere, since `deferred-items.md` had no entry for it. It is now **`DI-15.4-06`**, with the three options a ruling has to choose between recorded there — accept the bound and state it wherever the property is claimed; derive the vocabulary from installed entry points and accept that a structural invariant becomes environment-dependent, green or red by virtualenv; or a separate non-lint check that runs where the installed set is known. Meanwhile the bound is not silent: `15.4-SECURITY.md` records `T-15.4-48` as accepted risk **R-15.4-C** rather than unqualified CLOSED, so no threat-register row rests on a guarantee wider than the lint gives. **Also recommended by that audit and not yet actioned:** a new register row `T-15.4-50` (Information disclosure, mitigate) for the third-party import-exception disclosure that finding F1 fixed — `T-15.4-05` covers Pydantic `ValidationError` echo only and does not reach it, and this phase is what opened the seam by which an arbitrary installed distribution's exception text could reach an unauthenticated `503` body.

**D-IMPL-94 — Mode 2 packaging attaches above `serve()`; Phase 16's scope carve-outs.** Date: 2026-08-10. Decided by: Dave. Provenance of the parts, stated because they did not all arrive the same way: `D-02`, `D-13`, `D-14` and `D-15` are Dave's locked planning-time rulings recorded in `.planning/phases/16-documentation-rewrite-the-deterministic-path-the-adoption-ar/16-CONTEXT.md`; `Q-2`, `Q-6`, `Q-7` and `Q-8` are dispositions this entry makes and which plan 16-01's blocking `checkpoint:human-verify` puts to Dave before any downstream plan proceeds. Every claim below was read against the tree at `3cbaa0c` on 2026-08-10, not taken from the plan text. **The ruling.** Mode 2 (`llm_packaged`) packaging attaches **above** `serve()`, consuming the `ServedProduct` it returns, and never inside `serve()`. The argument is structural rather than a preference. `serve()`'s inputs are an already-gated `ServableProduct` — only `ccf.products.gates` can mint one, because its constructor takes a module-private token — and a fully-built `DecisionReplayRecord`. It performs exactly two acts: persist the executed queries' canonical bytes through the `QueryPinWriter`, then append the record through `ReplayWriter.write_replay_record`, whose success *returns* the `DeliveryCapability` that delivers. It contains no rendering and no transformation of the product payload; its only branches are the `QueryPinMismatch` refusals raised before any store write, so exactly one path reaches a return and that path runs through the append (`src/ccf/replay/serve.py:214-266`). A packaging stage inside it would introduce the branch the Phase 04 decision exists to forbid — *"serve() is one expression because the replay append returns the delivery capability — there is no branch that reaches delivery without a recorded decision"* — and would place a model call inside the function that mints the audit record, in a module that declares `__ccf_mode__ = "algorithmic"` and is therefore the `@algorithmic` lint's business (CINV-03, CLAUDE.md §11). Attaching above keeps the algorithmic substrate the artifact a supervisor inspects and makes the LLM rendering a presentation layer over it, which is what whitepaper Ch 7 §7.6 *Context Products — System of Delivery* specifies — cited by section number and title only, never body text (CLAUDE.md §11; Phase 14 D-18; `pub01-whitepaper-shingle`). **What `assembly_mode` describes (Q-2).** `ProductClassDeclaration.assembly_mode` (`src/ccf/controlplane/artifacts.py:602`, typed by `AssemblyMode` at `src/ccf/products/contract.py:71`) describes the **substrate** — how the *Context Product* was assembled — and not the delivered artifact. It is therefore `algorithmic` for a product whose packaging sits above `serve()`, and it stays `algorithmic` when Phase 17 lands that packaging, because a presentation layer above `serve()` does not change how the product was assembled. The delivered artifact's mode is recorded where the models invoked are recorded: `ModelVersionRecord.assembly_mode` (`src/ccf/replay/record.py:356`), replay dimension 3, whose docstring already commits that Mode 2 supplies the real version alongside the other pinned rendering primitives when the packaging stage lands. This sub-question is answered here rather than deferred because Section 1's prose cannot be written honestly without it, and the consequence for that prose is direct: `assembly_mode: algorithmic` in a product-class declaration is a **real governance choice with two siblings arriving in Phase 17** — not boilerplate, and not a constant — and Section 1 must teach it that way. **No code accompanies this ruling.** It is a paper act, verified by `git diff --stat -- src/ runtime/` showing nothing for plan 16-01, and nothing across the phase but the single enumerated exception below. **Criterion 10's one enumerated exception (D-13).** Correcting the docstring of `ProductClassDeclaration` in `src/ccf/controlplane/artifacts.py` is **not** "the fabric changed": no behaviour, no signature and no contract change — the class's fields, defaults and validation are untouched — and mkdocstrings publishes that docstring into the site, so the edit is squarely documentation. The occasion is a failure that predates this phase: `tools/publish_scan_tests/test_docstring_leaks.py::test_no_docstring_reproduces_whitepaper_body_text` reports **20 shingle hits** against `src/ccf/controlplane/artifacts.py::ProductClassDeclaration`, re-measured at `3cbaa0c` on 2026-08-10, with every other docstring in the tree clean. ROADMAP criterion 10's `git diff --stat -- src/ runtime/` assertion therefore carries **this single enumerated exception** — one symbol, `ProductClassDeclaration`, in one file, `src/ccf/controlplane/artifacts.py` — rather than requiring zero. The enumeration is literal, not a category: plan 16-04 makes the edit, plan 16-19's `tools/gates/gate_16.py` allowlists exactly that path-and-symbol pair mechanically rather than trusting this prose, and nothing else anywhere under `src/` or `runtime/` is authorised by this carve-out. **The four Gate-2 tripwire residuals are NOT in Phase 16 (D-14).** `.planning/phases/15.1-ergonomics-gap-closure/deferred-items.md` — the authoritative inheritance list, explicitly not `docs/SURFACE-AUDIT.md` §6.4 — places four Gate-2 tripwire residuals here, and none of them is documentation work. Named by their ids in that file: **R4-WR-03**, a loop-carried rebinding is out of both tripwires' reach because they resolve a name to the binding textually last before the read and a loop executes lines out of source order; **R5-WR-01**, `_Binding.until` covers the comprehension's outermost iterable, which Python evaluates in the enclosing scope, measured as a regression in both directions against `6cf00d3` and whose outermost-iterable **walrus** case has never been measured by anyone; the **augmented-assignment mutable-set opacity**, where `ops |= x` records an unreadable binding so a body that mutates the lineage's own set in place and hands it to the gate is admitted; and the **attribute/subscript `global`/`nonlocal` exception**, where attribute and subscript targets are unfollowed rather than misfollowed except when the redirected assignment lives in a nested body, in which case the enclosing body's stale binding stays in force. Each is a change to what `tests/products/test_gate_two_call_shape.py` **detects** — mechanism, not prose. They **carry forward unclosed to Phase 17**, which supersedes the "Where it belongs: Phase 16" lines in `deferred-items.md`; if Phase 17's planning finds its Mode 2/3 scope the wrong home, they move by an appended dated entry, never by silence. The carry is explicit rather than tacit for one reason worth stating: a phase claiming "no fabric changed" that quietly takes on mechanism work invites exactly the criterion-10 argument `D-13` settles. The carry is then **bounded on two limbs**, because without the bound this ruling blocks the phase it exists to protect — the first limb was found by round-1 review of the plans and the second by round-2 re-verification, and each would stop a different wave on its own. **Limb 1 — re-counting a non-vacuity floor.** Several non-vacuity floors in `tests/products/` are counts observed in the tree **with no headroom, on purpose**: `MINIMUM_GATE_CALL_SITES` (9), `MINIMUM_PROJECTING_BODIES` (11) and `MINIMUM_RESOLVED_BINDER_SITES` (11) in `tests/products/test_gate_two_call_shape.py`, and `MINIMUM_IMPLEMENTATIONS` (9) in `tests/products/test_required_operators_guard.py`. They are fed almost entirely by the examples `DOCS-17` retires. **Re-counting such a floor after a deletion this phase's own ruling authorises is bookkeeping forced by the deletion — not one of the four carried residuals, and not Gate-2 mechanism work.** Plan 16-18 relies on this limb; without it that plan meets a red `make ci` it would have no authority to fix. **Limb 2 — retiring an assertion whose sole in-tree witness a ruled deletion removes.** Not every count coupling has a constant to lower. **An assertion in `tests/products/` whose evidence base is a single in-tree witness, where that witness is a path this phase's own ruling deletes, may be retired deliberately in the same commit as the deletion** — on the same footing as re-flooring, and for the same reason. The limb is stated generally rather than as a single named permission, because the phase deletes ten examples and a second witness of this shape would otherwise stop a later wave with no authority to proceed. The measured instance is `tests/products/test_gate_two_call_shape.py::test_the_plan_recognition_refuses_an_unrelated_required_keyword`, whose docstring states its own evidence base as **n = 1** and names the witness — `examples/03-harness-portability/run.py:693`, the `add_argument` call whose `required=True` keyword sits on the following line, verified at `3cbaa0c` as the only `required=True` anywhere under `examples/` — and whose docstring already sanctions the disposition: *"If the last such call ever leaves `examples/`, this fails loudly and can be retired deliberately — which is the right way round."* Plan 16-15 owns it. Both limbs turn on one distinction: **the four carried residuals are changes to what the tripwire *detects*; both limbs of the bound are changes to what there is left to detect over, forced by a smaller tree.** Neither limb permits any change to detection logic, and weakening, skipping or `xfail`ing an assertion remains forbidden under both. The discipline that applies to both is the one `test_gate_two_call_shape.py` already carries in `FLOOR_REMOVAL_INSTRUCTION`: a deliberate removal and an accidental one need the identical edit, so make the edit **in the same commit as the deletion** and **name every removed site or witness in the commit message**, because `git log` is then the only thing that tells the two apart afterwards. Limb 2 additionally requires one thing `FLOOR_REMOVAL_INSTRUCTION` does not cover, because a retired assertion leaves no failure site to carry the instruction: **the retired assertion's measurement must be preserved in the module** — a docstring or a comment carrying the counts and the identity of the removed witness — since a rule whose justification is deleted alongside its witness invites the next reviewer to propose the rejected design again. **ERGO-03's measurement is frozen; the running test retires (D-15).** `tests/examples/test_surface_audit.py` compares `examples/` against `docs/surface/examples/before/`, a baseline frozen at Phase 15's start, and `tools/measure_examples.py` warns in its own comment that re-freezing mid-phase destroys the comparison; the greenfield rewrite makes the comparison meaningless from the first new example directory onward. ERGO-03 is a **Complete** requirement, so its shipped evidence is preserved rather than overwritten and rather than silently deleted: the measured Phase 15 before/after figures are captured as scripted output, with the date and the tree SHA they were measured at, into `docs/surface/examples/ERGO-03-FROZEN.md` **before** any example changes, and only then does the running test retire. The retirement carries a rationale citing this entry in `docs/SURFACE-AUDIT.md`'s ERGO-03 section, so a later reader finds the measurement rather than an absence. **The three open questions this phase answers by disposition rather than by ruling.** **Q-6** — whether `docs/SURFACE-CHANGES.md` publishes into the site (the open editorial question at `docs/SURFACE-AUDIT.md` §5.4): it **does not**. The A-2 maintainer page describes the surface toolchain — `tools/dump_surface.py`, `make surface`, baseline immutability — and links nothing that would drag a `.planning/` path past `pub02-internal-path`. **Q-7** — `DI-15.4-05` and the addendum-corrected `DI-15.4-06` (the public-versus-private adapter surface, and `substrate_vocabulary` deriving from in-tree adapters only) are **not ruled here**. `how-to/write-a-graph-backend-adapter.md` is rewritten against the surface that is settled — a `BackendRegistration(name, config_model, secret_fields, open_store, make_writer)` declared as `REGISTRATION` in a `*_write.py` module, discovered either by reading the adapter package on disk or through the `ccf.graph_backends` entry-point group — and the open question is recorded in the phase record, **never in the published page** (plan 16-06). **Q-8** — `make ci` **does** gain the three gate-checker suites (`tools/lints/tests`, `tools/publish_scan_tests`, `tools/docs_tests`), so that its documented claim to be the full local reproduction of the always-on pipeline becomes true rather than aspirational; plan 16-04 makes the three pre-existing failures green and plan 16-12 owns the `Makefile` composition. Originates: `16-CONTEXT.md` `D-02`, `D-13`, `D-14` and `D-15`; `16-RESEARCH.md` § D.4 and its Open Questions Q-1..Q-8; `src/ccf/replay/serve.py`; `src/ccf/products/contract.py`; `src/ccf/controlplane/artifacts.py`; `src/ccf/replay/record.py`; `src/ccf/graph/registry.py`; `tests/products/test_gate_two_call_shape.py`; `tests/products/test_required_operators_guard.py`; `tools/publish_scan_tests/test_docstring_leaks.py`; `.planning/phases/15.1-ergonomics-gap-closure/deferred-items.md`; `.planning/ROADMAP.md` Phase 16 criterion 10; `.planning/STATE.md` (the Phase 04 decision); whitepaper Ch 7 §7.6.

**D-IMPL-95 — Systems of record are read-only; CCF's Context Graph gets its own store on the same substrate.** Date: 2026-08-10. Decided by: Dave, verbatim: *"create your own db so there is no collision - I want the existing stores to provide the proxy for the enterprise data stores. This is what the CCF reads (never updates or modifies). The CCF can use the same backend to store its own KG for the Context Product. Lets make sure we do not contaminate the source data."* **The ruling.** A deployment binds two distinct stores per substrate, and the boundary between them is structural rather than conventional. The **system of record** — on the four-database FIBO harness, Fluree ledger `fibo:main` and the `fibo` databases on MongoDB, Neo4j and PostgreSQL — is an enterprise data store that CCF's L1 Signal Layer **reads and never writes**. The **Context Graph** (L3) is CCF-owned, lives in a separate ledger or database *on the same substrate*, and is written only through L2. No CCF write path may target a system of record, and no example, test, matrix leg or adapter configuration may name a source store as its graph target. **Why it is structural and not hygiene.** CLAUDE.md §10 makes single-writer an architectural invariant on one side of the fabric: only L2 holds a write handle to L3. This entry states the complementary constraint on the other side: L1 holds only a *read* handle to the systems of record. Together they make the fabric non-destructive to the enterprise **by construction**, which is the property that makes CCF adoptable where it matters — no institution grants a new platform write access to its book of record, and an SDK that requires one is unadoptable regardless of what else it proves. The whitepaper assumes ingestion is non-destructive (Ch 8 §8.3 Pattern 1, CDC→G) without stating the prohibition; this entry states it. **What it changes in Phase 16.** Plan 16-07's opt-in DGX legs resolve their graph target from environment-supplied, CCF-owned names — never `fibo:main` and never a `fibo` database. The existing no-host-literal rule already keeps endpoints out of the tree; this adds that the *target name* is likewise configuration, and that a source-store name appearing as a graph target is a defect, not a convenience. The always-on `sqlite` and `memory` legs are unaffected: both are CCF-owned by construction. **The measured state of the source estate at this date.** Plan 16-02 extended the KYC/UBO estate so the adoption argument's own question becomes answerable — at HEAD, `ownershipPercent` was an attribute of the owning **Party entity** and every `hasOwnershipInterestIn` ran Party→Corporation in exactly one hop, so *"who ultimately owns Acme?"* had no chain to traverse. The extension is a strict superset of the shipped FIBO data, verified rather than asserted: 0 entities lost, 0 relationships lost, 5 corp→corp edges added, and `ownershipPercent` moved onto **9 edges** where the originals carried it on none. Dave loaded it into the source stores on 2026-08-10, and the per-edge percentage is now present in **MongoDB, Neo4j and PostgreSQL** — 16 relationships, 9 carrying the property, confirmed by direct query. **Fluree is the exception, and the reason is modelling rather than tooling.** Fluree holds 4 of the 9 ownership pairs and no per-edge percentage, because there is no Fluree loader in the harness — `fluree_to_mongo.py` runs export-only, out of Fluree into the mirrors — and because RDF has nowhere to hang a qualifier on a triple. That absence is precisely *why* the source modelled `ownershipPercent` as a Party attribute and why every chain was one hop; it is not an oversight in the loaders. CCF's own Fluree adapter already solves this with the **interposed-edge layout** (`src/ccf/graph/backends/fluree_write.py`, 15.3-RESEARCH.md §R5): a CCF relationship is not a Cypher relationship there, because a property-reading relationship variable sees only reifier-bundled edges, so both the edge properties and the CCF type move onto node properties of an interposed node. Bringing the *source* estate to parity needs the same reification decided deliberately — FIBO's own `OwnershipInterest` modelling is the obvious candidate — and it writes to a live ledger, so it is proposed before it is run and is **not** carried out as a side effect of this entry. Until it lands, Fluree is a knowingly incomplete system of record and any claim of cross-substrate source parity must say so. **What was changed outside the repository.** `load_neo4j.py` and `load_postgres.py` in `/home/parkave/fluree/examples/fibo/` — Dave's out-of-tree harness, not SDK code — were patched to carry the per-edge percentage: one `SET rel.ownershipPercent = $pct` clause on the MERGE, and one nullable `ownership_percent NUMERIC` column with its INSERT binding. Both drop-and-reload, so both are idempotent; originals are preserved under `.backups/`. Recorded here because the phase's evidence depends on the source estate's shape, and a later reader re-running the harness needs to know the shipped scripts were amended and why. **What this entry does not rule.** Whether `compare_backends.py`'s own presence matrix should be extended to report percentages rather than owner/company pairs alone (it currently cannot distinguish a faithful mirror from a lossy one — the defect that hid this for a full load cycle); and whether a later phase promotes the four-substrate source estate into a fixture the SDK ships. Originates: Dave's ruling of 2026-08-10 during Phase 16 wave 3; CLAUDE.md §10 (single-writer, L1-L6) and §13 (out of scope: distributed multi-writer coordination); `16-RESEARCH.md` Assumption A3, which asked whether the DGX stores match the JSONL files and is hereby answered — they diverged, and the divergence was measured rather than assumed; `src/ccf/graph/backends/fluree_write.py`; `.planning/phases/16-.../16-02-SUMMARY.md`; whitepaper Ch 8 §8.3 Pattern 1.

**D-IMPL-96 — Criterion 10's "no fabric changed" is revoked; Context Debt must reach the consuming agent.** Date: 2026-08-10. Decided by: Dave, verbatim: *"The condition 'no fabric changed' needs to be revoked. It was established to prevent external adapters leaking into the core CCF product. In this case this is a true defect that was not implemented or caught during testing. And yes the fabric MUST change to do this the right way… Going forward I don't want to use the 'not fabric change' because it has been used out of context."* **What is revoked.** ROADMAP Phase 16 criterion 10 — the `git diff --stat -- src/ runtime/` assertion — is withdrawn, and with it the elaborate machinery built to work around it: `D-13`'s single enumerated exception for `ProductClassDeclaration`'s docstring, plan 16-19's `gate_16.py` allowlist of exactly that path-and-symbol pair, and `D-14`'s two-limb bound on what counts as bookkeeping versus carried Gate-2 residual. Those constructs were sound reasoning *inside* a premise that no longer holds; none of them survives the premise's withdrawal, and re-litigating them is wasted motion. Work already committed under them stands — the docstring correction was a real fix and the retirement-coupling sweep is real machinery. **Why it was there, and why that is not what it was doing.** The rule's purpose was **anti-leakage**: keep substrate adapters, harness bindings and domain values out of the core, which is the standing commitment CLAUDE.md §1 makes as harness neutrality and general-purposeness and which CI already enforces through the import lint, the `@algorithmic` lint and the No-Hardcoding lint. Those enforcements are unaffected and remain in force. What criterion 10 actually did was something else: it converted "do not let the wrong things in" into "do not change anything," and a documentation phase that cannot change the thing it documents will document a defect rather than fix it. That is what happened here. The rule is withdrawn rather than narrowed because a narrower wording invites the same substitution the next time a phase is scoped. **The defect it was concealing.** `DebtAssessment` — `debt`, `signal`, and `factors` carrying `freshness`, `completeness` and `semantic_consistency` — is computed by `ccf.halflife.debt`, exercised in five shipped examples, and appears on **neither** `ContextProductContract` **nor** `DecisionReplayRecord`. It is calculated and discarded. The whitepaper makes `D_c` load-bearing (§7.7.4–§7.7.8: debt gates Forced LLM and Fail-Closed), so a delivered product that carries no debt is a fidelity defect against §7.7 and not merely an ergonomic gap — measured at `6e9fd2f` by reading both contracts field by field. It was not caught because every gate the phase inherited tests what the fabric *does* rather than what the delivered product *carries*, and no test asserts the absence. **Why it matters more than a missing field.** The question that surfaced it is the adoption argument itself. Given a Context Product answering *"who ultimately owns Acme?"*, a consuming agent that cannot tell whether the ownership data was refreshed this morning or eighteen months ago has been handed a database query with extra ceremony. Five of the six axes reach the wire today — `E`/`R` as payload, `T` as `temporal_boundary`/`expires_at`/`ttl_anchor`, `P` as `policy_bundle_versions`, `Π` as `plan_id`, `L` as `operators_invoked`/`graph_snapshot_at` — and the sixth signal, the one that says how much to trust the other five, does not. Dave's stated shape for it is **richer than a scalar**: *"the response for ACME could return something that stated the last time ACME key investor data was updated - or if an event had transpired with one of the key shareholders that should be considered by the consuming agent."* That is per-subject recency **and** material-event salience, not a single product-level number — so the design question is what shape `D_c` takes on the wire, not merely where to put the existing `Decimal`. **Consequences, recorded rather than resolved here.** This entry withdraws a constraint and names a defect; it does not design the remedy. The remedy is a Phase D mini-cycle per CLAUDE.md §3, carrying at least: the on-the-wire shape of debt (scalar, per-factor, per-subject, or per-claim); whether it lands on `ContextProductContract`, on `DecisionReplayRecord`, or on both, and what replay determinism requires of each; how per-entity last-observed timestamps reach it, given `λ_c` already lives in Control Plane configuration; what "a material event transpired" means mechanically without encoding domain values in the core; and whether the three validation gates gain a fourth. Also open: whether the Section 1 example's fixed subject and fixed temporal boundary — both currently literals in artifacts — become runtime arguments in the same cycle, since an agent asking about any company at any time is the use case that exposed all of this. Originates: Dave's ruling of 2026-08-10 during Phase 16 wave 3, on reading `examples/s1-01-hello-context-product`; supersedes ROADMAP Phase 16 criterion 10; withdraws the premise of `D-13` and `D-14` in `D-IMPL-94`; whitepaper Ch 7 §7.7.4–§7.7.8 (`D_c` gates Forced LLM and Fail-Closed) and §5.2 (the six axes); `src/ccf/halflife/debt.py`; `src/ccf/products/contract.py`; `src/ccf/replay/record.py`; CLAUDE.md §1, §3 and §11.

**D-IMPL-97 — A Context Product is one standardised vessel; the assembler is a Protocol whose implementation is a declared agent.** Date: 2026-08-10. Decided by: Dave, across the Phase 16 wave-3 review of `examples/s1-01-hello-context-product`. Two rulings, recorded together because the second only makes sense given the first. **Ruling 1 — the vessel.** Verbatim: *"The true ContextProduct is nothing more than a vessel that has been assembled to represent a unique capability for the calling agent to consume. Kind of like MCP — a standard ContextProduct doesn't really need to subclass, it just needs to have certain operations and payloads which we have already determined via the whitepaper."* A Context Product is **one standardised vessel**, not a class hierarchy. What makes a vessel a `KYC_ContextProduct` is **how it was assembled**, not its Python type. Class identity stays data — a `schema_name` resolved through the Control Plane registry — and the domain payload is disciplined by a **declared payload schema** the class registers, in the shape MCP tools declare `inputSchema`. **This is a wording correction to whitepaper §7.6, not a reversal of it** (Dave, explicitly: *"Vessel wording is not reversal"*). §7.6 currently reads *"the typed scaffold every per-product subclass inherits and extends; the per-product subclasses carry the domain-specific payload"*; its **intent** — a typed payload with cross-cutting invariants living once on the base — is fully preserved by a declared schema, which delivers both without Python inheritance. Four arguments carried the ruling, in the order they matter: **debt by construction**, since debt on the base vessel means every product carries it while every subclass is a place to forget, and *debt computed and discarded* is exactly the defect this review found; **language neutrality**, since a subclass is a Python artifact and a product crossing A2A to a Java or TypeScript consumer cannot inherit a Pydantic class, so a Python-shaped type does not belong at a seam CCF commits to federating across organizational boundaries; **the No-Hardcoding Rule** (CLAUDE.md §6.4), since a `KYC_ContextProduct` class in code makes the product taxonomy code while `schema_name` plus a declared schema makes it configuration, and code contains interpreters, never the things interpreted; and **the code already works this way** — `ContextProductContract.schema_name` is documented verbatim as *"Class identity"*, a string resolved through a registry, so subclassing would layer a hierarchy over a registry that already does the job. Bounding the MCP analogy so it is not over-applied: MCP deliberately carries no governance semantics, being a capability and transport standard, whereas a Context Product's reason for existing is that it carries policy versions in force, lineage that must strictly equal what ran, a freshness SLA, debt, and a replay record that must exist before delivery. The accurate statement is **MCP-shaped in its typing discipline, with a governance envelope MCP has no equivalent for**. **Ruling 2 — the agent is the assembler implementation.** Verbatim: *"The assembler, which I agree should be a Protocol, is what makes the ContextProduct a KYC_ContextProduct"*, and then *"Agent becomes the implementation protocol."* The split is **Protocol for the producer, standardised vessel for the produced**, and the Protocol's implementation is a **declared agent** — a Control Plane artifact produced by the Agent Factory from the `context_assembly` archetype, not SDK code and not a subclass. What the assembler owns, per Dave: it knows where its data lives and how to get it; it talks to the six backends directly, so the adapter work of 15.2/15.3/15.4 is not lost; it creates or uses tools to gather what else it needs; it may enlist other agents to produce content for inclusion, or stay wholly deterministic; it may keep its own KG in whichever of the six stores is simplest; and the calling agent invokes the product rather than an MCP server in front of a database, so the orchestration mess is handled inside. **A correction to a finding recorded earlier in this review, made here so the record is not wrong.** An earlier pass asserted that `ContextAssemblyAgent` "does not exist in `src/`" and that "the producer side has a designated home and the home is empty." **That is false, and the grep behind it searched for the wrong symbol.** All six archetypes ship: `src/ccf/agents/archetypes.py` registers `workflow`, `document_intelligence`, `analytics_insights`, `monitoring_surveillance`, `content_generation` and `context_assembly` in `ARCHETYPES`, the last as `_ContextAssemblyComponent` declaring `fabric_interaction_pattern() == "typed-product-emission"` and two replay obligations — an emitted-product replay envelope, and policy composing before similarity at every assembly step. What is *actually* missing is narrower and more useful to know: `ArchetypeComponent` is a **declarative** Protocol — `archetype_id`, `fabric_interaction_pattern`, `replay_obligations`, `configuration_defaults` — so the archetype declares what the fabric requires of this class of agent and carries **no assembly behaviour**: no source binding, no tool or agent enlistment, no product emission. Its own docstring says so — *"The emission pattern is declared here… the transports (in-process, MCP egress, A2A) bind in I.3."* The assembler Protocol is therefore a **new behavioural surface** rather than a fill-in-the-blank, and the archetype is the seam it attaches to. **Why the agent is the right implementation, and this is confirmation rather than convenience.** The six specialization axes of CLAUDE.md §6.2 already describe what an assembler needs, and one of them is decisive: **axis 5, the half-life and debt profile**, is already a **required** field on agent definitions — `halflife_debt_profile`, a pinned `ccf-artifact://` reference, with `DebtProfile` a shipped `VersionedArtifact` at `src/ccf/controlplane/artifacts.py:225` and a published schema at `docs/schemas/ccf.debt-profile.json`. So the home for a product's debt configuration already exists, on the agent, declared and version-pinned. Axis 2 binds which product schemas it emits, axis 3 its perspective, axis 4 the policy regime bounding what it may consult, axis 6 its instruction artifacts; and channel 2 — skilling — governs which tools and peer agents it may enlist, with every grant and revocation already landing in replay. A product's identity therefore becomes **auditable**: replay answers not only what it returned but what it was permitted to consult. **What this entry does not settle.** The on-the-wire shape of debt (scalar, per-factor, per-subject, per-claim) and whether recency and salience are one field or two; whether debt lands on the product, the replay record, or both; what "a material event transpired" means mechanically without domain values in the core; whether payload validation becomes a fourth gate or binds at class registration; whether the request surface is a typed request contract per class — Dave's *"company name and top investors above 25%"* — which is what makes a product **callable** rather than configurable and would collapse the example's fixed-subject and fixed-instant defects into one design; and debt composition weighting for aggregate products. These are enumerated with their evidence in `docs/CONTEXT_PRODUCT_REVISION.md` §9 and are the agenda for the Phase D mini-cycle this ruling implies. Originates: Dave's rulings of 2026-08-10 during Phase 16 wave 3; corrects whitepaper §7.6's wording without reversing its intent; `docs/CONTEXT_PRODUCT_REVISION.md`; `src/ccf/products/contract.py`; `src/ccf/agents/archetypes.py`; `src/ccf/controlplane/artifacts.py`; `docs/schemas/ccf.agent-definition.json`; CLAUDE.md §6.1, §6.2, §6.3 and §6.4; whitepaper Ch 6 §6.3, Ch 7 §7.6 and §7.7.

**D-IMPL-98 — The request surface is a typed request contract per product class.** RESOLVED — option (a). Date: 2026-08-11. Approver: Dave. **The ruling.** Every product class declares a **typed request contract as a Control Plane artifact**, in the `SkillArgumentSchema` shape. Subject and instant become arguments of that request rather than literals in an artifact, which is what makes a Context Product **callable** rather than configurable, and which collapses the fixed-subject and fixed-instant defects into one design instead of two patches. **Measured cost the ruling was made against** (`docs/CONTEXT_PRODUCT_RULING_EVIDENCE.md` § Q1, option (a), measured at `3df4e91` on 2026-08-11 by `tests/spikes/test_contract_field_addition_cost.py`): **one** new artifact class plus **one** new `docs/schemas/*.json` under the bytes-equality drift gate (`Makefile:253`); the declaration threads through **29** `register_product_class` call sites across 26 files and **18** governed `serve(` call sites across 12 files; door-side validation lands on the three delivery paths enumerated under `D-IMPL-100`; and **0** `ContextProductContract` call-site repairs, because the request surface stays off the vessel. **What the alternatives were measured to cost, and why they were not taken.** Option (b) — no contract, subject and instant as explicit parameters of the existing serve path — is **18** `serve(` sites across 12 files, of which 9 are in `examples/` across 8 files, with zero new artifact classes; its measured consequence is that whitepaper §6.3 **Discovery** (`docs/CCF_Whitepaper_1-2.md:1463`) and **Addressability** (`:1465`) remain unrepresented in code, which is **2 of the 3** elements `docs/CONTEXT_PRODUCT_REVISION.md` §1.2 measured as absent. Option (c) — defer the contract, add the parameters now — is (b)'s 18 sites now plus (a)'s full population later, with the two populations overlapping at the 12 `serve(` files, so those 12 files are edited twice. The ruling therefore buys two of the three absent §6.3 elements for a cost that lands entirely on registration and serve, and not at all on the vessel. **Scope consequence, ruled explicitly: discovery and addressability are NOT declaration-only this phase.** `15.5-CONTEXT.md`'s `<deferred>` block permitted a declaration-only landing; under option (a) that permission is moot, because addressability and the request contract are the same commitment. Both land for real. **What this does not re-open.** The slot this contract fills is already reserved — `D-IMPL-49`'s canonical selection signature carries an optional typed per-class block declared in the Control Plane, and this entry supplies that block's shape for product requests rather than altering the signature. Cross-referenced, not restated. **Governs:** plan `15.5-08` (built entirely against this ruling), and the request-path work in `15.5-10` and `15.5-13`; requirement `CPS-07`; ROADMAP Phase 15.5 criterion 7. Originates: `docs/CONTEXT_PRODUCT_REVISION.md` §9 Q1 and `D-IMPL-97`'s closing enumeration of what it did not settle; whitepaper Ch 6 §6.3 *Addressability* at `docs/CCF_Whitepaper_1-2.md:1465`, worked there as `/context-products/credit-risk/counterparty/{counterparty-id}?intent=…&freshness=…`; Dave's stated shape, *"maybe it's just the company name and 'top investors above 25%'."*

**D-IMPL-99 — Debt's shape on the wire is per-factor, using the shipped `DebtAssessment`.** RESOLVED — per-factor. Date: 2026-08-11. Approver: Dave. **The ruling.** Debt travels as the shipped `DebtAssessment` — `debt`, `signal`, and the `factors` carrying freshness, completeness and semantic consistency — not as a scalar. **Measured cost** (`docs/CONTEXT_PRODUCT_RULING_EVIDENCE.md` § Q2): **0 new type work.** The type already ships at `src/ccf/halflife/debt.py:149-165`, is already `Decimal`-safe for replay, and has **6** construction sites in 6 files with **9** `assess_debt` sites in 3 files; adding it to a contract costs `D-IMPL-100`'s placement cost and nothing else. The scalar option was measured as one `Decimal` field wherever the placement ruling puts it — cheaper by nothing, since the placement cost is the whole cost either way — and loses which of F/C/S collapsed, which is the case `DebtAssessment`'s own docstring makes. **Per-subject and per-claim were ruled out as NOT MEASURABLE, and the reason is a missing key rather than a missing budget.** `Observation` (`src/ccf/halflife/decay.py::Observation`) carries exactly `("observation_type", "observed_at")` — no claim id, no entity URI, no join key — so the per-subject key does not exist anywhere on the debt path, and there is no structure in this tree to count a per-subject cost against. That is the same missing link `D-IMPL-101` discharges; building it is a precondition, not a field addition. **Sub-question, ruled: recency and salience are not one field, because only one of them exists.** Recency is computable today by `FreshnessScorer.score(self, observations: Sequence[Observation], *, now: datetime) -> Decimal` (`src/ccf/halflife/debt.py:233-262`, signature read rather than assumed); salience has **no producer anywhere in `src/` or `runtime/`**. Recency ships in the per-factor payload; salience defers under `D-IMPL-101`. **What this does not re-open.** The computable definitions of F, C and S, and the scorer-version pinning that makes a per-factor payload replayable at all, are `D-IMPL-47`'s and stand unaltered — cross-referenced, not restated. **Governs:** plan `15.5-11`; requirements `CPS-01` and `CPS-02`. Originates: `docs/CONTEXT_PRODUCT_REVISION.md` §9 Q2; `D-IMPL-96`, which named debt computed-and-discarded as a fidelity defect against whitepaper Ch 7 §7.7.4–§7.7.8 and left the wire shape open.

**D-IMPL-100 — Debt lands on both the product and the replay record.** RESOLVED — both. Date: 2026-08-11. Approver: Dave. **The ruling.** `DebtAssessment` is carried on `ContextProductContract` **and** on `DecisionReplayRecord`. **Measured cost** (`docs/CONTEXT_PRODUCT_RULING_EVIDENCE.md` § Q3, the four-placement table): the content address of the spike's stand-in vessel **moves** from the measured baseline `14217148e333aee2004640a66f5bdcfff609cbd808753c49ce9fa94af6c50372` to `012f542e…f4f4904`, **and is reconstructible** — a rehydrator reading debt back off the record reproduces the identical bytes, an **observed byte-equality**, not an inference. The cost is therefore product-only's address move **plus** record-only's record work **plus** a signature change to `ReplayEnvironment.rehydrate_product`, a **public Protocol with 7 implementations across 6 files** (`src/ccf/replay/engine.py`, `tests/replay/test_engine_rehydration.py`, `tests/replay/test_query_sequence_pin.py`, `perf/suites/replay/conftest.py`, `examples/06-decision-replay/run.py`, `examples/external/00-hello-context/run.py`), plus a `docs/surface-changes/` fragment. **Product-only is NOT VIABLE, by observed measurement rather than by argument.** The same field added to the vessel with nothing on the record to reconstruct it from makes all **7** `rehydrate_product` implementations return a product the engine's hash check at `src/ccf/replay/engine.py:449-455` rejects with `ReplayDivergence`, because `canonical_bytes` walks a model field-by-field over `type(value).model_fields` (`src/ccf/contracts/canonical.py:102-111`) and the field is therefore in the address. Record-only is deterministic — address unchanged, **0** of the 42 `ContextProductContract` sites move, the tripwire stays green — and reaches no consumer at all, failing ROADMAP criterion 1 and whitepaper `:2696` (*"a runtime signal the agent must consume"*). The fourth placement derived during research, debt on `ServedProduct` beside the product, is one type and one line at its single construction site in `src/ccf/replay/serve.py` and moves no address — and reaches **0 of 3** wire consumers, which is the measured cost of what it does not do. **The three doors, named because criterion 1 says no delivery path drops it, and because a ruling priced against one door understates the cost by two.** All three serialize `servable.product` and **none** touches `ServedProduct.replay_ref`: (1) fabric-internal MCP egress at `runtime/ccf_runtime/mcp/egress.py:152-163`, serializing `canonical_bytes(servable.product)`; (2) the HTTP API `retrieve` route at `runtime/ccf_runtime/http_api/routes/product.py:35-42`, serializing `canonical_response(servable.product)`; (3) the **external front door**, the Experience server's `context_product` resource at `runtime/ccf_runtime/mcp/experience.py:560-570`, serializing `canonical_bytes(servable.product)` — paths 1 and 3 carry the identical three-string signature `context_product(tenant, product_class, version)` and the identical body, which is why pricing against path 1 alone is the specific error the enumeration exists to prevent. **Under this ruling debt reaches all three doors plus in-process callers, and reaches them without a code change at any door**, because each already serializes the vessel and the vessel now carries debt. **The tripwire the implementing plan re-runs:** `pytest tests/replay/test_engine_rehydration.py -q` → **13 passed in 1.07s**, exit 0, measured at `3df4e91` before any change. Plan `15.5-11` runs it before its first edit and after every commit that changes a hashed contract. **Governs:** plan `15.5-11`, which implements against three doors rather than one; requirements `CPS-01` and `CPS-11`; ROADMAP Phase 15.5 criterion 1. Originates: `docs/CONTEXT_PRODUCT_REVISION.md` §9 Q3, whose enumeration offered only product / record / both; the fourth option was derived from the tree during `15.5-RESEARCH.md` and is costed in the evidence rather than adopted. Realizes the remedy `D-IMPL-96` named and deliberately declined to design.

**D-IMPL-101 — "A material event transpired": salience defers to Phase 17; recency ships now.** RESOLVED — option (d). Date: 2026-08-11. Approver: Dave. **The ruling.** The phase ships **recency only**. Salience — the *"an event had transpired with one of the key shareholders"* limb of Dave's Acme case — is deferred, and no mechanism for it lands in this phase. **Measured cost** (`docs/CONTEXT_PRODUCT_RULING_EVIDENCE.md` § Q4): **0**, because recency is already computable by `FreshnessScorer.score(self, observations: Sequence[Observation], *, now: datetime) -> Decimal` (`src/ccf/halflife/debt.py:233-262`), and salience has **no producer anywhere in `src/` or `runtime/`** to defer. **Option (c), supersession-as-Policy-event — the most whitepaper-faithful of the four — was ruled out on measurement as a build rather than a wiring task, and assumption A3 is discharged in the negative with it.** Traced: `supersed` occurs **0** times in `src/ccf/halflife/`, **0** in `src/ccf/projection/` and **0** in `src/ccf/products/`, against **348** in `src/ccf/graph/`; supersession lives at `src/ccf/graph/protocols.py:132-133` as `ClaimRecord.superseded_by` / `superseded_at`; the consumer that would need it is `FreshnessScorer.score`, whose only input is a `Sequence[Observation]`; and `Observation` carries no join key by which the two could meet. Decisively, **`Observation(...)` has 0 constructor call sites in `src/` or `runtime/` — no SDK code constructs one at all.** Making the link exist requires an identity field on `Observation` (or a parallel event sequence beside it), **plus** a producer reading `superseded_by`/`superseded_at` off the graph and joining the two, **plus** a path from that producer to the debt computation. None of the three exists. **Consequence for the phase, stated because a plan depends on it:** plan `15.5-11` edits `src/ccf/halflife/debt.py` under this ruling and **does not** make the A3 link exist, so the evidence module's reported-not-asserted A3 verdict stays true for the phase's life rather than being turned red by correct work. Options (a) opaque per-class salience identifiers compared structurally and never interpreted (the shipped `SkillRequirements` precedent, `D-IMPL-29`), and (b) a `SalienceScorerProtocol` beside the shipped `DebtFactorScorerProtocol`, are **not** ruled in and **not** ruled out — they remain the two shapes a Phase 17 salience cycle chooses between, with their costs already measured here (option (a): 29 `register_product_class` sites or 0 under a default, no new producer needed; option (b): one new Protocol, 0 existing `assess_debt` sites touched if the factor is optional). **Governs:** plan `15.5-11`; requirement `CPS-01`. Originates: `docs/CONTEXT_PRODUCT_REVISION.md` §9 Q4; `15.5-RESEARCH.md` assumption A3, rated MEDIUM-HIGH and explicitly untraced there, traced and discharged in the evidence; whitepaper Ch 7 §7.7.

**D-IMPL-102 — Payload validation is schema validity at registration and payload conformity at bind; no fourth gate.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-08-11. Approver: Dave. **Dave's ruling, verbatim:** *"Q5 payload validation → Schema validity at registration + payload conformity at Bind (request time). Gate scripts remain structural only."* **The ruling, in its three parts, because the third is as load-bearing as the first two.** (1) **Schema validity is checked at registration**: when a product class is registered, its **declared** payload schema is checked for well-formedness — a malformed declaration is refused at wiring time, before any request exists. (2) **Payload conformity is checked at bind, which is request time**: when an actual request is bound to a product class, the actual payload is checked against that class's declared schema. This limb **couples directly to `D-IMPL-98`** — the typed request contract per product class is what a request binds to, so bind is precisely where a payload meets its declared schema, and the two rulings describe one surface rather than two. (3) **No fourth gate is added to `run_gates`.** The three shipped validation gates — the empty-operator guard, lineage strict equality, TTL bounds — **stay structural and are not joined by a payload gate**, which keeps the whitepaper's three-validation-gate commitment intact rather than widening it. **Measured cost** (`docs/CONTEXT_PRODUCT_RULING_EVIDENCE.md` § Q5). Limb 1, registration, is option (b)'s measurement: **29** `register_product_class` call sites across 26 files if required, or **0** under a default on the `accepted_policy_binding_modes` precedent (`src/ccf/products/contract.py:193-198`), and **0** serve-time benchmark cost. Limb 2, bind-time conformity, lands on the request surface `D-IMPL-98` creates rather than on the gate path — that surface's own measured population is § Q1 option (a)'s **18** governed `serve(` call sites across 12 files and the three delivery paths enumerated under `D-IMPL-100`; conformity checking adds no separate call-site population of its own, because it rides the bind the request contract already introduces. Limb 3 is a cost **not** incurred: option (a)'s **43** `run_gates` call sites across 22 files are untouched, and none of the `source_attestation` keyword-only-defaulted machinery (`src/ccf/products/gates.py:306`) is needed, because nothing is added there. **A measurement that is deliberately NOT cited as support for this ruling.** The evidence's § A8 headroom figures — 80 ns, 230 ns and 507 ns of absolute margin on `perf/suites/micro/test_gates.py`'s three benchmarks — were measured because a *fourth gate* would have landed on the canonical `run_gates` sequence at serve time. **No gate lands, so those figures are not the relevant measurement for this ruling** and must not be quoted as though one were. They remain the correct figures for what they measure, and `D-IMPL-107` still governs how the battery around them is read. **Consequence for the phase, recorded because it changes a plan's premise rather than its detail.** Plan **`15.5-09` is written on the premise of a payload gate in `run_gates` and must be re-scoped**: it ships **bind-time conformity**, not a fourth gate. Its serve-time perf argument goes with the gate — there is no new gate to benchmark — and its verification narrows accordingly. This entry records the consequence and does not make the edit; the re-scope is the planning owner's, not this plan's. Plan `15.5-07` is unaffected in kind: it still declares the payload schema and binds it at registration, which is limb 1 exactly. **Governs:** plans `15.5-07` (schema declaration and registration-time validity) and `15.5-09` (re-scoped to bind-time conformity); requirement `CPS-03`. Originates: `docs/CONTEXT_PRODUCT_REVISION.md` §9 Q5; whitepaper Ch 6 §6.3 and Ch 7 §7.6, whose three validation gates this ruling deliberately leaves at three.

**D-IMPL-103 — `SkillArgumentSchema` is extended in place to one level of nesting.** RESOLVED — branch (i), extend in place. Date: 2026-08-11. Approver: Dave. **Dave's ruling, verbatim, because its scope is the whole of it:** *"Extend SkillArgumentSchema in place to support one level of nested objects and lists-of-objects (sufficient for the UBO owner list). The three typed facts previously lost under flattening become expressible. Existing depth-1 usages remain valid; the change is a widening, not a replacement. Record the schema change in the same surface-change fragment that plan 15.5-11 already needs for the rehydrate_product Protocol update."* **Two bounds, stated plainly because both bind and either one read loosely turns this into a different ruling. First: ONE level of nesting — nested objects and lists-of-objects, one deep — not arbitrary depth.** Depth 2 is the ceiling. **Second: a WIDENING, not a replacement.** Every existing depth-1 usage remains valid, no shipped declaration is rewritten, and no consumer of the current shape breaks. **This supersedes the standing depth-1 ruling on `SkillArgumentSchema` (`src/ccf/skills/catalog.py:194-206`) *only to the extent of that one level*** — the ruling is otherwise intact and continues to govern. **Measured cost** (`docs/CONTEXT_PRODUCT_RULING_EVIDENCE.md` § Q5 sub-question, branch (i)): **3** `to_input_schema()` call sites move (`src/ccf/skills/toolsurface.py`, `tests/skills/test_catalog.py`, `tests/skills/test_tool_surface.py`); **9** files mention `argument_schema` and are in the blast radius — including **all three harness adapters** (`adk`, `claude_agent`, `langgraph`), `cli/commands/skill_import.py`, `src/ccf/skills/catalog.py`, `src/ccf/skills/toolsurface.py` and 3 test modules; **1** committed schema regenerates, `docs/schemas/ccf.skill-catalog-entry.json`, under the bytes-equality gate; and **1** `docs/surface-changes/` fragment is required — which per the ruling is **the same fragment plan `15.5-11` already writes** for the `rehydrate_product` Protocol change, not a second one. **The two alternatives and their measured costs.** Branch (ii), a nesting-capable sibling `ProductPayloadSchema`, duplicates **5** symbols (`JsonSchemaType`, `SkillArgumentProperty`, `SkillArgumentSchema`, `to_input_schema`, and the required-names-exist validator) and moves **0** existing call sites — a second machinery where `D-IMPL-97` asked for reuse of the one already proven. Branch (iii), flattening v0 payloads to one level, moves **0** files and regenerates **0** schemas and **does not survive without loss**: measured against `examples/s1-01-hello-context-product/artifacts/expected.yaml`, **3** declared fields lose a typed fact — `ownership_percent_by_party` (object keyed by party URI), `beneficial_owners` (array of two-field objects) and `entity_count_by_class` (object keyed by entity class) — and flattening `beneficial_owners` into parallel arrays preserves the values while degrading the pairing to an index convention the schema cannot state. Those are the three facts the ruling's first sentence restores. **Assumption A1 is confirmed rather than corrected:** `SkillArgumentSchema` — a schema declared **as data** — is what `D-IMPL-97` meant by reusing the machinery already proven on eight artifact classes, as against the `docs/schemas/` export path, which generates schemas **from Pydantic models** and would therefore require one model per product class, i.e. exactly the subclassing `D-IMPL-97` rules out. **Governs:** plans `15.5-07` (the payload schema declaration) and `15.5-08` (the request contract, which sits in the same shape); requirement `CPS-03`. Originates: `docs/CONTEXT_PRODUCT_REVISION.md` §9 Q5's unavoidable sub-question; `15.5-RESEARCH.md` assumption A1; `D-IMPL-97` ruling 1 (the declared payload schema in the shape MCP tools declare `inputSchema`).

**D-IMPL-104 — Aggregate debt composes worst-factor-wins; the rule is stated now and implemented later.** RESOLVED as to meaning; **implementation DEFERRED**. Date: 2026-08-11. Approver: Dave. **Dave's direction, on why an entry exists for a surface that does not:** *"Record a D-IMPL that states the aggregation rule ... even while the aggregate-product surface does not yet exist. Implementation can wait until the surface appears; the meaning cannot."* **The rule.** An aggregate product's debt is the **per-factor maximum across its constituents** — worst factor wins, freshness against freshness, completeness against completeness, semantic consistency against semantic consistency. **Recorded as consistent with `D-IMPL-31` rather than as a new axiom:** that ruling already composes validity by taking the **most constraining** constituent, and worst-factor-wins is the same discipline expressed on a metric where higher means worse. An aggregate is no fresher than its stalest load-bearing constituent and no more complete than its emptiest; stating that on one axis and its opposite on another would be two rules where one will do. Cross-referenced, not restated. **Measured cost** (`docs/CONTEXT_PRODUCT_RULING_EVIDENCE.md` § Q6): all three weighting alternatives — class-declared decision-critical components, conjunctive-over-critical, and multiplicative-over-all — are **NOT MEASURABLE from this tree**, and the cell says why rather than estimating. An aggregate product — a `ContextProductContract` composed from constituent products — **has no representation in this tree at all**, so there is nothing to count against; and `union_lineage` (**10** call sites across 3 files, already property-tested) composes a **producer/consumer pair** across the peering boundary rather than an N-way sibling set, its own docstring recording order-independence as *"a law about the two set axes"* only, which leaves *whose* `graph_snapshot_at` undefined for N siblings. Option (d), deferring the debt limb, costs **0**. **Implementation is deferred until the aggregate-product surface exists.** Plan `15.5-12` ships criterion 8's three named limbs — lineage union, the TTL floor, and the SLA refusal — **without the debt limb**, and cites this entry for the meaning rather than inventing a rule at the moment it first needs one. When the aggregate surface arrives, the combinator is one pure function beside `context_debt`, adds **0** new weights, and therefore does not touch the additive-form foreclosure at `src/ccf/halflife/debt.py:16-22`. **Governs:** plan `15.5-12`; requirement `CPS-08`; ROADMAP Phase 15.5 criterion 8. Originates: `docs/CONTEXT_PRODUCT_REVISION.md` §9 Q6; `D-IMPL-31`, whose mixing-refusal rule criterion 8 realizes and whose composition discipline this rule extends; whitepaper Ch 7 §7.7 (INV-CH7-62/63, the multiplicative-conjunctive F·C·S commitment).

**D-IMPL-105 — Debt is not per-principal; the coupling dissolves.** RESOLVED — option (b). Date: 2026-08-11. Approver: Dave. **The ruling.** A refused consultation is **simply not part of `C_required` for that principal**. If a principal is not entitled to a source, that source is not among the things their decision requires, so its absence is not a shortfall and does not register as debt. Debt stays **one computation per assembled product**, identical for every principal who receives that product. **Measured cost** (`docs/CONTEXT_PRODUCT_RULING_EVIDENCE.md` § Q7, option (b)): **0**. `assess_debt` remains pure over `(factors, profile)`, its signature is unchanged, and all **9** call sites across 3 files are unchanged. Option (a) — debt computed against the effective entitlement set — is **NOT MEASURABLE from this tree**, because no per-principal entitlement surface exists at any door yet: `build_egress_server` binds **no** authorizer and has **2** call sites in 2 files, and the `TenantAuthorizerProtocol` action tuple is `(grant, tenant, action_id)` with **no product-class dimension**; its cost is bounded below by criterion 5's own work and cannot be separated from it until that lands. Option (c), carrying both figures, is (a)'s cost plus one more field on a surface that does not exist. **The threat this ruling forecloses, recorded because it was named for the first time in the ruling package and is the substantive reason to prefer dissolution over resolution.** Under options (a) and (c), completeness is computed against what the caller was permitted to consult, so the completeness figure **moves when a source is withheld** — and a caller can therefore **infer what they are not allowed to see from the debt they are shown**. That is an oracle over the entitlement configuration, reachable by any principal with ordinary delivery access and no privileged read, and it is worse than a plain refusal because it is quiet: nothing in the response says a consultation was refused, only that completeness is lower than it might be, and a caller who can vary the question can map the boundary. Dissolving the coupling closes the channel **by construction rather than by redaction** — there is no per-principal figure to differ, so there is nothing to difference. **What this does not move.** Entitlement-formative construction stands exactly as the whitepaper commits it (`docs/CCF_Whitepaper_1-2.md:1529`, `:1342`): different principals still legitimately receive different products, assembled from what each may consult. What is ruled is only that **debt is not one of the things that differs**. **Governs:** plan `15.5-11` (debt), and the entitlement track behind ROADMAP Phase 15.5 criterion 5; requirements `CPS-01` and `CPS-05`. Originates: `docs/CONTEXT_PRODUCT_REVISION.md` §9 Q7 and §10; `15.5-RESEARCH.md` § Open Questions, which put forward the dissolving reading; whitepaper Ch 6 §6.3 and Ch 7 §7.7.

**D-IMPL-106 — `freshness_sla` is class-level on `RegisteredProductClass`.** RESOLVED — option (b). Date: 2026-08-11. Approver: Dave. **The whitepaper inconsistency this resolves, quoted per CLAUDE.md §15's ambiguous-passage discipline rather than paraphrased.** The sidebar enumeration at `docs/CCF_Whitepaper_1-2.md:2381`: *"The seven contract fields enumerated below are the same seven fields Fig-CH07-13 renders as the Context Product Spec sidebar (schema, **freshness SLA**, TTL policy, policy binding, lineage graph, semantic version, payload) — the prose specification and the visual sidebar commit to the same contract surface."* The prose enumeration immediately following at `:2381-2405`, unpacked field by field: `schema_name`, `schema_version` (`:2385-2387`), **`plan_id`** (`:2391`), `expires_at` (`:2393`), `ttl_anchor` (`:2395`), `lineage` (`:2401`), `payload` (`:2405`). **The two enumerations of "the same seven fields" differ by exactly one element:** the sidebar names freshness SLA where the prose names `plan_id`. **The two readings and their consequences.** Reading 1 — the sidebar is authoritative, the instance carries an SLA field, and the base therefore has eight fields rather than seven, or else `plan_id` is not one of them. Reading 2 — the prose is authoritative, and the sidebar's "freshness SLA" names a **class-level promise the product was assembled under** rather than an instance field, in which case both enumerations are consistent, nothing is missing, and `plan_id` keeps its place on the vessel. **Reading 2 is ruled.** The SLA is a property of the product class, declared once at registration and pinned by version. **Measured cost** (`docs/CONTEXT_PRODUCT_RULING_EVIDENCE.md` § Q8, option (b)): **29** `register_product_class` call sites across 26 files if required-with-no-default, or **0** under a default on the `accepted_policy_binding_modes` precedent — and **0 content addresses move.** It is the **cheapest measured option of the three**, and the only one that moves no address. Option (a), an instance field on `ContextProductContract`, is **42** call sites across 38 files if required or **0** under a positive sentinel, and **moves the address** exactly as the `D-IMPL-100` product-only measurement shows for any added hashed field — replay-safe, unlike debt, because an SLA *is* reconstructible from the registered product class, but an address move nonetheless. Option (c), both, is (a) plus (b) plus a comparison function. **Two further things the ruling settles.** It **makes the currently-false `src/ccf/products/contract.py` docstring true**, which is why the placement was worth ruling rather than defaulting. And §6.3's *"Freshness SLA varies by signal and by decision"* (`:1453`) suggests a per-signal structure rather than a scalar; that structure's own cost is not separable from the placement until its shape is declared, so **the placement is ruled here and the internal shape is the implementing plan's to declare** — no scalar is ruled in by silence. **What this does not re-open.** `D-IMPL-30` already rules the §6.3 specification element count as nine and already rules the Fig-CH07-13 seven-field typed base a *different artifact* from those elements — which is precisely the distinction reading 2 rests on. ROADMAP Phase 15.5 criterion 2 already reads nine and already cites it at `.planning/ROADMAP.md:930`; **there is no eight-to-nine correction to make**, and none was made. Cross-referenced, not restated. **Governs:** plan `15.5-07`; requirement `CPS-02`. Originates: `15.5-RESEARCH.md` § Open Questions Q8 — surfaced by research, not present in `docs/CONTEXT_PRODUCT_REVISION.md` §9; whitepaper Ch 6 §6.3 at `:1453` and Ch 7 §7.6 at `:2381-2405`; Fig-CH07-13.

**D-IMPL-107 — The `test_composed_chain` perf regression is investigated and fixed inside Phase 15.5.** RESOLVED — option (c), fix in-phase, overriding the recommendation put to Dave. Date: 2026-08-11. Approver: Dave. **The measured state.** `make perf-micro` **already exits 1 at this phase's base commit**, on two benchmarks that are not on the Context Product surface (`docs/CONTEXT_PRODUCT_RULING_EVIDENCE.md` § A8): `perf/suites/micro/test_dispatch.py::test_run_coroutine_sync_overhead` at 3.264e-05 s against a 2.928e-05 s baseline, **+11.48%**; and `perf/suites/micro/test_operators.py::test_composed_chain` at 1.22429 s against a 0.368903 s baseline, **+231.87%** — the ruling was taken against a re-run of the same benchmark reading 1.21884 s, a +230% regression either way. Both predate this phase and neither was caused by it: plan `15.5-01` changed no `src/`, `runtime/`, `examples/` or `perf/` file. Recorded as `DI-15.5-01` in the phase's `deferred-items.md`. **The ruling.** The recommendation presented was option (a) — narrow the affected plans' `<automated>` blocks so they measure the per-benchmark `test_gates.py::*` verdicts rather than the battery's exit code, and carry the regression. **Dave overrode it: `test_composed_chain` is to be investigated and fixed within Phase 15.5.** Not deferred, and **not re-baselined** — a 230% regression absorbed by moving the baseline is a regression no later reader can see, and the baseline chain is the only thing that makes `CPS-13`'s 10% band mean anything. **This is new scope the phase carries, and it is recorded with an owner so that a plan takes it rather than every plan assuming another will.** **Two consequences that travel with the ruling.** First, plans `15.5-07` and `15.5-09` **keep `make perf-micro` in their `<automated>` blocks**, on the expectation that the gate goes green; if the fix has not landed when either runs, the per-benchmark `test_gates.py::*` margins — **80 ns**, **230 ns** and **507 ns** of absolute headroom to the 10% ceiling, § A8 — are the figures that carry the verdict for this phase's work, and the battery's exit code is evidence about neither direction — noting that under `D-IMPL-102` **no fourth gate lands**, so those three margins are headroom this phase does not spend rather than a budget it draws against. Second, **a separate defect worth correcting whatever happens to the gate**: in `15.5-09` `make perf-micro` is the **first** term of an `&&` chain (`15.5-09-PLAN.md:197`), so while it exits 1 it **short-circuits the entire remainder of that verification** — `tests/test_surface_drift.py`, `tests/perf_smoke` and `tests/perf_gate` never run at all, and the plan reports red for a reason unrelated to the three suites it silently skipped. `15.5-07` places it **last** in its chain (`15.5-07-PLAN.md:345`) and therefore skips nothing; the asymmetry is accidental rather than designed, and `15.5-09`'s ordering should be corrected independently of the fix. **Not in scope of this entry:** `test_run_coroutine_sync_overhead`'s +11.48% stays carried as `DI-15.5-01`; only `test_composed_chain` is ruled in. **Governs:** the phase; requirement `CPS-13`; the `<automated>` blocks of plans `15.5-07` and `15.5-09`. Originates: `docs/CONTEXT_PRODUCT_RULING_EVIDENCE.md` § A8 and its Provenance note that the perf figures required one deliberate `make perf-micro` run because that battery is outside `make ci` by design; `.planning/phases/15.5-…/deferred-items.md` `DI-15.5-01`.

**D-IMPL-108 — The product resolver seam is widened once, by a new plan `15.5-15`, carrying both the typed request and the authorized perspective.** RESOLVED — a new wave-5 plan. Date: 2026-08-11. Approver: Dave. **The gap this closes, which was two gaps that turned out to be one.** `DI-15.5-03` recorded that all three exposed doors resolve and enforce an entitled `Perspective` but do not *forward* it into the assemble-and-gate path, so a door guarantees the **refusal** leg while leaving unproven that the product it served was shaped under the perspective it authorized.
