Separately, plan `15.5-08` declares the must-have truth *"The request surface is validated where it crosses the door, not downstream"* while its `files_modified` names **no door file** — only `src/ccf/products/`, `src/ccf/controlplane/artifacts.py` and `docs/schemas/`. Both are blocked on the same structural change: `ProductResolverProtocol` (`runtime/ccf_runtime/mcp/egress.py:136`) and `ExperienceProductResolverProtocol` (`runtime/ccf_runtime/mcp/experience.py:215`) are **three-string seams** (`tenant, product_class, version`) through which neither a `Perspective` nor a typed request can pass. **Measured blast radius**, counted at `db4fdce` rather than estimated: **2** Protocol definitions; **3** invocation sites (`mcp/egress.py:267`, `http_api/routes/product.py:107`, `mcp/experience.py:629`); **1** dependency field (`http_api/dependencies.py:71`); and **24** files across `runtime/`, `examples/` and `tests/` that supply or reference a resolver. `DI-15.5-03`'s planning-time estimate of "roughly twenty call sites" is confirmed accurate. **The ruling.** Plan `15.5-08` proceeds in wave 4 as scoped — it builds the request contract as a Control Plane artifact with its committed schema, and does **not** wire it. A **new plan `15.5-15`** lands in wave 5 and reshapes the seam **exactly once**, carrying the typed request and the authorized `Perspective` through the same widening. **The reason it is one plan and not two is the reason Q1 option (c) was rejected**: reshaping this seam twice means editing the same 24 files twice, and `D-IMPL-98` declined that cost for the request surface on identical grounds. Doing it once for both is the same argument applied consistently. **Why wave 5 and not wave 4.** Wave 4 already serializes on `src/ccf/products/__init__.py` and `docs/SURFACE-CHANGES.md` across plans `15.5-08`, `09`, `11` and `12`; adding the largest plan in the phase to it would serialize the whole wave behind it. Wave 5 currently holds only `15.5-10`, which touches `src/ccf/agents/` and does not collide with `runtime/`. `15.5-15` therefore runs parallel to `15.5-10` and depends on `15.5-08`. **Consequence for the phase:** the phase is **15 plans, not 14**, and `DI-15.5-03` acquires an owner rather than reaching the gate unowned — Dave named it *"the highest-priority structural debt for the later waves"* on 2026-08-11. **Governs:** new plan `15.5-15`; the door-validation limb of plan `15.5-08`'s must-haves; requirements `CPS-07` and `CPS-12`. Originates: `DI-15.5-03` in the phase's `deferred-items.md`, recorded by plan `15.5-06`; plan `15.5-08`'s unmet must-have truth, found by the orchestrator at wave 3; `D-IMPL-98`'s double-edit argument; `D-IMPL-102` limb 2, whose bind-time conformity check needs the same widened seam to run at the door at all.

**D-IMPL-109 — The ungoverned HTTP product door refuses rather than serving a product no perspective authorized.** RESOLVED — accept the refusal. Date: 2026-08-11. Approver: Dave. **What changed and why it was forced rather than chosen.** Plan `15.5-15` widened `ProductResolverProtocol` and `ExperienceProductResolverProtocol` so the `Perspective` a door authorizes reaches the assembler (`D-IMPL-108`, closing `DI-15.5-03`). The widened seam **requires** the perspective — deliberately not defaulted, because a resolver handed nothing and constructing its own is indistinguishable from one honouring the door's, which is the exact ambiguity the deferred item existed to close. The HTTP door in the **ungoverned** posture can name no perspective, so it now returns **503 `product-door-ungoverned`** where it previously served. The plan's own must-have anticipated this: *"A door that cannot pass a perspective refuses rather than silently constructing one."* **The ruling.** The refusal stands. A door that cannot name the perspective it authorized should not serve, and manufacturing a perspective to preserve availability reintroduces precisely the defect this phase closed. **What it costs, stated rather than buried.** This **supersedes `T-07-24`**, which preserved that posture, and **narrows `D-IMPL-73`'s acknowledged-insecure posture by one route**; `ccf product get` reports the refusal as well. Three shipped tests were **rewritten, not deleted**, to assert the new posture, and the canonical-bytes and 404 claims moved to the governed app where they still assert something. **Restoration is available and documented:** two `create_app` arguments, with code, in `docs/surface-changes/15.5-15-resolver-seam.md` — the ungoverned posture is narrowed, not removed, and a deployment that needs the old behaviour can have it explicitly rather than by default. Removing the ungoverned posture entirely was considered and NOT taken: `D-IMPL-73` exists deliberately for local development and withdrawing it needs its own ruling. **Governs:** `runtime/ccf_runtime/http_api/`; the availability posture of the ungoverned product route; supersedes `T-07-24`. Originates: plan `15.5-15`, flagged by its executor as `threat_flag: availability-posture-change` and escalated to the phase gate rather than resolved in-plan.

**D-IMPL-110 — The surface-drift gate's Protocol blind spot is recorded as debt and fixed in Phase 17.** RESOLVED — defer, with the inventory recorded. Date: 2026-08-11. Approver: Dave. **The defect, verified independently by the orchestrator rather than taken on report.** `tools/dump_surface.py` resolves a class's shape with `inspect.signature` on the **class**, which for a `Protocol` returns `__init__` — universally `(*args, **kwargs)`. It never reads `__call__`. Measured at `4d16cb9`: **56** manifest entries carry the information-free shape `"(*args, **kwargs)"`, of which **30 are named `*Protocol`**, against **54** total Protocol classes across `src/` and `runtime/`. The affected set includes `ArtifactStoreProtocol`, `ControlPlaneProtocol`, `HarnessAdapterProtocol`, `OrchestrationProtocol`, `HITLTransportProtocol`, `LLMClientProtocol` and `DebtFactorScorerProtocol` — that is, most of the pluggable substrate CLAUDE.md §11 mandates Protocols for. **The demonstration.** Plan `15.5-15` took both resolver seams from **three arguments to five** — breaking for every adopter implementing them — and `docs/surface/v0.2-surface.json` is **byte-identical across that change**. Two plans hit the wall independently: `15.5-11` for `ReplayEnvironment` and `15.5-15` for the two resolver Protocols. Both were forced to classify their change as `behavior` rather than `reshaped`, because `reshaped` fails `test_surface_completeness` when the manifest shows no diff to point at. **The ruling.** Recorded as `DI-15.5-06` and carried to **Phase 17**, not fixed in 15.5. The blind spot predates this phase and was not caused by it. **The two consequences of deferring, recorded so the next reader does not have to rediscover them:** (1) Phase 15.5 ships a **breaking Protocol change that its own drift gate cannot see**, so the surface manifest is not evidence of surface stability for this phase and must not be cited as such at the gate; and (2) the `behavior`-instead-of-`reshaped` classification stands as **precedent**, so a later author reading those two fragments will reasonably copy it. Phase 17 should expect to reclassify both entries when the tooling can see them. The orchestrator recommended fixing in-phase via `15.5-14`; Dave ruled otherwise, and the recommendation is recorded here rather than silently dropped. **Governs:** `tools/dump_surface.py`; `docs/surface/v0.2-surface.json`; the `reshaped`/`behavior` classification of the `15.5-11` and `15.5-15` fragments; Phase 17 scope. Originates: plan `15.5-15`'s `DI-15.5-06`, independently verified by the orchestrator at `4d16cb9`.

**D-IMPL-111 — The request seeds the traversal AND lands in the replay record; both halves, because they are not substitutes.** RESOLVED — option (c), both. Date: 2026-08-11. Approver: Dave. **The gap, found at plan `15.5-13`'s checkpoint and verified by the orchestrator rather than taken on report.** `D-IMPL-98` made a Context Product **callable** — subject and instant became request arguments. Nothing carried the question into replay behind it. Two consequences, measured at `d85faf8`: (1) two different *subjects* pin **identically** in `graph_query_sequence`, because the subject enters at the projection and `src/ccf/projection/engine.py:527` calls `compile_segment_query(..., seeds=None)` with a hardcoded literal; two different *instants* do pin differently, because the boundary compiles into the query. (2) `ProductRequest` appears **nowhere in `src/ccf/replay/`** — confirmed by grep over the package — so `intent` and `freshness` are recorded in none of the five dimensions. `graph_query_sequence` therefore answers *"what did this decision ask the graph?"* and not *"which question did this decision answer?"* **Why both, and why they are not alternatives.** Limb **(a)** makes the *graph query* distinguish subjects; it can never record `intent` or `freshness`, which are not graph concepts. Limb **(b)** makes the *record* carry the question; it leaves two subjects pinning identically, with a test asserting that as correct. Each alone leaves half the gap open, so the ruling takes both. **Measured cost of (a):** ONE hardcoded literal. The seeds plumbing already exists end to end — `compile_segment_query` accepts `seeds` and passes it through (`src/ccf/projection/segmentation.py:271`) and `src/ccf/graph/fallback.py:408` already reads `query.seeds`. An earlier framing of this limb as "an operator and query-compilation change" **overstated it** and is corrected here. The real risk is not the edit but its consequence: composition-preservation `(A∘B)(G) = A(B(G))` must still hold with a seeded traversal, gated by four property suites (`tests/properties/test_composition.py`, `test_staged_vs_direct.py`, `test_lineage_union.py`, `test_aggregate_composition_laws.py`). **Measured cost of (b):** **32** `build_replay_record` call sites across **28** files, or **0** forced repairs under a sentinel default — the positive-sentinel pattern this phase has now used five times and which `docs/CONTEXT_PRODUCT_RULING_EVIDENCE.md` § Q1 priced at 0 against 42 vessel sites. The record shape is whitepaper §7.10.1 surface, so this is a fidelity-facing change and not merely an additive field; expect a record content-address move, which must be traced and shown reconstructible exactly as `D-IMPL-100` required of the product address. **What this ruling makes true that was not true before:** plan `15.5-13`'s failure criterion 4 — *"rows 1 and 3 show the same PINS"* — becomes a meaningful test rather than a vacuous one, and criterion 1's promise that a different subject yields a different answer is matched by a different pinned question. **A note on how this was found, worth preserving.** The plan asserted that two different subjects produce two different pinned sequences. They did not. The executor **reported the plan false rather than producing output that looked right**, shipped a test asserting the true property, and added a guard that fails loudly if rows 1 and 2 ever stop pinning alike. That is the behaviour the checkpoint exists to elicit. **Governs:** `src/ccf/projection/engine.py`; `src/ccf/replay/record.py` and the five-dimension shape; the continuation of plan `15.5-13`; requirements `CPS-07` and `CPS-12`. Originates: `DI-15.5-07` in the phase's `deferred-items.md`; `D-IMPL-98`, whose callable-product ruling opened the gap; CLAUDE.md §11 *"Decision Replay is enforced at write time, not retrofitted."*

**D-IMPL-112 — The `s1-01` demonstration is approved, and debt is informative but not yet decision-complete.** RESOLVED — approved with the limitation recorded. Date: 2026-08-11. Approver: Dave. **What was demonstrated, and verified by the orchestrator running it rather than relaying an agent's report.** One product class answered three questions: two companies at one instant, and one company at two instants. A different subject returns a different beneficial-owner list (Jane 30%/John 45% for Acme; Jane 60% alone for Beta). A later instant surfaces Marcus Vale at 30% with **nothing re-ingested** — the transfer was already in the graph on 1 August and became legally effective in September, and the temporal boundary found it. Debt is measured rather than decorative: six weeks of decay moves `D_c` 0.035 → 0.221 and `signal` `ok` → `forced_llm`, driven entirely by freshness (0.995 → 0.803) while completeness and semantic consistency hold. Under `D-IMPL-111` the pins now distinguish both the subject and the instant, and dimension 5 carries the request verbatim. **Dave's verdict, recorded in his own terms because the limitation is the useful part.** A KYC analyst would **not act on `D_c=0.221 / forced_llm / F=0.803` alone**. They would accept it as a correctly computed warning that freshness has decayed into the Forced-LLM band, and would then immediately need three things the product does not carry: (1) **which specific observations contributed the decay**; (2) **when the underlying source filings were last refreshed**; (3) **what operational obligation `forced_llm` actually imposes** — re-pull, accept supervised synthesis, escalate, or something else. His summary: *"The signal is informative and correctly attributed. It is not yet decision-complete."* **Why this is an approval and not a gap.** Phase 15.5 set out to prove that the measurement **exists**, is **attached to both the product and the replay record**, and **correctly names the weakened factor**. All three hold, demonstrably. Decision-completeness — evidence pointers and a prescribed action — is a **different commitment** that this phase did not scope and does not claim. Recording the boundary explicitly is what keeps the phase record honest: a later reader must not infer from "debt is delivered" that an analyst can act on it unaided. **What this makes future work, stated so it can be planned rather than rediscovered:** closing the gap means (a) debt carrying evidence pointers back to the observations whose decay it summarises — which is `D-IMPL-99`'s per-subject and per-claim options, both ruled NOT MEASURABLE because `Observation` carries no entity or claim identity, so the join key must be built first; (b) source-refresh recency as a distinct fact from computed freshness; and (c) a declared obligation vocabulary attached to each debt signal, which is Control Plane configuration and therefore user values, not SDK mechanism (CLAUDE.md §11). Item (a) is the same missing link `D-IMPL-101` discharged when it deferred salience. **Governs:** the phase record's claim about what debt delivery achieves; ROADMAP Phase 15.5 criterion 1; requirements `CPS-01` and `CPS-02`; the scope of any future debt-completeness work. Originates: plan `15.5-13`'s blocking human-verify checkpoint, the demonstration Phase 15.5 was built to make possible, answering Dave's 2026-08-10 question *"What is the benefit of using CCF?"*

**D-IMPL-113 — Bind-time payload conformity is an adopter obligation the SDK documents, not a door the SDK enforces.** RESOLVED — adopter obligation. Date: 2026-08-11. Approver: Dave. **The question.** `refuse_bound_payload` and `refuse_request` (`src/ccf/products/bind.py`, `src/ccf/products/request.py`) ship complete and tested, and **no shipped door calls either** — mechanism without a call site, raised as residual **R1** by the close-time panel and verified against the tree. **The ruling.** The SDK ships the mechanism; the deployment's own resolver calls it. This follows plan `15.5-09`'s own reasoning, which the panel confirmed rather than contradicted: the bind's precondition is that a request has already resolved to a `RegisteredProductClass` **and** the payload for that bind exists, and **the door never holds the registered class** — `ProductResolverProtocol` hands the deployment three strings plus a perspective and a request, and the class is resolved behind that seam. Wiring a call at the door would require the door to acquire the registered class, which is a different seam than the one `D-IMPL-108` widened. **Why not enforce it.** Placing the call is `D-IMPL-102`'s own question, and the natural enforcement point sits adjacent to limb 3's *"gate scripts remain structural only"* line. An SDK-enforced payload check on the serve path is the shape limb 3 declined; enforcing it one layer out would re-litigate that ruling by implementation rather than by decision. The executor declined to place it for exactly this reason and escalated instead, which was correct. **The obligation this creates, and it is the SDK's to discharge.** *Documented* is not the same as *mentioned*: the adopter has to be told, at the seam, that a resolver which does not call `refuse_bound_payload` serves an unvalidated payload against a schema its class declared. **`CPS-03` therefore stays Pending by design, not by omission** — and the requirement row must say which, or a later reader will read an unmet requirement as an oversight. **What this does not license.** It is the second instance of convention-not-enforcement in this phase (`DI-15.5-05` records the first, the binder refusals with no calling path) and the class already travels to Phase 16. Two instances is a pattern worth watching: a Protocol the SDK ships and never calls is indistinguishable, from the tree, from one an adopter forgot. **Governs:** `src/ccf/products/bind.py`; `src/ccf/products/request.py`; requirement `CPS-03`'s disposition. Originates: close-time panel residual R1, verified; plan `15.5-09`'s recorded join point; `D-IMPL-102` limb 3.

**D-IMPL-114 — Prose cites `path::Symbol`, not a line range.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-08-11. Approver: Dave. **The defect, second occurrence.** Three citations of `src/ccf/replay/engine.py:449-455` — in `docs/DECISIONS.md`, `docs/SURFACE-CHANGES.md` and plan `15.5-11`'s landed fragment — drifted by 11 lines when `D-IMPL-111`'s edit moved the code, raised as residual **R3**. They were deliberately not rewritten in place: an append-only ruling record, a whole-tree-assembled artifact, and a landed plan's fragment are all things a later editor should not silently revise. `DI-15.4-02` already recorded the same class at larger scale — **45 drifted anchors**. **The ruling.** A line-anchored citation is wrong the moment code moves, and code moves every phase; the anchor therefore encodes a fact with a shorter half-life than the claim it supports. **Prose cites `path::Symbol`** — a module path and a symbol name, which survives an edit that moves the symbol and *correctly* breaks when the symbol is renamed or deleted, which is the case a reader actually needs flagged. **Consequences, stated so the work is plannable rather than assumed.** (1) `cite02-anchor` must accept and prefer the symbol form. (2) Existing line-anchored citations need a sweep; this phase's three and `DI-15.4-02`'s 45 are the known population, and neither was measured tree-wide. (3) The sweep is **not** Phase 15.5 work — the gate is ruled approved with the three stale citations extant, and they are recorded as such. **The rejected alternative and why.** Widening `cite02-anchor` to accept bare ranges was considered: it is cheaper, and it is what a checker-shaped fix looks like. It was not taken because it makes the checker stop catching citations that are *genuinely* wrong in order to tolerate ones that merely drifted — trading a real signal for a maintenance saving. **Governs:** `tools/lints` `cite02-anchor`; the citation convention in `docs/`, `.planning/` prose and source docstrings; a future anchor sweep. Originates: close-time panel residual R3, verified; `DI-15.4-02`.

**D-IMPL-115 — `D-IMPL-31`'s expiry formula gains a third term; the strengthening is adopted as an amendment.** RESOLVED — accept as a strengthening. Date: 2026-08-11. Approver: Dave. **What plan `15.5-12` shipped, and flagged rather than slipped.** `D-IMPL-31` ruled `expires_at = min(class MAX_TTL ceiling, derivation over constituent signal validities)`. The executor implemented `compose_expiry` with a **third term, `min(validities)`**, so that *"no aggregate is fresher-labelled than its stalest load-bearing constituent"* is a property **of the function** rather than a property of whichever derivation a class happened to configure. Under the ruled reference default (`derivation = min`) the third term is an **identity** and changes nothing; for any derivation returning later than `min(validities)` it clamps where the two-term formula would not. The executor reported this as a deviation from a ruled formula rather than presenting it as the formula. **The ruling.** Adopted, and recorded **as an amendment to `D-IMPL-31`** rather than as an executor deviation tolerated after the fact — the formula now has three terms and `D-IMPL-31` should be read through this entry. The reasoning: `D-IMPL-31` is a mixing-**refusal** rule, so erring conservative is its intent rather than a departure from it, and a safety property that holds structurally beats one that holds only for well-behaved configuration. A deployment cannot now configure its way past the floor. **The alternative considered and not taken:** constraining the derivation at declaration time instead — forbidding a derivation that returns later than `min(validities)` — reaches the same guarantee but enforces it where a class is declared rather than where an aggregate is composed, leaving the composition function correct only by precondition. The third term needs no precondition. **Governs:** `src/ccf/products/composition.py::compose_expiry`; amends `D-IMPL-31`. Originates: plan `15.5-12`, flagged by its executor; carried to the gate by the orchestrator.

**D-GATE-15.5 — Phase 15.5 approved.** Date: 2026-08-11. Approver: Dave. **15 of 15 plans complete** (14 planned, plus `15.5-15` created mid-phase by `D-IMPL-108`). `make ci` **exit 0** at the gate HEAD, verified by the orchestrator: **2858 passed / 81 skipped**, all eleven examples green including the new `example-s1-01`, `docs-strict` clean with **0** publish-safety violations, `make perf-micro` 12/12 PASS with `perf/baselines/local.json` **never modified** across the whole phase. **Eighteen rulings** — `D-IMPL-98` through `D-IMPL-115` — each recorded with the measured cost it was ruled against. **The close-time protocol ran in the CLAUDE.md §3.1 order**: execute → cross-AI panel against shipped code → single-agent review → verify every finding → fix blocking findings in-phase → present. **Two blocking findings were found and fixed inside the phase**: a cross-tenant authorization hole at the entitlement door, where a policy artifact declaring one tenant and registered under another's key would have authorized (`7453e87`); and an `AGNT-01` capability check blind to `ast.Attribute` and `getattr`, found *independently by two reviewers* (`c6693f4`). **Five findings were rejected as fabricated**, each verified against the tree before rejection — `DebtAssessment.timestamp` (the type has four fields, none a datetime), `VesselAssembler`, `validate_vessel_conformity`, `tests/invariants/test_import_invariants.py`. This is the **second** fabricated-citation output on this project and the rejection is recorded with its evidence. **Accepted as known-stale or known-blind, explicitly rather than by silence:** the regenerated surface manifest is **not** evidence of surface stability for this phase (`D-IMPL-110`) — neither resolver Protocol appears among the 21 reshaped symbols despite going from three arguments to five, the phase's largest adopter break; `docs/schemas/` and `openapi.json` sit outside the D-20 scanner and were swept **manually** (27 files, 638 description strings, 0 shingles), which is clean but is not a gate; and `CPS-03` remains Pending **by design** under `D-IMPL-113`. **Carried to Phase 17:** `DI-15.5-01` and `DI-15.5-04` (a perf pass), `DI-15.5-05` (convention-not-enforcement, now with a second instance), `DI-15.5-06` (the Protocol drift blind spot, with its measured 56/30/54 inventory), `DI-15.5-08` and `D-IMPL-114`'s citation sweep, and the debt-completeness work `D-IMPL-112` scoped. **What the phase answered.** Dave's question of 2026-08-10 — *"today I would put an MCP server in front of the fluree database and run a query and return the results. What is the benefit of using CCF?"* — is answered by `examples/s1-01-hello-context-product`, demonstrated at the `15.5-13` checkpoint and approved under `D-IMPL-112` with its limitation recorded: one product class answers for two companies at two instants, a later instant surfaces an ownership change with **nothing re-ingested**, debt is measured and names *freshness* as what weakened, and the replay record pins both the graph question and the product question. Debt is *informative and correctly attributed*, and **not yet decision-complete** — that boundary is on the record, not papered over.

**D-IMPL-116 — Phase 15.6 runs before Phase 16 resumes, as two explicit tracks.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-08-11. Approver: Dave. **The question Dave asked, which is the right one:** *"Will fixing the known defects affect the programming interface?"* **Measured answer: the two halves of the outstanding work have opposite API profiles, and that is what decides the sequencing.** **Track A — the five carried defects — is API-neutral.** `DI-15.5-01` (a perf flake) touches nothing. `DI-15.5-04` (`IntermediateCache`'s unreachable-cache key) is internal to `.run()` and behaviour-identical. `DI-15.5-05` (binder refusals with no calling path) needs a ruling, not a signature. `DI-15.5-06` is the **opposite** of a surface change — teaching `tools/dump_surface.py` to read a Protocol's `__call__` makes the *already-shipped* 3-arg → 5-arg resolver break newly visible; it is an audit fix. `DI-15.5-08`/`D-IMPL-114` is a citation sweep. Every one could be carried to Phase 17 without touching an adopter. **Track B — `D-IMPL-112`'s three named gaps — carries every API change there is.** `Observation` is **public surface** (present in `docs/surface/v0.2-surface.json`, referenced across 10 files) and gap 1 requires it to gain an identity field; `DebtAssessment` then gains evidence pointers; and because `debt: DebtAssessment | None` is a **field on `ContextProductContract`** (`src/ccf/products/contract.py::ContextProductContract`), the **product content address moves a third time**. Gap 2 (source-refresh recency, distinct from computed freshness) is new surface. Gap 3 (an obligation vocabulary per debt signal) is a new Control Plane artifact class. **Why 15.6 precedes Phase 16, and the reason is Track B rather than Track A.** The defects are cheap to carry; the API changes are expensive to carry. Two measurements decide it: (1) **Phase 16 has already been invalidated once by exactly this** — 6 of 21 plans landed before 15.5 moved the surface underneath, and **4** of the remaining 15 name the product or door surface directly; (2) **exactly one example artifact currently holds content addresses**, and Phase 16's entire output is examples that encode expected outputs. Moving the address now regenerates **one**; moving it after Phase 16 regenerates ten. And substantively: *"would someone act on this?"* is the question examples exist to answer, so an example built on debt an analyst cannot act on teaches the wrong lesson while Phase 16's adoption argument rests on it. **Two tracks, planned separately, because they differ in risk.** Track A is bounded and mostly mechanical. Track B contains one genuine build. **Scope Track B to the three named gaps, NOT to the open question** — *"answer would someone act on this"* is unbounded and would swallow the phase; `D-IMPL-112` already enumerates exactly three things an analyst asked for. **Gap 1 gets a research spike first (Dave, 2026-08-11), in the `15.5-01` shape.** That spike's precedent is the argument: it cost one plan and *deleted an option from the decision space for free* by measuring Q3's product-only placement dead rather than debating it. The 15.6 spike measures what an `Observation` identity costs across its 10 files and the manifest, what it does to the content address, and — the question most likely to change the design — **whether evidence pointers can ride the replay record rather than the product**, which would avoid the third address move entirely. `D-IMPL-99` ruled per-subject and per-claim NOT MEASURABLE precisely because the join key does not exist; the spike is how that stops being true. **Governs:** Phase 15.6's scope and shape; Phase 16's resumption, which waits on it. Originates: Dave's question of 2026-08-11 after `D-GATE-15.5`; `D-IMPL-112`'s three named gaps; the measured API-impact split above.

**D-IMPL-117 — Track B ships carrying mechanism, not judgement; surface impact is accepted.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-08-11. Approver: Dave. **Dave's scoping, which materially narrows `D-IMPL-116`'s Track B:** *"I'm ok with impacts to the surface in order to increase the value of the SDK at this point. Regarding judgement, the context product creator will have an idea of what is needed by the client and can provide that as part of the evolutionary capability of the context product. What matters now is having the data structure and api in place to populate and extract this content."* **What this settles.** (1) **Surface impact is accepted.** The `Observation` identity field, the `DebtAssessment` evidence pointers and the third product-content-address move are authorized costs, not risks to be designed around. `D-IMPL-116`'s framing of the spike as a way to *avoid* the address move is superseded: the spike's purpose is to get the **shape** right, not to dodge the cost. (2) **The three gaps are carrying mechanisms, not judgement calls.** `D-IMPL-112` recorded three things a KYC analyst would ask for; it is now explicit that the SDK owes the **structure and the API to populate and extract** each, and owes **none of the content**. Concretely — the SDK ships an `Observation` identity and a way for debt to point at what it summarises, and owes nothing about *which* observations matter; a slot for source-refresh recency distinct from computed freshness, and owes no definition of a source or a refresh cadence; and a signal-to-obligation binding that survives replay, and owes **no obligation vocabulary** (that is user configuration — CLAUDE.md §11, and the same posture `D-IMPL-101` took on salience). (3) **The judgement belongs to the context product creator**, who knows the client, and is expressed through the product's *evolutionary capability* rather than through SDK code. **Why this makes Track B more clearly SDK work rather than less.** *"Answer whether someone would act on this"* is unbounded and would swallow a phase. *"Ship three carrying structures a creator populates"* is bounded, testable, and is mechanism-not-values by construction. **The design fork this raises, and it is the spike's primary question now.** `D-IMPL-97` ruled the vessel carries cross-cutting governance as **fixed structure** and domain content as a **declared schema**. Debt evidence sits across that line: the *pointer mechanism* is governance and belongs in fixed structure, but *what evidence is worth carrying* is precisely the creator judgement this entry assigns away from the SDK. Fixed in the wrong direction, every deployment carries a shape someone else chose; declared in the wrong direction, debt evidence becomes unvalidated free-form and replay cannot reason over it. The spike measures which, against the vessel model and against the replay-reconstruction constraint `D-IMPL-100` established — every field added must be reconstructible from the record, the class, or the projection output, or `src/ccf/replay/engine.py::ReplayEnvironment` raises. **What does NOT change.** Track A stays API-neutral and bounded. Track B stays scoped to `D-IMPL-112`'s three named gaps, not to the open question. Gap 1 still gets the research spike first, in the `15.5-01` shape. **Governs:** Phase 15.6 Track B's scope and the spike's charter; supersedes `D-IMPL-116`'s address-avoidance framing of the spike. Originates: Dave, 2026-08-11, after `D-IMPL-116`.

**D-IMPL-118 — The three Track B carrying structures are new top-level fixed fields on `ContextProductContract`, and the record-side reconstruction they cost is an authorized expense, not a reason to place them elsewhere.** RESOLVED — `qa-toplevel`. Date: 2026-08-12. Approver: Dave. **Dave's selection, verbatim:** *"Q-A (D-IMPL-118) : qa-toplevel."* One clean selection of one presented option id; no hybrid was given and no limb was split. **What the ruling reaches.** `D-IMPL-117` made the fixed-versus-declared fork the spike's primary question, and `docs/DEBT_COMPLETENESS_RULING_EVIDENCE.md` § Q-A prices the four placements as properties of the placement **shape** applied to a member of `ContextProductContract` — *"These four rows are properties of the placement _shape_ applied to a member of `ContextProductContract`, not of any one gap's field. They therefore price all three Track B vessel-carried members identically."* This ruling therefore governs all three: plan `15.6-06`'s debt-evidence carrier, plan `15.6-07`'s source-refresh recency slot, and plan `15.6-08`'s assessment-side obligation member, which rides `ContextProductContract.debt` exactly as the other two do. **Not** in scope: `Observation`'s identity, which is an input to debt computation rather than a member of the vessel; its fixed-field placement was already authorized by `D-IMPL-117` and only its required-versus-optional question was open — that is `D-IMPL-120`. **The measured figure this was ruled against**, quoted from § Q-A row 2 rather than paraphrased: the content address **moves**, `f4cd0517…` → `e358be39…`, and the value is **NOT** reconstructible from `(record, projection)` — *"Rebuild hashes to `84799e67…`, which is neither the delivered address nor the baseline"*, and *"The token is **absent** from the canonical bytes of both inputs. `ProjectionOutput` carries exactly `(plan_id, payload)` and dimension 5 carries no member naming the value, so no implementation of the `(record, projection)` signature can produce it. That is the `ReplayDivergence` raise path."* **This is the not-replay-reconstructible branch, and the ruling therefore carries an obligation rather than a preference.** Every one of the three structures obliges **a matching member on `ContentGenerationPath`** *plus* **an edit to all 7 shipped `rehydrate_product` implementations across 6 files** — the public-Protocol population `D-IMPL-100` enumerated (`src/ccf/replay/engine.py`, `tests/replay/test_engine_rehydration.py`, `tests/replay/test_query_sequence_pin.py`, `perf/suites/replay/conftest.py`, `examples/06-decision-replay/run.py`, `examples/external/00-hello-context/run.py`). Without **both**, every replay of every product raises `ReplayDivergence`, because `canonical_bytes` walks a model field-by-field over `type(value).model_fields` and the new field is therefore inside the address. That obligation is inherited by plans `15.6-06`, `15.6-07` and `15.6-08` and is recorded here as an **authorized cost under `D-IMPL-117`, not a defect**: *"surface impact is accepted … the third product-content-address move [is an] authorized cost, not [a] risk to be designed around."* An executor of any of the three plans that ships the vessel field without the record-side member and the seven rehydrator edits has not implemented this ruling. **The alternative considered and not taken, with its measured cost.** `qa-nested` — the carrier as an optional member of the `DebtAssessment` that already rides `ContentGenerationPath.debt` — was the **cheapest** measured option and was declined: address moves `f4cd0517…` → `7c32baeb…`, reconstructible **YES** with *"Rebuilt bytes are byte-identical to the delivered bytes"* and **0** rehydrator implementations changing, because *"the shipped `debt=record.content_generation_path.debt` carries a reshaped assessment verbatim."* The ruling forgoes that free ride deliberately, buying the field its own identity on the vessel rather than making it a rider on debt. Also declined: `qa-declared` (address moves → `fecd33a2…`, round-trips because *"`payload` comes back verbatim on `ProjectionOutput.payload`"*, but *"replay never compares the evidence against the declared schema"* and `refuse_bound_payload` is called by no shipped door under `D-IMPL-113`, so a declared schema would constrain nothing on the serve path today); and `qa-record` (address does not move, and reaches **0** wire consumers across all three shipped doors — `egress.py::build_egress_server`, `routes/product.py::build_router`, `experience.py::build_experience_server` all serialize `servable.product` and **none** reads `ServedProduct.replay_ref` — deleted by measurement in § Q-B, and independently emptied of purpose by `D-IMPL-117`'s acceptance of the address move). **Governs:** plans `15.6-06`, `15.6-07` and `15.6-08` — the three structures carried on the product vessel — and requirements `DCD-02`, `DCD-03`, `DCD-04`, `DCD-05`; `src/ccf/products/contract.py::ContextProductContract`, `src/ccf/replay/record.py::ContentGenerationPath`, and every implementation of `ReplayEnvironment.rehydrate_product`. **Implementing plans and tasks:** plan `15.6-06` **task 1** (the debt-evidence carrier), plan `15.6-07` **task 1** (the source-refresh recency slot), plan `15.6-08` **task 2** (the assessment-side obligation member); each is written to implement the same branch unless this entry distinguishes them, and it does not. Originates: plan `15.6-01` (the measurement); `D-IMPL-117` (which assigned the fork to Dave and accepted the surface impact); `D-IMPL-97` (where the fixed/declared line is drawn); `D-IMPL-100` (the reconstructibility constraint and the seven-implementation count).

**D-IMPL-119 — Evidence pointers are entitlement-sensitive, and until the assembly path is principal-scoped an evidence pointer is an opaque handle or it is not emitted at all.** RESOLVED — `qb2-scoped`, clarified in four limbs. Date: 2026-08-12. Approver: Dave. **This is the first ruling on evidence pointers.** `D-IMPL-105` ruled the analogous question for **completeness** — debt is pure over `(factors, profile)` and not per principal — and ruled it precisely because of an inference channel: *"a caller can therefore infer what they are not allowed to see from the debt they are shown — an oracle over the entitlement configuration, quieter than a refusal because nothing in the response says a consultation was declined."* That argument transfers to evidence pointers and **no shipped ruling covered it**; plan `15.6-01` task 2 measured it, offered no mitigation and reached no verdict, exactly as `D-IMPL-117` required. **Dave's selection, verbatim:** *"Q-B2 (D-IMPL-119) : qb2-scoped."* **The measured finding the ruling was then clarified against**, quoted from `docs/DEBT_COMPLETENESS_RULING_EVIDENCE.md` § Q-B2 measurement 3: *"**On the shipped path the two are the same set, so the delta is empty — and that is the finding.** There is no perspective-scoped view to derive a narrower pointer from."* Three hops establish it, read off shipped parameter lists rather than described: `src/ccf/deployment/operators.py::build_operator_registry` takes `(parameters, view, pins, policy_bundle_key, similarity_index_version)` — **no perspective, no principal**; `src/ccf/operators/categories.py::PolicyFilter.__init__` takes `(self, parameters)` — **no principal**; `examples/s1-01-hello-context-product/spine.py::assemble_and_serve` reads the graph as `reader.as_of(tenant_id=…, at=…)` — **tenant and instant only**. Measurement 2 completes it: two differently-entitled principals **enumerate the same `entity_uri` set today**, because paths converge at `src/ccf/projection/engine.py::ProjectionEngine` and diverge only at `src/ccf/projection/plan.py::ProjectionPlan`; entitlement is decided **before** assembly at `runtime/ccf_runtime/authz/product_entitlement.py::entitled_perspective`, on the `(tenant, product_class, role)` triple, which is a per-class decision and not a per-entity one. **Dave accepted that finding and clarified the ruling rather than reversing it. Four limbs, in Dave's terms:** **(1)** Evidence pointers **are entitlement-sensitive**; emitting an unfiltered pointer set **is a leak**. This is the normative claim and it stands — it is `qb2-scoped`'s safety property, and it is the SDK's, not the adopter's. **(2)** **This phase does not introduce a perspective-scoped view into the assembly path.** That work is explicitly out of scope for Phase 15.6. **(3)** Consequently plan `15.6-06` must take **one of exactly two paths**: **(a)** ship **opaque / non-revealing handles** that carry **no** entity or claim identity the principal can interpret; or **(b)** **omit evidence pointers entirely** until a later phase adds principal scoping to the assembly path. The choice between (a) and (b) falls to plan `15.6-06`. **(4)** **Raw, interpretable pointers are FORBIDDEN until the scoping gap is closed.** This is a **standing prohibition, not advice**: a pointer naming any of `EntityClaim`'s eight fields (`tenant_id`, `observed_at`, `valid_from`, `valid_to`, `lineage`, `entity_uri`, `entity_class`, `attributes`) in a form the reading principal can interpret is refused by this entry, whatever the deployment's judgement, until the precondition below is met. **The named precondition, recorded as a precondition rather than filed as an open defect.** The absence of a perspective-scoped view in the assembly path is a **precondition for any future "real" evidence-pointer feature** — the three hops above and the same-`entity_uri`-set finding are its evidence. A later phase that wants interpretable pointers closes the scoping gap first; nothing in this phase is blocked on it, and nothing in this phase may work around it. **The recorded interaction with `D-IMPL-118`.** `D-IMPL-118` places the carrier as a top-level field on `ContextProductContract`, which puts it **inside the content address**. Principal-dependent pointer *contents* inside a content address would give two differently-entitled principals **different content addresses for the same assembly** — precisely the coupling `D-IMPL-105` dissolved when it kept debt pure over `(factors, profile)`. **Limbs 3 and 4 are what keep that from arising in this phase**, since neither an opaque handle nor an omitted pointer varies by principal. Recorded as an interaction, not as a new question. **What this entry does not license**, in the voice `D-IMPL-113` used for its own pattern warning: it does not license a deployment reading limb 3(a) as permission to mint a handle that is merely *encoded* rather than genuinely non-revealing — an obfuscated `entity_uri` is an interpretable pointer with an extra step, and limb 4 refuses it; it does not license treating the disclosure decision as the adopter's, which is what `qb2-opaque` would have done and this ruling does not; and it does not license a later plan inferring, from limb 2, that scoped derivation is unwanted — limb 1 says the opposite. **The alternatives considered and not taken, with their measured costs.** `qb2-pure` — evidence stays pure over the assembly as debt does, with entitlement enforced elsewhere — keeps one value for one assembly and is consistent with `D-IMPL-105`'s purity, and was declined because *"a principal could infer the existence of withheld sources from pointers they can read"*, the precise inference `D-IMPL-105` cited as its own reason; on the shipped path, where the enumerated set is identical for every principal of a class, that inference is not hypothetical. `qb2-opaque` — the pointer is opaque and the deployment owns whether it discloses anything — reaches limb 3(a)'s *shape* but was declined as a *ruling*, because it *"moves a real disclosure question onto every adopter, and the SDK cannot then say the surface is safe by construction"*; under this entry the opaque handle is the SDK's obligation, not the adopter's discretion. **Governs:** plan `15.6-06` **task 2**, which is where the derivation it constrains actually happens; requirements `DCD-02` and `DCD-05`; `examples/s1-01-hello-context-product/deployment.py::KycScenario` as the population site. **Implementing plan and task: plan `15.6-06` task 2** — the population of the evidence carrier at the `s1-01` assembly, the only place in the phase where the constrained derivation is written. That plan's task-2 acceptance criterion *"if `D-IMPL-119` constrained derivation to the perspective-scoped assembly, the constraint is implemented at the population site rather than assumed, and the summary names the symbol the scoped set is read from"* is satisfied under this entry by limb 3: there is no such symbol, so the task names the limb it took — (a) or (b) — and shows the handle carries nothing interpretable, or that no pointer is emitted. Originates: plan `15.6-01` task 2's three measurements; `D-IMPL-117`; `D-IMPL-105` (the analogous ruling for completeness).

**D-IMPL-120 — `Observation`'s subject identity is optional, carried behind a named positive sentinel rather than required.** RESOLVED — `qc-optional`. Date: 2026-08-12. Approver: Dave. **Dave's selection, verbatim:** *"Q-C (D-IMPL-120) : qc-optional."* **Scope.** This entry decides **required-versus-optional only**. The field's placement on `src/ccf/halflife/decay.py::Observation` is not in question — `D-IMPL-117` already authorized it — and `Observation` is not a member of `ContextProductContract`, so it sits outside `D-IMPL-118`'s Q-A fork entirely. **The measured figure this was ruled against**, quoted from `docs/DEBT_COMPLETENESS_RULING_EVIDENCE.md` § Q-C, which was **executed rather than inferred** — each of the three named artifacts' *actual* observation mapping was `model_validate`d against a required stand-in and against an optional one, and what each raised was recorded: the optional shape costs *"**3 code files** (the 10 construction sites, which populate it) and **0 artifacts** — every artifact validates and the sentinel is carried."* **The alternative considered and not taken, with its measured cost.** `qc-required` costs *"**6 code files** (10 `Observation(…)` call sites across 3 files — 9 in `tests/`, 1 in `examples/` — plus 3 `Observation.model_validate` sites in 3 example `run.py` files) **plus all 3 YAML artifacts**, each of which **raises**"*: `examples/00-quickstart/artifacts/decision.yaml` (1 mapping) — `ValidationError`, 1 error, type `missing`, loc `subject_uri`; `examples/01-agent-basics/artifacts/debt-evaluation.yaml` (2 mappings) — `ValidationError` on **both**, type `missing`, loc `subject_uri`; `examples/08-e2e-demo/artifacts/decision.yaml` (1 mapping) — `ValidationError`, 1 error, type `missing`, loc `subject_uri`. This discharges `15.6-RESEARCH.md` assumption A7 by execution. **The `loc` in those three quoted `ValidationError`s is `subject_uri`, which is the name the spike's stand-in field carried; the field this ruling governs ships as `subject` on `src/ccf/halflife/decay.py::Observation`** — the quotes are reproduced verbatim because they are what the measurement raised, so the difference is the stand-in's name and not a rename of shipped surface. (The Wave-2 presentation's option cells quoted the research-era *"10 files against 13"* split; the measured split above is the figure the ruling was made against and supersedes it.) **The governance cost this ruling accepts, stated rather than elided.** `D-IMPL-97`'s decisive argument for fixed structure — *"every subclass is a place to forget"* — cuts toward **required**, and the optional shape accepts its consequence: **an assembler that could populate the identity and does not is indistinguishable, from the type, from one that has none.** What makes the cost bearable is `D-IMPL-38`'s no-silent-defaults discipline together with the shipped positive-sentinel precedent (`NO_SCORER_PINS`, `NO_GRAPH_QUERIES`, `NO_PAYLOAD_SCHEMA`): the absent value is **a named positive assertion, not `None`-as-unknown**, so an omitted identity and a dropped one are not the same artifact. An implementation that expresses the absence as `None` has not implemented this ruling. **Governs:** plan `15.6-05` and requirement `DCD-02`; `src/ccf/halflife/decay.py::Observation`; the three example artifacts named above, which under this ruling **do not change**. **Implementing plan and task: plan `15.6-05` task 1** — *"`Observation` gains the identity, in the shape Dave ruled"* — with its task 2 populating the identity at `examples/s1-01-hello-context-product/deployment.py::KycScenario`, where `docs/DEBT_COMPLETENESS_RULING_EVIDENCE.md` § Q-D measured **7** fields in hand and discarded. Originates: plan `15.6-01` task 2 (the executed `model_validate` measurements); `D-IMPL-117`; `D-IMPL-97`; `D-IMPL-38`.

**D-IMPL-121 — `D-IMPL-113` extends to `refuse_request`: both request-time refusals are adopter obligations the SDK states at the seam, not doors the SDK enforces.** RESOLVED — `q1-extend`. Date: 2026-08-12. Approver: Dave. **Dave's selection, verbatim:** *"Q-1 : q1-extend."* **The question.** `D-IMPL-113` ruled the *bind* refusal an adopter obligation on reasoning that is structural rather than case-specific — *"the door never holds the registered class — `ProductResolverProtocol` hands the deployment three strings plus a perspective and a request, and the class is resolved behind that seam"* — and `DI-15.5-05` left open whether that reasoning transfers to `src/ccf/products/request.py::refuse_request` or whether the SDK wires it. It transfers, and the SDK does not wire it. **The re-measured population this was ruled against, taken at `4b407e0` rather than quoted.** `git grep` across `src runtime tests examples tools perf`, hand-classified into invocation versus mention: `src/ccf/products/bind.py::refuse_bound_payload` has **one** invocation outside its own tests — `examples/04-cross-process/producer_child.py::producer_child` — and **zero** in `runtime/`; `src/ccf/products/request.py::refuse_request` has **one** — `examples/s1-01-hello-context-product/spine.py::assemble_and_serve` — and **zero** in `runtime/`. The correct statement is narrower than either prior record: **no `runtime/` door calls either function; one shipped example calls each.** **Correction to the record, and it is a process finding rather than drift.** The `DI-15.5-05` entry in `.planning/phases/15.5-the-context-product-surface-vessel-assembler-debt-entitlem/deferred-items.md` states `refuse_request` has **zero** callers. Git says otherwise, and says it about the same day: the call site landed in commit `e4db82c` at **2026-08-11 11:46:21 -0700**, and the entry claiming zero landed in commit `9fd6c12` at **2026-08-11 20:54:59 -0700** — a gap of **9 h 08 m 38 s, inside the same phase**. The entry was **wrong when written, not stale by drift**. The distinction is preserved deliberately: drift is normal and is what `D-IMPL-114` addresses, whereas a figure that was false at the moment of authorship is a process defect, and a phase built on it re-commits the error. **A second correction, in the same entry, of `DI-15.5-08`'s own defect class.** Two of that entry's line anchors have rotted: it cites the payload refusal at `bind.py:145` where `src/ccf/products/bind.py::refuse_bound_payload` now begins at line 164, and the wired registration-time sibling at `contract.py:662-664` where the call in `src/ccf/products/contract.py::register_product_class` now sits at lines 753 to 755. Two anchors in the same entry are still accurate. Recorded because `DI-15.5-05`'s own text demonstrating `DI-15.5-08` is the tightest available evidence for `D-IMPL-114`'s premise. **Why not wire it, restated at this commit rather than inherited.** Both seams were re-read: `runtime/ccf_runtime/mcp/egress.py::ProductResolverProtocol` and `runtime/ccf_runtime/mcp/experience.py::ExperienceProductResolverProtocol` each take five keyword-only arguments — `tenant`, `product_class`, `version`, `perspective`, `request` — and **neither holds the `RegisteredProductClass`**. `D-IMPL-113`'s structural premise is therefore verified against the shipped signatures, not taken on report. Wiring would require the door to acquire the registered class, which is a different seam than the one `D-IMPL-108` widened, and would put an SDK-owned verdict on the serve path that `D-IMPL-102` limb 3 declined — re-litigating that ruling by implementation rather than by decision. **The obligation this discharges, and it was measurably undischarged.** `D-IMPL-113` created it — *"Documented is not the same as mentioned: the adopter has to be told, at the seam, that a resolver which does not call `refuse_bound_payload` serves an unvalidated payload against a schema its class declared"* — and never discharged it: at `4b407e0`, `git grep` for either refusal name across all of `runtime/` returned **zero hits of any kind**, not an import, not a call, not a mention. Under this ruling both resolver Protocol docstrings state what a resolver omitting each refusal serves, why the SDK cannot call it for them, and where a working example call site is, cited as `path::Symbol`; `tools/docs_tests/test_resolver_seam_obligations.py` asserts the statement remains, because a docstring nobody checks is a docstring that rots and `DI-15.5-08` is this phase's own evidence of it. **A false docstring, corrected.** `src/ccf/products/request.py::refuse_request` opened *"Called by the door, once the seam that can carry a typed request exists."* The seam now exists — plan `15.5-15` landed it under `D-IMPL-108` — and no door calls the function, so the sentence asserted something false at this commit. It now says what is true: the deployment's own resolver calls it, at the join point the seam docstrings name. **The alternative considered and not taken.** `q1-wire` — wire `refuse_request` into the shipped doors — was declined. Its argument is real and is recorded rather than dismissed: *mechanism the SDK ships is mechanism the SDK calls*, and no adopter can forget a call the SDK makes. It was not taken because the door does not hold what the refusal needs, because reaching it widens a seam `D-IMPL-108` settled one phase ago, and because it would re-open `D-IMPL-102` limb 3 by implementation. **What this does not license, in `D-IMPL-113`'s own voice.** This is the **third** instance of convention-not-enforcement, and `D-IMPL-113` flagged two as *"a pattern worth watching: a Protocol the SDK ships and never calls is indistinguishable, from the tree, from one an adopter forgot."* Three is not a smaller pattern. What changes with this ruling is that the tree can now tell the two apart — the seam says the join point exists and names a working example — but the watch stands, and a fourth instance should be read as a signal about the seam rather than as another documentation task. **`CPS-03` stays Pending by design, and the requirement row says so, naming both this entry and `D-IMPL-113`** — `D-IMPL-113`'s own instruction, *"the requirement row must say which, or a later reader will read an unmet requirement as an oversight."* **Governs:** `src/ccf/products/request.py::refuse_request`; `src/ccf/products/bind.py::refuse_bound_payload`; `runtime/ccf_runtime/mcp/egress.py::ProductResolverProtocol` and `runtime/ccf_runtime/mcp/experience.py::ExperienceProductResolverProtocol` docstrings; `tools/docs_tests/test_resolver_seam_obligations.py`; requirements `CPS-03` and `DCD-08`. Extends `D-IMPL-113` rather than amending it. **Implementing plan and tasks: plan `15.6-09` tasks 2 and 3.** Originates: `DI-15.5-05`; `D-IMPL-113`; `D-IMPL-102` limb 3; plan `15.6-09`'s re-measurement at `4b407e0`.

**D-IMPL-122 — `DI-15.5-06` is fixed by reconciling the diff against a baseline that stays frozen, with `__call__` capture and the type aliases in scope and the 39 multi-method Protocols descoped on a measured cost.** RESOLVED — `q2a-reconcile`, `__call__`-only fix scope, `q2b-in`. Date: 2026-08-12. Approver: Dave. **Dave's selections, verbatim:** *"Q-2a : reconcile (frozen baseline stays frozen; the diff is reconciled)"*; *"Q-2 fix scope : `__call__`-ONLY (12 of 51 Protocols, 11 new reshaped diff lines)"*; *"Q-2b : q2b-in (the type aliases ARE in scope — 18 distinct aliases / 20 entries)."* Three limbs of one question, ruled together. **Limb 1 — the frozen baseline stays frozen and the diff is reconciled.** `docs/surface/v0.2-surface-baseline.json` is not regenerated. It is pinned by **two** assertions, both named here because naming them is what makes this a ruling rather than a repair: `tests/test_surface_completeness.py::test_the_frozen_baseline_is_byte_identical_to_what_15_01_committed`, which pins `sha256` against the constant `_BASELINE_DIGEST` (`cef0d469db249947f8392331a50bc94bf92d46a4266e4945e2b59944dac043cc`), and `tests/test_surface_completeness.py::test_the_frozen_baseline_was_written_only_by_plan_15_01`, which pins the file's provenance against its git history. An executor cannot regenerate the baseline without failing both, which is exactly what they exist for. **A measured caveat on the second, recorded because it changes how much weight it carries:** its own docstring states it is *"corroboration for the digest, not an independently unfakeable provenance proof"* — it keys on commit-subject text rather than a pinned hash, and it returns without asserting where git is absent or the history is shallow. The digest is the load-bearing pin. **Limb 2 — the fix captures `__call__` and nothing wider.** `tools/dump_surface.py` resolves a class's shape with `inspect.signature` on the class, which for a `Protocol` returns `__init__` and therefore `"(*args, **kwargs)"`. It will be taught to read `__call__`. It will **not** be taught to render a multi-method Protocol's method set. **Limb 3 — the information-free type aliases are in scope.** All **18 distinct aliases / 20 manifest entries** move with the same commit. **The re-measured figures this was ruled against, taken at `4b407e0` and reproducing the manifest rather than quoting a prior count.** Of **80** manifest entries recording `"(*args, **kwargs)"`: **60 are class-kind** (51 distinct classes) and **20 are alias-kind** (18 distinct aliases). Every one of the 51 distinct classes was imported and confirmed `_is_protocol` — there are no false positives in that set. Of those 51, **exactly 12 define `__call__`**: `ccf_runtime.mcp.egress.ProductResolverProtocol`, `ccf_runtime.mcp.experience.ExperienceProductResolverProtocol`, `.AgentDirectoryProtocol`, `.AgentInvokerProtocol`, `.ContextProviderProtocol`, `.LineageProviderProtocol`, `.ReplayRecordReaderProtocol`, `ccf_runtime.mcp.hitl_server.HitlActionRouteProtocol`, `.HitlQueueViewProtocol`, `ccf_runtime.authz.product_entitlement.PerspectiveResolverProtocol`, `ccf_runtime.peering.lf_a2a.PeerCardResolver`, `ccf_runtime.peering.typed_http.PeerEndpointResolver` — **all twelve in `runtime/`, none in `src/`**. **Cost, measured by diffing the frozen baseline against the live manifest.** The current diff is 219 added, 0 removed, 29 reshaped. `tests/test_surface_completeness.py::test_every_diff_line_has_a_matching_public_log_entry` requires every diff line to carry a fragment entry, so a fix's cost is counted in new `reshaped` lines: the `__call__`-only fix moves **12** entries of which **11** are already in the baseline, therefore **11 new `reshaped` diff lines**; a full method-set fix would move **80** entries of which **65** are already in the baseline, therefore **65**. Dave chose 11 over 65 knowingly. **THE DESCOPE, RECORDED UNSOFTENED, BECAUSE THIS PHASE MUST NOT READ AS "THE BLIND SPOT IS FIXED."** `__call__` capture fixes **12 of 51** information-free Protocols. `q2b-in` closes all **18** aliases. That leaves **39 multi-method Protocols still information-free after this fix lands** — their entire public contract is a method set, `__call__` capture reaches none of them, and a signature change to any of their methods will still produce no manifest diff line. **Every one of the seven Protocols `D-IMPL-110` named by name is in the descoped 39:** `ccf.artifacts.protocol.ArtifactStoreProtocol` (4 methods), `ccf.controlplane.registry.ControlPlaneProtocol` (6), `ccf.harness.HarnessAdapterProtocol` (5), `ccf.orchestration.OrchestrationProtocol` (2), `ccf.hitl.HITLTransportProtocol` (6), `ccf.llm.LLMClientProtocol` (1), `ccf.halflife.debt.DebtFactorScorerProtocol` (3) — that is, most of the pluggable substrate CLAUDE.md §11 mandates Protocols for. Also descoped: `ccf.graph.protocols.GraphReader` (5) and `.GraphWriter` (3), `ccf.replay.engine.ReplayEnvironment` (3), `ccf.operators.base.Operator` (4), `ccf.agents.ArchetypeComponent` (4), `ccf.peering.protocol.PeeringProtocol` (2), and 26 more. `ccf.graph.reader.Row` has **zero** members and has nothing to show under any fix. **This is `q2b-out`'s record-honesty argument landing on the Protocol side rather than the alias side, and it is stated here rather than discovered later:** after this fix, the surface manifest remains *not* evidence of surface stability for a multi-method Protocol, and must not be cited as such at any gate. `D-IMPL-110`'s consequence (1) survives the fix for the 39. **The alternatives considered and not taken, with their measured costs.** `q2a-rewrite` — regenerate the baseline and re-pin `_BASELINE_DIGEST` — buys a smaller fragment and a baseline reflecting the tool's corrected view, and was declined because it requires defeating a provenance test whose whole purpose is to make that impossible, and because it would make the already-shipped resolver break invisible again, which is the opposite of the audit `DI-15.5-06` exists to produce. **Full method-set capture** — 51 of 51 Protocols, **65** new `reshaped` diff lines — was declined on that measured cost; it remains the shape that actually closes the blind spot, and a later phase taking it should expect 65 claimed entries plus the reclassification of the `15.5-11` and `15.5-15` fragments `D-IMPL-110` already anticipated. `q2b-out` — descope the aliases — was declined; its own argument is the one this entry applies to the 39 Protocols instead. **Corrections to the record, both measured at `4b407e0` and both given with the prior value.** (1) **`D-IMPL-110`'s inventory has grown and its per-name framing is superseded.** It measured at `4d16cb9`: 56 information-free entries, 30 named `*Protocol`, 54 Protocol classes across `src/` + `runtime/`. Measured now: **80** information-free entries, **34** named `*Protocol`, **56** Protocol definition sites. More consequentially, `DI-15.5-06` states that teaching the tool to record `__call__` *"would move **every** Protocol entry"*; measured, it moves **12 of 51**, because 39 of the 51 have no `__call__` to read. (2) **The "five `Literal` type aliases" figure is wrong and inverted.** Measured, the 18 distinct information-free aliases are **13 `Literal`** — `ArtifactRole`, `AssemblyMode`, `AuditAction`, `DebtFactorName`, `EffectCapability`, `GrantState`, `LineageMode`, `OperatorCategory`, `PayloadViolationReason`, `PolicyBindingMode`, `ProductRequestViolationReason`, `RegistrationMode`, `TTLAnchor` — and **5 not `Literal`**: `ExpiryDerivation` and `HttpClientFactory` and `SkillCallable` (`Callable`), `JsonWebKey` (`Mapping`), `WorkflowOutcome` (`Union`). "Five" is exactly the count of the **non**-`Literal` aliases, so the prior scoping sentence named the wrong five. `q2b-in` covers all 18. **Governs:** `tools/dump_surface.py`; `docs/surface/v0.2-surface.json`; `docs/surface/v0.2-surface-baseline.json`, which does **not** change; `tests/test_surface_completeness.py`; the scope of `DI-15.5-06`; the 39 descoped Protocols, which remain open debt with no owner assigned by this entry. **Implementing plan: plan `15.6-10`** — the manifest fix and this phase's single manifest regeneration. Originates: `DI-15.5-06`; `D-IMPL-110`; plan `15.6-09`'s re-measurement at `4b407e0`.

**D-IMPL-123 — `DI-15.5-08`'s sweep covers every unanchored `.py`-target citation except the 13 in the records `D-IMPL-114` says a later editor should not silently revise: 101 of 114.** RESOLVED — the measured fourth shape. Date: 2026-08-12. Approver: Dave. **Dave's selection, verbatim:** *"Q-3 : the measured FOURTH shape — everything EXCEPT the 13 `D-IMPL-114` names = 101 citations."* This option did not exist in the plan's list; it exists because the measurement produced it. **The framing that must travel with this entry, because a later reader will otherwise assume the opposite.** **The citation gate is GREEN.** At `4b407e0`, `python3 -m tools.lints --report` reports **762 citations matched across 948 files and 0 findings**. The unanchored population is a **coverage** statement — citations the checker declines to check because they carry no anchor to check against — not a set of failures. This sweep raises coverage; it does not repair a red gate. **And `D-IMPL-114`'s consequence (1) is already discharged**: `tools/lints/citations.py::RULE_NODE_ID` implements `cite03-node-id`, and **150** `path::Symbol` citations are already in gated scope with **144 checked and passing**. This ruling is about the sweep, not about the checker. **The measured population, derived by re-using the checker's own scanner rather than counted by hand.** `tools.lints.citations.iter_scanned_files` plus its own exemption, historicity, resolution and anchor predicates reproduce the tool's `no_anchor` bucket **exactly — 435 of 435** — and that bucket filtered to citations whose *target* is a `.py` file gives **114 citations across 27 host files**: `.planning/` **47** in 6 files, `docs/` excluding `surface-changes/` **24** in 4, `src/` **16** in 3, `tests/` **13** in 6, `docs/surface-changes/` **11** in 5, `tools/` **3** in 3. `runtime/`, `examples/`, `perf/` and `public/` host **zero**. **The 13 held back, named by file so the boundary is checkable rather than asserted:** `docs/surface-changes/15.5-11-debt-delivery.md` (**5**), `docs/surface-changes/15-03-audit-baseline.md` (**3**), `docs/surface-changes/15-11-operator-builder.md` (**1**), `docs/surface-changes/15.5-08-request-contract.md` (**1**), `docs/surface-changes/15.5-13-request-in-replay.md` (**1**) — landed plan fragments — plus `docs/SURFACE-CHANGES.md` (**2**), the whole-tree-assembled artifact, which `make surface-changes` regenerates from those fragments in any case, so editing it directly is overwritten rather than preserved. `docs/DECISIONS.md`, the third record `D-IMPL-114` names, contributes **zero** to the 114 because the citation gate already exempts it wholesale. **101 = 114 − 13.** **Correction to the record, with both values.** The population was carried as **125 across 31 files**, with **49** in `.planning/`, **5** in `docs/surface-changes/`, and a remediable floor of **38** (`src/` 17 + `tests/` 17 + `tools/` 4). Measured at `4b407e0`: **114 across 27**, `.planning/` **47**, `docs/surface-changes/` **11**, and the code-trees floor **32** (`src/` 16 + `tests/` 13 + `tools/` 3). **A premise also fails, and it is the one that shaped the options.** The carried framing held that the `.planning/` citations live in files *"`D-IMPL-114` itself says a later editor should not silently revise."* Measured, **none of them does**: `tools/lints/citations.py` already exempts dated records through `HISTORICAL_RECORDS` — `docs/DECISIONS.md`, the whitepaper, `docs/PHASE_*.md`, and the whole of `.planning/phases/*` — so a dated planning record never enters this count at all. The 47 are entirely in living or explicitly maintained files: `.planning/phases/15.1-ergonomics-gap-closure/deferred-items.md` **24**, `.planning/REQUIREMENTS.md` **8**, `.planning/phases/15.5-the-context-product-surface-vessel-assembler-debt-entitlem/deferred-items.md` **8**, `.planning/STATE.md` **5**, `.planning/ROADMAP.md` **1**, `.planning/phases/15.4-backend-registration-seam-the-substrate-stops-naming-its-ada/deferred-items.md` **1** — the first, third and sixth of which are in `MAINTAINED_RECORDS` by name. That is why a shape covering 101 rather than 32 or 56 is available at all. **The alternatives considered and not taken, with their re-measured costs.** `q3-code-trees` — `src/` + `tests/` + `tools/` only — is **32**, not the 38 it was offered as; it touches only living code where a citation's claim is load-bearing, and was declined because it leaves **82** citations line-anchored and rotting, including the 24 in `15.1`'s maintained deferred-items file. `q3-code-plus-docs` is **56**, not roughly 76; it adds `docs/CONTEXT_PRODUCT_RULING_EVIDENCE.md` (15) and `docs/SURFACE-AUDIT.md` (6), both actively maintained and actively cited, and was declined for stopping short of the maintained planning records. `q3-all` — **114** — was declined because it rewrites the 13 landed-fragment and assembled-artifact citations `D-IMPL-114` names by class. **Worth knowing, and recorded so the sweep is planned rather than discovered.** **Five** of the 114 target the exact stale range `D-IMPL-114` was written about — `src/ccf/replay/engine.py` lines 449 to 455 — and **two of those five sit inside the held-back 13**, in `docs/surface-changes/15.5-11-debt-delivery.md`. The sweep therefore leaves the originating defect visibly extant in two places by ruling, which is the intended outcome and not an oversight. **Governs:** the `DI-15.5-08` sweep's scope; `tools/lints/citations.py` and its two-direction ratchet; the citation convention in `docs/`, `.planning/` prose and source docstrings. Does **not** amend `D-IMPL-114`, whose convention and whose leave-alone classes stand unchanged. **Implementing plan: plan `15.6-11`** — the citation sweep and its ratchet. Originates: `DI-15.5-08`; `D-IMPL-114`; plan `15.6-09`'s re-measurement at `4b407e0`.

**D-IMPL-124 — Source-refresh recency publishes a freshness signal, not a source enumeration: the human-interpretable source identities come off the vessel and the inference channel is CLOSED rather than accepted as residual.** RESOLVED — Shape B. Date: 2026-08-12. Approver: Dave. **Dave's ruling, verbatim and in full:** *"Source-set / recency: the field's purpose is freshness, not source enumeration. Publish the freshness signal without human-interpretable source identities (Shape B). The inference channel is closed rather than accepted as residual."* **Where the question came from, and it was named rather than ruled by the plan that shipped the field.** Plan `15.6-07` shipped `ContextProductContract.source_refresh_recency` **populated**, correctly: it was instructed that `D-IMPL-119` governs evidence pointers rather than refresh timestamps and that limbs 3 and 4 must not be applied by analogy, and it did not apply them. Its executor then named a new question instead of ruling it — `.planning/phases/15.6-decision-completeness-and-defect-closure/15.6-07-SUMMARY.md` Findings § 3, *"a reader could learn that a source **exists** and **when it last published** without being entitled to its contents … This is a new question, not a limb of an existing entry, and it is not ruled here."* Reporting it rather than disposing of it silently is the behaviour the checkpoint exists to elicit, and it is recorded as such. **This is the THIRD instance of one inference-channel shape in this project.** `D-IMPL-105` closed it for **completeness** — *"a caller can therefore infer what they are not allowed to see from the debt they are shown … an oracle over the entitlement configuration, quieter than a refusal because nothing in the response says a consultation was declined."* `D-IMPL-119` closed it for **evidence pointers**, ruling them entitlement-sensitive and forbidding interpretable pointers until the assembly path is principal-scoped. This entry closes it for **source recency**. **The measured finding this was ruled against, taken at `4b407e0`.** `src/ccf/halflife/assessment.py::SourceRefresh` carries exactly two members — `source_ref: str`, documented opaque to the SDK and declared by the deployment, and `refreshed_at: datetime`, timezone-aware. `examples/s1-01-hello-context-product/artifacts/product-governance.yaml` declares **three** entries whose `source_ref` values are **human-interpretable strings** — `corporate-registry`, `kyc-registry`, `name-screening` — which is the exact contrast with `D-IMPL-119` limb 3(a)'s opaque handle and is the substance of the question. **The whole set reaches every principal who can reach the product:** `runtime/ccf_runtime/mcp/egress.py::build_egress_server` returns `canonical_bytes(servable.product)` and `runtime/ccf_runtime/http_api/routes/product.py::build_router` returns `canonical_response(servable.product)` — the whole vessel, serialized verbatim. **And nothing scopes the set:** `D-IMPL-119`'s three hops were re-read off the shipped parameter lists and all three still hold — `src/ccf/deployment/operators.py::build_operator_registry` takes `(parameters, view, pins, policy_bundle_key, similarity_index_version)` with no perspective and no principal; `src/ccf/operators/categories.py::PolicyFilter` takes `(parameters)` with no principal; `runtime/ccf_runtime/authz/product_entitlement.py::entitled_perspective` decides on `(grant, tenant, product_class, requested_role, …)`, a **per-class** decision with no per-source dimension. So a reader entitled to the product learns that `name-screening` and `kyc-registry` exist and when each last published, with no check that they are entitled to those sources' contents. **`D-IMPL-118`'s content-address coupling does not arise, and the reason is worth stating precisely.** The declared set is identical for every principal, so one assembly still yields one content address — the coupling `D-IMPL-105` dissolved does not reappear. But it holds because nothing varies, **not** because anything prevents it from varying, and Shape B keeps it that way by removing the identities rather than by scoping them. **Shape B, as ruled.** Replace, or parallel, the current per-source map with an **opaque, non-identifying freshness summary** — for example `oldest_source_refresh_at` and `newest_source_refresh_at`, or a single `sources_freshest_at` / `sources_stalest_at` pair. **No `source_ref` string leaves the vessel.** Cost: a small shape change plus a content-address move. Gain, in Dave's terms: it *removes the oracle entirely while still delivering the freshness information the field exists for*. The closure is the point of this entry — the channel is **closed**, not accepted as residual, and a later reader must not record it as a tolerated risk. **The alternatives considered and not taken, with Dave's own stated costs.** **Shape A** — keep the identities and accept the residual: zero code change, and the risk is a third open oracle of the same family. **NOT TAKEN.** **Shape C** — opaque tokens on the product, with resolution to a human-interpretable `source_ref` only behind an entitlement-checked door: Dave's own words, *"the right long-term design but is new work."* **NOT TAKEN**, and recorded here as **the named long-term shape**, so a later phase adding an entitlement-checked resolution door is completing a design already on the record rather than re-opening a closed one. **Shape D** — filter the set by entitlement now: **blocked**, because it requires the perspective-scoped view in the assembly path that this plan's own measurement showed does not exist, and which `D-IMPL-119` limb 2 puts explicitly out of scope for Phase 15.6. **NOT TAKEN.** **Scope boundary, stated because this entry revises shipped code and the recording plan did not touch it.** Plan `15.6-09` **records** this ruling and **does not implement it**. Shape B revises what plan `15.6-07` shipped: `src/ccf/halflife/assessment.py::SourceRefresh` and `::SourceRefreshRecency`, `src/ccf/products/contract.py::ContextProductContract`, the `src/ccf/replay/record.py::ContentGenerationPath` twin, **all 7** shipped `rehydrate_product` implementations across 6 files, the `s1-01` artifacts and spine, and a **fourth** content-address move in `examples/08-e2e-demo/artifacts/expected_output.txt`. **Implementing plan: plan `15.6-13`**, dedicated to it. **Sequencing constraint, and it is a constraint rather than a preference: `15.6-13` must land BEFORE plan `15.6-10` regenerates the surface manifest.** `15.6-10` owns this phase's single manifest regeneration; a regeneration taken before Shape B lands would capture the pre-Shape-B vessel and be **stale on arrival**, and the phase would then need a second regeneration it has ruled it will not take. **Governs:** `src/ccf/halflife/assessment.py::SourceRefresh` and `::SourceRefreshRecency`; `src/ccf/products/contract.py::ContextProductContract`'s `source_refresh_recency` member; `src/ccf/replay/record.py::ContentGenerationPath`'s matching member; every implementation of `ReplayEnvironment.rehydrate_product`; `examples/s1-01-hello-context-product/artifacts/product-governance.yaml` as the population site; the ordering of plans `15.6-13` and `15.6-10`. Does **not** amend `D-IMPL-118`, whose `qa-toplevel` placement is unchanged — only the member's *contents* change — and does **not** amend `D-IMPL-119`, whose limbs continue to govern evidence pointers and not this field. **Implementing plan: plan `15.6-13`.** Originates: plan `15.6-07` Findings § 3, raised by its executor and deliberately not ruled there; `D-IMPL-105`; `D-IMPL-119`; `D-IMPL-117`; plan `15.6-09`'s re-measurement at `4b407e0`.

**D-IMPL-125 — "Hello CCF" is plan `16-05` rebuilt in place: a Fluree backend, output a human reads, and the produce and consume paths shown as two separate examples.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-08-13. Approver: Dave. **Origin: the blocking human-verify checkpoint in plan `16-05` returned a change request rather than an approval — twice.** That checkpoint exists because a structural test can prove markers are present, ordered and closed but cannot prove a reader can *see* what the example teaches; its own text said *"This shape is copied by every other example in the suite. If it is wrong, it is cheapest to say so now."* It was right both times, and neither defect was reachable by any gate in the tree. **First reading, 2026-08-13 morning.** Two defects: the example ran on `sqlite` and it printed **nothing at all** — `grep -rnE "print\(|sys\.stdout\.write" examples/s1-01-hello-context-product/*.py` returned no matches across `run.py`, `spine.py`, `deployment.py` and `source_estate.py`, while `run.py::main` assembled three Context Products inside a `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory` and discarded them. `make example-s1-01` exited 0 having shown the operator nothing. Rulings: **Fluree, not sqlite**; **it prints its work**; **Fluree now and the six-backend matrix later at `16-07`**, so nothing may hard-wire the substrate in a way that blocks parameterisation — the backend comes from `artifacts/backends.yaml` through the Phase 15.4 registration seam. **Phase 16's scope is UNCHANGED by this entry** — 21 plans, all 10 ROADMAP success criteria unedited, Sections 1–3 all still ship; Dave's words, *"I don't want to throw away the scope of phase 16, just insert 'hello ccf' before the existing scope begins."* An earlier reading of the same conversation as a *narrowing* — Phase 16 reduced to one example with the remainder deferred to a new Phase 16.1 — was **wrong and is recorded here as rejected**, because it would have rewritten criteria 1, 3, 4, 5, 7 and 9 that the phase still satisfies at close across waves 4 through 12. **Second reading, 2026-08-13 evening, and it is the substantive one.** The rebuilt example ran on Fluree in 6 seconds and printed 339 lines, and Dave rejected it again: *"what this example does not show me is 1) how do I create a context product and 2) as a client how do I receive a context product.
