A third-party deployment could then quietly hold two Python modules where `D-IMPL-141` Amendment A.3 grants exactly one, its projection — and Amendment A.4 requires that the exception cannot widen silently, which is precisely what a second module arriving through the server key would do. **THE RULING (Dave, 2026-08-18).** It is a hole and it is closed **in this phase**. `~ccf.client.adapters.binding_document::load_binding_document` refuses a `server:` value resolving inside the deployment root, **by name**, in the `RULED_OUT_KEYS` register's voice rather than as an unrecognised path: the message states that the value resolves inside the deployment root, that Amendment A.3 grants that directory one Python module (its projection), that a server program is not deployment content, and the remedy — **name it beside the deployment, not inside it** — with a pointer to `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-16-reference-plan-factory-and-debt-scorer.md` Amendment A. The register matters: an author who writes an inward value has not made a typo, and a message about an unrecognised path would invite a re-spelling of the thing that was declined. **IT IS A VALUE REFUSAL, NOT A KEY REFUSAL, AND A LATER READER MUST NOT MISTAKE IT FOR ONE.** `"server"` is a member of `~ccf.client.adapters.binding_document::OPTIONAL_KEYS` and is deliberately **NOT** a member of `~ccf.client.adapters.binding_document::RULED_OUT_KEYS`. That mapping refuses a key unconditionally by name; `server:` is legitimate and the shipped `examples/hw1-companies-over-revenue` deployment declares one. What is refused is one class of *value*. **THE TWO REJECTED ALTERNATIVES, WITH THEIR REASONS.** (1) **Allow it and record the rejection in prose.** Rejected because it leaves `assert document.server.parent != root` in `tests/examples/test_hw1_two_transports.py` as the only thing holding the line, and that assertion covers the shipped example and **no adopter**; Amendment A.3's one-module grant would then be enforceable by nothing except review, when the entire value of A.3 is that it is mechanical. (2) **Defer it to the Context Product assembly examples**, where the server moves to the top level anyway. Rejected because the parent-relative base **ships in this phase**, so the gap it opens is open from this phase onward rather than from a later one, and deferring hands the gap on **without the measurement that found it**. **WHAT IT GOVERNS.** `~ccf.client.adapters.binding_document::load_binding_document`'s `server:` value-read, and nothing else. No other key's containment changed, `_contained`'s absolute / `..` / symlink rules are untouched, and `tests/client/test_binding_document.py::assert_one_python_module` — the shared helper `tests/client/test_data_only_deployment.py` drives — is **byte-unchanged** — `D-03` of this phase's context ruled that it needs no amendment, and that was confirmed by running its two shipped controls rather than by claiming it. **WHERE IT IS ENFORCED.** Two places, deliberately, because a refusal that fires in a loader and is never reached by a client is a gate wired to nothing (`CLNT-12`): `tests/client/test_binding_document.py::test_binding_document_refuses_a_server_reaching_back_inside_the_deployment` (the loader, plan `18.1-01` Task 2), and `tests/client/test_data_only_deployment.py::test_a_server_reaching_inside_the_deployment_is_refused_end_to_end` (a **client**, driven from a `CCF_BINDING` string through `~ccf.client::ProductClient.ask`, plan `18.1-01` Task 3). Both were sabotage-verified — removing the refusal turns the first red, and neutering the control's own mutation turns the second red at its `"the control did not change anything"` assertion. **THIS IS THE ONE PIECE OF NEW MECHANISM PHASE 18.1 SHIPS**, roughly four lines and one test, in a phase that was scoped and announced as shipping none. The claim is **narrowed rather than deleted** at all three places it was written in `.planning/ROADMAP.md` — the Phases-list bullet, the Phase 18.1 goal paragraph and the scope preamble — because a reviewer who finds a new by-name refusal in a phase that disclaimed all mechanism reads it as scope creep rather than as a ruling. The surface record is `docs/surface-changes/18.1-04-the-deployment-declares-its-server.md`. **Governs:** `src/ccf/client/adapters/binding_document.py`; `examples/hw1-companies-over-revenue/deployment/binding.yaml`; the Phase 18.1 claims in `.planning/ROADMAP.md`. **Related:** `D-IMPL-141` Amendment A.3/A.4 (the one-module grant this protects, and the requirement that it cannot widen silently), `D-IMPL-152`, `D-GATE-18`, and this phase's `D-09` (a server program is not deployment content), `D-10` (the parent-relative base that opens the gap), `D-06`/`D-07`/`D-08` (the transport-side refusals that are separate from this one) and `C-1` (the documentation must not generalize that servers live in deployments).

**D-IMPL-154 — `tools/retirement_sweep.py --report` rewrites a tracked file; the flag name is the defect.** RESOLVED — ADVISORY, DEFERRED. Date: 2026-08-19. Approver: Dave. **Context.** Found during Phase 18.1's `D-19` second sweep, and found the way such things are found: the `18.1-04` executor ran `--report` intending only to **measure** staleness, and it performed `D-19`'s scheduled fix, rewriting `docs/surface/examples/RETIREMENT-COUPLINGS.md` in place and printing a one-line confirmation. It took its measurement from the resulting diff and reverted. No damage followed, because the mutation was noticed; a `--report` flag is however read as read-only by every convention the word carries, and the next caller may not check `git status`. **The argparse help text is already honest** — it says `"rewrite …"` — so this is not a documentation gap. The defect is that the flag's *name* contradicts its own help. **THE RULING (Dave, 2026-08-19).** Minted as a tracked entry rather than left in a phase SUMMARY, **specifically so it stops being invisible inheritance** — the phase's `18.1-04` and `18.1-05` SUMMARYs both carry it and neither is a document a later tools pass would read. **Deferred, not reopened as in-phase work**: Phase 18.1 is a client-experience phase and a tools rename is not its scope. A later tools pass should rename or split the flag — `--check` (read-only, exits non-zero when stale) and `--write` (the current behavior) is the shape suggested, not ruled. Related: `D-19` (the two-sweep design that surfaced it), `D-IMPL-155` (the other tooling hazard from the same close review), `D-GATE-18.1`.

**D-IMPL-155 — a misnamed surface-changelog fragment is silently dropped, and the obvious remedy deletes the record while every gate reports green.** RESOLVED — ADVISORY, DEFERRED. Date: 2026-08-19. Approver: Dave. **Context.** Found by sabotage during Phase 18.1's close, and sharpened on re-measurement. Dropping the `18.1-04-` prefix from a fragment in `docs/surface-changes/` makes the assembler's glob skip it. The first reproduction went **red**, not green — but the red says *"the assembled document is out of date"* and **never** *"your fragment is misnamed."* Re-run `make surface-changes` once and the red disappears **together with the record**: 117 lines and four entries gone, register counts falling silently 727 → 723, `--check` clean, all 20 surface tests green. **Nothing compares the fragment directory against what was assembled.** So the naming rule is load-bearing, nothing enforces it, and the remedy a confused caller will reach for first is the one that destroys the evidence. **THE RULING (Dave, 2026-08-19).** *"This is the don't-know-collapsed-into-pass shape with data loss."* Minted as a tracked entry rather than left in review files, so a later gate can be written against it: **compare the fragment directory against the assembled document**, so a fragment that exists but was not assembled is a named failure rather than a silent subtraction. **Deferred, not reopened as in-phase work.** This is the same defect class Phase 18.1 recorded four times inside its own test suite (`D-GATE-18.1`), arriving one layer out in the tooling that records surface changes. Related: `D-IMPL-110` (the precedent for minting an entry rather than trusting a regenerated manifest), `D-IMPL-154`, `D-GATE-18.1`.

**D-GATE-18.1 — Phase 18.1 approved.** Date: 2026-08-19. Approver: Dave. **5 of 5 plans complete**, plus an in-phase close-fix set (`18.1-06`). `make ci-core` **exit 0** at the gate HEAD `04cccc2`, verified by the orchestrator: **3909 passed / 118 skipped / 0 failed**, plus 400 lint and 154 docs/publish; the `+8` over the pre-review baseline is **exactly** the eight tests added, so nothing was silently dropped or skipped. **What the phase delivered against its own goal:** the client's documented command no longer names `serve.py` anywhere (`CCF_BINDING="mcp+stdio:examples/hw1-companies-over-revenue/deployment"`); the two documented commands differ by exactly one token, the scheme, **and a gate now holds that property**; `serve.py` is cut 292 → 197 lines with the fabric composition moved off-stage to `compose.py`; and the README states *why* a server is present before showing one. **One deliberate piece of new SDK mechanism** — `D-18`'s inward `server:` refusal, ruled and recorded in `D-IMPL-153` — with the ROADMAP's "ships no new SDK surface" claim narrowed at its source rather than left standing. **`C-1` was approved by Dave's own passage-by-passage read** (2026-08-19), `README:186` explicitly considered and left unchanged; **no automated proxy for `C-1` was invented**, and its unmeasurability was **demonstrated rather than asserted** — the entire README frame was deleted and 381 example tests stayed green. **The close-time protocol ran in the CLAUDE.md §3.1 order**: execute → cross-AI panel against the **shipped code** (written to `18.1-CLOSE-REVIEWS.md` so the pre-execution plan review survives) → single-agent review → verify every finding against the tree → fix blocking findings in-phase → present. **Three blocking findings were found by the panel and fixed inside the phase**, each independently re-sabotaged by the orchestrator so that the mutations which previously passed silently now fail: `D-18`'s predicate is a disjunction and **both existing tests fed only the second limb** — removing the first left **752 tests green** (`0ec22ca`; the mechanism was correct, nothing held it); a **root path containing a space** was diagnosed as the pre-migration two-token address and advised to *"drop it from the address"*, which destroys the path (`/tmp/My Deployments/deployment` → `mcp+stdio:/tmp/My`), a new instance of the `B0b` report-quality class **in the phase whose own `D-08` cites `B0b`** (`002cb55`); and the README **credited a test with a check it does not make** — repointing the documented address at a nonexistent `OTHERDEPLOYMENT` in **both** README and Makefile left all 17 purity tests green, so `D-15`'s observable rested on a property no gate held, in the very document `C-1` was approved on (`6cea25d`, fixed **both** ways on Dave's ruling: the gate strengthened and the prose rewritten against it). **The lesson recorded against the close process itself:** the `gsd-verifier` scored 40/40 and sabotaged `D-18` **entirely** (`if False:`), got two reds, and concluded it was held; the panel removed **one limb** and found nothing red. Same mechanism, same technique, **different granularity, opposite answers** — a sabotage as coarse as the whole guard proves only that *some* test mentions it, never that *each branch* is held. **And the seventh instance of this phase's defect class was inside the proposed remedy for the sixth**: both the review and the orchestrator's brief proposed `binding.partition(":")[2].partition(":")[2]` to extract the address; measured against real tokens it yields `""` for **both** commands, so the assertion would have passed **on an empty set**. The executor measured it, refused it, and shipped a guarded splitter plus five parametrized vacuity controls instead. **One panel finding is recorded as UNVERIFIED and deliberately NOT actioned**: Codex's only HIGH, a case-insensitive-filesystem bypass of the inward-root rule, **cannot be tested on this Linux host**, and Gemini asserted the opposite **without testing either**. It remains an open question, not a defect. Gemini produced no actionable findings. **Seven confirmed advisories are carried un-fixed and were explicitly fenced out of the close fixes as scope creep** — blank/whitespace/null `server:` reported as absent; non-string `server:` coerced through `str()`; nothing distinguishing `Path.parents` containment from a naive `startswith`; `server_shape_violations` not holding `D-12`'s import criterion; `declare_server`'s ability to write `D-18`-illegal values; the Windows half of the ManifestEntry rule `_contained` cites; and the two tooling hazards now minted as `D-IMPL-154` and `D-IMPL-155`. **Two orchestrator process defects are on the record, against the orchestrator**: the goal verifier and the single-agent code reviewer were dispatched **in parallel onto one working tree** and both run sabotages that mutate source — they observed each other's mutations (the verifier flagged a README reading `OTHERDEPLOYMENT` as possible injection; it was the reviewer's control), both re-verified against `git show HEAD:`, neither acted on foreign state, and the tree ended byte-identical to HEAD, but **the isolation was the orchestrator's to provide**; and the orchestrator's own STATE.md write broke the citation ratchet by putting a line anchor into prose — the same defect cleared at wave 1, caught by the gate that clearing preserved. **The phase executed without worktree isolation, deliberately** (five waves of one plan each, so no parallelism to buy, and `18.1-04` edits `ROADMAP.md`, which the worktree cleanup path backs up and restores across the merge and would have silently reverted). **No `state.*` or `roadmap.*` SDK writer was run against either tracking file** after the one at session start, which collapsed 113 lines of `last_activity` and the whole `progress:` block and was restored from backup; every tracking write in this phase was made by hand. No merge is required — the work landed on `main`. Related: `D-IMPL-153`, `D-IMPL-154`, `D-IMPL-155`, `D-IMPL-141` Amendment A.3, `D-GATE-18`, and `D-19`.

**D-IMPL-156 — Phase 19's decision set (`C-01` … `C-18`) is RATIFIED, and `D-IMPL-151` finding `B0` is CLOSED on the axes measured.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-08-20. Approver: Dave — `C-01`..`C-14` ruled 2026-08-17, `C-15`/`C-16`/`C-17` ruled 2026-08-19, and `C-18` ruled 2026-08-19 at planning revision in response to a plan-check finding against the shipped tree. **Why this entry exists.** The eighteen rulings live in `.planning/phases/19-the-client-seam-integrity-checks-must-be-able-to-fail-insert/19-CONTEXT.md`, which is a planning artifact, not the decision log. A ruling recorded only in a phase folder gets re-litigated by the next reader; a ruling recorded **without its rejected alternatives** gets re-litigated worse, because it reads as an arbitrary preference rather than as a choice with a stated cost. Each is therefore restated below **with what it rejected**. Four of them — `C-05`/`C-08`, `C-14`, `C-15`, `C-16`/`C-18` — additionally carry their own entries (`D-IMPL-157` … `D-IMPL-160`) because they amend a standing ruling, break wire compatibility, accept a cost, or defer a defect. **`B0` IS CLOSED, NOT CARRIED.** `D-IMPL-151` deferred `B0` to this phase as an **open blocking defect and explicitly not accepted risk**, and `D-GATE-18` reserved it out of the Phase 18 approval with a standing prose constraint. Both checks are now able to fail, and both were **watched failing**: `19-03` discharged the phase's own success sentence with **two single-transport assertions** — one over `inprocess`, one over `mcp+stdio` — **neither of which names a second subject**, so the failure mode is never *"the two transports disagreed"*; it observed **19 sabotages red** across the two client-seam checks, the codec's byte path, the refused half and the ordering guard, restoring after each; and sabotage 15 of that set is the measurement `C-04` never had — swapping `check_outcome`'s echo comparison and its `product_json is None` return turned **exactly two** tests red out of forty-one and left every served-half leg green, which is the silent uncovering the shipped ordering guard now holds. **THE EIGHTEEN RULINGS, EACH WITH ITS REJECTED ALTERNATIVES.** **`C-01` — the producer's echo is the question the door re-states**, filled from the request the door itself resolved and answered, never passed through from client state. *Rejected:* a canonical digest of the question (a failure then names two digests rather than the wrong question, losing the diagnosis); a client-minted correlation token (proves the call, not the content); both together (two members, two comparisons, two controls for one property). **`C-02` — on the temporal axis the echo is *as asked***: a client that sent `as_of=None` gets `None` back, so the comparison stays a **total three-axis equality with no wildcard on the default path**, and nothing is lost because the instant actually used is already reported on the served vessel. *Rejected:* echoing the resolved instant, which forces a sent-`None` to match anything and reintroduces the vacuity one field over. **`C-03` — the echo is a `WireRequest`, compared by total equality** — no projection, no field selection, and nothing on the wire that no check reads. *Rejected:* reusing `RequestIdentity` on both halves, whose `product_version` has no client-side referent without a second assertion, and whose three-axis variant leaves a wire member no check reads. **`C-04` — the echo sits at outcome level**, so one comparison covers a served answer and a refusal identically: a crossed refusal is a governed "no" attributed to a question nobody asked, and is as detectable as a crossed vessel. `RefusalEnvelope.request` is untouched and stays what `D-28` ruled it — the refusal's own audit record, not a transport control. *Rejected:* asserting additionally that the envelope agrees (a second comparison and a second control for producer-internal consistency, which is a different property); covering the served half only. **`C-05` — the adapter seam is retyped to return bytes.** Own entry: `D-IMPL-157`. **`C-06` — one shape for envelope-carrying doors.** `ccf.products.door.DoorOutcome` is the shape and `ccf.client.wire.WireOutcome` is an **alias** of it rather than a subclass, so the door emits exactly what the client decodes and the MCP adapter's decode step reduces to passing the door's bytes through. The point is **the absence of a transcoding step**, because a transcoding step is precisely where an adapter can re-source the echo from client state. *Rejected:* two shapes with the adapter transcoding (preserves a door/client separation whose only concrete expression was the construction step that *is* the defect); one shape for tool-style doors with HTTP deferred (two answers to *"what does a door emit"* live in the tree at once). **`C-07` — symmetric serialization.** The request is encoded too, and a producer-side door entry decodes it and echoes **what it parsed**. Over `mcp+stdio` that independence already existed because tool arguments genuinely cross a pipe; this ruling is what makes the check live **in-process**, the transport every quickstart, fixture and dev path uses, and without which the whole repair would be cosmetic on the most-used transport. In-process becomes a true degenerate wire in **both** directions, which is the client spec's `D-13` argument applied to the question half. *Rejected:* outcome bytes only (live over MCP, inert in-process); in-process echoing its translated `ProductRequest` (one translation step of apparent independence, but both values still descend from one object). **`C-08` — the seam signature is `ask(WireRequest) -> bytes`.** Own entry: `D-IMPL-157`. **`C-09` — the HTTP door is reconciled, not converted.** Its body stays the vessel and the request echo joins the `X-CCF-*` siblings beside the content address it already publishes, as `X-CCF-Request-Echo`, **absent rather than empty** when no question was posed. `D-IMPL-126` and `canonical_response`'s ruling stand **verbatim** — *"each surface publishes the same sibling values through whatever channel it actually has"* — and `19-06` verified that by diff hunk rather than by reading: `git diff -U0` showed no changed line inside the four-`ETag`-reasons block. *Rejected:* an envelope representation alongside the bare body (one door, two representations, two serializations to keep in agreement); making the body the envelope (uniform, but contradicts `D-IMPL-126` and breaks zero-dependency verification). **Two measured consequences, recorded because neither was predicted.** First, building the echo forced the HTTP door to **refuse** two classes of value it previously served — a `float` inside `parameters`, and a **naive** `asked_at` — which narrows this door into agreement with the MCP tool rather than widening the MCP tool to match, the same direction `D-IMPL-151` finding `B2` chose for this pair, under `D-08`'s posture that the fabric never silently degrades a caller's value. Second, and worth keeping: the shared five-case width table `test_the_neither_door_is_wider_than_the_other` runs contains **no float case**, so **the two doors already disagreed on a float, invisibly, with every gate green** — and `WireRequest`'s own temporal guard already claimed in its docstring that *"both product doors refuse a naive `asked_at` by name"*, a sentence that was **false of this door** until `19-06` made it true by moving the code rather than by softening the claim. **A carried ruling, dispositioned here.** `19-06` reused `ERROR_PRODUCT_REQUEST_INCOMPLETE` for the naive-`asked_at` refusal because `runtime/ccf_runtime/http_api/errors.py` was outside its declared file set, and flagged the question forward. **Ruled: the reuse stands, and a dedicated code is ADVISORY and DEFERRED.** The reused constant's own recorded meaning — *"a defaulted axis is a question nobody asked, answered anyway, so the door refuses the partial address rather than filling one in"* — genuinely covers an axis supplied **without the offset that makes it unambiguous**, and the refusal's message names the guard's own wording so the caller is told the spelling that works. A dedicated `product-asked-at-naive` would read better and is a strictly cosmetic improvement to a message that is already correct; it is not worth a wire-visible error-code addition inside a phase whose subject is claims matching code, and it belongs to whatever later pass touches `errors.py`. Recorded here rather than left in a SUMMARY so that it is a tracked item and not invisible inheritance — the same reason `D-IMPL-154` was minted. **`C-10` — the restored claim is non-adversarial integrity, stated precisely.** Own detail below, under *THE NARROWER TRUE CLAIM*. **`C-11` — failure is proven by a hostile in-repo adapter and by codec-level byte sabotage, both single-transport**, so they falsify the check itself rather than a divergence between two subjects. *Rejected:* a real crossing proxy on the stdio pipes (highest fidelity, but concurrency and timing risk for the same proposition); both together. *Measured:* `19-03`'s controls subclass or wrap the **shipped** adapters, and under the bytes seam a crossing adapter is **one expression** — `super().ask(request.model_copy(update={"parameters": …}))` — where before `19-01`/`19-02` the same class had to re-label the echo from client state to be a crossing at all. That there is nothing else to write **is** the property. **`C-12` — tamper legs become a conformance obligation**: the suite wraps each registered adapter in a byte-corrupting decorator, generic and possible only because `C-05` made the seam bytes, and asserts the client raises — one leg for a crossed echo, one for an altered vessel. *"Official adapter"* comes to mean *"its integrity checks are demonstrably live."* *Rejected:* adapter-agnostic controls outside the suite (arguably one proof covers all, but nothing per-adapter demonstrates liveness); adapters supplying their own fault injector (a weak injector passes while proving little). *Measured, and it is the arithmetic the reconciliation with `D-GATE-18` rests on:* each binding module went **8 → 10** collected, gaining exactly **two call lines and two docstrings and no constant** — so this adds a new **property**, where `D-GATE-18`'s zero-diff claim was about binding a new **adapter** without touching the suite. *Also measured, against the plan's own claim:* the controls fail safe when an edit stops being an involution, and **do not** fail when an edit becomes the identity — identity composed with identity is still the identity. Half of that plan's *"fails safe"* claim was false, and the false half is recorded in the shipped `_reversing_subject` docstring, naming the two binding modules as where the identity case **is** caught. **`C-13` — stay narrow on `B0`**: no sweep of the defect class and no general obligations gate, because `D-IMPL-151`'s recorded lesson — *parity is blind to a check broken identically on both subjects* — does the generalizing, and `D-IMPL-146`'s accretion principle governs. *Rejected:* sweeping and recording every runtime integrity check (cheap to measure, but the findings become open defects that unscope the phase); shipping an obligations gate for the class (*"what counts as an integrity check"* is a judgement that goes stale). **`C-14` — the in-process path's two extra serializations per `ask` are accepted with no benchmark owed.** Own entry: `D-IMPL-160`. **`C-15` — stay narrow on the clock; correct the prose only.** Own entry: `D-IMPL-159`. **`C-16` — break cleanly at the MCP tool, and rule both wire breaks in one entry.** Own entry: `D-IMPL-158`. **`C-17` — a narrow AST gate proves no adapter constructs the outcome**, scoped to `src/ccf/client/adapters/` only, mirroring `CLNT-06`'s already-controlled `count_result_construction_sites` pattern and carrying its own named sabotage control per `CLNT-12` / `D-22`. It exists because a **type change binds `mypy` over `src`/`runtime` only and is invisible to an out-of-tree adapter**, so the ROADMAP's *"a fix that leaves the seam bypassable re-opens the defect for the next adapter"* is discharged by a red check rather than by a convention. *Rejected:* relying on the type change alone; a general obligations gate (`C-13`). *Measured:* the shipped scan counts **two** shapes — a call to a name bound by an import, resolved against both `ccf.client.wire` and `ccf.products.door` and honouring `as` aliases, **and** any attribute-spelled `….WireOutcome(...)` / `….DoorOutcome(...)` call — walking the whole module rather than module scope, because an adapter constructs inside `ask`. Both rules' **necessity** is pinned by two controls carrying deliberately weakened reference walks, so a later *"simplification"* goes red and says what it costs; and the gate itself was observed red twice, once against a forging copy of the **real** adapters directory. The gate's docstring **names what it cannot reach** — `getattr` dispatch, and decode → `model_copy` → re-encode **re-labelling**, which is not a construction at all — and names `C-12`'s conformance obligation as what covers the second. **`C-18` — cross-check the temporal axis where it is checkable, and declare the residual where it is not.** Ruled in `D-IMPL-158` (the cross-check) and `D-IMPL-159` (the residual). It is recorded here as well because it was ruled **after the plans were first written**, which makes it the decision most likely to be dropped by a later writer working from the original discussion log. *Rejected:* declaring the whole temporal axis unprotected, which would ship a comparison `C-03` calls **total** while it is inert on one of three axes; and dropping `asked_at` to single-source the instant, which is structurally the strongest option and was rejected only because it contradicts `C-16`'s ruling against reshaping the four §6.3 axis arguments and discards the tool docstring's own argument for why they are separately required. **THE NARROWER TRUE CLAIM (`C-10`), AND THE CONSTRAINT IT REPLACES.** `D-GATE-18`'s standing constraint — *"the SDK must not be described … as detecting a transport that answered a different question, or a vessel altered in transit"* — is **REPLACED BY A NARROWER TRUE SENTENCE, NOT LIFTED**, and `src/ccf/client/codec.py`'s module docstring says exactly that at the source, under its heading *"The follow-on landed, and this is what the checks detect — and do not"*. The shipped replacement sentence, quoted verbatim: *"the SDK detects a crossed question and an altered vessel against the five conditions named above; it **does not detect** an adversary who can rewrite the envelope, and it **does not detect** a transport that alters only the instant a question asked with `as_of=None` was answered at."* The **five** conditions the checks detect, verbatim: **corruption** of `product_json` in transit; **truncation** of it; **mis-routing** that swaps a vessel for another producer's, or crosses two in-flight questions that are not identical; **a re-serializing intermediary**, because any re-render changes the bytes and not the claim travelling beside them; and **producer/consumer canonicalization drift**, because the consumer hashes the text it received rather than re-canonicalizing it, so a producer that renders differently from what it claims is caught on its own bytes. The **four** cases they do **not** detect, and the count is four rather than three because `C-18`'s residual is one of them: **(1)** an adversary who can rewrite the envelope, since the claim rides *in* the envelope — this is non-adversarial integrity and nothing more; **(2)** a producer that mis-canonicalizes *consistently*, which states a matching address for its own wrong bytes, and is caught by the vessel's contract validation and by cross-adapter parity, never by this comparison; **(3)** two *identical* in-flight questions crossing, knowingly accepted because the echo **is** the question and every field a correlation token would add is a field no check reads (`C-03`); and **(4)** on a question asked with `as_of=None` **only**, a transport that alters the instant the door answered against — see `D-IMPL-159`, where that residual and the half of the axis that **is** held are stated together. **Signing is out of scope and NO SIGNATURE MEMBER IS RESERVED ON THE WIRE** (`C-10`): reserving one would put a member on the wire that nothing sets and nothing reads, which is precisely the shape that made both checks inert in the first place. **The four-item count was cross-checked between the two records** — this entry and `codec.py`'s shipped list — because the plan required that if they disagreed, one of them was wrong; they agree. **What parity is still for, measured rather than argued.** `19-03` found that deleting the Phase 18 echo re-label from `tests/client/conformance/test_the_mcp_binding_fires.py::_AnswersAnotherQuestion` destroys **both** of that module's parity controls, because the client now raises before either leg compares anything. Rather than retarget them into assertions about nothing, a new subject was written — a door **honest about the question and divergent in the answer**, with its `content_address` recomputed over the altered vessel so the producer's claim about its own bytes is true. Nothing in `check_outcome` can object to it, and **only a comparison across transports catches it**. That is the sharpest available statement of why the cross-adapter suite still earns its keep after this phase, and `D-IMPL-149`'s control survives with something to prove. **Governs:** `src/ccf/client/codec.py`; `src/ccf/client/wire.py`; `src/ccf/client/client.py`; `src/ccf/products/door.py`; `src/ccf/client/adapters/`; `runtime/ccf_runtime/mcp/egress.py`; `runtime/ccf_runtime/http_api/routes/`; `tests/client/conformance/`. **Related:** `D-IMPL-151` (the `B0` deferral this closes), `D-GATE-18` (the reservation and the replaced constraint), `D-IMPL-157`, `D-IMPL-158`, `D-IMPL-159`, `D-IMPL-160`, `D-IMPL-161`, `D-IMPL-146` (the accretion principle `C-13` applies), `D-IMPL-149`, `D-IMPL-126` (`C-09` preserves it), `D-IMPL-38` (the naive-instant refusal), `CLNT-05`, `CLNT-06`, `CLNT-08`, `CLNT-12`.

**D-IMPL-157 — the adapter seam is retyped to `ask(WireRequest) -> bytes`; the adapter no longer constructs the outcome. AMENDS the client design spec's `D-11` and `CLNT-05`.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-08-20. Approver: Dave (`C-05`, `C-08`, 2026-08-17). **What is amended, and where.** `D-11` in `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-15-ccf-client-design.md` §5 and in `.planning/phases/17-client-access-ccf-client-and-the-transport-agnostic-first-ex/17-CONTEXT.md` typed the seam `TransportAdapter.ask(WireRequest) -> WireOutcome`, with `WireOutcome` *"the canonical serialized form of either a served product or a refusal"* built by the adapter. It is amended to `ask(WireRequest) -> bytes`: the **request** stays typed, because an adapter genuinely needs its fields to build a tool call or a URL, and only the **answer** becomes bytes. The spec records this as **Amendment 2**, appended in Amendment 1's dated-block form with §5 left unedited; `.planning/REQUIREMENTS.md`'s `CLNT-05` records it in the amend-never-delete form, original text kept and this entry named. **Why a type change and not a lint.** `D-11`'s permission for an adapter to construct the outcome **is what admitted the defect**. `D-IMPL-151` measured it precisely: with no request identity on the wire, both shipped adapters set `request` from the request object they were handed, and `ProductClient` passed that *same object* as `sent`, so `check_outcome`'s `outcome.request != sent` was an object compared with itself and `verify_content_address` was `sha256(x) != sha256(x)`. A permission cannot be closed by a convention that asks adapters not to use it. Removing the return type removes the thing there was to construct. *Rejected:* keeping the object seam and gating the construction with a lint — it reaches this repository's adapters and **nothing out-of-tree**, which is precisely the ROADMAP's *"a fix that leaves the seam bypassable re-opens the defect for the next adapter"*; and an object seam whose outcome carries its own provenance, which reaches third-party adapters at runtime but puts a **trust token inside a data shape**, where anything that can build the shape can build the token. *Rejected on the signature itself:* `ask(bytes) -> bytes`, fully symmetric, but the MCP adapter decodes immediately so the blindness would be nominal while the adapter loses the typed fields it actually needs. **What the change bought, measured.** `decode_outcome` — the one function that parses `request` and `content_address` out of **sender-produced** bytes, and which had **no shipped call site** through Phase 18 — is now on the shipped path, called by `ProductClient.ask` on the bytes the adapter returned. `CLNT-08` stops being a claim about an unshipped function. `grep -cE "WireOutcome\(|DoorOutcome\(" src/ccf/client/adapters/*.py` is **0** in both modules, `McpStdioAdapter._decode` and `InProcessAdapter._encode` are **deleted**, and there is **no shim**: no `ask` overload accepting either shape, because a fallback that reconstructs the echo is the bypass this repair closes. `C-17`'s AST gate (`D-IMPL-156`) holds the zero permanently, over a directory rather than over a type checker's reach. **A consequence the design did not anticipate, and how it was resolved.** Moving the checks onto the decode path stranded the one `Result` construction site without a parsed vessel: `decode_outcome` had been discarding `check_outcome`'s return while `ProductClient._result_from` sourced the vessel from a **second** `check_outcome` call. Both escapes were forbidden — re-parsing `product_json` is a second contract validation on a second decode path, against `D-12`. So `decode_outcome` returns a frozen `DecodedOutcome(outcome, vessel)` pair and the vessel travels out beside the outcome; `check_outcome`'s call **and** its import are gone from `client.py`, and it now runs exactly once per `ask`. **The blast radius, measured against the estimate.** `19-RESEARCH.md` estimated 50–95 broken tests and marked the per-file split as estimated rather than measured. The retype broke **46** (45 failures and one error) across **six** modules, **all six in `tests/client`** — and both shipped transports' conformance modules passed **8/8 on the first run** after the retype, which is the load-bearing measurement: `B0` is mechanically closed on both real transports and not merely on a stub. The estimate was wrong in kind as well as in size; it anticipated breakage outside `tests/client` and there was none. **TWO CARRIED RULINGS, DISPOSITIONED HERE.** **(1) `ProductClient._result_from`'s `sent` parameter: RULED — it goes; ADVISORY, DEFERRED, and explicitly not accepted as it stands.** Nothing in the method's body reads it once the echo cross-check moved into `decode_outcome`; `19-02` kept the signature only because its plan prescribed it verbatim, and `19-07` corrected the `Args:` entry, which had claimed a use that no longer exists. It is the *"a member nothing sets and nothing reads"* shape `C-10` names, one scope over — private to the package, invisible to `mypy --strict` and to every lint, and therefore exactly the kind of residual that survives by being nobody's job. The removal is **not made here**: this phase's final plan changes no code by its own scope statement, and moving a signature — even a private one — inside a documentation plan is the accretion `D-IMPL-146` governs. The interim record is the docstring paragraph `19-07` wrote, which states plainly that the body does not read it. The next change that touches `ccf.client.client` removes the parameter. **(2) `TransportError` dropped from `src/ccf/client/adapters/inprocess.py` by `19-02`, against that plan's explicit instruction to keep it: RULED — the drop STANDS, NO ACTION.** The plan reasoned that `served_answer` inside `door_answer` raises `TypeError` for the wrong shape, *"the same diagnosis in the right place"*, and that the import should stay. Measured after `_encode` was deleted: the name appeared in the module **only** in its import and one docstring cross-reference, and an imported name nothing uses is the same `C-10` shape one scope over — so it was dropped. No in-tree test asserted the deleted raise's wording, so nothing had to be retargeted. `19-07` re-verified against the tree: the name is **not imported**, and its single surviving occurrence is a prose cross-reference stating that `BindingError` is *"a `TransportError` by inheritance"*, which is true and correct. `BindingError` is still imported and still used, so `D-10`'s catch-all is intact. Confirmed and closed. **Governs:** `src/ccf/client/wire.py`; `src/ccf/client/codec.py`; `src/ccf/client/client.py`; `src/ccf/client/adapters/inprocess.py`; `src/ccf/client/adapters/mcp_stdio.py`; `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-15-ccf-client-design.md` Amendment 2; `.planning/REQUIREMENTS.md` `CLNT-05`. **Related:** `D-IMPL-156` (the ratification), `D-IMPL-158` (the out-of-tree adapter break this type change causes), `D-IMPL-160` (the serialization cost `C-07` buys), `D-IMPL-151`, `D-GATE-18`, `CLNT-05`, `CLNT-06`, `CLNT-08`, `D-IMPL-146`.

**D-IMPL-158 — BOTH of Phase 19's wire-compatibility breaks, ruled in one entry with NO deprecation window; and the door's three-axis cross-check against the encoded question.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-08-20. Approver: Dave (`C-16`, `C-18`, 2026-08-19). **Why one entry.** `C-16` requires both breaks ruled together, stating the reasoning either way, because two entries invite a reader to conclude that one of them was weighed and the other inherited. **BREAK 1 — `PRODUCT_REQUEST_TOOL` gains the encoded `WireRequest` as a REQUIRED argument.** The tool's argument count moves from seven to eight, asserted by set **equality** against the generated input schema rather than by membership. The reasoning is the tool docstring's own, and is reused rather than invented: the four §6.3 axes are required **together** so that *"a partial address is unrepresentable rather than merely refused"* — and required-together is strictly stronger than optional, because a Tool's input schema can enforce it where a query string cannot. *Rejected:* an optional argument with a reconstruction fallback — a fallback that reconstructs the echo is **precisely** the bypass this phase closes, and an argument nothing sets is the pattern `C-10` names; and reshaping the four axis arguments wholesale into one encoded question, a larger break that discards the docstring's own argument for why the axes are separately required. **This is a wire-compatibility break for any non-SDK consumer of the tool, and there is no deprecation window.** **BREAK 2 — out-of-tree `TransportAdapter` implementations break at the `C-08` type change** (`D-IMPL-157`), cleanly, **with no deprecation window and no shim.** `19-CONTEXT.md` left the window question to planning; it is ruled here, with the three reasons stated so a reader can check them: **(a)** the package is pre-1.0 and the surface manifest is a **v0.2** baseline, so the compatibility promise being broken is one nobody was given; **(b)** a shim accepting **either** a `WireOutcome` or bytes re-opens exactly the bypass `C-05` closes, because the branch that accepts an object is a branch in which an adapter constructs the answer; **(c)** `D-11`'s permission is what admitted the defect in the first place, so a deprecation window is a window **on the defect** — a period in which the SDK ships a documented path to the shape it is repairing. The migration is recorded adopter-facing in `docs/surface-changes/19-01-one-outcome-shape-and-the-encoded-question.md` and `docs/surface-changes/19-02-the-adapter-seam-carries-bytes.md`, each carrying a `Migration` line and each stating the absence of a window and why. **THE DOOR REFUSES A CALL THAT ASKS TWO THINGS, BY NAME, ON EVERY AXIS WITH A SECOND SOURCE.** Break 1 creates a hazard it must close in the same change: with the question encoded **and** the address arguments still present, a caller could encode question A, supply address arguments for question B, have A echoed and B answered, and a consumer's cross-check would pass on a perfectly matching echo. That is `B0`'s own failure mode reappearing one layer up. So the MCP handler cross-checks the decoded request against the address arguments and **refuses a disagreement by name** on `product_class`, on `parameters`, and — guarded on `temporal_boundary is not None` — on `asked_at`; and the answer resolves from the **decoded** request's parameters, so there is one source for what is answered and the echo is that same source. `runtime/ccf_runtime/mcp/egress.py` contains **zero** outcome constructions after the change; the emission is `ccf.products.door.door_answer`, which serializes the vessel exactly once and derives the content address from those same bytes. **THE THIRD AXIS IS `C-18`, AND IT WAS FOUND AGAINST THE SHIPPED TREE RATHER THAN DESIGNED IN.** A plan-check found that because `C-15` keeps the clock client-side (`D-IMPL-159`), `asked_at` remains a separate tool argument, so a **concrete** `as_of` crosses the `mcp+stdio` pipe **twice** — once inside the encoded `WireRequest` that becomes the echo, and once as the argument the door actually answers against. A transport altering only `asked_at` would produce a **perfectly matching echo for an answer computed at a different instant**, on the third axis of a comparison `C-03` defines as **total**. The cross-check is therefore extended to the temporal axis rather than a new mechanism being invented. *Measured:* `19-03` drove a hostile subject that overrides the MCP adapter's `_call` — not its `ask`, because `ask` is what builds the arguments mapping — and moves exactly **one** entry of that mapping, `asked_at`, by one microsecond, leaving the encoded `request` byte-identical. The client raises. It was observed **not** raising when the move is held to the identity, and observed **not** raising when the door's own `temporal_boundary is not None` block is deleted from an out-of-tree copy of `egress.py` — so the guard is demonstrably what catches it, rather than something else in the path. `C-18`'s **own rejected alternatives**, recorded because they are as load-bearing as the ruling: **declaring the whole temporal axis unprotected**, which would ship a comparison called *total* while it is inert on one of three axes; and **dropping `asked_at` to single-source the instant**, which is structurally the strongest option available and was rejected only because it contradicts this same entry's ruling against reshaping the four §6.3 axis arguments and discards the tool docstring's argument for why they are separately required. **The residual `C-18` leaves is real, is on the `as_of=None` path only, and is recorded in `D-IMPL-159`** — where it belongs, because it is a **cost of the clock deferral** rather than a limit of this cross-check. **What is NOT cross-checked, and why that is a measurement rather than an omission.** In-process, `C-18`'s cross-check has no subject: the resolved instant is derived from the very `WireRequest` the client just encoded, inside one process, so a comparison would compare a value with itself — the defect this phase exists to close, not a check. On the HTTP door the same holds for the same reason: the echo's boundary is built from the one `asked_at` the route parsed. Both absences are stated at the source rather than left to be read as oversights. **Governs:** `runtime/ccf_runtime/mcp/egress.py` (`PRODUCT_REQUEST_TOOL` and its handler); `src/ccf/products/door.py`; `src/ccf/client/wire.py`; every out-of-tree `TransportAdapter`. **Related:** `D-IMPL-156` (the ratification), `D-IMPL-157` (the type change causing break 2), `D-IMPL-159` (`C-15`'s deferral and `C-18`'s residual), `D-IMPL-151`, `D-GATE-18`, `D-IMPL-98` (the four-axes-together argument this reuses), `D-IMPL-133`, `D-IMPL-155` (the fragment-naming hazard the migration records had to avoid).

**D-IMPL-159 — both adapters resolve `as_of=None` CLIENT-side while `ProductClient.ask` promised the deployment does: the false sentence is amended here, the DEFECT IS DEFERRED AND REMAINS OPEN, and its integrity cost is `C-18`'s `as_of=None` residual.** RESOLVED as a **deferral**; the underlying defect is **OPEN**, not accepted. Date: 2026-08-20. Approver: Dave (`C-15`, 2026-08-19; `C-18`, 2026-08-19). **THE MEASUREMENT.** Both shipped adapters resolve a `None` temporal boundary to `datetime.now(UTC)` **in the client process** — `src/ccf/client/adapters/mcp_stdio.py::McpStdioAdapter` and `src/ccf/client/adapters/inprocess.py::InProcessAdapter`, each on the line that builds the request it forwards. `ProductClient.ask`'s docstring promised the opposite: that *"the producing deployment answers against its own clock"*. That sentence was **false on both transports**, and it had been false since the client shipped. **THE PROSE IS CORRECTED HERE; THE CODE IS NOT.** `C-13` governs — this phase stays narrow on `B0` — and the clock read cannot simply move into `src/ccf/products/door.py`, whose module carries `__ccf_mode__ = "algorithmic"` and therefore may not read a clock at all. So `19-07` **amended** the paragraph rather than deleting it, in the shape `src/ccf/client/adapters/binding_document.py` already uses in this tree: the false clause is **quoted verbatim inside the correction and explicitly labelled false**, and what is true is stated beside it — both adapters resolve the instant client-side, the instant actually used is reported on the served vessel, and the echo carries `None` **as asked** (`C-02`). *Rejected:* moving the clock to the door in this phase (scope beyond `B0`, and the algorithmic-module constraint); and saying nothing, which would leave a knowingly false claim in the shipped surface across the one phase whose subject is claims matching what the code does. **A criterion that could not be satisfied honestly, recorded because it generalizes.** `19-07`'s plan required `grep -rn "answers against its own clock" src/ runtime/ examples/ docs/ public/` to return nothing. That is unsatisfiable without **two** violations of this project's own rules: `docs/DECISIONS.md`'s `D-GATE-17` entry quotes the sentence as the docstring read on 2026-08-16, and this log is append-only; and `src/ccf/client/client.py` contains it inside the amended paragraph, where it is the record of the false claim. The plan **reported the defective criterion instead of satisfying it**, and separately measured that the criterion had been **vacuously green all along** — the false sentence wrapped across two lines, so the literal grep never matched it. A grep criterion defeated by a line wrap is not a measurement. **WHAT REMAINS OPEN, AND WHAT A LATER PHASE HAS TO DO.** The defect is recorded **as a deferred defect, not as accepted risk**, in `D-IMPL-151`'s own register: a client-resolved instant means the *"one question, one instant, one decision"* story rests on the caller's clock rather than the deployment's, and two clients with skewed clocks asking the same default question get two decisions. The fix is to **move the resolution of `as_of=None` producer-side**, which the encoded-request design now makes nearly free — the door already parses the question and already stamps its own `asked_at` — and which cannot live in the algorithmic `door.py` entry, so it needs a home on the emitting side, in `runtime/`. **THE COST OF THE DEFERRAL, STATED SO IT CAN BE PRICED (`C-18`).** Keeping the clock client-side is **what leaves `asked_at` a separate transport argument**, and that is what makes a **concrete** `as_of` cross the pipe twice. Both halves of the consequence, in the same breath, because either half quoted alone is false: **on the concrete path the door cross-checks the two copies and refuses a disagreement by name** (`D-IMPL-158`), so a transport that moves the instant is caught; **on the `as_of=None` path the instant crosses exactly once**, because the client resolved it, so a transport that alters **only** `asked_at` returns a perfectly matching echo for an answer computed at another instant and **is UNDETECTED**. The residual is exactly as wide as the deferral and **not one axis wider** — a sentence declaring the temporal axis unprotected would be as false as the sentence this phase replaced, in the other direction. **This residual is a PASSING MEASUREMENT, not a caveat.** `19-03` ships `tests/client/conformance/test_a_crossed_question_is_caught_on_one_transport.py::test_an_absent_boundary_leaves_the_moved_instant_undetectable`, which carries **no expected-failure marker** and asserts more than *"nothing raised"*: the served vessel's `lineage.graph_snapshot_at` **equals the instant the hostile transport substituted**, so the test states what the transport got away with rather than merely that the client was silent. It was observed failing when the hostile subject is made to record an instant it did not substitute. The residual is also **declared in the shipped surface** — it is item 4 of the four undetected cases in `src/ccf/client/codec.py`'s module docstring (`D-IMPL-156`), stated two-sidedly there for the same reason it is stated two-sidedly here. **Moving the clock producer-side closes this residual as a side effect**, because the instant would then have exactly one origin and the client would hold nothing to be lied to about. That is the strongest argument on this entry for doing it, and it is why the deferral is recorded with its cost rather than as a bare "later". **Governs:** `src/ccf/client/client.py` (`ProductClient.ask`); `src/ccf/client/adapters/inprocess.py`; `src/ccf/client/adapters/mcp_stdio.py`; `src/ccf/products/door.py`; a later phase. **Related:** `D-IMPL-156`, `D-IMPL-158` (the cross-check whose residual this is), `D-IMPL-151` (the register this deferral is recorded in), `D-GATE-17` (which quotes the false sentence as it read), `D-GATE-18`, `D-IMPL-146`.

**D-IMPL-160 — the in-process path's two extra serializations per `ask` are ACCEPTED, with no benchmark owed.** RESOLVED — ACCEPTED COST. Date: 2026-08-20. Approver: Dave (`C-14`, 2026-08-17). **The cost.** `C-07` makes the in-process transport a degenerate wire in **both** directions: `InProcessAdapter.ask` encodes the question to text and hands text to its producer half, which parses it with `ccf.products.door.door_question` and echoes **what it parsed**. That is one serialization and one parse per `ask` on top of the answer half's existing pair. **The reasoning, recorded rather than assumed.** The client design spec's `D-13` already accepted *"a microsecond of serialization"* on the answer half, and accepted it for reasons that apply unchanged here: in-process becomes a true degenerate wire rather than a privileged fast path, a parity bug has exactly one place to live, and the adapter is *physically* prevented from leaking live producer-side objects across the seam. **The question is far smaller than the answer** — a product id, a parameters mapping and a temporal boundary, against a whole context product — so the added cost is strictly less than the cost `D-13` already accepted. **No benchmark is owed.** *Rejected:* accepting the cost and measuring it in the performance battery, which turns a cost into a number and a number into a threshold somebody has to maintain; and avoiding the cost by letting in-process skip request serialization, which reverses the ruling that made the check live in-process at all. **What the cost BUYS, which is why it is not merely tolerable.** Without it the repair would be **cosmetic on the most-used transport**. In-process is what every quickstart, every fixture and every dev path runs, and it is the transport on which the client and the producer share an address space — so it is precisely where an echo re-sourced from the caller's own object is easiest to write and hardest to notice. `19-02` landed the assertion that pays for the cost: over in-process, the echo **equals** the question sent (total equality, `C-03`) and **is not the same object** — a round trip actually happened — observed over a question carrying a nested mapping parameter, which is `D-IMPL-103`'s one declared level of nesting and the shape a lossy wire mangles first. Its vacuity guard was observed red against a question differing in exactly one parameter. **Governs:** `src/ccf/client/adapters/inprocess.py`. **Related:** `D-IMPL-156`, `D-IMPL-157`, `D-13` (the spec ruling this extends to the question half), `D-IMPL-103`, `CLNT-08`.

**D-IMPL-161 — Phase 19 landed directly on `main` with no phase branch, which DIVERGES from CLAUDE.md §2.2 and MATCHES what Phases 18 and 18.1 actually did.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-08-19. Approver: Dave. **What was asked and what was ruled.** `19-01`'s SUMMARY stopped and asked, because that plan's standing hazards said phase work belongs on `phase-19` with a single merge at the gate, and all seven of its commits had landed on `main`. Dave ruled on 2026-08-19, when asked directly: **the work stays on `main`**. The reasons, recorded so the ruling is checkable rather than inferred: there are **no SDK consumers**, so `main` carrying un-gated phase work costs nothing that a branch would protect; and git history still permits **carving a branch retroactively** if a consumer ever appears, so nothing is foreclosed. **Why this is minted rather than left in a SUMMARY.** CLAUDE.md §2.2 states that *"`main` is the approved-state branch"*, that phase work happens on a phase branch, and that the merge happens at the `D-GATE-<Phase>` entry. That is written law, and **three consecutive phases have not followed it**: `D-GATE-18.1` already records *"No merge is required — the work landed on `main`"*, Phase 19 did the same, and `.planning/config.json` carries `git.branching_strategy: "none"`, which is the mechanical reason the executors never had a branch to be on. An undocumented divergence between written law and three phases' practice is exactly the drift this phase exists to correct, one document over — a rule nobody follows and nothing enforces is the governance twin of a check that cannot fail. **What this entry does and does not do.** It records the divergence and Dave's ruling for Phase 19. It does **not** amend CLAUDE.md §2.2, because CLAUDE.md is Dave's document and rewriting it is not an executor's act; and it does **not** rule the general case. A later revision should either bring §2.2 into line with the practice — stating that a phase branch is optional while the SDK has no consumers, and what changes when it has one — or bring the practice back into line with §2.2 by setting `git.branching_strategy` and having the orchestrator create the branch. Leaving both as they are is the one option this entry is written to prevent. **Governs:** Phase 19's placement on `main`; the reading of CLAUDE.md §2.2 against Phases 18, 18.1 and 19. **Related:** `D-GATE-18.1` (the same practice, recorded), `D-GATE-18` (which *does* record a merge from `phase-18`), `D-IMPL-156`, `D-IMPL-154` and `D-IMPL-155` (the same *mint-it-so-it-stops-being-invisible-inheritance* discipline).

**D-IMPL-162 — a STRUCTURALLY UNBYPASSABLE seam is DEFERRED, not done; Phase 19's three prose overclaims are corrected instead.** RESOLVED as a **deferral**; the claim is narrowed and the underlying expressibility **remains open by design**. Date: 2026-08-20. Approver: Dave, at the Phase 19 close review. **What the panel found.** The §3.1 cross-AI panel reviewed the shipped code (`19-CLOSE-REVIEWS.md`), and **three of four reviewers converged independently** on one finding: `src/ccf/client/wire.py::TransportAdapter.ask` claimed that *"an adapter that cannot construct the outcome cannot fill the echo from the request it was handed"*, and the antecedent is false. `ccf.client.wire.WireOutcome` and `ccf.client.codec.encode_outcome` are both public — **deliberately**, because `TransportAdapter` is a `Protocol` and out-of-tree adapters are the point of one — so an adapter may parse the producer's bytes, copy its own caller's request over the echo, re-encode, and return bytes satisfying `ask(WireRequest) -> bytes`. **Measured, not argued:** an out-of-tree probe with two deliberately different vessels showed forwarding another question's bytes unchanged raises `TransportError`, while **re-labelling that outcome's echo raises nothing** and serves the other question's vessel under the caller's identity. The first version of that probe was **vacuous** — its attack leg and its control produced byte-identical outcomes — and was discarded and rebuilt; the vacuity is recorded because it is the same defect class the phase is about, occurring in the code written to test the phase. **What was ALREADY known, and what was not.** `D-IMPL-156` already records that `C-17`'s gate docstring **names re-labelling as beyond its reach** — *"decode → `model_copy` → re-encode re-labelling, which is not a construction at all"* — and names `C-12`'s conformance obligation as what covers it for registered adapters. So the mechanism's limit was known and written down **at the gate**. What was NOT written down is that `wire.py`'s own seam docstring asserted the opposite, unscoped, one module over. The defect was therefore a **claim that contradicted a limit the phase had already documented elsewhere** — which is why it is a blocking finding in a phase whose subject is claims matching code, and why it is a **prose** finding rather than a mechanism one. **Dave's ruling.** *"Narrow the claim. That is what `C-17` already implied. Record any desire for a structurally unbypassable seam as a future item, not as Phase 19 work."* Turning the seam into something structurally unbypassable — a non-public encoder, or a producer signature over the outcome — **is a different project**, and doing it inside Phase 19 would reopen scope after the mechanism landed cleanly. `C-17` scoped the gate to `src/ccf/client/adapters/` **on purpose**; this entry does not disturb that. **What was corrected, and what stands.** Three prose-only amendments, no code-path change, no new gate: **(1)** `ccf.client.wire.TransportAdapter.ask` now states exactly what the bytes seam buys — it removes the *convenient* path to `B0` and `C-17`'s gate closes construction **in-tree outright** — and states what it does not buy, that an out-of-tree adapter may still re-label, that both checks then pass because the adapter supplied both sides of each comparison, and that making it unreachable needs a producer signature or a private encoder, deferred here. **(2)** `ccf.client.codec`'s residual paragraph no longer generalizes *"the residual is the `None` path and only the `None` path"* from the one door where the cross-check was established: the MCP door cross-checks and refuses by name; the HTTP door builds its echo from the single `asked_at` it parsed, so a cross-check would compare a value with itself and **its absence is a measurement, not an exemption**; the in-process adapter derives `asked_at` from the encoded question it is handed, so on the shipped path the two cannot disagree, but it carries **no door-side refusal**, so an adapter passing a moved `asked_at` beside a concrete boundary would not be refused the way the MCP door refuses it. No shipped adapter does this and `C-17`'s gate does not reach it, because it is an argument value rather than an outcome construction. **(3)** `ccf.client.codec.decode_outcome` no longer says the client *"runs again"* on whatever an adapter returns — a pre-`C-05` story that outlived the amendment in this module while `ccf.client.client` had already amended it correctly. The superseded sentence is kept and marked amended rather than deleted, per the project's amend-never-delete practice. **The residual, stated so a later reader can act on it.** An adapter author who goes out of their way can still defeat both client-seam checks by re-labelling. This is **non-adversarial integrity** — the same posture `C-10` already records for the envelope — and the remedy, if the threat model ever expands to untrusted adapters, is a producer signature over the outcome, which `C-10` explicitly declined to reserve a wire member for on the grounds that a member nothing sets and nothing reads is what made both checks inert in the first place. A future phase taking this up should therefore expect to add **both** the member and the mechanism that reads it, in one change. **Governs:** `src/ccf/client/wire.py`; `src/ccf/client/codec.py`. **Related:** `D-IMPL-156` (`C-10`'s claim, `C-12`'s obligation and `C-17`'s gate, whose docstring already named this limit), `D-IMPL-157` (the bytes seam this qualifies), `D-IMPL-159` (the `as_of=None` residual amendment (2) stops over-generalizing), `D-IMPL-151` and `D-GATE-18` (`B0`, which stays closed on the axes measured), `CLNT-06`, `CLNT-12`.

**D-GATE-19 — Phase 19 (The Client-Seam Integrity Checks Must Be Able to Fail) is APPROVED. `D-IMPL-151` finding `B0` is CLOSED on the axes measured.** APPROVED. Date: 2026-08-20. Approver: Dave. **What is gated.** Eight plans in six waves, 60 commits, `0fe0a22` → `2b97009`, executed and merged directly on `main` (see `D-IMPL-161` for that divergence and its ruling). `make ci` **exit 0** at `cff00ae`: **4013 passed / 118 skipped / 0 failed**, 400 lint-tool, 154 publish/docs, nine examples, `mkdocs build --strict` green, and the three validation gates — empty-operator, lineage strict equality, TTL bounds — all passing. The suite grew 3901 → 4013 (**+112**) across the phase. **`B0` IS CLOSED ON THE AXES MEASURED, AND THE MEASUREMENT IS WHAT CLOSES IT.** The outcome now carries the question the **door** parsed and a content address the **producer** computed; the adapter seam is `ask(WireRequest) -> bytes`, so no adapter constructs the outcome; and a crossed question and an altered vessel are each caught by a **SINGLE-TRANSPORT** client — two assertions, one over `inprocess` and one over `mcp+stdio`, **neither naming a second subject**. That last clause is the ROADMAP's own success sentence and it is the property Phase 18's cross-adapter suite was structurally incapable of proving, because parity between two subjects is blind to a check broken identically on both. The verifier discharged 63/63 plan `must_haves` by **breaking ten properties in an out-of-tree copy and observing 43 control-reds**, plus four direct probes; **controls it could not make fail: none**. `D-GATE-18`'s standing prose constraint is **REPLACED BY A NARROWER TRUE SENTENCE, NOT LIFTED** — see `D-IMPL-156`. **THE `C-17` GATE WAS MADE TO MATCH ITS OWN RULING, IN-TREE.** The §3.1 close review found that the AST gate this phase shipped **did not do what `C-17` ruled it does**: `_outcome_construction_sites` matched only an import-bound `ast.Name` call or an attribute literally spelled `WireOutcome`/`DoorOutcome`, so three in-tree spellings scored **zero** — pydantic construction classmethods, relative imports, and subclassing. Reproduced end-to-end before any fix: an adapter spelling `WireOutcome.model_validate({...})` scored 0, **passed** the gate, passed `mypy --strict`, `ProductClient.ask` **raised nothing**, and the caller received another question's vessel. **`B0` was re-openable in-tree with the entire build green**, and the shipped prose credited a compensating control (`19-04`'s conformance obligation) that is **inert** — the tamper legs measure the *client's* reaction to corruption, never the adapter's honesty, and both pass against a forging adapter. Ruled Option A: **fix the existing gate, test-file only**. After the fix the forger scores 1 and the gate **fails**; relative import 1; subclass 1. The fix derives `_CONSTRUCTING_FORMS = PYDANTIC_MODEL_FORMS - _SERIALIZING_FORMS`, naming only what it **excludes**, so a fourteenth pydantic spelling is counted automatically — a hand-maintained positive list is the drift shape that produced the defect. `git diff --stat b1c40f4..cff00ae -- src runtime` is **empty**. **SUCCESS CRITERIA WERE ABSENT FROM THE ROADMAP FOR THIS PHASE, AND THIS PHASE IS GATED WITHOUT THEM.** `gsd-sdk query roadmap.get-phase 19` returns `success_criteria: []` — the Phase 19 entry has no Success Criteria section at all, so there were no phase-level criteria to verify against. **Dave ruled that they must NOT be authored retroactively**: criteria written after the outcome, to fit what shipped, would be gating against a post-hoc target, and that is the wrong direction for a phase whose entire subject is claims matching code. Phase 19 is therefore gated on **plan `must_haves` plus the verification, panel and review record that actually ran** — `19-VERIFICATION.md` (63/63), `19-CLOSE-REVIEWS.md` (four reviewers), `19-REVIEW.md` (single-agent), `19-CLOSE-FIXES-SUMMARY.md`. **FORWARD-BINDING RULE, RULED HERE:** *Success Criteria must be present in the ROADMAP entry before a phase is executed.* This is recorded so the gap does not become a pattern; the natural homes for enforcement are `CLAUDE.md` §3.1's per-phase verification list and the plan-phase workflow, and amending `CLAUDE.md` is Dave's act, not an executor's (the same boundary `D-IMPL-161` observed). Note also `roadmap-success-criteria-parse-one-per-line`: the parser takes **one entry per line**, so a criterion wrapped for prose width parses as one truth — Phases 15.3 and 15.4 each shipped gated against a single parsed criterion for exactly that reason. Whoever authors criteria for a future phase must confirm the parsed count equals the authored count. **THE §3.1 SEQUENCE WAS FOLLOWED IN ORDER, AND THE ORDER MATTERED.** Execution → cross-AI panel → single-agent review → every finding verified against the tree → blocking findings fixed in-phase → presented to Dave. The panel (codex, cursor, gemini, ollama; `claude` skipped for independence) reviewed the **shipped code**, not the plans, over 202KB of inlined line-numbered source — inlined because Codex's sandbox cannot create user namespaces on this host and would otherwise review nothing at exit 0, which is itself a check that cannot fail, in the review tooling. **Three of four reviewers converged independently** on one finding: `wire.py` claimed an adapter cannot construct the outcome, and it can. Confirmed by an out-of-tree probe; three prose overclaims fixed at `2119ca6`; the structural-unbypassability question deferred as `D-IMPL-162` because it is a different project. **Four panel findings were REJECTED, two of them fabricated citations to files that do not exist.** The single-agent review then found what the panel structurally could not — it had read only client-side source — which is why §3.1 requires both and why neither substitutes for the other. **WHAT THIS PHASE KEPT FINDING WAS ITS OWN DEFECT, ONE LEVEL UP EACH TIME.** `B0` was a comparison that could not disagree. Then **five plan criteria that could not fail** — one satisfiable only by *deleting the paragraph stating the phase's own thesis*, one already green at baseline, one **vacuously** green because the target sentence wrapped across two lines, one requiring an edit to append-only `DECISIONS.md`, one its own plan made unsatisfiable. Then a **gate** that could not fail. Then `F-2` and `F-3`, two checks in the **gating apparatus** that cannot fail. And the orchestrator's own first probe of the panel's finding was **vacuous** — its attack leg and control produced byte-identical subjects — caught, discarded, rebuilt, and recorded rather than hidden. **None of it was found by running the suite, which was green throughout.** All of it was found by sabotaging a property and watching for red, which is the only method that distinguishes a check that works from a check that merely passes. Every executor also found its own plan measurably wrong and said so rather than conforming silently. **CARRIED, NOT REOPENED — none blocks this gate.** `F-1` is ruled above. **`F-2`** — `gsd-sdk query verify.key-links` **can never pass**: it reports `Invalid regex pattern` for any pattern containing an escaped paren and marks the link `verified: false` **without running it**, affecting 6 of this phase's 12 links (all six checked by hand; all six hold). **`F-3`** — the citation lint **silently drops citations with ambiguous basenames**, so a stale citation survives every gate; the adjacency sweep hand-resolved all 16 dropped citations across 8 ambiguous basenames, the **two this phase introduced are fixed** at `cf47bf8`, one other (`product.py:330`) is stale and predates the phase, and the structural hole **remains open**. **`WR-04`** — `runtime/ccf_runtime/mcp/egress.py` names `asked_at` as the single-copy axis where whitepaper §6.3 has **four** (`subject`, `intent`, `freshness`, `asked_at`) and `WireRequest` echoes three fields; deferred because correcting it **widens `C-10`'s undetected list**, which `D-IMPL-156` records as deliberately cross-checked at four items across two records — a claim change requiring a ruling, not a correction absorbed into a fix pass. It is **not** claimed that altering those axes in transit is exploitable, only that the prose and the mechanism disagree and the gap is unrecorded. **Governs:** the Phase 19 approval; the reading of `B0` as closed; the absence of Success Criteria for this phase and the forward-binding requirement that future phases carry them. **Related:** `D-IMPL-151` and `D-GATE-18` (the deferral this closes and the reservation it discharges), `D-IMPL-156` … `D-IMPL-162` (this phase's rulings), `D-IMPL-154`/`D-IMPL-155` (the tooling-hazard discipline `F-2` and `F-3` continue), `D-GATE-18.1`.
**D-IMPL-170 — a one-shot mutation probe recorded in a plan SUMMARY does NOT discharge `CLNT-12`; a gate's sabotage control must be a standing test that can still go red.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-08-21. Approver: Dave (ruling given at the Phase 20 close, in answer to close-panel finding `B-3`). **The ruling, in Dave's words:** *"A control is something the suite can still run and that can still go red. A narrative measurement in a SUMMARY is evidence that someone looked once; it is not enforcement. This phase's own standard (and the project's repeated defect class) is that a check which cannot fail is not a check."* The required shape is a standing test — or an explicitly named sabotage control in the test tree — that is observably red when the property is broken, and *"not solely a paragraph in a plan SUMMARY."* Where a property is not worth a standing test, the claim is dropped or narrowed rather than left with *"a SUMMARY probe wearing a control's clothes."* **What raised it.** Phase 20's three runner gates — `marker_violations`, `payload_violations` and `compare_addresses` in `examples/hw1-harness-clients/runner/drive.py` — carried `CONTROL A`-`F` as one-shot probes recorded as a RED→GREEN table in `20-03-SUMMARY.md`. No test imported, called or probed any of the three. The close panel's `B-1` is the direct cost: the guard compared whole WORDS while the reader matched raw SUBSTRINGS, so a row named `product`, `text` or `ntex` was accepted as a payload marker and then satisfied by chrome alone — an address-only leg passing the check written to refuse it. A standing control over `marker_violations` would have been positioned to see it; a SUMMARY table from a prior plan could not. **Discharged by** `tests/examples/test_hw1_harness_clients_runner_gates.py`, which carries `CONTROL 1`-`9b` plus the `B-1` and `CR-01` regressions, each verified red under deliberate sabotage of the property it guards. **Governs:** every future gate added under `CLNT-12`; the reading of a SUMMARY control table as evidence rather than as enforcement. **Related:** `CLNT-12`, `D-GATE-20`, and the close-panel record at `.planning/phases/20-client-access-from-three-harnesses-adk-anthropic-agent-sdk-a/20-CLOSE-REVIEWS.md` (`B-3`) and `20-REVIEW.md` (`CR-01`, `CR-02`).
**D-GATE-20 — Phase 20 (Client Access from Three Harnesses: ADK, Anthropic Agent SDK, LangGraph) is APPROVED.** APPROVED. Date: 2026-08-21. Approver: Dave. **What is gated.** Eight plans, 51 commits, `9e4bd0e` → `921e3b9`, executed on branch `phase-20` and merged to `main` at this entry per `CLAUDE.md` §2.2. Three agents, each built in a different third-party harness, reach the same Context Product through the Phase 18.1 MCP door as an ordinary registered tool. **The harness is the variable and the product is the constant, and that is the sentence the phase had to make true.** CI run `32534167036` at `921e3b9` is **green on all four jobs**; the suite collects **4223 tests**, and `tests/examples` alone is **478 passed / 37 skipped**. **SUCCESS CRITERIA WERE PRESENT IN THE ROADMAP BEFORE EXECUTION, WHICH IS THE FORWARD-BINDING RULE `D-GATE-19` MINTED BEING HONOURED AT THE FIRST OPPORTUNITY TO BREAK IT.** `gsd-sdk query roadmap.get-phase 20` returns ten criteria, authored at planning, one per line and therefore ten parsed truths rather than one wrapped one — the hazard `roadmap-success-criteria-parse-one-per-line` records, and the reason Phases 15.3 and 15.4 each shipped gated against a single parsed criterion. **Criterion 7 is asserted mechanically and it holds:** `git diff --stat 9e4bd0e..HEAD -- src/ccf/client/` prints nothing, and so does the same diff over the whole of `src/` — **no new SDK mechanism shipped, no transport, no adapter, no `HarnessAdapterProtocol` implementation.** The diff base is pinned in `.planning/phases/20-*/20-BASE-COMMIT.txt` rather than resolved from a branch name at close time, because a base that does not resolve makes the assertion vacuous instead of failing it. **FIVE BLOCKING FINDINGS WERE FOUND AT CLOSE AND ALL FIVE ARE FIXED IN-PHASE, EACH WITH A STANDING CONTROL WATCHED GO RED.** The close-time cross-AI panel (gemini, codex, cursor; `claude` skipped for §3.1 independence) read the **shipped tree** over 5,889 inlined lines, was handed the phase's three known defect classes and told not to re-derive them — and returned `B-1`, `B-2`, `B-3`. `B-1`: `marker_violations` compared whole lowercased **words** while `observed_markers` matched raw **substrings**, so a declared name of `product`, `text` or `ntex` was accepted by the guard and then satisfied by console chrome alone — **an address-only leg passing the very check written to refuse it**, proven by running the shipped functions against doctored stdout. `B-2`: the `CINV-01a` destination arm followed only the **positional** env default, so `default=` as a keyword escaped it. `B-3`: the three runner checks carrying Criteria 1-4 had **no standing sabotage control** — only a one-shot RED→GREEN table in `20-03-SUMMARY.md`, which is ruled insufficient at `D-IMPL-170`. The additive single-agent review then found what the panel structurally could not, having been briefed to spend its budget on what is *adjacent* to each known defect: `CR-01`, `--live` failed by construction on every leg and blamed the client for it; `CR-02`, the destination arm's "follows the value to the sink" contract failed for at least eleven spellings and the `B-2` fix did not close them. Fixed at `08826ba` (`B-1`/`CR-01`), `86142a0` (`B-2`/`CR-02`) and `ad3edb0` (`B-3`, the standing controls). **THE PANEL'S FINDINGS WERE VERIFIED AGAINST THE TREE BEFORE BEING RECORDED, AND FOUR WERE REJECTED AS FALSE.** Three findings were confirmed by running the shipped code against doctored inputs, three by reading, and `R-1`..`R-4` are recorded **as rejected** rather than quietly dropped — including three reviewers' independent clean bills on the purity and no-model gates, which the executing model did not accept as clearance. The orchestrator's own first `CR-02` probe was **wrong** — it asserted an instruction sink that does not exist and reported the control case as escaping — and was discarded and rebuilt rather than hidden. **TWO PRE-EXISTING CI FAILURES WERE FOUND WHILE CLOSING AND FIXED HERE.** The `tests` job ran on a shallow clone, so a pinned base commit did not resolve and the assertions reading it could not run; fixed with `fetch-depth: 0` at `921e3b9`. And `docs/surface/examples/RETIREMENT-COUPLINGS.md` is **generated** and walks `.planning/`, so the docs gate had been red since `7f59289` — every planning commit invalidates it, and it must be regenerated **last** in a mixed pass because code edits shift its rows too (`499cca3`). This is recorded because it is a standing trap for the next phase, not a Phase 20 defect. **CARRIED, NOT REOPENED — none blocks this gate.** Four panel advisories (`A-1` the destination arm's finding message claiming a length-independence the code lacks; `A-2` `model_stub.py`'s write-only `seen`; `A-3` `reference_run`'s subprocess having no timeout while the leg's does; `A-4` a leg timeout leaving the door grandchild unreaped) and **nine** single-agent warnings `WR-01`..`WR-09` — note the review's own frontmatter says `warning: 8` and **undercounts by one**. Of these, `WR-08` continues the standing tooling hazard `D-IMPL-155`/`F-3` carried at `D-GATE-19`: this phase made three client filenames **ambiguous basenames**, and the citation gate drops ambiguous citations **silently**, so a stale citation survives every gate. **Requirement ledger:** `CLNT-23`..`CLNT-32` are all **Complete** and match the tree; the ledger's other 52 `Pending` rows belong to earlier phases and are **not** discharged by this gate — Phase 16's eighteen are genuinely undischarged against a **retired** approach (`D-IMPL-152`), and the remainder are unreconciled bookkeeping against gated phases.
