Reconciling them is owed before v0.2 can honestly close, and this entry records that it is owed rather than absorbing it. **Governs:** the Phase 20 approval; the merge of `phase-20` to `main`; the reading of Criteria 1-10 as met. **Related:** `D-IMPL-163` … `D-IMPL-166` and `D-IMPL-170` (this phase's rulings), `D-GATE-19` (the forward-binding Success-Criteria rule this phase is the first to honour), `D-IMPL-154`/`D-IMPL-155` (the tooling hazards `WR-08` continues), and the review record at `.planning/phases/20-client-access-from-three-harnesses-adk-anthropic-agent-sdk-a/20-CLOSE-REVIEWS.md` and `20-REVIEW.md`.
**D-IMPL-171 — the ten phases with no `D-GATE` entry are gated by their ROADMAP completion rows; the gap is RECORDED HERE ONCE AND NOT BACKFILLED.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-08-21. Approver: Dave. **What was found.** `CLAUDE.md` §3.1 step 4 requires every phase to end with an approval logged as a `D-GATE-<Phase>` entry. Measured 2026-08-21 by `grep -o "^\*\*D-GATE-[0-9A-Za-z.]*" docs/DECISIONS.md`: entries exist for `D-GATE-R`, `D-GATE-D`, `D-GATE-F`, `D-GATE-I` through `D-GATE-I.4.1`, and then from `D-GATE-15` onward — **but not for Phases 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 13.1, 13.2, 13.3, 14 or 16.** All ten carry a "Complete" row in `.planning/ROADMAP.md`'s progress table with an approval date (Phase 16's row reads RETIRED, `D-IMPL-152`); none carries a gate entry. The convention was applied consistently only from Phase 15, and these ten predate that. **The ruling.** The ten phases are **gated by their ROADMAP completion rows**, which is the record that actually exists for them, and **no gate entry is backfilled**. Dave's reasoning: writing ten gate entries now would be authoring gates *after* the outcome, to fit what shipped — the same direction `D-GATE-19` refused when it ruled that Phase 19's absent Success Criteria must **not** be written retroactively. A reconstructed gate reads exactly like a contemporaneous one and a later reader cannot tell them apart, which makes the backfill worse than the gap it closes. The gap is therefore stated **once, here, in the open**, rather than papered over with ten plausible entries. **What this ruling does NOT do.** It does not certify those ten phases' *requirements* as discharged — that is a separate debt, and it is the subject of the reconciliation phase Dave commissioned at the same sitting. It does not lift `CLAUDE.md` §3.1 for any future phase: from Phase 15 onward every phase has a gate entry and every future phase must have one. It does not rule on Phase 16's eighteen orphaned `DOCS-` requirements, which Dave deferred until the audit reports the split between already-satisfied and genuinely orphaned. **Governs:** the absence of `D-GATE-9`, `-10`, `-11`, `-12`, `-13`, `-13.1`, `-13.2`, `-13.3`, `-14` and `-16`; how a reader of this log should interpret that absence. **Related:** `D-GATE-19` (the retroactive-authorship refusal this reasoning follows), `D-GATE-20` (which records the ledger debt this ruling's sibling addresses), `D-IMPL-152` (Phase 16's retirement).
**D-IMPL-172 — criterion 3's `path::symbol` binds as a READING, not as a literal form; the operative clause is the criterion's own final one, “that the citation lint resolves.”** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-08-21. Approver: Dave (ruled at the Phase 21 planning sitting, after research and before any plan was written; recorded in `21-CONTEXT.md` as `D-17`). **What was asked.** Phase 21's Success Criterion 3 requires each of the 54 not-`Complete` requirement rows to carry evidence in `path::symbol` form. The research pass measured whether that form is even expressible for every row, and it is not. **The forcing fact, measured in the tree.** `tools/lints/citations.py` anchors its `NODE_ID` pattern's path group to `\.py` — `(?P<path>[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_./+-]*\.py)::(?P<symbol>[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)`. There is no `::symbol` form for any other suffix, so a markdown document has no `path::symbol` citation at all; a `docs/foo.md::heading` matches neither citation regex and is invisible to the lint. Roughly 24 of the 54 rows are about documentation. A literal reading of criterion 3 would therefore be unsatisfiable for nearly half the working set, not because the evidence is missing but because the form does not exist. **The ruling.** `path::symbol` binds as a reading: the criterion's operative clause is its own final one — *a citation the lint resolves*. `path::symbol` stays the PREFERRED form and is REQUIRED wherever the evidence is Python. Where the evidence is a document, an anchored line citation that the lint resolves is admissible. **This is a reading, NOT a relaxation granted to make the criterion reachable**, and the plan, the standing check's docstring and the phase record all say so in those words, because a later reader will otherwise reconstruct it as the criterion being softened to fit what shipped. The distinction is real: the citation still has to resolve, and the machinery that resolves it is the machinery that already ships. **What is unchanged.** `D-06` still binds in full: a citation in a requirement row is a FULL repo-relative path, and a bare basename is REFUSED by the standing check `tools/docs_tests/test_requirement_ledger.py` lands, whether or not that basename happens to be unique today. `D-07` is unchanged too — the citation lint is NAMED, not fixed, in this phase. **Governs:** what evidence form each of the 54 rows may carry; how `refuse_unresolvable` treats a `::` citation whose path is not `.py` (it refuses it by name, because the lint would never see it). **Related:** `D-IMPL-155` and `WR-08` (the ambiguous-basename hazard this reading deliberately does not touch), `D-IMPL-173`, `D-IMPL-174`.
**D-IMPL-173 — `CPS-03` takes the verdict `Complete as ruled`, citing `D-IMPL-113` AND `D-IMPL-121`; the verdict vocabulary stays at six words and no seventh is minted.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-08-21. Approver: Dave (ruled at the Phase 21 planning sitting; recorded in `21-CONTEXT.md` as `D-18`). **What was asked.** `CPS-03`'s traceability row reads `**Pending**`, and its evidence entry in the same document already reads *“Pending by design (`D-IMPL-113` and `D-IMPL-121`)”*. The audit needs a verdict from the fixed vocabulary, and “pending by design” is not one of the six words. The question was whether to mint a seventh verdict for the shape *closed by a recorded ruling rather than open by omission*. **The ruling.** No seventh word. `CPS-03` takes **`Complete as ruled`**, and its status cell names **both** `D-IMPL-113` and `D-IMPL-121` — both, per `D-IMPL-113`'s own instruction that the row must say which, or an unmet requirement reads as an oversight. **Why the existing word fits.** `DCD-09` already carries `Complete as ruled` for exactly this shape: descoped against a recorded ruling, with the reason travelling alongside the requirement. Minting a seventh verdict to describe a case the sixth already describes would grow the vocabulary that `D-09` fixed, and `D-09` fixed it precisely so that a strict scheme could not re-open `DCD-02`, `DCD-09` and `DCD-10`, which Dave has already ruled on. **The constraint on the wording.** The row's status cell must carry the *by design, not by omission* clause, so `Complete as ruled` is not read as a claim that enforcement shipped. Declaration and both request-time refusals do ship and are tested; calling them is the adopter's obligation, stated at both resolver seams. **Governs:** `CPS-03`'s verdict in `.planning/REQUIREMENTS.md`, written in plan `21-03`; the vocabulary membership check in `tools/docs_tests/test_requirement_ledger.py`, whose `VERDICT_VOCABULARY` therefore admits exactly `Complete`, `Complete as ruled`, `Complete over the ruled scope`, `Partial`, `Not built`, `Orphaned` (plus `Pending` while the phase is in flight). **Related:** `D-IMPL-113`, `D-IMPL-121`, `D-IMPL-122` (the `DCD-09` precedent), `D-IMPL-172`, `D-IMPL-174`.
**D-IMPL-174 — the three stale counters are CORRECTED in this phase, not merely reported, under three named constraints.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-08-21. Approver: Dave (ruled at the Phase 21 planning sitting; recorded in `21-CONTEXT.md` as `D-19`). **What was found.** The research pass's strict parse of `.planning/REQUIREMENTS.md` exposed three counters that no longer describe the documents they sit in. (1) `.planning/REQUIREMENTS.md`'s *“Coverage: 94/94 v0.2 requirements mapped”* sentence — cited BY CONTENT rather than by line, deliberately: it sat at `:423` at this phase's pinned base, and plan `21-01` task 2 inserts ten checkbox bullets and ten table rows above it, moving it by roughly eleven lines before the plan ends. (2) `.planning/ROADMAP.md` **§ Coverage**'s *“All 42 v0.2 requirements mapped”* — cited BY SECTION and never by line: the counter sat at `:1946` when this was ruled and at `:1959` once the Phase 21 plans were committed, and `docs/DECISIONS.md` is exempt from the citation lint, so nothing in the toolchain would ever catch that drift. If a line number is wanted at all, re-resolve it at write time by searching for the sentence. That drift, inside the ruling about drift, is the hazard this phase exists to name. (3) The ROADMAP's Phase 21 entry, which says **54** not-`Complete` rows and *“each of the 52 gets a verdict”* in the same paragraph — at `:47` and again in the phase body at `:1888` and `:1890`. The commissioning prose disagrees with the criterion it commissioned. **The ruling: corrected, not merely reported**, under three constraints, all binding. (a) **Replacement figures are produced by the strict parse and never assumed.** 133 is the traceability table's row count at the pinned base and is not automatically the right number for a sentence about *v0.2 requirements mapped*, which may be a defined subset; where the parse cannot settle what a counter is counting, the counter is REPORTED rather than guessed, and the phase record says that is what happened. (b) **Every edit is a hand-edit under `D-15`**, with a backup taken first and a diff showing insertions only, or the intended replacement and nothing else — no `gsd-sdk query state.*` or `roadmap.*` writer touches either file. (c) **The phase record names each correction and its old value**, because a phase about honest counters that silently edits three counters would be its own defect one level up. **Adjacent and NOT covered by this ruling.** `DEMO-03`'s re-homing note points at `public/tutorial/hello-ccf.md`, which is not in the tree. That row is ticked and sits OUTSIDE the 54. It is reported as an observation and is not flipped. **Governs:** plan `21-05`'s three counter corrections and `RECON-10`; what the phase record must state about each. **Related:** `D-IMPL-154` and `D-IMPL-155` (the GSD writers that corrupt these two files, which is why `D-15` mandates hand-edits), `D-IMPL-172`, `D-IMPL-173`.
**D-IMPL-175 — Phase 16's eighteen `DOCS-` rows take the split's proposed verdicts AS WRITTEN; `DOCS-18` limb 1 stays closed and is not to be re-opened.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-08-22. Approver: Dave (Ruling 1 at the `D-GATE-21` sitting). **What was asked.** At the Phase 20 close Dave deferred Phase 16's eighteen orphaned `DOCS-` rows in three words — *"tell me after the audit"* — and `D-12` bound the audit to report the split and to flip nothing. Plan `21-04` produced `.planning/phases/21-requirement-ledger-reconciliation-what-is-actually-discharge/21-DOCS-16-SPLIT.md`: one section per row, evidence on both sides, a proposed verdict per row, and seven ruling questions. **The ruling, verbatim:** *"Accept the proposed verdicts as written."* **Complete** — `DOCS-07`, `-08`, `-09`, `-16`, `-19`, `-20`, `-21`, `-23`, `-24`, `-25` (ten). **Partial**, each limb named — `DOCS-10`, `-11`, `-12`, `-13`, `-18` (five). **Not built** — `DOCS-14`, `-15`, `-17` (three). **Zero wholly `Orphaned`.** *"All eighteen ids remain in both ledger channels. Nothing flipped without evidence."* **`DOCS-18` limb 1 — the one orphaned limb — stays closed.** Dave's words: *"Orphaned by your own D-IMPL-96. **Stays closed.** Do not re-open."* The limb is Phase 16's no-fabric-change assertion; `D-IMPL-96` revoked criterion 10 in Dave's own words — *"it has been used out of context"* — taking `D-13`'s enumerated exception and `gate_16.py` with it, and `tools/gates/` holds no module today, only a stale `__pycache__`. The ledger cell names that limb `ORPHANED` so a later reader does not open it as work. **Why the orphan side is thin, which is the finding rather than a failure of the audit.** `.planning/RETIRED.md` retires the APPROACH and not the NEED, so an obligation about a need survives the rejection of the approach that was to satisfy it. Eight rows had real work the ledger never recorded: `DOCS-19`..`-21` and `DOCS-23`..`-25` shipped in Phase 16's own post-stop plans, and `DOCS-13`'s three harness legs shipped in **Phase 20**, gated harder than the row asked. **Governs:** the eighteen verdicts standing in `.planning/REQUIREMENTS.md`; that `DOCS-18` limb 1 is not re-opened as work. **Related:** `D-IMPL-96` (the revocation that orphaned the limb), `D-IMPL-152` (Phase 16's retirement), `D-GATE-20` (where the deferral was made), `D-GATE-21`, and the split at `21-DOCS-16-SPLIT.md`.
**D-IMPL-176 — all five `Not built` rows stay on the work list; the knot is sequenced; and `s3-` is NOT a required naming scheme because Phase 16 is not resumable.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-08-22. Do not drop any in this gate."* **The sequencing, in Dave's four numbered points.** (1) ***"DOCS-15 first"*** *(when you take the list up) — cheapest, highest adoption leverage, one page, subject already gated in `s1-01`. Only coupling is that tree's survival under CLNT-17.* (2) ***"Replacements before removals"*** *— DOCS-14 / EXAM-02 substance must exist* **before** *DOCS-17 / CLNT-17 delete the trees that currently hold skilling, HITL, cross-process, and `refuse_request` witnesses. Quarantine stands until you explicitly choose delete-and-re-cut vs keep-quarantined."* (4) **THE NEW RULING NOBODY HAD LOGGED — Section-3 naming is freed.** *"**do not keep `s3-` as a required scheme.** Phase 16 is not resumable. Re-derive the demonstration against today's surface under whatever directory name fits; the obligation is the content, not the old section label."* This settles the second of the two questions plan `21-04` returned as Dave's alone; before this entry, `EXAM-02` and `DOCS-14` were both judged against a named home (`examples/s3-02-agentic-skills`) whose absence was the measured basis of their `Not built` verdicts. Those verdicts stand — the substance is genuinely absent — but a future phase discharging them is **not** obliged to build under an `s3-` directory, and a later reader must not reconstruct the section scheme as binding from the verdict cells. **And one workstream, not four.** *"Published-pages limb across DOCS-12/13/14/15 is* **one documentation workstream**, *not four independent pages projects — plan it as one surface for the examples that actually shipped."* The audit had already measured that those four rows are short by the same thing. **Governs:** the ordering of any future phase that takes the work list up; that no `Not built` row is dropped at this gate; that `s3-` is not a required directory scheme; that the `00`–`08` half of `D-27` stays undecided and quarantined. **Related:** `D-IMPL-145` limb 2 (the quarantine), `D-27` (partial retirement forbidden; its `00`–`08` half still open), `D-25`/`D-26`, `D-IMPL-175`, `D-GATE-21`, and the work list at `21-FINDINGS.md` §2.
**D-IMPL-177 — "v0.2 requirements" in the ROADMAP's §Coverage sentence means the milestone-definition set plus what inserted phases minted through 15.1: the 42 the breakdown already enumerates, NOT the 143-row traceability table.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-08-22. Approver: Dave (Ruling 3 at the `D-GATE-21` sitting). **What was found.** `D-IMPL-174` required three stale counters to be CORRECTED rather than reported, under constraint (a) that a counter the strict parse cannot settle is reported and never guessed. Two were corrected in plan `21-05`. The third could not be: `.planning/ROADMAP.md` §Coverage reads *"All **42** v0.2 requirements mapped, each to exactly one phase — the figure `.planning/REQUIREMENTS.md`'s traceability table carries, counted from it rather than remembered."* **The sentence describes itself two incompatible ways.** Its first clause claims to be the traceability table's row count, which is **143** today and was never 42 — the table held 56 rows even before Phase 16's minting. The two paragraphs immediately beneath it enumerate the figure as **21 + 21**: the 21 defined at milestone definition (2026-08-01) plus the 21 minted by inserted phases through Phase 15.1, internally consistent, summing to exactly 42, and followed by a line saying outright that *"Phase 16 mints its own (DOCS-07..NN) at planning and is **not yet counted above**."* A parse cannot settle which the sentence means; settling it is a milestone-scope question. **The ruling, verbatim:** *"**'v0.2 requirements' for that ROADMAP sentence means the milestone-definition set plus what inserted phases minted through 15.1 (the 42 that the breakdown already enumerates).** It is **not** the whole traceability table (143)."* Dave's three reasons, verbatim: *"The breakdown under the sentence is internally consistent (21 + 21 = 42) and explicitly excluded Phase 16+. Replacing 42 with 143 without rewriting the breakdown would make the next line false. Correct the descriptive clause so it no longer claims 'the figure the traceability table carries'; say it is the milestone-scoped count through 15.1. Leave the number 42 unless you later redefine milestone scope."* And: *"D-19 was right to report rather than guess; this ruling makes the sentence correctable in one line."* **What was done under this entry.** A ONE-LINE correction at the site: the number **42 is unchanged**, the descriptive clause no longer claims to be the traceability table's row count and now names the milestone-scoped set through Phase 15.1, and the wave-5 marker recording the counter as unsettleable is REMOVED, because it is now settled. Hand-edited under `D-15` with a backup outside the tree and a diff. **`RECON-10` is not amended by this entry.** Its verdict is taken against its own text — *the three counters are CORRECTED* — as that text stood while the phase ran, and at that time the third was correctly reported rather than guessed. The row stays `Partial` with its outstanding limb named; this ruling is what a future phase would cite to close it, and closing it is not this gate's business. **Governs:** the reading of `All **42**` in `.planning/ROADMAP.md` §Coverage; that the number stays 42 until milestone scope is redefined. **Related:** `D-IMPL-174` (constraint (a), which produced the report rather than a guess), `D-IMPL-175`, `D-IMPL-176`, `D-GATE-21`.
**D-GATE-21 — Phase 21 (Requirement Ledger Reconciliation: What Is Actually Discharged) is APPROVED.** APPROVED. Date: 2026-08-22. Approver: Dave. **What is gated.** Seven plans, seven serial waves, executed on branch `phase-21` from the base pinned at `c51406b` and merged to `main` at this entry per `CLAUDE.md` §2.2. **The phase FOUND and RECORDED; it built nothing** — `git diff --stat c51406b..HEAD` over `src/`, `runtime/`, `examples/`, `public/`, `tests/` and `pyproject.toml` prints nothing on every path, and `tools/lints/citations.py` and all eleven `human_verification` records are byte-identical too. **All fifty-four not-`Complete` rows now carry a verdict in both status channels: 38 `Complete`, 2 `Complete as ruled`, 9 `Partial`, 5 `Not built`, 0 `Orphaned`** — counted by a STRICT parse and by MEMBERSHIP against the Complete family, never by a string inequality, which is the miscount the phase exists over: `grep -c "| Pending |"` reports 52 because two cells are bolded, and `grep -vc "| Complete |"` reports 56 because it drags in `DCD-09` and `DCD-10`, both already ruled. Dave's own summary of the result: *"Two-thirds of the 'outstanding' debt was already shipped and never ticked. That is a real result."* **THE PHASE'S OWN TEN `RECON-` ROWS WERE MINTED IN WAVE 1 AND VERDICTED IN WAVE 6, BEFORE THE CLOSE PANEL** — never inside the gate checkpoint — so the ledger the panel read and the ledger Dave approved are the same document, verified byte-identical at `773775a`. Rows entering a ledger carrying verdicts no reviewer and no approver had seen would have been this phase's own subject one level up. **CRITERION 14 IS THIS ENTRY, AND `RECON-09` CLOSES ON IT.** `RECON-09` read `Partial` through the whole of execution because its outstanding limb was `D-GATE-21` itself; it is amended to `Complete` in both channels under this entry and not before, which is the difference between a verdict and a hope. **THREE BLOCKING FINDINGS WERE FOUND AT CLOSE AND ALL THREE ARE FIXED IN-PHASE, EACH WITH A STANDING CONTROL WATCHED GO RED.** The cross-AI panel (gemini, codex, cursor; `claude` skipped for §3.1 independence) read the **shipped artifacts** — 182 KB inlined: the whole of `tools/docs_tests/test_requirement_ledger.py`, all 143 traceability rows with their real file line numbers, and `21-FINDINGS.md` — was briefed on the phase's five known defects and told not to re-derive them, and **two reviewers independently walked into the same two holes, both of them this project's defect class inside this phase's own machinery.** `B-1`: `git diff --stat <base>..HEAD -- scr/` exits ZERO and prints NOTHING, so a one-key typo in `FABRIC`, `FENCE`, `UAT_RECORDS`, `PINNED_FILES` or `TESTS_TREE` made its emptiness assertion vacuous — and `CONTROL A` and `CONTROL 13` could not see it because **both diff `CHANGED_TREE`, never the constant they vouch for**; `CONTROL 13` is named `a_changed_tests_tree_would_be_detected` and never mentions `tests/`. Proven both ways: `TESTS_TREE → tests-typo/` is **45 passed, all green** against the wave-6 module and **2 failed** against the fix, one of the two being criterion 6's own assertion. Closed by a fourth refusal in `fabric_diff` via `tracked_under`, with `CONTROL 16` on four NEAR-MISS spellings and a positive twin. `B-2`: **no standing check required a verdicted row to carry a citation at all** — `refuse_unresolvable` answers *given a citation, does it resolve*, plus one GLOBAL floor that some citation exists somewhere, so a row reading `**Complete** — asserted without evidence` returned `[]` from every checker in the module, measured. **That is how `DCD-02` survived five waves**, found in wave 6 only by running criterion 3's predicate by hand. Closed by `uncited_verdicts` with `CONTROL 17` (green-before/red-after) and `CONTROL 17b` (the SAME cell must PASS as `Not built` and FAIL as `Complete`, so `D-10`'s named-absence carve-out survives and the rule is not red-on-everything); ROSTER-SCOPED, because 79 rows outside the working set carry the same pre-existing debt under `D-IMPL-174`'s carve-out and a ledger-wide form would be red on landing for rows `D-11` forbids touching. `B-3`: the `DOCS-06`/`DOCS-08` unguarded-`ci`-composition gap was handed by plan `21-03` to plan `21-05`, reached the ledger cells and one SUMMARY, and **never reached `21-FINDINGS.md`, the document Dave rules from** — `D-IMPL-170`'s prohibition exactly. RECORDED in §5, **not closed**, because closing it means a test that reads the `Makefile`, which is building (`D-11`). **THREE FINDINGS WERE REJECTED AND ARE RECORDED AS REJECTED, WITH THE EVIDENCE THAT REFUTES THEM.** `R-1` (codex, *"the module never verifies a cited symbol"*) is false at the repo level — `.planning/REQUIREMENTS.md` is in the citation lint's `GATED_TREES` with no exemption, and `check_source` returns `cite03-node-id` on a missing symbol, measured. `R-2` (gemini, *"`fabric_diff` is blind to the working tree"*) is true, documented in the function itself, known since wave 1, and not a defect: the claim is about what the phase COMMITTED. `R-3` (gemini, *"the gate is blind to new `Pending` rows"*) reproduces but is INTENDED and documented — a gate refusing `Pending` would be red the moment the next phase is planned. **SEVEN ADVISORIES ARE CARRIED AND DAVE RULED NO ACTION AT GATE:** `A-1` (nothing prevents a FUTURE ledger accumulating unverdicted rows the way these 54 did — a staleness-policy question), `A-2`, `A-3`, `A-4`, `A-5` (79 pre-existing uncited Completes outside the working set), `A-6`/`A-8` (unguarded limbs; the 28 uppercase `**COMPLETE**` spellings this phase added to the checkbox channel, 8 → 36, none in the table the vocabulary gate reads), `A-7` (`_table_line` is non-unique for all fourteen `CPS-` rows because the CPS-lane evidence table is a THIRD status channel no gate reads). Two of the eight came from the additive single-agent review alone; neither is derivable by reading. **THE STANDING MACHINERY THIS PHASE LEAVES BEHIND.** `tools/docs_tests/test_requirement_ledger.py`, 51 tests, reached by `gate-tools` → `ci-core` → `ci` with nothing else to wire: a citation in a status cell must be a full repo-relative path that EXISTS as written (dodging the citation lint's two silent-drop holes from the outside without opening the lint, `D-07`); the two status channels must agree id-for-id on every id the ledger contains; the verdict vocabulary is six words and no seventh; one verdict per cell; every member of a FROZEN ROSTER OF NAMED IDS re-derived from the pinned base and compared ID FOR ID must carry exactly one verdict and none may read a bare `Pending`; every verdicted roster row must cite something; `tests/` must be byte-identical to the base; and every asserted pathspec must name a tracked subject. **Per `D-21` (the phase's own context ruling), NO standing check in this module carries a hardcoded row count** — verified, the guard returns 0 matches — because the phase's own first action, minting ten rows, falsified the criterion that did. Seventeen numbered controls plus positive twins, every one watched RED under a mutation of the SHIPPED function and restored from a backup taken first. **CI at the merge commit: `make ci` exit 0 on all six legs** — `lint` 0, `typecheck` 0 (211 source files), `test` 0 (**4105 passed / 118 skipped**, byte-for-byte the wave-1-through-6 baseline, which is the mechanical proof `D-05` held and that no test was written to manufacture a citation), `gate-tools` 0 (406 + 205, up from 406 + 154 at the phase's start), `examples` 0 (three harness legs, one content address), `docs-strict` 0. **THE VERIFICATION DEBT IS NAMED, NOT DISCHARGED.** All **27** `human_needed` items across **11** phase records are quoted verbatim in `21-FINDINGS.md` §3 and held untouched by a standing diff over all eleven paths. `gsd-sdk query audit-uat` reports 24 across 9 because it FILTERS ON FRONTMATTER `status:`, dropping Phase 12 (`status: passed`) and Phase 18 (`status: gaps_found`) — the phase's own subject arriving a third time, in a third tool. That filter is NAMED, NOT FIXED (`D-20`), on `D-07`'s reasoning: tooling repair inside an audit stops it being an audit. At the discuss sitting Dave chose *"out, name them"* over a separate phase, so none is commissioned. **WHAT THIS GATE DOES NOT DO.** It does not discharge the 79 uncited Complete-family rows outside the working set, nor the five `Not built` rows (`D-IMPL-176` keeps all five on the work list and sequences them), nor `DOCS-18` limb 1 (`D-IMPL-175`: stays closed), nor `RECON-10`'s outstanding limb, nor any of the 27 human items. Each is stated rather than absorbed. **Governs:** the Phase 21 approval; the merge of `phase-21` to `main`; the reading of all fourteen Success Criteria as met; the `RECON-09` `Partial` → `Complete` amendment. **Related:** `D-IMPL-172`, `D-IMPL-173`, `D-IMPL-174` (this phase's planning rulings), `D-IMPL-175`, `D-IMPL-176`, `D-IMPL-177` (this sitting's three rulings), `D-IMPL-170` (a control is a standing test, never a SUMMARY probe — the bar `B-3` was measured against), `D-IMPL-171` (the ten ungated phases, whose requirement debt this phase addressed without backfilling their gates), `D-GATE-20` (which recorded this debt as owed), and the review record at `.planning/phases/21-requirement-ledger-reconciliation-what-is-actually-discharge/21-CLOSE-REVIEWS.md`.

**D-IMPL-178 — the cross-AI panel is DEFINED as the set of available external AI reviewers with the executing model excluded, and at close time its payload is the committed tree however it is invoked; a hand-assembled close-time payload is conforming, not a deviation.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-08-22. Approver: Dave (ruling given immediately after `D-GATE-21`, on the provenance question raised at the Phase 21 close). **What was found.** `CLAUDE.md` §3.1 contained a contradiction that had gone unnoticed across every phase close to date. It says *"`/gsd-review --all` … and nothing else satisfies it"*, naming a command; and it separately says *"when execution has already happened, the panel reviews the shipped code, not the plans."* But `$HOME/.claude/get-shit-done/workflows/review.md` is plan-oriented by construction — its own purpose line reads *"invoke external AI CLIs to independently review phase plans … the same prompt (PROJECT.md context, phase plans, requirements)"*, and its gather step collects `*-PLAN.md`, `*-CONTEXT.md` and `*-RESEARCH.md`. The command's default payload therefore contradicts the close-time requirement in the same section that mandates the command. Plan `21-07` resolved the contradiction in favour of §3.1's *meaning* — it hand-assembled a 182 KB payload of shipped code (the whole of `tools/docs_tests/test_requirement_ledger.py`, all 143 traceability rows with real line numbers, the whole of `21-FINDINGS.md`), invoked gemini, codex and cursor with the workflow's own credentials and model selection, and declared the difference as Deviation 1 in `21-07-SUMMARY.md` rather than concealing it. **Why this ruling.** Accepting the hand-built run without a rule change would leave a standing *"did the official path actually run?"* question at every future close, which is the same class of unfalsifiable claim the whole of Phase 21 exists to eliminate. **The ruling, in three limbs.** (a) The panel IS the external reviewers, executing model excluded for independence — it is not a particular command invocation, and it is discharged by the reviewers having read the right subject. (b) At close, the payload is the committed tree: either `/gsd-review --all` gathers the shipped subjects, or the payload is assembled by hand from those subjects with the three reviewer invocations otherwise following the workflow exactly. Plans remain the pre-execution review target. (c) A hand-assembled close-time payload is conforming and must be recorded as such in the phase record, naming every subject left out of it — plan `21-07` left out `21-DOCS-16-SPLIT.md`, gave it to the additive single-agent pass instead, and said so. **Consequence.** §3.1 is amended in `CLAUDE.md` with the panel definition, the close-time payload rule, and the standing requirement to inline source rather than pass paths (on this host codex's `bwrap` sandbox can fail such that it exits 0 having read nothing; a reviewer whose cited symbols and line numbers do not resolve is recorded as FAILED, not as a reviewer). `D-GATE-21` stays in force; the re-run ordered alongside this ruling is provenance confirmation, and only a NEW blocking finding would open a `21.1` fix wave. Related: `D-GATE-21`, `D-IMPL-170` (a probe written up in a SUMMARY is not a control), `D-IMPL-171`.

**D-IMPL-179 — the three residual rulings at the Phase 21.1 plan gate: `DOCS-22`'s ledger cell IS amended (narrowly), a refusal limb MAY be repaired rather than deleted, and the selector proof stays a per-task verify rather than becoming a standing gate.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-08-22. Approver: Dave (plan-gate sitting, immediately before Wave 1). **Limb 1 — `DOCS-22`'s cell.** Research logged assumption `A1` that the cell could be amended because `DOCS-22` sits outside the 54 and criterion 11 scopes to those 54; plan `21.1-04` correctly refused to act on an assumption and carried it as an OPEN QUESTION. Dave ruled amend, and the reasoning is the binding part: *"Sitting outside the 54 does not make a false or incomplete cell harmless. Criterion 11 may not require it for 21.1's must_haves, but the phase family is about ledger honesty."* Bounded explicitly: ONE cell, in the `DCD-10` status-cell shape, with a citation that RESOLVES and the checkbox tick moved with the verdict — *"Do not widen into a full re-verdict of rows outside the working set."* The other 78 rows carried as advisory `A-5` are untouched. Note the dependency this creates: the amendment's natural citation is a `.planning/` document, which **had no legal spelling at all** until this phase — `CITATION`'s path group excludes a leading dot, so the citation did not survive extraction, and the `::symbol` alternative is refused on a non-Python path. Plan `21.1-03`'s `LOOSE_CITATION` is what makes the ruling executable, so `21.1-04` now halts if it is absent. **Limb 2 — repair over deletion.** Criterion 12 as authored offered two dispositions, *reachable-and-watched* or *unreachable-and-REMOVED*, and needed a third: taking the literal reading would have deleted `base_ledger_text`'s shallow-clone guard, unreachable only because the function took no argument, and guarding a failure this project actually hit at the Phase 20 close. Dave ruled repair permitted: *"Deletion is for unreachable or revoked limbs (e.g. `DOCS-18` limb 1 under `D-IMPL-96`), not for a limb that can be made true."* Consequence noted at the gate and accepted: once repaired, the limb satisfies criterion 12's FIRST disposition outright, so repair-to-reachable is arguably not a third disposition at all. Every repair is recorded in its plan SUMMARY so it cannot be mistaken for silent scope change. **Limb 3 — the selector proof stays per-task.** Seven stale `-k` selectors were found at plan-check that all exited 0 because each matched a real, already-green control; a selector matching NOTHING would have exited 5 and been seen. The fix is a per-task collect-and-grep proof rather than a standing in-module gate, and Dave accepted the weaker form on the fence argument: `.planning/phases/*` sits in `HISTORICAL_RECORDS` in `tools/lints/citations.py`, whose stated policy is that a file whose record discipline forbids correcting it cannot be gated on current-tree truth — such a gate would go permanently red the moment a later phase renumbers plans nobody may edit. Decisive point: selectors exist ONLY in PLAN files, so there is no in-module standing form to choose instead; the module-side half of the concern did land, as the frozen `CONTROLS` roster asserted set-equal to the enumeration. **Consequence.** Wave 1 is authorized. `D-GATE-21` stays parent and untouched; Phase 21.1 closes with its own gate note. Related: `D-GATE-21`, `D-IMPL-178`, `D-IMPL-175`, `D-IMPL-170`.

**D-IMPL-180 — `RR-11` closes in the next module-writing wave (21.1-05) by comparing SPANS rather than path strings, not at wave 9 and not by withholding `.planning/` citations until close.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-08-22. Approver: Dave (wave-4 boundary of Phase 21.1). **What was found.** Plan `21.1-04` was the first to actually USE the `LOOSE_CITATION` pattern that plan `21.1-03` shipped, and discovered that wave 3 had shipped the pattern **and, beside it, a gate that forbids using it for the thing it was built for**. `test_each_widened_pattern_subsumes_the_lint_pattern_it_replaced` computes `set(lint_pairs) - set(widened_pairs)` over PATH STRINGS. Measured on a dotted citation: the lint's `CITATION` matches at offset 17 yielding the truncated twin `planning/ROADMAP.md`, while `LOOSE_CITATION` matches at offset 16 yielding the correct `.planning/ROADMAP.md`. The widened match starts one character EARLIER and covers the lint's span entirely — nothing was corrected away — but as path strings the twin scores as a silent drop, so a dotted citation can never satisfy the gate. **This is failure mode 1 of this phase's own taxonomy — the subject never reached the branch under test — and it took an entire wave to produce a subject.** The check was green in wave 3 only because no dotted citation existed anywhere in the tree. **Why it could not wait.** `VAC-03`'s verdict at plan `21.1-09` requires a `.planning/` citation, so leaving `RR-11` latent until then is ordering debt of exactly the kind this phase family exists to end. Dave rejected three alternatives explicitly: pushing it to wave 9, withholding all `.planning/` citations until close, and widening into a general citation-lint redesign. **The fix shape, ruled.** Subsumption by SPAN CONTAINMENT, with the anti-vacuity clause kept: a widened match that does not cover the lint's span still fails, and an empty widened set still fails. Three properties must hold — a citation whose span covers the lint's span is admissible; truncated-twin path strings alone must not produce a silent drop; a real dotted citation passes while a genuine vacuous or loose misuse still fails. `D-07` is untouched: `tools/lints/citations.py` stays byte-identical and remains the reference the check measures against. **On numbering.** Dave ruled both "use the next free control number" and "control numbers 24+ can stay as allocated"; those conflict, because the literal next free number is 24 and 24-33 belong to plan `21.1-06`. Resolved as **`CONTROL 23b`** — the module's own companion convention (`4b`, `5b`, `9b`, `17b` all precede it), landing beside `CONTROL 23` whose gate it repairs, disturbing no allocation and forcing no renumber. **Consequence.** Plan `21.1-05` gains a Task 0 carrying the repair and `CONTROL 23b`, watched RED before the fix per `D-IMPL-170`. `DOCS-22`'s amended cell keeps the prose citation wave 4 chose; no further sweep of the other 78 `A-5` rows happens in 21.1, per `D-IMPL-179` limb 1. Related: `D-IMPL-179`, `D-IMPL-170`, `D-GATE-21`, `D-IMPL-178`.

**D-IMPL-181 — `RR-12`: the four degradation shims take a THIRD criterion-12 disposition and are controlled under a new aim kind `shim` with an INVERTED obligation, rather than being deleted as unreachable or excused by a frozen exempt roster.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-08-22. Approver: Dave (wave-6 boundary of Phase 21.1). **What was found.** Plan `21.1-06` swept all thirty registered limbs before writing a control — neuter one, re-run the module, record what noticed — and found four limbs reachable ONLY with a sibling neutered: `_duplicated_table_row.twin_identical` and all three `_duplicated_checkbox_bullet` limbs. Deadness proven by enumeration, not inferred. **They are not dead code and not ordinary refusals.** They are the degradation shims plan `21.1-05` installed so that neutering a sibling limb produces SILENCE rather than an `AttributeError`. That distinction is load-bearing: a crash and a caught defect are indistinguishable to a meta-control, so if neutering limb X makes the suite explode, wave 7's coverage assertion would conclude "the control reaches limb X" when all it reached was the wreckage. **Why the letter of criterion 12 was wrong here.** As authored it admits two dispositions — reachable-and-watched, or unreachable-and-REMOVED. By the letter these four are unreachable, so removal would follow, the crashes would return, and the hole the shims were installed to close would re-open behind a green suite. That is the cheapest-looking and worst available answer, and it is precisely this phase's defect class: a check passing for a reason unrelated to what it claims to test. **The alternatives Dave rejected, with his reasons.** A frozen roster of named exempt ids *"excuses them without proving they work"*. Reshaping them for independent reachability is *"new mechanism in a prove-existing-mechanism wave"*. Deferring for a walkthrough was unnecessary — *"the role is clear enough to rule"*. **The ruling.** Add aim kind `shim`. Its obligation is INVERTED: a control aimed at a shim proves that, with the sibling neutered, the shim keeps the failure SILENT, and goes RED when the shim is removed or broken so the crash returns. Coverage quantifies over `shim` exactly as over every other kind — no exempt roster. The four limbs are NAMED in the plan and SUMMARY so the roster is explicit, while `D-21` still forbids any hardcoded count in the assertion itself. **Criterion 12 is rewritten rather than patched**, and the rewrite lands BEFORE wave 7's coverage assertion so wave 7 is not gated against superseded wording — the ordering mistake this phase family has now found four times. Criterion 15 is added to carry the inverted obligation. This is the THIRD case criterion 12 as authored did not cover: repair-to-reachable (`D-IMPL-179` limb 2), the four positive twins with no mutation and no aimed limb, and now the shims. **Consequence.** Phase 21.1 now carries FIFTEEN success criteria. Controls 24-33 stay as landed; plan `21.1-07` gains `shim` in its kind set. Related: `D-IMPL-179`, `D-IMPL-180`, `D-IMPL-170`, `D-GATE-21`.

**D-IMPL-182 — the general `guard` reading is RATIFIED as shipped, and with it criterion 13's inverted obligation for the three no-mutation control families; no seventh disposition is introduced and no registry rename is required.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-08-22. Approver: Dave (wave-7 boundary of Phase 21.1). **What was found.** Plan `21.1-07` assigned the `guard` aim kind to two controls — the ones holding `_refuse`'s unregistered-limb check and the autouse fixture asserting `_NEUTERED` is empty, the two mechanisms whose silent failure makes every other control in the module vacuous. Working through the actual control set, the executor found that **nineteen controls fit none of the five kinds**: they hold checkers that RETURN their findings (`channel_disagreements`, `unverdicted`, `refuse_unresolvable`, `uncited_verdicts` and others) rather than raising through a named limb, so there is no limb to neuter and the sabotage shape is instead "make the checker return nothing and require the control to notice". Criterion 13 quantifies over EVERY control, so the choice was binary: read `guard` generally, or leave seventeen controls aim-unproven pending a seventh disposition. The executor took the general reading — which is the plan's own literal definition, *"the control holds one of the module's own guard mechanisms"* — shipped it, and flagged it for ratification rather than burying it. **The ruling and its reasoning.** Dave ratified as shipped: *"Criterion 13's job is every control declares an aim, and that aim is proven — not a perfect ontology of sabotage shapes."* Splitting `guard` into disarming-mechanism and returns-findings kinds was rejected as *"a rename pass for taxonomy purity; it does not change what is proven"*. A seventh disposition was rejected because it *"leaves criterion 13 unsatisfied until Wave 8 and turns a closed generator into an open design task"*. Two explicit prohibitions for the remainder of the phase: **do not introduce a seventh disposition**, and **do not require a registry rename before Wave 8**. Wave 8 may PROPOSE a finer split if its own work naturally wants one and the cost is small; it is not a blocker. **Criterion 13's inverted obligation, ratified with it.** Three control families have no mutation and no aimed limb — the four positive twins (whose whole purpose is to prove that "red on everything is not a check"), the eighteen `guard` controls, and the four `shim` controls under `D-IMPL-181`. For these, "watch the mutation redden the control" is unsatisfiable as written, and the honest equivalent is inverted: force the guarded predicate to refuse everything, and require the control to go RED. This reading is recorded HERE, in the append-only decision log the close panel reads, rather than only in a plan SUMMARY — a criterion whose real meaning lives in a SUMMARY is the same defect this phase family exists to end. Criterion 13's ROADMAP text is deliberately NOT amended: it is already discharged by what shipped, and editing a criterion after the wave it gated is the retroactive-authoring mistake `D-GATE-19` exists to prevent. **The measured state this rests on.** 54 controls, 54 `CONTROL_AIM` entries, every one declaring an aim — `limb` 23, `guard` 18, `meta` 5, `discriminator` 4, `pathspec` 2, `shim` 2. `CONTROL 36b` proves 21 aim pairs under the general reading. **Every red across all 56 aim proofs was the control's own `AssertionError`, not one crash**, and `CASCADING_REDS` is frozen as a named, today-empty roster so a control that starts crashing where it used to assert reddens the run rather than counting as coverage. **The generator is closed.** Related: `D-IMPL-181`, `D-IMPL-180`, `D-IMPL-179`, `D-IMPL-170`, `D-GATE-21`.

**D-IMPL-183 — `DOCS-22` is amended AND rostered: one row, both channels, no `A-5` sweep.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-08-23. Approver: Dave (Ruling 2 at the `D-GATE-21.1` sitting). **What was asked.** Plan `21.1-10` reserved one question the phase deliberately did not settle: may `DOCS-22`'s LEDGER cell be amended to a bolded, cited verdict, given that it sits outside the fifty-four and criterion 11 therefore does not reach it on the planner's reading? **What the close panel added to the question.** gemini's finding 3, verified: `test_every_verdicted_roster_row_cites_its_evidence` quantifies over `WORKING_SET_ROSTER | PHASE_OWN_ROSTER`, measured at **70 ids, and `DOCS-22` is not one of them**. The wave-4 amendment gave the row citations that NO gate held — strip them tomorrow and nothing goes red. **The ruling, verbatim:** *"Amend and roster — bolded, cited verdict; one row only; both channels; no A-5 sweep."* **What this settles.** (a) The wave-4 amendment under `D-IMPL-179` limb 1 STANDS and is ratified unchanged — the row keeps the `DCD-10` shape in both channels and its tick does not move, because the verdict was and stays in the Complete family. (b) The row is now rostered so the citation-presence rule actually reaches it. (c) **The other 78 `A-5` rows are NOT swept in** — the ruling is about one row, which is why the mechanism is a named roster of one and not a predicate. **Discharged by** `tools/docs_tests/test_requirement_ledger.py::RULED_IN_ROSTER` and `tools/docs_tests/test_requirement_ledger.py::citation_roster`, with `CONTROL 45` (`tools/docs_tests/test_requirement_ledger.py::test_control_45_the_ruled_in_row_is_actually_held_to_the_citation_rule`) proving the rostering is not decorative: it asserts the row clean on the real ledger, strips every citation, and requires the refusal to name it — watched RED under the pre-ruling roster, which is its registered saboteur. `DOCS-22` could not simply be added to either existing roster: it is outside `WORKING_SET_ROSTER` by construction — that absence IS `RR-3`'s mechanism, an unevidenced `Complete` at the pinned base never entering the working set — and `PHASE_OWN_ROSTER` is now derived from the ledger's `Phase` column under `D-IMPL-184`'s machinery, so widening it by hand reddens `CONTROL 42`. **Related:** `D-IMPL-179` (the wave-4 amendment this ratifies), `D-IMPL-175` (`DOCS-18` limb 1, unamended), `D-GATE-21` (unamended), and the close record at `.planning/phases/21.1-the-guard-that-did-not-guard-closing-the-check-vacuity-class/21.1-CLOSE-REVIEWS.md`.

**D-IMPL-184 — the six criterion readings recorded in `21.1-09-SUMMARY.md` are CONFIRMED as recorded.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-08-23. Approver: Dave (Ruling 3 at the `D-GATE-21.1` sitting). **What was asked.** Phase 21.1's fifteen Success Criteria were authored before execution and six of them turned out to conflict, either with each other or with the shipped module. Each was resolved by an executor reading, carried to the gate rather than settled quietly, and recorded in `21.1-09-SUMMARY.md`. Dave was asked to confirm or override each. **The ruling, verbatim:** *"Confirm as recorded in `21.1-09-SUMMARY.md`."* **The six, in the order recorded.** (1) **Criteria 2 and 8 invert RED and GREEN and cannot both be met literally** — criterion 2's RED/GREEN describes THE SUBJECT (the mutated member reads clean before the fix, refused after); criterion 8's describes THE CONTROL TEST's own pytest outcome. Both evidenced separately in a four-cell table per control, rather than one being quietly dropped. (2) **Criterion 8 versus criterion 12, for a control over a refusal that ALREADY ships** — there is no pre-fix module in which such a control could fail, so the RED is produced by NEUTERING the aimed limb against the SHIPPED module. Stronger evidence, not weaker: it shows the control failing with exactly one NAMED branch disarmed, which is what *proven to reach that branch* means. (3) **Criterion 12's disposition for a limb unreachable only because its subject was hardcoded** — repair-to-reachable is NOT a third disposition; once repaired the limb satisfies criterion 12's FIRST disposition outright, reached honestly. The genuine third disposition is the `shim` (`D-IMPL-181`). (4) **Criterion 13's discriminator case.** (5) **Criterion 14's scope against the pinned base and `UNRESOLVABLE_BASE`** — criterion 14 scopes to a control that DERIVES a base in order to produce a differing diff; a SHA pinned in a versioned artefact with its own rationale, and a SHA chosen because it resolves to nothing, are not the defect the criterion names. (6) **Criterion 5's collision with `D-IMPL-175`.** **Why this is logged rather than left in a SUMMARY.** `D-IMPL-170`'s standard: a reading that lives only in a plan record is evidence that someone decided once. Six criteria were read against their authored wording and the readings now bind. **Related:** `D-IMPL-179`, `D-IMPL-180`, `D-IMPL-181`, `D-IMPL-182` (the four rulings made mid-phase), `D-IMPL-170`.

**D-IMPL-185 — `R-α`, `A-7`, `RR-5`/`RR-7`/`RR-8`/`RR-10` and `A-1`..`A-8` are CARRIED; no reopen.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-08-23. Approver: Dave (Ruling 4 at the `D-GATE-21.1` sitting). **The ruling, verbatim:** *"R-α, A-7, RR-5/7/8/10, A-1..A-8 — carried; no reopen."* **`R-α` is the one that matters and it is stated rather than absorbed.** A ledger cell in which BOTH verdicts are unbolded is still invisible to the one-verdict gate. It was found in wave 2 and left open deliberately: every stronger predicate MEASURED against the real ledger flags rows Dave has already ruled on — *any vocabulary word anywhere* flags THIRTEEN including `DCD-02`, `DCD-09`, `DCD-10`, `CPS-03` and `EXAM-02`, and *the leading verdict must be bolded* flags SEVENTY-FIVE, roughly half the table. **It needs a vocabulary decision, not a stronger regex**, and this gate does not make one. **What carrying means here:** the findings stay named in `21.1-CLOSE-REVIEWS.md` and in `21-FINDINGS.md` where they already sit, no phase is commissioned against them, and no standing check is written that would be red on landing. It does NOT mean they were assessed and found harmless. **Related:** `D-IMPL-174` (the `A-5` carve-out on the same reasoning), `D-GATE-21` (which carried `A-1`..`A-8` the first time).

**D-IMPL-186 — `VAC-06`'s aim-proof figure is stated as wave-7 HISTORY, not as a present-tense count.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-08-23. Approver: Dave (Ruling 5a at the `D-GATE-21.1` sitting). **What raised it.** The single-agent close review's finding 5, verified: `VAC-06`'s ledger cell reads *"56 aim proofs"* in the present tense. 56 was the figure at wave 7. Measured at the close, after four controls were added by the close fixes, the module runs **72** non-`meta` aim-proof pairs — 33 `limb`, 26 `guard`, 5 `pathspec`, 4 `discriminator`, 4 `shim`. Every other figure in this module carries a *HISTORY, read by no assertion* caveat; this one did not. **The ruling, verbatim:** *"Amend to wave-7 history — not a present-tense count."* **Why the fix is not a corrected number.** A present-tense count in a document no gate reads is stale the moment the next control lands — which is `D-21`'s whole subject, arriving in prose rather than in code. The figure is therefore dated to the wave that produced it rather than re-measured, and the row's verdict is unchanged. **Related:** `D-21` (no carried counts), `D-IMPL-181`, `D-IMPL-182` (the two rulings `VAC-06`'s `Complete as ruled` names).

**D-IMPL-187 — `Aim.kind` being scalar is CARRIED as design debt; a mixed-kind registry is not a close fix.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-08-23. Approver: Dave (Ruling 5b at the `D-GATE-21.1` sitting). **What raised it.** The single-agent close review's finding 8, and it is the direct answer to the question the close panel was aimed at — *is there an aim the registry cannot express?* **Yes.** `tools/docs_tests/test_requirement_ledger.py::Aim` carries `kind` as a single string, so a control spanning two kinds can declare only one of them. `CONTROL 23b` is registered `kind="limb"` with one target while its docstring declares FOUR limbs, three of them the `RR-11` span-containment repair; the other three cannot be declared as `guard` targets because `CONTROL 34` forbids a saboteur on a non-`guard` entry. Three of four limbs, plus the shipped assertion `test_each_widened_pattern_subsumes_the_lint_pattern_it_replaced`, are therefore proven by no aim. **The ruling, verbatim:** *"Carried as design debt — not a close fix."* **Why carried rather than fixed.** Making `kind` plural changes the shape of every entry in a 63-entry registry and every direction of `CONTROL 34`'s completeness check, at a gate sitting, with no plan. That is redesign inside a close, which `CLAUDE.md` §3 forbids. **This is the most substantive residual Phase 21.1 leaves open** and it is recorded as such rather than as an advisory. **Related:** `D-IMPL-181` (which added the `shim` kind and is the precedent for extending the registry deliberately), `D-IMPL-182`, `D-IMPL-185`.

**D-GATE-21.1 — Phase 21.1 (The Guard That Did Not Guard: Closing the Check-Vacuity Class) is APPROVED.** APPROVED. Date: 2026-08-23. Approver: Dave. **What is gated.** Ten plans in ten serial waves on branch `phase-21.1`, branched at `c0d35f8` and merged to `main` at this entry per `CLAUDE.md` §2.2. **`D-GATE-21` REMAINS IN FORCE AND IS NOT AMENDED**; this phase is a fix wave on the verification machinery, never a re-opening of the 54-row audit. **What the phase closed.** The check-vacuity class — checks that pass for a reason unrelated to what they claim to check — across the ledger-verification module in one pass: a pathspec typo in ANY member now refuses; a cell that says two things is caught however it says them; a duplicate id in either channel refuses by name; the resolver index refuses when it has no subject; Phase 16's lane is nineteen rows in the document Dave rules from, not eighteen; and every refusal in the module has an identity (`LIMBS`), a control, and a standing proof that its control reaches it (`CONTROL_AIM` plus the meta-controls). **THE §3.1 CLOSE FOUND FOUR MORE INSTANCES OF THE PHASE'S OWN DEFECT CLASS, ALL IN THE MACHINERY BUILT TO CLOSE IT, AND ALL FOUR ARE FIXED IN-PHASE.** The panel (gemini, codex, cursor; `claude` skipped for independence) read the SHIPPED tree per `D-IMPL-178` — 553 KB / 8,272 lines inlined, the payload's omissions named — and was briefed on the known defects and told to report what is ADJACENT to each. **Reviewers converged from four directions on one thing: `RR-1`'s fix quantifies PER MEMBER and the controls vouching for it quantified PER CONSTANT.** Each was proven by sabotage against the shipped module, not by argument: `fabric_diff` degraded to validate only the two ends of a pathspec left **all 94 tests green** (`CONTROL 18` mutated only first and last, so nine of `UAT_RECORDS`' eleven members were watched by nothing); `CONTROL A` narrowed to read only the first member left **all 94 green** (`CONTROL 38` corrupts every member at once and cannot tell the two apart); a `VAC-07` row minted in BOTH channels with an unevidenced `**Complete**` and never rostered was named by **ZERO of eight gates** (`PHASE_OWN_ROSTER` was the one id-roster in the module with no derivation counterpart — `RR-3`'s mechanism on the roster of the phase whose subject `RR-3` is); and `_index()` accepted an index thinned from **5,073 basenames to 1** so long as it retained the anchor, after which `refuse_unresolvable` returned `[]` over the real ledger. Closed by `CONTROL 41`, `CONTROL 38b`, `CONTROL 42` with `derived_phase_own_roster`, and `_index.thinned_index` with `CONTROL 43`; plus `dispatcher_bypasses` widened to bare raises and `async def` with `CONTROL 44`. Six fix commits, five new controls, every one REGISTERED in `CONTROL_AIM` so the meta-controls hold it to the same aim discipline — a control added at the close cannot ship mis-aimed either. **TWO THINGS ABOUT HOW THE CLOSE WENT ARE RECORDED BECAUSE THEY ARE THE EVIDENCE, NOT THE ANECDOTE.** (1) **A close fix regenerated the phase's own defect class and the machinery caught it in seconds.** Adding `_index.thinned_index` made `CONTROL 22` — which asserted `"index" in str(failure)`, a substring BOTH limbs satisfy — go GREEN with the limb it names neutered. `CONTROL 35` reported it by name. That is the `CONTROL 5` defect wave 5 fixed, reproduced by the executor and caught by the instrument this phase built. `CONTROL 22` now asserts the limb id. (2) **A red for the wrong reason nearly passed for a caught defect, inside the verification of a finding about exactly that.** The first `fabric_diff` sabotage made the suite go red — via an `IndexError` on an unrelated path with a limb neutered, not `CONTROL 18` catching anything. Taken at face value, the blocking finding would have been recorded REJECTED. The empty-safe sabotage is the one in the record. **FIVE FINDINGS WERE REJECTED AND ARE RECORDED AS REJECTED, WITH THE EVIDENCE THAT REFUTES THEM** — including one whose CAUSE was the executor's own review brief paraphrasing `D-IMPL-123`'s ceiling scope loosely, which is named as such. Twenty-two panel findings plus nine from the additive single-agent review; every citation resolved against the tree individually rather than sampled; no reviewer failed to review. **CI at the merge commit: exit 0 on all six legs** — `lint` 0; `typecheck` 0 (211 source files); `test` **4105 passed / 118 skipped**, byte-for-byte the `D-GATE-21` baseline, which is the mechanical proof that `D-05` held and that the phase changed no behaviour; `gate-tools` 0 (406 + 266, up from 406 + 205 at the phase's start); `examples` 0 (eleven, three harness legs at one content address); `docs-strict` 0. **The test leg was run as THREE pytest invocations rather than one**, because background runs on this host were terminated twice at 68%; every `tests/` directory is covered and the total lands exactly on the known baseline, and it is recorded here rather than glossed. The fence diff over `src/`, `runtime/`, `examples/`, `public/`, `tests/`, `pyproject.toml` and `tools/lints/citations.py` is EMPTY on every path, and the only file written under `tools/` is the ledger module itself (`D-11`). Module 51 -> 112 tests across the phase; `CONTROLS` 63; `LIMBS` 36. **CRITERION 11 IS THIS ENTRY, AND `VAC-05` CLOSES ON IT.** `VAC-05` read `Partial` through the whole of execution because its outstanding limb was `D-GATE-21.1` itself; it is amended to `Complete` in both channels under this entry and not before — the `RECON-09` discipline, which is the difference between a verdict and a hope. **WHAT THIS GATE DOES NOT DO.** It does not close `R-α`, `A-7`, or the carried `RR-` and `A-` findings (`D-IMPL-185`); it does not make `Aim.kind` plural (`D-IMPL-187`, the most substantive residual); it does not sweep the 78 other `A-5` uncited Complete-family rows (`D-IMPL-183` is one row only); and it does not touch the five `Not built` rows, `DOCS-18` limb 1, `RECON-10`'s outstanding limb, or any of the 27 human verification items. Each is stated rather than absorbed. **Governs:** the Phase 21.1 approval; the merge of `phase-21.1` to `main`; the reading of all fifteen Success Criteria as met; the `VAC-05` `Partial` -> `Complete` amendment. **Related:** `D-GATE-21` (parent, unamended, in force), `D-IMPL-178` (the panel reads the shipped tree), `D-IMPL-179`, `D-IMPL-180`, `D-IMPL-181`, `D-IMPL-182` (the four mid-phase rulings), `D-IMPL-183` through `D-IMPL-187` (this sitting's five), `D-IMPL-170` (a control is a standing test), and the close record at `.planning/phases/21.1-the-guard-that-did-not-guard-closing-the-check-vacuity-class/21.1-CLOSE-REVIEWS.md`.

**D-IMPL-188 — Phase 21's four untouched-tree assertions are BOUNDED to Phase 21.1's close commit; they stop making a claim about the future.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-08-23. Approver: Dave (Phase 22 Wave 1 checkpoint, presented as four options). **What raised it.** Phase 22's first commit — `public/concepts/answers-no-document-contains.md`, the `DOCS-15` adoption page — turned `tools/docs_tests/test_requirement_ledger.py::test_the_scope_fence_holds` RED on a correct tree. **The defect, measured rather than argued.** `fabric_diff(base, paths)` hardcoded `..HEAD`, and four assertions read the pinned base from `21-BASE-COMMIT.txt` through it: `test_the_fabric_is_untouched` (`FABRIC`), `test_the_scope_fence_holds` (`FENCE` — `src/`, `runtime/`, `examples/`, `public/`, `pyproject.toml`), `test_the_human_needed_verification_records_are_untouched` (`UAT_RECORDS`), and `test_the_citation_lint_is_not_modified` (`PINNED_FILES`). With `HEAD` as the upper bound each one said *"Phase 21 did not write here"* on the day it landed and **"no phase may ever write here"** thereafter — a forward prohibition over five paths that nobody ruled on and that no phase boundary could lift. `git diff --stat <base>..951eb4a -- <the fence>` is EMPTY; `git diff --stat <base>..HEAD -- <the fence>` is the adoption page. The window, not the tree, was wrong. **The ruling.** Bound the four to Phase 21.1's close commit `951eb4a3e2d8e072ec7f059e372545753d415a25`, pinned in `.planning/phases/21-.../21-CLOSE-COMMIT.txt` in the same shape as the base and for the same stated reason — a ceiling that does not resolve, or that silently falls back to `HEAD`, makes an "is empty" assertion vacuous rather than failing it. Each assertion keeps **exactly** the claim it carried during Phase 21 and the historical record survives. Docstrings amended, never replaced. *Rejected, and recorded as rejected:* **retiring** the four now Phase 21 is closed (loses the standing record that Phase 21 stayed inside its fence, and nothing re-checks it); **dropping `public/` from the fence** (retroactively weakens what the fence meant during Phase 21, and leaves the other four members frozen so the same collision returns on the next phase touching any of them); **reverting Phase 22** (discards correct, fully measured work and only defers the collision). **THE REPAIR HAD TO MOVE THE CONTROLS, NOT ONLY THE ASSERTIONS, AND THAT IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING.** `CONTROL 18` replicates the assertion's own `git diff <base>..HEAD` to establish that a mutated pathspec is the *silent* kind before watching the refusal fire. Four of its five `FENCE` cases were red and `[FENCE-3]` was green — index 3 IS `public/`, so mutating it removed the only member with a real diff. A control that kept `HEAD` while the assertion it vouches for gained a ceiling would be this module's own defect class arriving inside its repair, so `CONTROL A` (per member, with `derived_base` deriving against the ceiling), `CONTROL 16` and its positive twin, and `CONTROL 18` were bounded with them. `CONTROL 13` deliberately did NOT move: it vouches for the `TESTS_TREE` assertion, which stays at `HEAD`. **A NEW REFUSAL LIMB, BECAUSE AN EMPTY CEILING IS SILENT.** `git diff <base>.. -- <paths>` is not an error — `git` reads the missing right-hand side as `HEAD` — so an empty ceiling would silently restore the exact unbounded comparison this ruling removes. `fabric_diff.empty_ceiling` refuses it by name, is registered in `LIMBS`, and is watched by `CONTROL C`. **AND THE CEILING ITSELF IS PROVEN, NOT TRUSTED.** `test_the_pinned_diff_ceiling_resolves` requires a full 40-hex SHA, resolution through `git rev-parse --verify <sha>^{commit}`, ancestry of `HEAD`, and a **STRICT DESCENDANT** relation to the base — strictness asserted separately, because `git merge-base --is-ancestor A A` succeeds. That last check is the load-bearing one and it was measured: with `ceiling == base` substituted, **all four bounded assertions pass**, and that test is the only thing in the tree that catches it. **Every claim above was watched, not asserted:** each bounded assertion was given a window that genuinely differs over its own pathspec and observed RED with its own message, then reverted GREEN on the real pin; the `FENCE` case was sabotaged with the window `951eb4a..HEAD` and correctly reported the adoption page, proving the bounded assertion would still have caught Phase 22's write had it fallen inside Phase 21's window. Module 106 -> **113 passed, 0 failed**; `gate-tools` 406 + 267; `lint` exit 0. **THREE RESIDUALS, NAMED RATHER THAN ABSORBED.** (1) **There is a FIFTH unbounded assertion, not four**: `test_no_test_was_written_to_manufacture_a_citation` diffs `TESTS_TREE = ("tests/",)` against `HEAD` and carries the identical defect — it forbids any future commit under `tests/`, forever, and is green today only because Phase 22 happens not to write there. This ruling names four and four were bounded; the fifth is **OPEN and needs its own ruling**, not a default. (2) Nothing structurally stops a control's window drifting off its assertion's window again — that drift is exactly how `CONTROL 18` broke here. The instances are fixed; no source-level guard in the `dispatcher_bypasses` idiom requires a control replicating a bounded call to pass the same ceiling. (3) Nothing stops the ceiling being **advanced**: a future executor hitting a red fence can edit `21-CLOSE-COMMIT.txt` forward and go green — the narrowing move the fence's own docstring forbids. That is governance rather than mechanism, and it is recorded so it is visible. **Governs:** `tools/docs_tests/test_requirement_ledger.py`; `.planning/phases/21-requirement-ledger-reconciliation-what-is-actually-discharge/21-CLOSE-COMMIT.txt` (new) and `21-BASE-COMMIT.txt` (appended to, never rewritten); the unblocking of Phase 22. **Does NOT govern:** the `TESTS_TREE` assertion, which is residual 1. **Related:** `D-GATE-21`, `D-GATE-21.1` (whose close commit is the ceiling), `D-IMPL-170` (a control is a standing test), `D-IMPL-179` limb 2 (repair over deletion — the precedent for bounding rather than retiring), `D-11` (the scope fence), `D-15`. Commit: `59de8ae`.

**D-IMPL-188 AMENDMENT — the FIFTH untouched-tree assertion is bounded at the same ceiling; the class is closed rather than left one instance short.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-08-23. Approver: Dave (Phase 22, between Wave 2 and Wave 3, ruling on residual 1 of the entry above). **What raised it.** The executor that bounded the four found and REPORTED a fifth carrying the identical defect rather than quietly bounding it or quietly skipping it: `test_no_test_was_written_to_manufacture_a_citation` diffs `TESTS_TREE = ("tests/",)` against `HEAD`, forbidding any future commit under `tests/` forever. It was green only because Phase 22 happens not to write there. **Dave's ruling, verbatim on the reasoning:** *"The defect is the same class you just closed for the other four... Leaving `tests/` frozen against the Phase 21 base forever means the next phase that legitimately adds a test goes red for archaeology, not for manufacturing a citation. 'Phase 21 wrote no test to manufacture a citation' is a WINDOWED claim. It needs the same ceiling, the same non-empty window check, and a control that still goes red under sabotage — including the CONTROL-18 pattern of proving the mutated pathspec is silently empty before watching the refusal."* Directed: fold into `D-IMPL-188` as an amendment; land it BEFORE Wave 3 so the phase does not keep running under a known sibling hole; and **do not advance the ceiling opportunistically** — the same bound as the four. All three were followed; the pin is unchanged at `951eb4a3e2d8e072ec7f059e372545753d415a25` and no second pin file was created. **`CONTROL 13`'S REASONING INVERTED, AND THAT IS THE POINT.** In the first round `CONTROL 13` correctly did NOT move — `derived_base`'s docstring said in as many words that its `HEAD` default existed to keep `CONTROL 13` reading as it did *because the assertion it vouches for was unbounded*. That premise is now false, so the control moved in lockstep with its assertion. A control left at `HEAD` while its assertion gained a ceiling is the drift that broke `CONTROL 18` in the first round. **THE ARITY-ONE HOLE, MEASURED.** Dave required the `CONTROL 18` pattern here. `CONTROL 18` does not cover `TESTS_TREE` at all: its parametrization collects `FABRIC-0/1`, `FENCE-0..4`, `UAT_RECORDS-0..10` — eighteen cases driven by `MULTI_MEMBER_PATHSPECS`, and `TESTS_TREE` is arity one, which is why `RR-1` never reached this constant. `CONTROL A` does not cover it either (`CONTROL_A_PATHSPECS` is the other four). `CONTROL 16` DOES run the silent-empty step over `("test/",)` and was already bounded by the first round — **but its subjects are hardcoded literals written down BESIDE `tests/` rather than derived FROM it**, so it would go on passing unchanged if the constant drifted; it proves the limb fires, not that this assertion's pathspec is guarded, which is exactly the distinction `CONTROL 38`'s banner draws. The derived form therefore lived nowhere and was added inside `CONTROL 13` — near miss derived through `near_miss` from the constant resolved at call time, proven to match nothing by running the predicate, proven silent through raw `git diff` **in the assertion's own window**, then the refusal watched naming the member. `CONTROL 18`'s step 2 (every other member still live) is omitted with the reason stated: there is no sibling at arity one. **Measurements:** module **113 passed, 0 failed** before and after (no new test function, so no increase was available); `tools/docs_tests` + `tools/publish_scan_tests` 267; `gate-tools` 406 + 267. The real window is clean — `git diff --stat <base>..<ceiling> -- tests/` prints nothing. **Sabotage, observed and reverted:** the bounded assertion given a window that genuinely differs over `tests/` went RED with its own `D-05` message naming a 384-line test file; `CONTROL 13` went red four ways — `fabric_diff` degraded to `""`, the `untracked_member` limb neutered (the newly added step, red for its own reason), `TESTS_TREE` substituted with its own near miss (`[limb:derived_base.no_history]`), and the ceiling forced back to `HEAD` (see residual 2). **A CORRECTION TO THE RECORD.** `21-BASE-COMMIT.txt` was not merely stale on a COUNT — the `tests/` assertion was **never listed in it at all**, because it landed in a later plan than the one that wrote the file. Both pin files were appended to, never rewritten above their separators. **RESIDUAL 2, VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY BY THE ORCHESTRATOR AND MORE PRECISE THAN FIRST REPORTED: nothing asserts that a bounded assertion actually READS the pin.** `test_the_pinned_diff_ceiling_resolves` proves the pin is SANE; nothing proves it is USED. Deleting the `phase_close_commit()` argument from `test_no_test_was_written_to_manufacture_a_citation` leaves the module at **113 passed** — measured, not argued. **But it is not uniform, and the flat statement would be false:** deleting the same argument from `test_the_scope_fence_holds` IS caught (`1 failed, 112 passed`), because Phase 22 has since written under `public/`. **The bound proves itself only where the tree has since moved**; on the four windows that are clean at both ends it is invisible, and it costs nothing to remove until the day it matters — which is this module's own defect class, one level out. Closing it needs an assertion over the module's own SOURCE SHAPE (every `fabric_diff` call inside an untouched-tree assertion passes three arguments), a class of check this module does not yet have. NOT built, NOT accepted; open. **Residual 3 carried from the entry above** — nothing stops the ceiling being ADVANCED by a future executor who hits a red fence, which is a governance question about who may move a pin rather than a mechanism one. Dave: *"can still be named at `D-GATE-22` if you want a policy on who may move it; that does not justify leaving this instance unbounded."* Carried to the `D-GATE-22` sitting as a policy question. **Governs:** `tools/docs_tests/test_requirement_ledger.py::test_no_test_was_written_to_manufacture_a_citation` and `CONTROL 13`; the amendment blocks appended to `21-BASE-COMMIT.txt` and `21-CLOSE-COMMIT.txt`. **Related:** `D-IMPL-188` (parent), `D-05`, `D-11`, `D-GATE-21.1`. **D-IMPL-189 — archive-with-repoint is an ALLOWED INTERMEDIATE STATE for `DOCS-17` and `CLNT-17`; `Complete` still requires delete plus re-cut to the replacement examples.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-08-23. Approver: Dave (ruling given while scoping Phase 22.1, on the cost measurement below). **What raised it.** The four `Not built` rows the Phase 21 audit delivered (`21-FINDINGS.md` §2) are one knot, and the two retirement rows in it were quoted at 2–3 days on the assumption that retiring the condemned trees means deleting them and re-cutting every published page that sources from them. Dave asked why the code could not simply be moved somewhere it exists but is not used. **The measurement that decided it.** The condemned set is **265 files and roughly 26,000 lines across ten trees** (`examples/00-quickstart` … `examples/08-e2e-demo` plus `examples/external/00-hello-context`), and the two Section-1 trees `CLNT-17` names add **37 more**. Three things couple them to the project: the always-on CI `examples` aggregate and its nine `example-0N` targets; **31 test files** under `tests/examples`; and the published documentation — **99 snippet includes and 108 prose paths across 15 pages**, concentrated in `public/tutorial/adopters-guide.md` (35) and `public/tutorial/demo-walkthrough.md` (18). Moving the trees discharges the first two in about an hour. It does **not** discharge the third, because the published pages do not link to the examples — they `--8<--` **inline the source at build time**, so a moved file is a broken strict build unless every include path is rewritten. Rewriting 99 include paths to an archive location is a mechanical path substitution of roughly two hours; re-cutting the same pages against a replacement surface requires the replacement (`DOCS-14`/`EXAM-02`) to exist first and is the expensive half. **The ruling.** (1) Archive-with-repoint — the trees moved **intact** under an archive location, dropped from the `examples` aggregate and the always-on CI job, their paired tests moved with them, and every published include and prose path re-pointed so `docs-strict` stays green — is an **allowed intermediate state** for both rows. (2) It is **not `Complete`**. `Complete` continues to mean deletion plus a re-cut of the published pages against the replacement examples. (3) Both rows may then read **`Partial`**, split on the same seam: limb done — out of live CI, sources preserved under archive, includes re-pointed, strict build green; limb owed — full retirement and the re-cut. (4) **The `Partial` verdicts are written in the archive phase, when the state exists on the tree, and not before.** Dave, on being offered the wording early: *"Do not write Partial (or any 'archived / out of CI') wording until that state exists on the tree. Logging a verdict for a future move is the same ledger dishonesty this pass is cleaning up."* Phase 22.1 therefore leaves both rows `Not built` and performs no part of the move. **Why this does not collide with `D-27`.** `D-27` forbids a partial retirement — a state in which some of the condemned set is gone and the machinery that referenced it is left half-repaired. Nothing is deleted under this ruling, so no such state arises; the archive move is one change that leaves every witness readable at a new path. The `00`–`08` half of `D-27` remains Dave's and remains undecided. **What this does not authorize.** It does not re-scope `DOCS-14` or `EXAM-02`, which still owe a replacement surface; it does not permit the published pages to be re-cut against the archive as though the archive were the teaching material; and it does not discharge the standing observation that those pages currently teach the pre-Phase-15 integration surface (Phase 14's `G-01`), which the replacement closes and the archive move only relabels. **Governs:** the sequencing of `DOCS-17` and `CLNT-17`; the verdict vocabulary available to them. **Related:** `D-27`, `D-11`, `D-IMPL-145` limb 2 (the original quarantine), `D-IMPL-176` point 2 (replacements before removals), `D-GATE-21`, `D-GATE-22`, `D-15`.

**D-GATE-22.1 — Phase 22.1 (The Hygiene Block — The Tool That Could Not Tell "None" From "Could Not Look") is APPROVED.** APPROVED. Date: 2026-08-23. Now held, with a false-positive control proving `sweep()` resets rather than accumulates. **Thirteen findings: nine confirmed and fixed in-phase, one confirmed and accepted, two rejected with refuting evidence, one confirmed correct by all three independently** (the `_comment_lines` tokenize exemption — its degraded path OVER-reports a coupling, the safe direction for a deletion tool).
