(2) Any remaining `D-IMPL-188`-style *pin-not-read* cousins **outside this module** stay open as verification-tools debt and are not 22.1 scope. (3) `DOCS-17` and `CLNT-17` remain **`Not built`** until the archive phase makes `Partial` true (`D-IMPL-189` point 4). (4) The 27-item packet is delivered for Dave's later ruling and is **not discharged here**. **WHAT THIS GATE DOES NOT DO.** It performs no part of the archive move; it closes none of the four `Not built` rows; it discharges no human-verification item; and it does not touch the `00`–`08` half of `D-27`, which remains Dave's and undecided. **Governs:** the Phase 22.1 approval; the reading of all nine Success Criteria as met; `RECON-10` discharged as `Complete as ruled`; the four carried items above. **Related:** `D-IMPL-189` (the archive ruling this phase logged but did not act on), `D-IMPL-188` and its amendment (whose residual the panel reproduced here), `D-IMPL-177` (the ruling that closed `RECON-10`'s third limb), `D-GATE-19` (criteria before Wave 1), `D-GATE-22`, `D-IMPL-178` (the panel reads the shipped tree), `D-11`, `D-15`, `D-20`, `D-21`, `DCD-02`, and the close record at `.planning/phases/22.1-the-hygiene-block-the-tool-that-could-not-tell-none-from/22.1-CLOSE-REVIEWS.md` with the inlined payload and the three raw reviewer transcripts committed beside it.

**D-IMPL-190 — Phase 23 scope: the archive move carries TEN trees, not twelve, and the paired tests STAY under `tests/`. Amends `D-IMPL-189` point 1 on a measurement.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-08-24. Approver: Dave (both rulings given at the Phase 23 discuss sitting, before planning and before any criteria were written). **What raised it.** The Phase 23 ROADMAP entry was first drafted carrying all twelve condemned trees and quoting `D-IMPL-189` point 1 verbatim, including its clause *"their paired tests moved with them"*. Dave challenged the first half — *"Isn't the s1 pair what we just completed, client side examples?"* — and the check falsified the entry rather than the question. **RULING 1 — `CLNT-17` and the `s1` pair are EXCLUDED from Phase 23 and `CLNT-17` stays `Not built`.** The client-side pair is `examples/hw1-companies-over-revenue` (created 2026-08-16, Phases 17/18) and `examples/hw1-harness-clients` (2026-08-20, Phase 20), neither condemned; `examples/s1-00-companies-over-revenue` (2026-08-14) is the PREDECESSOR that `hw1-companies-over-revenue` rebuilt — same scenario, its README titled *"HW-1 — companies over a revenue threshold you choose"* — and `examples/s1-01-hello-context-product` (2026-08-10) is not a client example at all. Three measurements exclude them, and the argument is NOT cost-versus-benefit: **(a) the benefit is ZERO, not small** — neither `s1` tree is in the `examples:` aggregate (`example-s1-01` needs a Fluree server, `example-s1-00` needs Docker or `CCF_TEST_POSTGRES`), so both are ALREADY outside the always-on job that archiving exists to clear; **(b) archiving `s1-01` would make a `D-IMPL-189` commitment FALSE** — all 7 published references to the pair are to `s1-01`, all on `public/concepts/answers-no-document-contains.md` which Phase 22 shipped 2026-08-23, five of them `--8<--` includes, and `D-IMPL-189` forbids re-cutting published pages against the archive *"as though the archive were the teaching material"*; `s1-00` has ZERO published references; **(c) both trees are LIVE FIXTURES FOR CORE SUITES, not example tests** — `s1-00` is named by 11 test files including `tests/deployment/test_config_derivation.py`, `test_config_document.py`, `test_config_equivalence.py` and a `tests/deployment/fixtures/s1-00-multifile/` tree, and `s1-01` by 6 including `tests/products/test_gate_two_call_shape.py`, `test_request_contract.py`, `test_resolver_seam.py`, `tests/replay/test_engine_rehydration.py` and `tests/halflife/test_debt.py`. **RULING 2 — the ten trees' SOURCES move; their paired tests REMAIN under `tests/` and are re-pointed at the archive paths.** This amends `D-IMPL-189` point 1 and the old and new clauses are both named here per the standing policy `D-GATE-22` set for `D-IMPL-188` (*a pin moves only by an explicit entry naming the old pin, the new pin and why*). **OLD:** *"their paired tests moved with them"*. **NEW:** the paired tests stay under `tests/` and are re-pointed. **The measurement that decided it:** `pyproject.toml:142` sets `testpaths = ["tests"]`, so moving the paired tests OUT of `tests/` removes them from the suite entirely; `tests/examples` collects **515 tests**, and the suite baseline is **4105 passed / 118 skipped**, byte-for-byte identical across `D-GATE-21`, `D-GATE-21.1`, `D-GATE-22` and `D-GATE-22.1`, each of which cites it as the mechanical proof that the phase changed no behaviour. Moving them would drop the suite to roughly 3590 and move that baseline for the first time — to achieve a DOCUMENTATION archive. `D-IMPL-189`'s clause was written before anyone checked `testpaths`, which is why this is an amendment on a measurement rather than a preference. **The 4105 / 118 baseline is expected to HOLD across Phase 23 and is to be written as a Success Criterion at the sitting.** **TWO FINDINGS ABOUT `CLNT-17` RAISED HERE AND EXPRESSLY NOT RULED — no plan in Phase 23 may act on either.** (1) `CLNT-17`'s stated blocker is WRONG ON THE TREE: its cell says deleting `s1-01` removes *"the last shipped `examples/` call site of `ccf.products.request::refuse_request`"*, which is why `17-08-SUMMARY.md` carries `status: blocked-at-task-3`; there are THREE `.py` call sites and two are in `s1-00` — `s1-00/consume.py`, `s1-00/produce.py`, `s1-01/spine.py`. The premise has been carried unexamined since Phase 17. (2) `CLNT-17` may be MIS-FRAMED as an example-retirement row at all, given (c) above; if the `s1` pair is core test infrastructure then *"retire these example trees"* is the wrong obligation and will keep reading as owed work nobody can safely do. **What this does not change.** `D-IMPL-189` points 2, 3 and 4 stand unamended — `Complete` still means deletion plus the re-cut, `Partial` is still split on the same seam, and the `Partial` verdict is still written in the archive phase when the state exists on the tree. Nothing is deleted, so `D-27`'s undecided `00`–`08` half and `D-IMPL-176` point 2 still do not bind. It does not re-scope `DOCS-14` or `EXAM-02`. **Governs:** the scope of Phase 23; the disposition of the paired tests; the exclusion of `CLNT-17`. **Related:** `D-IMPL-189` (amended at point 1), `D-IMPL-188` and `D-GATE-22` (the naming policy this entry follows), `D-IMPL-176` point 2, `D-27`, `D-08`, `D-GATE-19`, `D-GATE-22`, `D-GATE-22.1`, `D-11`, `D-15`, `D-19`, `D-IMPL-174`.

**D-IMPL-191 — Phase 23 sitting: archive location, runnability, the sweep's ownership table, and what `Partial`'s done-limb may claim. Amends `D-IMPL-189` point 3's "out of live CI" wording.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-08-24. Approver: Dave (four rulings taken together at the Phase 23 discuss sitting, before planning and before criteria were written). **RULING 1 — the archive lives OUTSIDE `examples/`.** The ten trees move to an archive location that is not a subdirectory of `examples/`, so that `examples/` continues to mean *things we teach with*. Ten of the twelve remaining subdirectories being archive reads worse to a newcomer than an `examples/` holding only the `hw1-*` and `s1-*` trees. Mechanically neutral: `pymdownx.snippets` resolves `base_path` against the repo root rather than `public/`, so includes resolve from either location. **RULING 2 — the archive STAYS RUNNABLE, but ships NO `make` targets.** It must stay importable and executable regardless of preference, because two condemned-tree tests actually execute rather than read — `tests/examples/test_cross_process_output.py` and `tests/examples/test_ext00_hardening.py` (6 of the 31 files under `tests/examples` invoke `subprocess`/`runpy`, and the other four are `hw1`, which is not condemned). All ten `example-0N`-family targets are DROPPED rather than renamed to an archive form: a `make` target is an invitation to run, and these are no longer the teaching path. **RULING 3 — the sweep's `Retirement` table is RE-POINTED and archived paths STILL COUNT as couplings.** `tools/retirement_sweep.py` lines 131-167 hardcode the twelve trees against owning plans `16-15`, `16-17`, `16-18` and `17-08` — a RETIRED phase (`D-IMPL-152`) and a plan that blocked at task 3 — so no live plan owns those rows today. The ten moved trees re-point to Phase 23 plans. An archived path CONTINUES to count as a live coupling, because deletion is still owed and the coupling is still a real obligation; making the sweep blind to the archive would reproduce the exact defect Phase 22.1 was commissioned to fix — a tool that reports clean because it did not look. **RULING 4 — the done-limb says "out of the `examples:` aggregate", NOT "out of live CI".** This AMENDS `D-IMPL-189` point 3, and both clauses are named per the standing policy `D-GATE-22` set for `D-IMPL-188`. **OLD:** *"limb done — out of live CI, sources preserved under archive, includes re-pointed, strict build green"*. **NEW:** *limb done — out of the `examples:` aggregate, sources preserved under archive and still exercised by the test leg, includes re-pointed, strict build green*. **The measurement that decided it:** after the move the trees leave the eleven-member `examples:` aggregate (`Makefile:256`), of which ten are condemned and the sole survivor is `example-hw1-harness-clients` — but they do NOT leave CI. Under `D-IMPL-190` ruling 2 the paired tests stay under `tests/`, so **25 of the 31 `tests/examples` files still READ the archived sources and 2 still EXECUTE them**. A cell reading *"out of live CI"* would therefore be false on the day it is written, which is the `RECON-09` failure — the difference between a verdict and a hope — and the same class `D-IMPL-190` was raised to avoid. The `DOCS-17` cell must additionally NAME what still exercises the archived trees, rather than leaving the reader to discover it. **What this does not change.** `D-IMPL-189` points 2 and 4 stand unamended — `Complete` still means deletion plus the re-cut, and the `Partial` verdict is still written in the archive phase when the state exists on the tree. Nothing is deleted, so `D-27`'s undecided `00`–`08` half and `D-IMPL-176` point 2 still do not bind. `CLNT-17` remains excluded and `Not built` per `D-IMPL-190` ruling 1. **Governs:** the archive location; the disposition of the `make` targets; the sweep's ownership table and its treatment of archived paths; the wording available to `DOCS-17`'s `Partial` cell. **Related:** `D-IMPL-190` (the same sitting's first two rulings), `D-IMPL-189` (amended at point 3), `D-IMPL-188` and `D-GATE-22` (the naming policy this entry follows), `D-GATE-22.1` (the fail-closed sweep this ruling relies on), `D-IMPL-152`, `RECON-09`, `D-08`, `D-11`, `D-19`.

**D-IMPL-192 — Phase 23 criterion **14** is amended to permit EXACTLY FOUR documentary path-string updates under `src/`/`runtime/`, and nothing else. The stale-node-id hole in `src/`/`runtime/` is logged as backlog, not closed here.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-08-24. Approver: Dave (Option 1 of three presented before research; ruling given pre-planning, so no plan was written against the superseded wording). **A NUMBERING CORRECTION FIRST, because the ruling was requested and given against the wrong ordinal.** The exchange called the diff-empty criterion *"criterion 13"*; on the tree it is **criterion 14**. Criterion 13 is `CLNT-17`'s BYTE-IDENTICAL protection — the one thing the same sitting said not to weaken — so amending 13 would have done the opposite of what was ruled. Dave's ruling text names the criterion by CONTENT (*"`src/`, `runtime/`, `pyproject.toml` diff-empty"*), which is unambiguous, and that is the criterion amended. **Criterion 13 is untouched.** **What raised it.** The Phase 23 sitting locked criterion 14 requiring `src/`, `runtime/` and `pyproject.toml` to be diff-empty. `docs/surface/examples/RETIREMENT-COUPLINGS.md` files **9 coupling rows inside `src/` and `runtime/`**, and **4 of them name condemned trees this phase moves**. They are not loose prose: they are `path::symbol` NODE IDS — the checked citation form — inside shipped library docstrings, and `tools/lints/citations.py:154-155` puts `src` and `runtime` in the lint's scope. **THE MEASUREMENT THAT MADE IT BLOCKING, TAKEN BY SABOTAGE RATHER THAN BY ARGUMENT.** `src/ccf/products/bind.py:74` was repointed from `examples/04-cross-process/producer_child.py::resolve` to `archive/examples/04-cross-process/producer_child.py::resolve` — a path that does not exist — and `python -m tools.lints --all` **EXITED 0 with zero mentions of the rule, the file or the bad path**; the file was then restored byte-identical (`git diff --quiet` clean). `cite03-node-id` treats a node id whose PATH does not resolve as UNCHECKED rather than as a finding. Phase 22's `test_every_published_node_id_resolves` closes exactly this hole but covers `public/` ONLY. **So without this amendment the phase would ship four citations in library code pointing at nothing, with no gate able to say so — this project's own defect class arriving inside `src/` PRECISELY BECAUSE the criterion forbade touching `src/`.** **THE RULING — Option 1 of three.** Criterion 14 is amended. **OLD:** *`src/`, `runtime/` and `pyproject.toml` are diff-empty against the phase base.* **NEW:** the same, **EXCEPT** the four path-string-only citation updates enumerated below — and nothing else under `src/`, `runtime/` or `pyproject.toml`. The four, by file and line: **(1)** `src/ccf/products/bind.py:74`, `examples/04-cross-process/producer_child.py::resolve` → `archive/examples/04-cross-process/producer_child.py::resolve`; **(2)** `runtime/ccf_runtime/mcp/egress.py:306`, same `04-cross-process` target; **(3)** `runtime/ccf_runtime/mcp/experience.py:334`, same `04-cross-process` target; **(4)** `runtime/ccf_runtime/mcp/experience.py:483`, `examples/external/00-hello-context/serve.py::context_provider` → `archive/examples/external/00-hello-context/serve.py::context_provider`. **Each change must be proven PATH-STRING-ONLY** — no symbol, signature, behaviour or surrounding prose altered — and the unmoved **4105 passed / 118 skipped** baseline is the mechanical proof that no behaviour changed. **THE FIVE `s1-01` CITATIONS ARE NOT TOUCHED** (`runtime/ccf_runtime/mcp/egress.py:304`, `runtime/ccf_runtime/mcp/experience.py:332`, `src/ccf/products/bind.py:76`, `src/ccf/products/request.py:365` and `:558`), because `s1-01` is not moving (`D-IMPL-190` ruling 1). **CRITERION 14 IS NOT WIDENED BEYOND THESE FOUR LINES.** A fifth edit under `src/`/`runtime/`/`pyproject.toml` in this phase is a scope breach, and the amended criterion is to be written so that it enumerates the four rather than describing a category — a category admits the next edit, an enumeration does not. **WHAT WAS REJECTED AND WHY.** *Option 2* (leave them stale, record them as knowingly stale) was rejected: it ships four dangling `path::symbol` citations in library docstrings that no gate will ever catch, which is the same defect class one tree over. *Option 3* (close the lint hole for all of `src/`/`runtime/` in this phase) was rejected as scope: it is real work, it is `D-06`'s twin, and it does not belong in an archive move whose criteria were already locked. **BACKLOG, LOGGED HERE SO IT IS NOT LOST** (this project keeps no backlog file; carried items live in this log and in the phase's `<deferred>` section): **a standing check that every `path::symbol` node id under `src/` and `runtime/` RESOLVES — the counterpart to Phase 22's `tools/docs_tests/test_adoption_wording.py::test_every_published_node_id_resolves`, which covers the published tree only.** It is the durable fix for the class this entry works around, and until it exists the workaround is a workaround. **Governs:** the wording of Phase 23 criterion 14 and the exact set of files a Phase 23 plan may touch under `src/`/`runtime/`. **Related:** `D-IMPL-190` and `D-IMPL-191` (the same phase's earlier rulings), `D-GATE-19` (criteria before Wave 1 — this amendment is PRE-planning, not retroactive), `D-IMPL-188` and `D-GATE-22` (the old-clause/new-clause naming policy this entry follows), `D-06`, `D-GATE-22` (the published-tree node-id check), `D-11`, `D-19`, `D-IMPL-174`.

**D-IMPL-193 — `CLNT-30`/`H-14`'s "stays CI-green" is CLARIFIED to mean ITS TESTS KEEP PASSING, not that the tree stays in the always-on `examples:` aggregate. `examples/external/00-hello-context/` therefore moves with the other nine and Phase 23 carries TEN trees, not nine.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-08-24. Approver: Dave (ruled pre-planning, after the Phase 23 researcher surfaced the collision). **What raised it.** The Phase 23 researcher performed the archive move against a scratch tree and found **five standing tests went red on `examples/external/00-hello-context/` alone**, then traced them to a Dave-RATIFIED requirement that none of `D-IMPL-189`, `D-IMPL-190`, `D-IMPL-191` or `D-IMPL-192` names. `CLNT-30` reads: *"`examples/external/00-hello-context/` stays CI-green and is marked historical in prose under an existing README heading, stating that its clients target the pre-Phase-17 surface over HTTP with bearer auth and that Phase 20's trio is canonical going forward (criterion 8, second half; `H-14`)"*, and `H-14` was ratified as recorded by `D-IMPL-167` (Dave, 2026-08-21). `DOCS-17` condemns that same tree as one of its ten. **Moving it without naming `CLNT-30` would have been a SILENT OVERRIDE of a ratified ruling — precisely what the `D-IMPL-188` policy exists to stop — which is why this is an amendment entry and not an executor's reading.** **THE AMBIGUITY, STATED AS BOTH READINGS RATHER THAN RESOLVED BY ASSERTION.** *"Stays CI-green"* admits two: **(a)** its tests keep passing; **(b)** it remains a member of the always-on `examples:` aggregate. Under (a) the archive move satisfies `CLNT-30` untouched, because `D-IMPL-190` ruling 2 keeps the paired tests under `tests/` where they continue to run. Under (b) the phase would drop to NINE trees and 226 files, and criteria 1, 2, 3 and 14 would each need amending. **THE RULING — reading (a).** **OLD (the reading the clause could bear):** *stays in the always-on `examples:` job.* **NEW (clarified):** *historical, and CI-green VIA ITS TESTS; it may leave the `examples:` aggregate and live under `archive/examples/external/00-hello-context/`.* All TEN trees move; the set is NOT reduced to nine; its `example-ext-00` target is dropped with the other nine. **WHAT THIS RULING DOES NOT DO.** It does **not** override *"marked historical"* — that prose obligation stands and the README heading stays. It does **not** authorize deleting the tree. It does **not** authorize dropping or weakening the tests that still execute it — `tests/examples/test_ext00_hardening.py` is one of the two executing tests criterion 8 names, and the five tests the researcher watched go red must be RE-POINTED and GREEN, not retired. A plan that satisfies this ruling by removing a test rather than re-pointing it is a scope breach. **DAVE'S REASONING, RECORDED BECAUSE IT IS THE PART A LATER READER WILL WANT.** The archive phase's goal is honest quarantine, not keeping condemned trees in the teaching aggregate; *"CI-green"* read as *tests still pass* preserves the ratification without blocking `DOCS-17` from reaching `Partial`; and keeping one condemned tree in `examples:` for a soft reading of `CLNT-30` would re-create the newcomer-facing problem `D-IMPL-191` ruling 1 already rejected. **Governs:** the membership of Phase 23's tree set at TEN; the reading of `CLNT-30`/`H-14` from here forward. **Related:** `D-IMPL-167` (the ratification), `CLNT-30`/`H-14`, `DOCS-17`, `D-IMPL-189`, `D-IMPL-190` (ruling 2, which is what makes reading (a) true), `D-IMPL-191` ruling 1, `D-IMPL-192`, `D-IMPL-188` and `D-GATE-22` (the old-clause/new-clause policy this entry follows), `D-GATE-19`.

**D-IMPL-194 — Phase 23's locked criteria set goes from SIXTEEN to EIGHTEEN: two enumerated mechanism fixes without which the move is neither achievable nor honest. The coupling report's source blindness is BACKLOG, not Phase 23 scope.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-08-24. Approver: Dave (approved pre-planning, on the measurements below; same footing as `D-IMPL-192`'s criterion-14 amendment). **What raised it.** The Phase 23 researcher performed the archive move against a scratch tree and reported three defects; all three were VERIFIED against the tree before being acted on, per `CLAUDE.md` §3.1, and the verification corrected the researcher's framing on one of them. **OLD SET:** sixteen criteria. **NEW SET:** eighteen — criteria 1-16 unchanged, plus the two below. **CRITERION 17 — `tools/publish_scan.py::INCLUDE_ALLOWED_PREFIXES` admits the archive root, and a test GUARDS that tuple, watched RED by removing a prefix.** Measured: the constant is `("examples/", "public/", "perf/baselines/")` and its own comment states it is *"a POSITIVE allowlist, because the charter is default-deny"*. `archive/` is not a member, so **every re-pointed include becomes a publication-boundary violation and `make docs-strict` cannot go green by re-pointing alone.** The fix is one line; the criterion exists because of the second half: a grep for any test naming that tuple returned NOTHING, so the boundary is unguarded, and widening an unguarded default-deny boundary as a side effect of getting a build green is exactly the move this project refuses. The widening is deliberate and provable or it does not happen. **CRITERION 18 — `tools/docs_tests/test_no_stale_example_paths.py::PATH_TOKEN` no longer strips a leading `archive/`, with controls in BOTH directions.** Measured live against the shipped regex: its negative lookbehind is `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]` and omits `/`, so the string *see archive/examples/04-cross-process/producer_child.py* yields the token `examples/04-cross-process/producer_child.py` — the `archive/` prefix silently stripped — which is then resolved against a path that will not exist after the move. **A CORRECTLY RE-POINTED PAGE THEREFORE PRODUCES FALSE OFFENDERS AND THE TEST IS RED ON A CORRECT TREE.** Criterion 5 names this module as the witness that must fail INDEPENDENTLY of the strict build, so criterion 5 is unachievable until this is fixed. The fix is one character; **the controls are required in both directions because a one-character widening of a lookbehind can blind the check entirely** — a correctly re-pointed page must yield ZERO offenders AND a genuinely stale `examples/…` path must still yield at least one. `tests/examples` continues to match through its own alternation branch. **THE THIRD FINDING WAS CONFIRMED BUT ITS FRAMING WAS CORRECTED, AND THE CORRECTION IS WHY NO COUNT CHANGED.** The researcher reported that `docs/surface/examples/RETIREMENT-COUPLINGS.md` is blind to the phase's two heaviest populations and warned *"do not plan from its counts"*. The blindness is real and measured: **267 rows, of which only 175 target the ten trees**; `public/tutorial/adopters-guide.md` appears in the report ONLY as the target of two rows and NEVER as a source, though it carries **35** includes into the ten; `public/tutorial/demo-walkthrough.md` carries **14** and sources zero rows; the eleven `tests/examples/test_*_output.py` modules source zero. **But the locked criteria never used those counts.** Criteria 4 and 6 cite 102 includes + 9 prose paths across 15 pages = 111, which are direct `git grep` measurements re-verified 2026-08-24, and `D-08`'s pinned figure. So the warning is sound and the conclusion does not follow: **no criterion rested on a number the inventory cannot see, and no count is amended.** **BACKLOG, EXPLICITLY NOT PHASE 23 SCOPE:** the sweep's SOURCE detection, which does not file rows for `adopters-guide.md`, `demo-walkthrough.md` or the `test_*_output.py` modules. **This is a DIFFERENT defect from the one Phase 22.1 closed** — 22.1 made the tool FAIL CLOSED when it could not examine a module; this is a tool that examines successfully and does not SEE. Fixing it is not an archive move. Logged beside the other Phase 23 backlog item (`D-IMPL-192`: a standing check that node ids under `src/` and `runtime/` resolve). **ALSO NOT IN THIS PHASE:** `CLNT-17`, and the `s1` trees. **A PROCEDURAL NOTE THAT IS PART OF THE RULING'S PROVENANCE.** The criterion-14 amendment in `D-IMPL-192` was itself written with line-anchored Python citations and turned `tests/invariants/test_citation_coverage.py::test_the_unanchored_python_citation_population_cannot_regrow` RED at `aefd072` (2 against a ceiling of 0, `D-IMPL-123`). It was fixed at `c2a117c` by CONVERTING to symbol form per `D-IMPL-114`, never by raising the ceiling — the Phase 21.1 wave 9 precedent. **Criteria 17 and 18 are written in symbol form for the same reason**, and any future amendment to this set must be. **Governs:** the Phase 23 criteria set at EIGHTEEN. **Related:** `D-IMPL-192` (the first amendment to this set), `D-IMPL-193`, `D-IMPL-190`, `D-IMPL-191`, `D-IMPL-189`, `D-IMPL-114`, `D-IMPL-123`, `D-GATE-19`, `D-IMPL-188` and `D-GATE-22` (the old-set/new-set naming policy), `D-GATE-22.1` (the fail-closed sweep, whose defect class this backlog item is NOT), `D-01` (publication default-deny), `D-20`.

**D-IMPL-195 — the two Wave-1 stop-and-asks are RULED, and criteria 3 and 12 are AMENDED: fourteen make targets deleted rather than ten, and criterion 12's "25 of 31" corrected to "19 of 31" on a re-measure that found the original figure was produced by a faulty regex.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-08-24. Approver: Dave (three rulings given after the plan set and the plan-checker report; pre-execution, nothing had run). **RULING 1 — THE FOUR LIVE-LEG TARGETS ARE DELETED, same treatment as the ten. Criterion 3 is AMENDED to enumerate FOURTEEN.** Measured: `example-03-live-ollama`, `example-03-live-anthropic`, `example-ext-00-live-anthropic` and `example-ext-00-live-adk` are declared in the `Makefile` and run `examples/03-harness-portability/run.py` and `examples/external/00-hello-context/run.py` — condemned trees both. Two are invoked by `.github/workflows/live-legs.yml` (the weekly `cron: "0 7 * * 1"` leg) and one is named in prose in `README.md`. **They were in a gap:** criterion 3 ENUMERATED ten and these four were not among them, while the same criterion forbids an archive-form replacement, so neither leaving them nor re-pointing them was authorized. Dave: *"Leaving them invites 'the teaching path.' Re-pointing into archive keeps CI load on unsupported trees."* **The targets are deleted, AND the cron entries that invoke them are dropped or adjusted so `live-legs.yml` does not go red on a missing target** — a deleted target with a live workflow still calling it is a broken workflow, not a retirement. **CRITERION 3 OLD:** *all ten of `example-00`…`example-08` and `example-ext-00` are DELETED, not renamed.* **CRITERION 3 NEW:** the same ten PLUS the four live-leg targets above — fourteen in total — with `live-legs.yml` carrying no reference to a deleted target. **The amendment is named here rather than left implicit, because a ruling that changes what must be true must also change the criterion that gates it; otherwise the criterion passes while the work is unverified.** **RULING 2 — THE FOURTEEN ORPHANED `RETIREMENT_SCHEDULE` ROWS ARE RE-POINTED TO PHASE 23 and their paths STILL COUNT as couplings.** Measured: the schedule holds 29 rows — 10 for the moved trees, 2 for the `s1` pair, 17 for neither; of those 17, three are `17-08`-owned and already disposed of by `D-IMPL-191` ruling 3, leaving **FOURTEEN owned by `16-15`/`16-17`/`16-18`, plans belonging to a phase `D-IMPL-152` RETIRED**: twelve `tests/examples/test_*.py` modules and `public/tutorial/adopters-guide.md` and `public/tutorial/demo-walkthrough.md`. The correction does not move the ruling, because it cuts the same way — `s1-00/produce.py::assemble_and_serve` is an independent, shipped, non-`s1-01` call site under `examples/`, so *"the last one"* is false under either reading. The reader's positive control is what makes the third file's empty result a finding rather than a blind spot: asked for `print`, the same reader returns `['main', 'report']` in `consume.py`, so it demonstrably reads the file that returns nothing for `refuse_request`; asked for `refuse_request_zzz` it returns nothing in all three. **And the gate the premise leans on does not say what the premise says it says**: `tools/docs_tests/test_resolver_seam_obligations.py::test_both_seams_cite_both_call_sites` requires each seam docstring to cite at least two DISTINCT example paths that resolve, and `::EXAMPLE_PREFIX` was widened by Phase 23 to `("examples/", "archive/examples/")`. Always batched"* — plus §10.3 invariant 3, *"Enrich is batched, always. One query per source per step."* No symbol in `src/` or `runtime/` implements this. Measured at `cfaa310`: `grep -rniE "enrich" --include=*.py src/ runtime/` returns **7 hits across 4 files**, all of them replay-trace enrichment or prose; the nearest structural neighbour, `src/ccf/projection/acquisition.py::ContentAcquirer`, acquires *content items* with a content hash rather than *attribute sets onto already-resolved references*. Controls on the same instrument: a class name that does not exist returns **0**, `class ContentAcquirer` returns **1**, and `^class .*Filter` returns **3** — so the zero is a measurement, not an instrument that could not fire. **CLASSIFICATION.** Per `D-08` it **PASSES**: Protocol-expressible on the exact `ContentAcquirer` precedent, and statable entirely without domain reference — references in, attribute names in, attributes out, batched, provenance recorded. Per `D-10` a remedy is **ADDITIVE**: as an operator its category would be `traversal`, and `src/ccf/operators/base.py::OperatorCategory` stays the closed four. **Per the `D-05` drift check there is NO divergence**: the Standard's own retired-names note (*"Batch Enrich — batch is mandatory, not a variant"*) shows the name was refined inside the Standard after the derivation rather than dropped from the SDK's requirements. **NOT BUILT, AND NOT PROPOSED FOR THIS PHASE** (`D-04`). `cp-00` reads one table and every attribute arrives in the row, so nothing here was blocked. `CP-SPEC-001` at Phase 24.2 spans five systems of record and is the first example that would exercise it for real. **THE PUBLISHED CLAIM THIS CREATES, already surfaced and accepted.** `D-63` limb (i) (Dave, 2026-08-26): the Standard→SDK operator mapping on `public/concepts/the-first-context-product.md` stays **MEASURED** — three of eight map 1:1 at L4, three land at other layers, `Evaluate` exists only as Π, and **`Enrich` is genuinely absent**. None is algebra** — no new operator category, no widening of `OperatorOutput`, no fourth gate, no change to the composition law. **THREE in TOOLING, not the SDK** — a numeric-majority blind spot in `tools/lints/no_hardcoding.py::_is_numeric_table`; no LLM-client import check reaching any example, because `tools/lints/__main__.py::RULE_TREE_SCOPE` scopes the `algorithmic` rule to `src` and `runtime` only; and nothing that ships gating criterion 9's four dataset statements. **A tooling blind spot is not a gap in what the fabric can express, and merging the two lists would manufacture a drift verdict out of three lint holes.** **THE DRIFT VERDICT (`D-05`).** *"A long gap list is a SIGNAL OF DRIFT, not a normal outcome."* Four seam-ergonomics findings across a full Standard-conforming specification is short, and the derivation held. Strongest single piece of evidence: the `Temporal` **inverse** asymmetry — the SDK holds `src/ccf/operators/categories.py::TemporalAsOf` as a first-class category exactly where the Standard folds it into a Traversal *mode*. **D-IMPL-213 — the short SDK phase `D-58` schedules is CONFIRMED, and it is scoped to `D-59` and `D-60` ONLY.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-08-27. Ruled by: Dave, at `D-GATE-24.1`. **The ruling.** `D-58` said: *"After `cp-00` is green, open a SHORT SDK PHASE for the two Protocol-shaped items — `build_operator_registry` has no deployment-operator seam, and `ContextAssemblerProtocol.assemble` cannot return a governed refusal — BEFORE the next CP example depends on them."* `cp-00` is now green and merged, so the precondition is met and the phase is confirmed to open **after** the `phase-24.1` merge. **WHAT IS IN SCOPE — exactly two, and they are the two `D-58` named.** `D-59`: `src/ccf/deployment/operators.py::build_operator_registry` gains a deployment-operator seam — it currently dispatches on artifact type and raises otherwise, so a deployment's own operator has no path into the operator plan's registry. Additive per `D-10`; Protocol-shaped per `D-08`. `D-60`: `src/ccf/agents/assembler.py::ContextAssemblerProtocol.assemble` gains a return channel for a governed refusal — it returns `AssemblyOutcome` and nothing else, so a conforming assembler receiving a refusal can only RAISE, in a codebase whose stated posture is that a refusal is DATA (`src/ccf/products/request.py::refuse_request` returns a `ProductRequestViolation`). **NOT additive** per `D-10` — widening a Protocol's return type makes every existing caller branch — which is the reason this is a scoped phase and not a drive-by, exactly as `D-57` requires: *"not two drive-bys inside 24.1."* **WHAT IS EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE, ruled at this gate rather than left to the planner.** The **other two** SDK-surface findings do NOT fold in: the empty-operator gate being two assertions sharing one name (any fix is a **fourth gate**, forbidden by `D-IMPL-102` limb 3), and `ProductClassDeclaration` carrying `max_ttl_key` with no field for the ceiling's seconds. The **three TOOLING findings** do NOT fold in either: the `_is_numeric_table` numeric-majority blind spot, the `RULE_TREE_SCOPE` hole that leaves examples unchecked for LLM-client imports, and the absence of any shipped gate on criterion 9's four dataset statements. **All five stay RECORDED and UNCLOSED.** So does `D-IMPL-212`'s `Enrich` absence, whose disposition — join this phase, wait for 24.2 where an example genuinely needs it, or be ruled a permanent documentation mapping — remains Dave's and is NOT settled here. **Why the fence is drawn at the gate.** A two-item phase that admits a third item is no longer short, and the two Protocol-shaped items are the only ones a *next* Context Product example is blocked by; the other five bound what a green gate means without bounding what the fabric can express. **A BOOKKEEPING CORRECTION carried into this entry.** `24.1-PRESSURE-TEST.md` §6.4 measured `D-IMPL-212` as the next free id and it was correct when written; Wave 9 then consumed it. Measured again at this gate: `D-IMPL-213` occurs **0** times in `docs/DECISIONS.md` and **0** times in `references/CCF_SDK_DE_REQUIREMENTS.md`, against a control of **4** occurrences of `D-IMPL-201` here — so the zeros come from an instrument that fires. `D-IMPL-202`…`211` remain RESERVED as the ten DE-requirement candidates. `D-31` — ids are stable, append only, nothing renumbered. **Related:** `D-GATE-24.1`, `D-IMPL-212`, `24-CONTEXT.md` `D-04`, `D-08`, `D-10`, `D-57`, `D-58`, `D-59`, `D-60`.

**D-IMPL-214 — Phase 24.1.1's `src/` fence is WIDENED BY EXACTLY ONE MODULE, to a NAMED ROSTER of three, and criterion 6 is discharged against the reference assembler rather than a test-local one.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-08-27. Ruled by: Dave. **WRITTEN BEFORE ANY EDIT, which is the whole point of it.** Criterion 9 as locked requires that a refusal returned as data land in the Decision Replay record *and* that any module needed beyond the two named in criterion 12 be **enumerated in a `D-IMPL` entry BEFORE any edit, silent widening being RED**. Planning research found that the two-module fence could not hold, the finding was verified against the tree rather than accepted from the reviewer, and this is that entry. **The mechanism worked as designed: the fence did not quietly move, it was moved on the record, before a line was written.** **WHAT WAS MEASURED, and every claim here was re-resolved against the tree at `a29bd0c` rather than taken from the research.** (1) `src/ccf/replay/record.py::build_replay_record` takes `execution: ExecutionResult` and `product: ContextProductContract` as **MANDATORY keyword arguments**; a refusal has neither, so it cannot be passed to the builder as the builder stands. (2) `src/ccf/products/resolver.py` returns `envelope_for(...)` on BOTH refusal branches — lines 693 and 746 — and calls `build_replay_record` at line 750, **after** those returns. (3) Therefore **NO refusal of any kind reaches the Decision Replay record today**, and criterion 9 asks for something NEW rather than the repair of something broken. That is stated plainly because it bears on how much of this belongs in a phase scoped as short. **THE RULING — READING B.** A refusal is recorded as a **named sub-structure on an existing replay dimension**, following the `hitl_actions` pattern already carried in `src/ccf/replay/record.py`: a **pre-serialized block with a sentinel default**, the same discipline `hitl_actions` and `workflow_step_sequence` use and which that module's own docstring names as a precedent. Dave: *"B is new persistence of refusal identity in the record without standing up a full refusal serve path."* **Reading A — persisting a real replay record for a refusal — is REFUSED for this phase** because it drags `src/ccf/replay/serve.py` and `src/ccf/products/resolver.py` in, and *"A pulls serve.py and resolver.py into a short phase."* **Reading C — record nothing — is REFUSED because it does not satisfy criterion 9's words**, and a criterion is not discharged by narrowing it to what is convenient (`D-38`). **THE ADMITTED SET, AS A NAMED ROSTER JUDGED BY SET EQUALITY — NOT AS A COUNT.** `src/` edits in Phase 24.1.1 are confined to exactly these three files and their tests: **`src/ccf/deployment/operators.py`** (the `D-59` seam), **`src/ccf/agents/assembler.py`** (the `D-60` return channel and the reference assembler's refusal path), and **`src/ccf/replay/record.py`** (this widening, and this widening only). **Any file outside that roster requires a NEW RULING, not a plan decision.** The roster form is deliberate and follows `24-CONTEXT.md` `D-66`, where Dave refused a bare count for exactly this failure: *"next claimant is silent if someone deletes a name from the list and the count stays 2."* A roster reports three faults where a ceiling reports one — arrival, departure, and the **swap** that holds the cardinality while moving the membership. **A NOTE ON THE COUNT, recorded rather than silently reconciled** (`D-19`, `D-IMPL-174`): the ruling as given said *"A fifth file is a new ruling"* while the roster it names holds **three** members. The ROSTER is operative and the cardinality is not; this entry is judged by membership, and any file not named above is outside it whether it would have been the fourth or the fifth. Each member is proven to name a **tracked** file, against a control — the misspelled `src/ccf/replay/reccord.py` is correctly untracked — because a misspelled pathspec diffs empty exactly like a clean one (the `VAC-01` guard). **CRITERION 6 — THE REFERENCE ASSEMBLER GAINS THE REFUSAL PATH.** `src/ccf/agents/assembler.py::DeterministicAssembler` is what deployments diff their own assembler against. Dave: *"If only a test-local assembler can refuse, the reference impl still demonstrates 'raise or succeed' and criterion 6 becomes theater."* Bounded explicitly: **ONE call into the existing `src/ccf/products/request.py::refuse_request` / `ProductRequestViolation` shape, plus a test watched RED. NO second vocabulary. NO domain rules taught to the reference implementation** — which is the same line `CLAUDE.md` §11 draws between mechanism and values, and which `DeterministicAssembler`'s own docstring already holds by consulting nothing and returning Π's payload unchanged. **A HAZARD THE RESEARCH RAISED THAT DOES NOT FIRE, verified rather than assumed.** The research warned that minting any new refusal type forces an edit to a fourth module, `src/ccf/products/refusal.py`, because `REFUSAL_KINDS` is closed by set equality against a structural walk — *"a route that is not replay, which criterion 12's PLUS clause does not cover."* **True in general, and it does not apply to the ruled design.** `src/ccf/products/request.py::ProductRequestViolation` is **ALREADY a `REFUSAL_KINDS` member** — measured by direct import, **16 members**, with `GateRefusal` as the control proving the instrument fires. The ruled shape REUSES it and mints nothing, so `refusal.py` stays outside the roster and stays unedited. **Had a new type been minted, this entry would have had to name a fourth file or the design would have had to change; it does neither, and that is a measurement rather than a hope.** **WHAT THIS ENTRY DOES NOT DO.** It does not amend criterion 9, 12 or any other criterion — the criteria are LOCKED (`D-GATE-19`, `D-IMPL-174`) and amending one to fit what execution turned out to want is the `D-38` shape, the violation rather than the remedy. It does not admit `serve.py` or `resolver.py`. It does not close, touch or reopen anything on the `D-IMPL-213` fence: the empty-operator gate (a fix would be a FOURTH GATE, `D-IMPL-102` limb 3), `ProductClassDeclaration`'s max-TTL-seconds field, the three tooling blinds, and `D-IMPL-212`'s `Enrich` absence all stay RECORDED and UNCLOSED. It creates no `OperatorCategory`, touches no composition law, and authorizes no second shipped example tree (criterion 16). **Numbering, measured before appending because getting it wrong collides with a reserved id.** `D-IMPL-214` occurs **0** times in `docs/DECISIONS.md` and **0** times in `references/CCF_SDK_DE_REQUIREMENTS.md`, against a control of **5** occurrences of `D-IMPL-201` here — so the zeros come from an instrument that fires. `D-IMPL-202`…`211` remain RESERVED as the ten DE-requirement candidates; `212` and `213` are consumed. `D-31` — ids are stable, append only, nothing renumbered. **Governs:** the Phase 24.1.1 `src/` roster; the Reading-B shape of criterion 9's discharge; and criterion 6's discharge against the reference assembler. **Related:** `D-GATE-24.1`, `D-IMPL-213` (the fence this widens by one and otherwise leaves intact), `D-IMPL-212`, `24-CONTEXT.md` `D-58`, `D-59`, `D-60`, `D-66` (the roster-not-a-ceiling form), `D-GATE-19` and `D-IMPL-174` (criteria locked before Wave 1), `D-38` (a proof that drifts outside the clauses is the violation, not the criteria).

**D-IMPL-215 — one pinned replay-record address in an ARCHIVED transcript is moved, and this is NOT a general right to edit `archive/`.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-08-28. Ruled by: Dave, during Phase 24.1.1 Wave 5. **THE FACT.** `D-IMPL-214` Reading B added `assembly_refusal` to `src/ccf/replay/record.py::ContentGenerationPath`, which changes the canonical bytes of every `src/ccf/replay/record.py::DecisionReplayRecord` and therefore its `content_hash`. `archive/examples/08-e2e-demo/artifacts/expected_output.txt` pins that address in its stage-6 narration, so `tests/examples/test_e2e_demo_output.py::test_the_staged_narration_matches_the_committed_transcript` went RED at commit `04ae21b` — **before Wave 5 touched anything**, confirmed by stashing Wave 5's edits and re-running. **THE MOVE.** `75365e18f4a1a675…` → `51f853861b2a8602…`, at `archive/examples/08-e2e-demo/artifacts/expected_output.txt` line 46, and **nowhere else**. The old address occurs seven other times in the tree — in `.planning/phases/15.6-*` records, `docs/surface-changes/15.6-12-*` and `15.6-13-*`, `docs/SURFACE-CHANGES.md`, and Phase 24.1.1's own Wave 5 SUMMARY. **Every one of those is a DATED RECORD describing what was true when it was written, and not one was altered** — the same discipline `D-GATE-24.1` applied when a rename stranded citations in historical entries: a historical entry is not falsified to suit a later change. **THE GUARD WAS HONOURED, NOT BYPASSED.** That test's docstring states: *"A failure here is **not** to be fixed by regenerating `artifacts/expected_output.txt` until the diff has been read line by line and every changed line traced to a deliberate change in the code or the artifacts. Narration edited to make a comparison pass is the exact failure mode the byte-identity discipline exists to prevent."* The diff WAS read line by line. **EXACTLY ONE LINE of the six-stage transcript differs** — the replay-record address. Every source-system count, row count, checksum verdict, envelope count, canonical-node count, operator count, entities-served and typed-edges-served figure, every gate verdict, the agent identity, the archetype, the skill invoked, the ring size, all five ring members, the freshness value to eighteen decimal places, **and the skill-set-in-force hash** are byte-identical; and the `dimensions` line still reads *"fabric snapshot, policy bindings, model version, perspective, generation path"* — five, so `INV-CH7-80` holds in the narration itself. The one changed line traces to a deliberate, ruled change. **PRECEDENT, which makes this a procedure rather than an intrusion.** `docs/surface-changes/15.6-13-source-refresh-window.md` records this exact move being performed before — `7d0a3d6061118799…` → `75365e18f4a1a675…`, on this same file, when `source_refresh_recency` landed on the same dimension. Moving the pin when the record's bytes deliberately change is established practice; what is new is only that the file now sits under `archive/` after Phase 23's move. **WHAT THIS RULING DOES NOT GRANT.** It is **not** a general right to edit `archive/`. Dave, at the ruling: *"Do not treat this as a general right to edit `archive/`. `D-07` still bars bulk retrofit of archived example code."* Measured at the gate commit: **0 archived `.py` files changed** — no archived example CODE was touched, only one pinned expectation that a ruled SDK change invalidated. **CRITERION 17 SURVIVES, and it was re-measured rather than assumed:** `archive/examples/` still holds **265** files; `git diff --diff-filter=D` and `--diff-filter=R` against `phase-24.1.1-base` are both **empty**; `--diff-filter=M` names **exactly one** file, this transcript, against a positive control reporting **2** on `examples/` so the filter is proven to fire. `D-IMPL-201`'s keep-quarantine of the archive is unaffected and deletion remains owed. **WHY OPTION B WAS REFUSED.** Leaving the test red makes criterion 19 — `make ci` green at the gate commit — **unreachable**, so the phase could not close on a defect that is a correct consequence of a ruling already made. Dave: *"B makes the gate impossible. Don't take it."* **A FINDING ABOUT THE VERIFICATION, recorded because it is the more useful half.** Wave 4's regression sweep did not catch this, because the sweep ran `tests/replay tests/products tests/agents tests/deployment tests/projection tests/client tests/mcp` — **a directory list chosen by the executor, which excluded `tests/examples`.** A green about a subset the measurer selected is this phase's own defect class landing in its own verification, and it is the second time in this phase a completeness proof was anchored on a hand-picked set rather than on the whole (`24.1.1-BASE.md` §0 is the first). The gate's sweep in `24.1.1-06` runs the full `make ci` recipe, not a directory list. **Governs:** the single pin move; the reading that criterion 17 is unbroken by a content-only modification; and the explicit refusal to generalize. **Related:** `D-IMPL-214` (the change whose bytes moved), `D-GATE-24.1`, `D-07` (no retrofitting), `D-IMPL-201` (the archive stays keep-quarantined, deletion owed), `D-16` (the byte-identity discipline this transcript enforces), `D-65` (never verify a claim against the document asserting it), and `docs/surface-changes/15.6-13-source-refresh-window.md` (the precedent).

**D-GATE-24.1.1 — Phase 24.1.1 (The Two Protocol-Shaped Seams — Deployment Operators and Refusal as Data) is APPROVED.** APPROVED. Date: 2026-08-28. Approver: Dave. **What is gated.** Seven plans in seven serial waves on branch `phase-24.1.1`, **eleven commits** from `phase-24.1.1-base` (`a29bd0c`), merged to `main --no-ff` naming this entry. `D-GATE-19` through `D-GATE-24.1` remain in force and are not amended. **All SEVENTEEN Success Criteria met**, locked in the ROADMAP entry 2026-08-27 **before planning and before Wave 1** per `D-GATE-19`'s forward binding, and **verified one-per-line by a CONTINUATION-LINE DETECTOR beside the count** — 17 ids, 1..17 contiguous, 0 continuation lines, the detector watched RED on a deliberately wrapped criterion **which the count read 17 in both runs**. The criteria block's sha256 at the close (`86c1ce4d…f15d2a6`) is **byte-identical** to the pin taken before Wave 1: not one criterion was authored, edited, renumbered or re-wrapped by execution. **WHAT THE PHASE SHIPPED.** `D-59` — `src/ccf/deployment/operators.py::build_operator_registry` gains a defaulted, keyword-only `deployment_operators: Sequence[Operator] = ()`, registered FIRST and sorted by `operator.key` through `register(operator)` with **no category argument**, so a deployment's own operator reaches the registry the operator plan resolves against. `D-60` — `src/ccf/agents/assembler.py::ContextAssemblerProtocol.assemble` returns `AssemblyOutcome | ProductRequestViolation`, and `src/ccf/agents/assembler.py::DeterministicAssembler` gains ONE optional `request_contract` field and ONE `refuse_request` call whose result it RETURNS, ordered AFTER the two identity checks. **Criterion 9** — a refusal has an identity in the Decision Replay record as a named sub-structure on dimension 5, sentinel-defaulted on the `hitl_actions` pattern, with a minting function, a write-time false-claim refusal and a block-admissibility check. **THE `src/` FENCE HELD, AS A NAMED ROSTER JUDGED BY SET EQUALITY.** `git diff --name-only phase-24.1.1-base -- src` names **exactly** `src/ccf/deployment/operators.py`, `src/ccf/agents/assembler.py` and `src/ccf/replay/record.py` — no fourth, re-asserted **after** the close-time fixes. Each member proven to name a **tracked** file against the misspelled `src/ccf/replay/reccord.py` control, which correctly fails, because a misspelled pathspec diffs empty exactly like a clean one (`VAC-01`). `runtime/` diff-empty, with the `src` diff as the positive control that the same instrument reports non-empty. **THE FENCE MOVED ONCE, ON THE RECORD, BEFORE AN EDIT.** Criterion 9's amendment required any module beyond the ruled two to be enumerated in a `D-IMPL` **before** any edit, silent widening being RED. Planning research found the two-module fence could not hold; the finding was verified against the tree rather than accepted from the reviewer; `D-IMPL-214` enumerated `replay/record.py`, refused Reading A by name, and bounded criterion 6's discharge. **That mechanism is the phase's most reusable result: the fence did not quietly move, it was moved deliberately and in public.** **THE §3.1 CLOSE PANEL READ THE SHIPPED TREE.** codex, cursor and gemini, `claude` excluded for independence, **238 KB of source INLINED across three bundles** rather than pointed at, nine invocations all rc=0, every payload on **stdin** — because a payload passed as a shell argument dies at `MAX_ARG_STRLEN` with `rc=126` and a 0-byte output indistinguishable from a clean review. Read-proofs against negative controls: **cursor 8/8, gemini 6/6, controls 0/2 and 0/1.** Subjects that went to no reviewer are NAMED in `24.1.1-CLOSE-REVIEWS.md` §1. **SEVEN BLOCKING FINDINGS, ALL FIXED IN-PHASE, THREE RE-SABOTAGED.** **THREE REVIEWERS INDEPENDENTLY FOUND ONE ROOT DEFECT**: `src/ccf/replay/record.py::_admissible_refusal_block` validated that a block *parsed* as a `ProductRequestViolation` and then returned the caller's own bytes, while the refusal it raises claimed it admitted only *"the canonical serialization"* — so one refusal admitted a FAMILY of blocks. **A replay-determinism defect inside criterion 9's own machinery, in code this phase wrote.** Fixed by re-canonicalising from the validated value. **THE PHASE'S WHOLE SUBJECT WAS UNGATED**: every control inspected `signature.parameters` and none inspected `return_annotation`, so narrowing `ContextAssemblerProtocol.assemble` back to `-> AssemblyOutcome` left the entire suite GREEN — `D-60`'s widening had no gate until the panel said so. **The documented identity-before-conformity ordering was never crossed** by any input; reversing it left every gate green. And **the phase's own public record cited a green over a set that excludes its subject**: a surface fragment offered *"`mypy` clean over 211 source files"* as evidence about `examples/`, which `[tool.mypy] files = ["src", "runtime"]` never reads — the exact defect class the phase spent itself on, in the document describing the phase. Also fixed: the example assembler still annotated `-> AssemblyOutcome` with a `Raises:` teaching raise-or-succeed; `deployment.py` and the specification still teaching that the `D-59` seam **does not exist**; and a closed-world gate saying *"both extended dimensions"* while testing one. **FIVE FINDINGS REJECTED AND RECORDED AS REJECTED**, each with its refuting command: a fabricated `serve.py` consumer (**0** `.assemble(` calls there, and **zero** `src`/`runtime` callers exist at all); a positional-argument bypass of a parameter that **does not exist** (`register(self, operator, *, version=None)`); a `REFUSAL_KINDS` removal claimed to leave the gate green which in fact turns it **RED at 4 failed**; a **pre-existing** `ASSEMBLER_ID` blamed on this phase; and an execution-ordering claim one reviewer independently refuted. **gemini resolved 6/6 citations and got five claims wrong — a resolved citation establishes that a reviewer LOOKED and nothing about whether it UNDERSTOOD.** **`make ci` GREEN AT THE GATE COMMIT** in the chunked FOREGROUND form: `make -n ci` printed FIRST and reconciled leg by leg, all ten legs rc=0, every exit code read **unpiped**. **THE CHUNKING DEVIATION IS NAMED, as `D-GATE-23` condition (3) requires:** the ten constituent commands were run individually in the foreground with the test leg split three ways, rather than as one `make ci` invocation, **because background jobs die at about ten minutes on this host and a killed run's output is indistinguishable from a pass**. Chunks proven a **PARTITION OF THE COLLECTED COUNT** — `1708 + 1515 + 1086 = 4309` = the unchunked collection — run to **4,191 passed / 118 skipped**. The collection moved 4,291 → 4,309 across the phase; the last three are gates the close panel bought. **`ls -d tests/*/` is never the basis**: Wave 1 recorded this phase's own partition proof failing that way, missing the 41 tests directly under `tests/*.py`. **CRITERIA RE-ASSERTED AT THE TRUE FINAL COMMIT, MECHANICAL AND DOCUMENTARY CLAIMS KEPT APART** — 12, 10, 17 and the `make ci` criterion RE-RUN; 1, 11, 10 and 16 **RE-READ** because close-time fixes touched their subjects; 13, 14 and 15 **PROVEN UNTOUCHED** by path-scoped diff. *"All seventeen re-asserted"* is deliberately not written as a single claim. **THE PHASE'S OWN DEFECT CLASS APPEARED IN ITS OWN MACHINERY IN EVERY WAVE, SEVEN FOR SEVEN, AND EVERY INSTANCE IS ON THE RECORD.** Among them: a criteria-extraction command that swept all 21 phase blocks and would have compared 210 lines against 210 at the gate and PASSED; a partition proof anchored on a directory listing; a call-site classifier using a line window that produced five false verdicts; a collision test that asserted *"a collision is fatal somewhere"* rather than that the seam's own registration is fatal, found because a sabotage went GREEN; a `run.py` branch whose deletion left the whole cp-00 suite green because both client tests assert `== 0`; six of nine surface entries silently dropped by a one-entry-per-section parser while three other instruments passed; and **stale `__pycache__` twice making a correct tree look broken.** **CRITERION 9 IS MET AS RULED AND NOT ABSOLUTELY, AND THE QUALIFIER IS IN ITS OWN ROW RATHER THAN A FOOTNOTE.** A caller who never calls the minter and hand-passes the sentinel while holding a refusal still produces a well-formed FALSE record; the block-shape check stops a fabricated block, not a truthful-looking silence. Closing it requires the refusal VALUE to travel into the builder — Reading A's shape, refused by `D-IMPL-214`. Named in the builder docstring, the surface fragment, the SUMMARY and `24.1.1-CLOSE-REVIEWS.md` §9. **WHAT THIS GATE DOES NOT DO.** It closes none of `D-IMPL-213`'s fenced-out items — the empty-operator gate, `ProductClassDeclaration`'s max-TTL-seconds field, the three tooling blinds and `D-IMPL-212`'s `Enrich` absence all remain RECORDED and UNCLOSED, verified as diffs against `24.1.1-BASE.md` with their own positive controls. It does not restructure `cp-00`, and it does not open a hygiene phase for the four tooling findings — both dispositions are `D-IMPL-216`. **Governs:** the Phase 24.1.1 approval; the reading of all seventeen criteria as met with criterion 9 qualified; the three-member `src/` roster as the phase's whole SDK footprint; and the chunked-foreground `make ci` reading. **Related:** `D-IMPL-213` (the fence), `D-IMPL-214` (the one-module widening, written before any edit), `D-IMPL-215` (the archived pin move), `D-IMPL-216` (the two residual dispositions), `D-GATE-24.1`, `D-GATE-23` condition (3), `D-GATE-19`, `D-IMPL-102` limb 3, `D-IMPL-137`/`D-66` (the roster-not-a-ceiling form this phase's fence follows), and the close record at `.planning/phases/24.1.1-the-two-protocol-shaped-seams-deployment-operators-and-re/24.1.1-CLOSE-REVIEWS.md`.

**D-IMPL-216 — two residuals from Phase 24.1.1 are RECORDED with named inheritors, and neither opens a phase.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-08-28. Ruled by: Dave, at `D-GATE-24.1.1`. **LIMB 1 — THE INVERSE REFUSAL ORDERING IN `cp-00`, NOT CORRECTED AT CLOSE.** `examples/cp-00-institutional-holders/assembler.py::HoldersAssembler.assemble` returns the governed `ProductRequestViolation` **before** its tenant and perspective checks; `src/ccf/agents/assembler.py::DeterministicAssembler.assemble` does the opposite, and this phase's close added the gate that keeps it that way. **So a caller asking a non-conforming question OF THE WRONG TENANT gets a contract refusal from the example and an identity refusal from the SDK, and the example is the teaching artifact.** Found by two reviewers at the close panel and verified on the tree. **Not corrected, deliberately.** The example learns its own tenant from the spine's return value (`assembled.tenant_id`), which exists only after assembly, so correcting the order means restructuring the example's data flow — `examples/cp-00-institutional-holders/deployment.py::tenant_id` reads it from config and would make the check possible earlier, but that is a redesign of the example's seam performed at close time under criterion 16, which fences rewriting `cp-00`. Dave: *"Do not restructure cp-00 at close … Correcting it is example data-flow, which criterion 16 fences."* **INHERITOR: the next Context Product example** — or a one-plan follow-on if the teaching tree is to be aligned sooner. **This is explicitly NOT a reopening of `D-59` or `D-60`**, both of which are closed and gated. **LIMB 2 — THE FOUR TOOLING FINDINGS GET AN INHERITOR, NOT A PHASE.** (1) The public-surface manifest records a Protocol's CONSTRUCTOR shape as `(*args, **kwargs)`, so widening a Protocol METHOD's return type — the single most consequential change in Phase 24.1.1 — moves **ZERO** manifest entries. (2) `unclaimed_drift` treats a drifting name as claimed when the name **or its dotted module** appears in any fragment, so a Phase 15 fragment silently claimed this phase's `ccf.deployment.operators` reshape. (3) `tools/assemble_surface_changes.py::_collect_fields` keeps ONE field-dict per `##` section, so a second `- Surface:` bullet **overwrites the first** — six of nine entries were silently dropped while `make surface-changes`, the assembled log and the drift gate all reported success, and only `tests/test_surface_completeness.py::test_every_diff_line_has_a_matching_public_log_entry` looked. (4) The same overwrite still affects `docs/surface-changes/19-02-the-adapter-seam-carries-bytes.md`, which stacks nine bullets under one heading; its entries are `tests/…` paths that never reach the manifest, so nothing has ever failed on it. **All four stay RECORDED and UNCLOSED, with the `DOCS-`/tools lane as the named inheritor.** Dave: *"No scoped hygiene phase now … Don't open a fourth phase this week. They are real; they are not what 24.1.1 was for."* **THE SIX ADVISORIES FROM THE CLOSE RIDE WITH THEIR INHERITORS** as recorded in `24.1.1-CLOSE-REVIEWS.md` §5, including the **pre-existing** `similarity = parameter` last-wins in `build_operator_registry` — present at `phase-24.1.1-base` and not introduced by `D-59` — and the unproven `sorted(deployment_operators, …)` discipline. **Numbering, measured at the gate commit rather than carried from memory**, as Dave required: `D-IMPL-216` occurs **0** times in `docs/DECISIONS.md` and **0** times in `references/CCF_SDK_DE_REQUIREMENTS.md`, against a control of **7** occurrences of `D-IMPL-201` here. `D-IMPL-202`…`211` remain RESERVED; `212`, `213`, `214` and `215` are consumed. `D-31` — ids are stable, append only, nothing renumbered. **Related:** `D-GATE-24.1.1`, `D-IMPL-213`, `D-IMPL-214`, `D-07` (no retrofitting), `D-IMPL-201` (the archive lane), and `24.1.1-CLOSE-REVIEWS.md` §5 and §7.

**D-IMPL-217 — every Context Product example ships a companion HTML documentation page, and `cp-00`'s is the reference realization.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-08-28. Ruled by: Dave. **What was ruled.** The page that had grown around `cp-00` was a **Phase 24.1 Wave 8 human-verify checkpoint** — six numbered questions put to Dave, with the example wrapped inside them. Dave ruled that the *example* half of it becomes a standing requirement for every Context Product the SDK demonstrates: *"the idea was to generate an html page like this for every example we demonstrate on developing Context Products."* Minted as **`EXAM-06`** in both ledger channels. **THE SHAPE, as approved.** (1) **Subject is the example and nothing else** — no phase, wave, gate, checkpoint or reviewer material. What was removed to get there is the measure of the rule: a masthead reading *"Wave 8 · checkpoint · gate blocking"* with a ribbon of `needs your ruling 5`, a section of executor findings, a tooling finding, the question numbering, every *"the plan asks…"* framing, and a footer inviting the reader to reply `approved`. (2) **A masthead naming the product and its shape** — stores, systems of record, assembly mode, declared operators — so a reader knows the scale of the thing before reading it. (3) **An authored SPINE, in order**: orientation, then **the build order**, then **the half the developer writes**, then what to change first and what would fail, closing with what the example is honest about *not* being. (4) **The build order names every file the developer completes, in dependency order**, and each file they fill in is **openable inline** rather than described. The order is not invented: it is the sequence Phase 24.1 itself built `cp-00` in — specification (front matter, §A–§C), then §D–§G with the assembly recipe, then the Control Plane artifacts, then the code, then the gates — and it holds because everything downstream is derived from something upstream. (5) **Every reproduction sits in a collapsible** — the printed run, the specification, `ccf_config.yaml`, the recipe artifact — so the page opens on guidance and reveals source on demand. Dave: *"This would allow me to view the yaml in html without bloating the document."* **WHY THE SPINE MATTERS MORE THAN THE REPRODUCTIONS, in Dave's words.** *"It's not clear to me what I have to do to develop a context product even a simple one like the one here… I don't even know what order I should operate in terms of filling out files and writing the implementation code."* The page had reproduced three whole documents and shown the fabric's half of the code — the half the adopter never writes — while naming the adopter's half without showing it. **A teaching page that reproduces everything and sequences nothing teaches nothing**, which is the defect this ruling closes. **TWO CLAUSES LEFT OPEN, and named rather than invented.** Whether the example README and the published concepts page are **reproduced inline or linked** — `cp-00` reproduces both, which makes the page carry two documents it does not own and accounts for most of its weight. And whether the **unlabelled *"which file is the SDK's?"* reveal** is required of every example or is `cp-00`'s alone — it is the sharpest device on the page for teaching the `[MECHANISM]`/`[ADAPT]` split and also the most expensive to produce per example. Both were surfaced at the ruling and neither was answered; **they are recorded as open rather than resolved by an executor** (`CLAUDE.md` §11). **THE REFERENCE REALIZATION.** `cp-00`'s page, at artifact `66047673-7537-4d21-addf-51f67b33f132`. It is **NOT yet in the repository** — it lives as a published artifact, and whether the template becomes a generator, a checked-in page under `public/`, or stays an artifact per example is not ruled here. **A DEFECT IN PRODUCING IT, recorded because it is the phase's own class.** The first strip classified a 108 KB block by its *first* heading, *"The published page"*, and dropped it — that block **was** the published concepts page reproduced, and nine example sections were its content, including *"The half you write"*. Nine of twenty sections vanished. It was caught by a section count of 11 against an expected 20 and a `<div>` balance of 58/60, and the rebuild neutralized the framing **in place** rather than excising ranges. **A container classified by its first label is the same defect as a green measured over the wrong universe.** **Governs:** the documentation obligation on every Context Product example; the ordering of its spine; and the collapsible treatment of reproductions. **Related:** `EXAM-06` (the ledger row this mints), `EXAM-01` (the seven-heading README obligation this sits beside), `24-CONTEXT.md` `D-21`, `D-GATE-24.1` and `D-GATE-24.1.1` (the phases whose example and seams the reference page documents), and `CLAUDE.md` §9 (the examples suite as the adoption contract).

**D-IMPL-218 — `EXAM-06` gains a third clause: the printed run is reproduced against a NAMED SNAPSHOT, because the bar is same question → same answer.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-08-28. Ruled by: Dave. **What was ruled.** The published *printed run* on every Context Product documentation page is reproduced against a **named snapshot** — a commit, an artifact id, or a graph pin — and the page **says which**, in one sentence, in the *what would fail* section the spine already carries (`D-IMPL-217`, spine element 3). One sentence per page is enough. A reader whose numbers differ has **re-derived, not replayed**. **THE BAR, in Dave's words:** *"same question → same answer, not correspondence with the live world. A printed run that can drift is a docs defect that looks like a fabric defect."* That last clause is the whole reason the clause is worth a rule rather than a habit: the failure does not present as a broken page, it presents as a broken fabric, and the reader debugs the wrong system. **WHAT THIS IS NOT — stated because the obvious reading is wrong.** It is **not a ban on live-fetch loaders**. Loaders stay off the *demonstrated* path. The demonstration assembles over the pin; *"run `load_xbrl_wave2.py`, then observe the product"* is the sentence that must not appear as a reproduction recipe. A product may acquire its data however it acquires it — what is fixed is what the page reproduces. **This does not disturb the ruling that context products are assembled per request and never precomputed** (`.planning/FUTURE-CONTEXT-PRODUCTS.md`, *"What must survive into that work"*; `CLAUDE.md` §9): the pin is on the *graph state the assembly reads*, not on the product, and a client parameter routed through config, a Makefile or an environment variable remains the tell that something has gone wrong. **WHY BANKED NOW rather than at the product that needs it.** `cp-00` satisfies the clause for free — its fixtures are fixed, so its page cannot drift. The first live-fetch product (`#3` and onward in the candidate set) is where a local rule gets invented under deadline, and by then `EXAM-06` would be closed and the invention would be precedent. The row was still open on two other clauses — reproduce-or-link, and whether the unlabelled *"which file is the SDK's?"* reveal is required of every example — so the clause lands on a page already being shaped, for the same failure mode. **The two open clauses stay open and stay two**: this one is ruled, not open. **Recorded in both ledger channels**, per the correction `D-IMPL-217` earned when its own row was minted into one channel only. **Governs:** the reproduction discipline on every Context Product documentation page. **Related:** `EXAM-06` (the row this amends), `D-IMPL-217` (the row's minting ruling, which stands amended rather than replaced), `.planning/FUTURE-CONTEXT-PRODUCTS.md` (assembled per request, never precomputed — carried there rather than in a `D-IMPL` entry, and NOT `D-IMPL-137`, which is the `refuse_operator_set_divergence` one-document ruling and was miscited once while this entry was being written), and `CLAUDE.md` §9 (the examples suite as the adoption contract).

**D-IMPL-219 — Context Products are built in the vault's complexity order, and readiness is never a reason to reorder.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-08-28. Ruled by: Dave. **What was ruled.** The `context-products` vault topic orders its 21 CB/CIB specs **simplest-first across a five-tier ladder**, and that order is the build order. In Dave's words: *"I want to build the context products in order of complexity. This has been assessed by the vault."* The first rung is `counterparty-reference-snapshot`. **WHAT PROMPTED IT — a proposal to jump the queue, refused.** The 2026-08-28 estate survey found three verified data gaps on rung 1 (only one of two required addresses with nothing recording which; **zero** no-LEI entities of 156; no jurisdiction column on `principal`), and the executing model recommended building `obligor-financial-spread` next instead **on the grounds that its data was richer**. That is a readiness argument wearing an ordering argument's clothes, and Dave rejected it. **THE DISTINCTION THIS ENTRY EXISTS TO HOLD:** *which* product is next is fixed by complexity; *when* it can be built is a data question, answered by loading the data, **never by promoting a better-supplied product over a simpler one**. Reordering on readiness would let the estate's accidents decide the teaching sequence, and the ladder's whole value is that each rung introduces exactly one new primitive over the rung below. **THE ORDER IS INDEPENDENTLY CORROBORATED, not merely deferred to:** store count rises monotonically by tier (T1 one store, T2–T3 two, T4 three, T5 four to five) and catalog size rises with it (4–10 §C rows at T1, 15–18 at T5), measured from the specs' own §C Data Catalogs. **CONSEQUENCE, accepted deliberately:** a rung whose data is not loaded **blocks** rather than yields — the fabric waits for `ccf_dataprep` to close the gap. Dave confirmed 2026-08-28 that dataprep is closing rung 1's three gaps. **Governs:** the build sequence for every Context Product example, and any future proposal to take a later rung first. **Related:** `.planning/CONTEXT-PRODUCT-LADDER-AND-ESTATE.md` (the ladder, the estate census, and §6.1.1's three gaps), `D-IMPL-217` and `D-IMPL-218` (`EXAM-06`, what each example's page must carry), and `D-GATE-19` (success criteria are locked at the discuss sitting, so no criteria are written for a rung in advance).

**D-IMPL-220 — no-LEI internal client identity is classed `synthetic — internal` per §C, REVERSING the `synthetic — engineered` label, and it lands in its own table with a NULL LEI.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-08-28. Ruled by: Dave, adopting the reversal `ccf_dataprep` flagged rather than silently applied. **WHAT WAS RULED.** The invented no-LEI entities that close rung 1's second gap carry provenance **`synthetic — internal`**, the class `§C` of `counterparty-reference-snapshot` assigns outright: *"Internal client identity for no-LEI entities | internal client master | **synthetic — internal** | Postgres | E"*. This **overrides** the earlier `synthetic — engineered` label, which was proposed before two facts were on the table. **THE PROVENANCE OF THE REVERSAL, stated because it is the useful half.** `ccf_dataprep` found the conflict, declined to resolve it in its own favour, and logged it: *"§C should win — it's one of the two sections this project treats as authoritative and it states the class outright. But you ruled explicitly, so I've logged the conflict rather than quietly overriding you."* A downstream repo refusing to override an upstream ruling it believed wrong, and escalating instead, is the behaviour this project wants; the entry records it so the pattern is citable. **THE TWO FACTS THAT CHANGED THE CALL, both re-verified here against the live store rather than transcribed.** (1) `ccf_v2.legal_entity.provenance` holds **exactly one distinct value across all 156 rows — `public`**. Labelling invention inside a reference table is not this estate's convention. (2) Invented *patterns* live in their own table, `engineered_entity`, **125 rows**. A no-LEI internal client is not that object — it is operational identity from the internal client master §C already names, and `synthetic — engineered` would shelve it beside typology and insider inventions. **A THIRD FACT NEITHER SIDE HAD, and it is the strongest of the three:** `synthetic — internal` is **already the live label on exactly this axis** — `principal.provenance` carries it on all 4 rows and `crosswalk.provenance` on all 83. The ruling is not merely what §C says; it is what the neighbouring tables already do. **WHAT ELSE THE RULING FIXES, and all three were verified on the tree after the load landed.** The no-LEI rows go in a **separate `internal_client` table**, not as a new row type inside `legal_entity` — which is structural rather than stylistic: `legal_entity.lei` is the **PRIMARY KEY** and **nine** tables hold a foreign key into it (`deal`, `debt_instrument`, `facility.borrower_lei`, `filing_profile`, `financial_fact`, `gdelt_mention`, `signal_event`, `trend_delta`, `warn_match`), so making it nullable is not a blast radius but an impossibility. `crosswalk.lei` becomes **nullable**, a one-line migration because that table's primary key was **already** `internal_client_id`; its `UNIQUE(lei)` survives untouched, since Postgres treats NULLs as distinct. And the LEI on an internal client **IS NULL** — **no `SYN-` placeholder**, because a placeholder resolves like a real anchor and would defeat the §D counterfactual the rows exist to demonstrate. **VERIFIED AS A ROSTER, NOT A COUNT.** Three `crosswalk` rows do carry a `SYN-` LEI, which is the literal shape this entry forbids. Enumerated, they are `CLI-000051`–`53` → `SYN-SDART-2022-6`, `SYN-SDART-2024-1`, `SYN-TAOT-2022-B` — **exactly and only** the three ABS trusts, a pre-existing convention for securitization vehicles that have no GLEIF record and never will. **Zero of the 30 internal clients carries any LEI.** A count would have reported a violation; the roster shows there is none. **Governs:** the provenance class on invented internal-client identity, the table it lands in, and the NULL-LEI discipline. **Related:** `D-IMPL-219` (complexity build order, which made rung 1 block rather than yield), `.planning/CONTEXT-PRODUCT-LADDER-AND-ESTATE.md` §6.1.1 (the gap as found) and §6.1.2 (the close, verified), `§C` of `counterparty-reference-snapshot` (the authority), and `D-65` (never verify a claim against the document asserting it — why the two counts above were re-derived from Postgres rather than read off the report that stated them).

**D-IMPL-221 — `cp-02-facility-terms-snapshot` was built with no ROADMAP phase home, and the remedy is a dated decision rather than a bullet.** OPEN. Raised: 2026-08-29, while locking Phase 24.3's criteria. Raised by: Claude Code; **Dave declined to resolve it in the same sitting, deliberately.** **THE FACT.** `24.1` is `cp-00-institutional-holders`, `24.2` is `cp-01-counterparty-reference-snapshot`, and `24.3` is now `cp-03-obligor-financial-spread`. **`cp-02` has no phase at all** — it was specified at `59f36f2`, built at `f1086bb` and documented at `749d1db`, none of it against a ROADMAP phase, success criteria or gate entry. It is the only Context Product on the ladder built entirely outside the phase machinery. **WHY IT IS NOT FIXED HERE.** Dave, 2026-08-29: *"Do not invent a retroactive phase in this sitting… a retroactive 24.x is a dated decision, not a bullet you sneak in while locking 24.3."* Numbering a phase after the fact changes what the phase counters have been reporting for the whole period the work was in flight, and doing that silently inside an unrelated commit is precisely the drift the ledger exists to prevent. It is also adjacent to the ten phases (9–14 and 16) that are `Complete` in `ROADMAP.md` with no `D-GATE` entry — the same class, not yet ruled. **THE SHAPE OF THE REMEDY, when it is taken.** A short bookkeeping pass, its own sitting: name the phase, add one Progress row, state plainly that the work was **built ahead of the close machinery**, and mint **no fake `D-GATE`** — the gate is a record of an approval that happened, and there was none to record. **Explicitly NOT the remedy:** backdating `24.2`'s meaning to cover two products, or widening an existing phase to absorb `cp-02` retroactively. **WHAT WAS DONE IN THE MEANTIME.** `24.2`'s missing *checklist* bullet was added — it had a detail section and no bullet, so inserting `24.3` alone would have left the checklist reading 24 → 24.1 → 24.1.1 → 24.3, as though `24.2` did not exist. That is a transcription gap in one of the four places the phase set lives, and correcting it is not the same act as minting a phase; the added row says in-line why it appears now.

**D-IMPL-222 — `basis` may change the content address for an obligor with no restatement, and the criterion requiring otherwise is amended.** RESOLVED: 2026-08-31, Dave. Raised by: Claude Code, while building gate `OFS-G11` in Phase 24.3. **THE REQUIREMENT.** `CP-SPEC-003` §D.4 and Success Criterion 38 required `basis=as-reported` and `basis=latest-restated` to produce DIFFERENT content addresses for a restated obligor and **IDENTICAL** ones for an unrestated obligor. The first half holds. The second does not, and cannot. **THE FIRST REPORT OF IT WAS INCOMPLETE, WHICH IS WORTH RECORDING BECAUSE IT NEARLY DECIDED THE QUESTION THE OTHER WAY.** It described the difference as "a label" — the payload echoes `basis_applied` on every line — which reads as cosmetic and invites removing the echo. Measured field by field against the two witnesses: for the unrestated obligor `basis_applied` differs on **75 of 75** cells, `accession` and `filed_date` on **20 of 75**, and `value` on **none**. For the restated obligor, `value` differs on 4 of 288. **So there are TWO independent causes and only one is cosmetic:** the two bases genuinely **read different filings** for 20 of 75 cells and report the same number from each.
