Removing the label would not have made the addresses match. **THE CHOICE.** Amend the specification, or normalize the provenance so both bases name one filing wherever the value agreed. The second satisfies the old wording by **suppressing a true fact** — `as-reported` would lose the ability to say which filing first reported a figure — at the rung whose entire subject is attribute-level provenance. A content address seals the served document; the documents differ; the address is right to differ. **RULED: amend.** Criterion 38 now requires DIFFERENT addresses for a restated obligor and IDENTICAL **figures** for an unrestated one — no served value moves. **No code changed**: `OFS-G11` already asserted the figures, having been rewritten when its address-only form survived a sabotage that stopped `basis` selecting the filing at all. Amended in `ROADMAP.md` criterion 38, `CP-SPEC-003` §D.4 and §G.2, `artifacts/question.yaml`, `artifacts/expected.yaml`, the example README, `summary_explanations.md` and the documentation page.

**D-GATE-24.3 — Phase 24.3, Credit Spreading: Obligor Financial Spread (cp-03), Gate 2.** **APPROVED — Dave, 2026-08-31.** Commits `294cb63`..`e350cde` on `main` (no phase branch; the phase ran on `main`, as 22 and 22.1 did). **WHAT SHIPPED.** The product assembles and serves end to end — `produce.py`, `deployment.py`, `assembler.py`, `run.py`, seven artifacts — plus the delivery set the recipe requires: an `example-cp-03` target, a README on the seven gated headings, `summary_explanations.md` for the three readers, and a documentation page whose generator and template are committed while the render is not. Published at `claude.ai/code/artifact/cd055c9c`. **THE GATES.** All FOURTEEN built and every one observed RED — they did not exist at the start of the phase; each `OFS-G` was a comment and `artifacts/expected.yaml` was read by nothing. Fifteen sabotages in the first pass, seven more against the gates the close panel rebuilt. **THREE GATES PASSED THEIR FIRST SABOTAGE**, all for one reason, and the form generalizes past this product: *a check that reads a token present in both the compliant and the violating case is measuring vocabulary, not content.* It was written down after the first and still shipped twice more in the same sitting, which is the argument for sabotaging every gate rather than reviewing them. **THE CLOSE PANEL FOUND A PRODUCT DEFECT, NOT A TEST DEFECT.** Codex and Cursor independently found that `OFS-G03` never served the product; chasing it found that `_read_cells` hard-coded a restatement key including `period_start` while `artifacts/restatement.yaml` declares one without it and names that exact variant to reject it. Measured: the declared key finds **321** restated cells, the key in force found **317**, and **four real corrections were hidden** — all annual revenue whose period boundary moved, precisely the case the artifact describes. Fixed, with a cell-level positive control; the first attempt at that control compared line names and showed nothing. **Nine blocking findings fixed in-phase, four advisory carried, one of my own suspicions (`OFS-G08`) rejected by both reviewers and recorded as rejected.** Gemini did not run — no API key — and is recorded as absent rather than as a reviewer that found nothing. Panel record: `.planning/phases/24.3-credit-spreading-obligor-financial-spread-cp-03-gate-2/24.3-CLOSE-REVIEWS.md`, naming the subjects it did **not** cover. **RULINGS INSIDE THE PHASE.** `D-IMPL-222` (the content address may differ under both bases for an unrestated obligor; criterion 38 amended rather than the product). Dave also ruled the anchor stays Digital Turbine, and that the debt signal is served with its verdict printed rather than refused. **CRITERIA.** 41 numbered, criterion 17 withdrawn with the Fluree design. `src/` was not touched (criterion 36, verified by pathspec diff). The externally-owned `[TBC]` rows remain open and none was invented (criterion 41) — **the figure "thirteen" was not re-derived against the §F.2 register and is carried from the criterion's own wording rather than measured here.** **CARRIED, NOT CLOSED.** `D-IMPL-221` — `cp-02` still has no ROADMAP phase, and no fake `D-GATE` was minted for it.

**D-IMPL-221 RESOLVED — `cp-02` is numbered `24.2.1`, recorded as built ahead of the close machinery, and no `D-GATE` is minted for it.** RESOLVED: 2026-08-31, Dave (*"fix cp-02"*). The original entry above is **preserved unedited** and still reads `OPEN`, per this log's own appending discipline; this entry is its resolution. **THE REMEDY, EXACTLY AS D-IMPL-221 SPECIFIED IT.** A short bookkeeping pass in its own sitting: the phase is named, one Progress row is added, the row states plainly that the work was **built ahead of the close machinery**, and **no fake `D-GATE` is minted** — a gate records an approval that happened, and there was none to record. **THE NUMBER.** `24.2.1`. `24.1` is `cp-00`, `24.2` is `cp-01`, `24.3` is `cp-03`; `cp-02` belongs between `cp-01` and `cp-03` in the ladder's own order, and `24.1.1` already establishes that a `.1` child sits after its parent and before the next sibling. **Nothing is renumbered**, so every existing reference to `24.2` and `24.3` stays true — the constraint that ruled out the alternatives. **EXPLICITLY NOT DONE**, as `D-IMPL-221` required: `24.2`'s meaning was not backdated to cover two products, and no existing phase was widened to absorb `cp-02` retroactively. **NO SUCCESS CRITERIA WERE INVENTED.** Authoring them now would describe the build that happened rather than gate it, which is the exact failure `D-GATE-19`'s forward binding exists to prevent — criteria are locked before Wave 1 or they are not criteria. The phase record says so in place of listing any. **WHAT `cp-02` ACTUALLY IS**, recorded so the row is not an empty marker: specified at `59f36f2`, built at `f1086bb`, documented at `749d1db`, all 2026-08-29; the full example (spec, seven artifacts, `deployment.py`, `produce.py`, `assembler.py`, `run.py`, README, `summary_explanations.md`, a documentation page) plus **20 tests** in `tests/examples/test_cp_02_output.py`, marked for the postgres leg. Written in three places, since the phase set lives in more than one: the checklist bullet, the `### Phase 24.2.1` detail section (the only one `roadmap.analyze` reads), and the Progress row. `.planning/STATE.md` deliberately untouched. **RAISED AND NOT FIXED HERE, because it is a different gap:** Phase **`24.2` (`cp-01`) is itself built with no Progress row, no `D-GATE` and an unticked checklist bullet.** That phase EXISTS and its bookkeeping does not, which is not the same act as minting a missing phase, and widening this sitting to cover it would repeat the drift `D-IMPL-221` was written to prevent. Unruled, and left for Dave.

**D-GATE-24.2 — Phase 24.2, The Second Context Product: Counterparty Reference Snapshot (`cp-01`).** **APPROVED — Dave, 2026-08-31**, on inspection of the shipped work. **THE SUCCESS CRITERION IS DAVE'S INSPECTION AND APPROVAL, RULED EXPLICITLY** (*"close both of them - the success criteria is my inspection and approval"*). This supersedes the position recorded hours earlier the same day, that these two phases could not be gated because no criteria were ever written. That position was right about the FACTS and wrong about the AUTHORITY: §2 and §3.1 make approval Dave's alone, so a criterion he states is a criterion, and it does not become invalid for arriving after the build when he is the one who set it. What would have been wrong is an executor inventing criteria and then declaring them met. **WHAT IS BEING APPROVED.** `cp-01` shipped 2026-08-29 across 15 commits: the full example — spec, artifacts, `deployment.py`, `produce.py`, `assembler.py`, `run.py`, README, `summary_explanations.md`, a documentation page — plus **13 gates proven by sabotage at the time** (`dd88f6e`) and 13 tests, re-run green 2026-08-31. Gate 1 was separately approved by Dave on 2026-08-29 (`2709a39`, spec authored, nothing implemented); this closes Gate 2. **WHAT THIS GATE IS NOT, STATED SO IT IS NOT MISREAD LATER.** **No close-time cross-AI panel ran for this phase**, no triage was performed, and no advisory findings were carried, because none were gathered. It is therefore **not** a §3.1-conforming close and does not claim to be. It is an approval by the approval authority on inspection, recorded as exactly that. A reader comparing it with `D-GATE-24.3` — which ran codex and cursor, verified thirteen findings and fixed nine — should read the difference as real rather than as a gap in the record.

**D-GATE-24.2.1 — Phase 24.2.1, Facility Terms Snapshot (`cp-02`).** **APPROVED — Dave, 2026-08-31**, on inspection of the shipped work, under the same ruling and with the same criterion. **WHAT IS BEING APPROVED.** `cp-02` was specified at `59f36f2`, built at `f1086bb` and documented at `749d1db`, all 2026-08-29, against no ROADMAP phase at the time; it ships the full example plus a documentation page and **20 tests** in `tests/examples/test_cp_02_output.py`, marked for the postgres leg. The phase itself was created retrospectively 2026-08-31 to discharge `D-IMPL-221`, numbered `24.2.1` so that nothing else needed renumbering. **THE SAME LIMITS APPLY AND ARE STATED AGAIN RATHER THAN CROSS-REFERENCED**: no close panel, no triage, no carried findings, not a §3.1-conforming close. **`D-IMPL-221`'s "mint no fake `D-GATE`" instruction is HONORED, not overridden.** It forbade recording an approval that never happened. One has now happened, so there is something to record — which is the precise condition that instruction was waiting on.

**D-IMPL-223 — Four scheduling classes, forever, as the scheduler; the Standard's eight names are spec vocabulary. `OperatorCategory` is CLOSED for v0, there are no user-extensible categories, and no fifth class is minted as an alias for a Standard word.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-08-31. Approver: Dave. **Dave's ruling, verbatim:** *"Don't pick 4 vs 8. Keep four scheduling classes. Treat Enrich / Evaluate / Federate / Resolve as authoring words, not SDK enums."*; *"no user-extensible categories for v0"*; and *"Until that product exists: four categories forever as scheduler; eight names as spec vocabulary. ... No phase to 'fix' 4-vs-8."* **WHAT WAS MEASURED BEFORE THE RULING, at `92761e0`, because the question had been argued from documents rather than from the tree.** Across the whole shipped ladder the Standard's four *extra* names — `Enrich`, `Similarity`, `Evaluate`, `Federate` — have **ZERO** uses. Per-recipe `operator:` declarations: `cp-00` names `Resolve`×2, `Policy`, `Traversal (mode: temporal)`, `Projection`, `contract assembly`; `cp-01` and `cp-02` each name `Resolve` (L2), `Policy` (L4), `null` (L6); `cp-03` names `Resolve` (L2), `Policy` (L4) and **four `null` steps**. **`cp-01`, `cp-02` and `cp-03` each invoke exactly ONE L4 operator, `Policy`** — `cp-03`'s `lineage.operators_invoked` holds exactly one entry, `policy.principal-subgraph`. `Resolve` has never once been an operator; it is L2 entity resolution in every product (`cp-03` step 1 names `sdk_mechanism: src/ccf/assembly/worker.py::SpecDrivenEntityResolution` and takes a `payload_key` witness precisely because *"this step runs outside the L4 registry, so no operator key would appear for it"*). **No example was ever blocked by a missing operator, so no example is rewritten.** **WHAT `OperatorCategory` ACTUALLY IS, and why the closure is not an oversight.** `src/ccf/operators/base.py:60` — `OperatorCategory = Literal["policy", "similarity", "temporal", "traversal"]` — and `CATEGORY_ORDER` at `:69` is the **planner dependency order** (whitepaper §7.4, INV-CH7-28), documented in place: Policy first *"because Similarity must rank only over the principal-permissible subgraph: admissibility is settled up front, so inadmissible content is never retrieved and no post-retrieval filter is required (INV-CH7-26)"*, and Temporal before Traversal *"because a walk should expand over temporally reconciled state, not over claims the boundary excludes."* **A category is a plan-order class carrying correctness rules, not a synonym for one of the Standard's eight names.** *"The name Enrich doesn't appear in `src/`"* and *"I can't schedule this work"* are therefore different failures, and **only the second is an SDK hole**. **THE EXTENSION SEAM ALREADY EXISTS AND IS NOT WIDENED.** `Operator` is a `@runtime_checkable` Protocol (`base.py:120`) with `key()`, `category()`, `parameters()`, `apply()`; `OperatorRegistry.register` (`registry.py:91`) admits any conformer, keyed by `key()`, refusing only on `DuplicateOperatorKey`. `PushableOperator` (`base.py:162`) is deliberately a **second** Protocol rather than further members on `Operator` — the comment says so in place — and that instinct is affirmed, not revisited. **Users extend by novel KEY; never by novel CATEGORY.** **A READING RAISED IN THE DISCUSSION AND REFUSED BY NAME.** It was proposed that a batched attribute fan-out could honestly register as `category="traversal"` on the ground that a category is a scheduling class and its scheduling genuinely resembles a walk. Dave, verbatim: *"Scheduling might match a walk; the name still teaches the wrong thing, and cp-03 already chose L2 assembly for that work. Leave that choice."* **`CP-SPEC-003` §D.2.1 stands as written**, and its characterization of such a registration as a *"FAKE MAPPING that made the lineage record say something untrue"* is not disturbed. **WHEN A FIFTH CLASS BECOMES REAL.** Only when some operator must run in a position **none of the four describe** — before Policy, or between Similarity and Temporal in a way that would violate INV-CH7-26. That would be a dated decision minting a new **scheduling class**, never an alias for `Enrich`. **`OperatorCategory` is not opened in Phase 24.4**, on the same rule applied to `ProductGate` in `D-IMPL-224`: earned by a product that **cannot** run correctly in any of the four slots. **CONSEQUENCES.** No ladder rewrite; no phase is created to "fix" 4-vs-8. **`D-IMPL-212` STAYS OPEN and is NOT resolved by this entry** — the `Enrich` gap is deferred to a product that cannot be scheduled in the four slots, not closed by ruling the vocabulary a naming layer. `OFS-G10` remains a valid tripwire and a RED there still means reopen `CP-SPEC-003` §F.2 row 1 rather than a regression. Recorded beside `D-IMPL-224`, per Dave's instruction that the two findings sit together.

**D-IMPL-224 — Product-level gates are a DECLARED ARTIFACT plus a CI coverage check, not a serve-time type. No `ProductGate` Protocol is built in Phase 24.4, and the Standard's extra gates are declared product gates rather than new members of `run_gates`.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-08-31. Approver: Dave. **Dave's ruling, verbatim:** *"v0 is the CI coverage check (option 1). Do not build a ProductGate Protocol in 24.4."*; *"Fourteen declared / fourteen running nothing is a **declaration↔test** hole, not a missing serve-time type. Closing it with a Protocol would add SDK surface before a product has earned serve-time product gates — the same move you refused for Enrich and for a fourth `run_gates` gate (D-IMPL-102)."* **WHAT SHIPS.** (1) Gates stay **declared in an artifact** — `expected.yaml` or a `gates.yaml`, **one place, closed keys**. (2) A checker **fails CI when a declared id has no executing test**, and when a test names an **undeclared** id. (3) **Non-vacuity**: a `cp-*` example that ships a gates artifact with **zero ids**, or ids with no executing test, is **RED** — zero declared gates is not green for a shipped ladder example. (4) **Scope is the `cp-*` ladder ONLY.** `hw1-*` and `s1-*` declaring zero product gates **stay legal**; the checker does not glob the whole `examples/` tree. (5) **No serve path, no `_GATE_TOKEN`, no metaclass.** The universal gates remain the only serve-time gates. This makes *"declared but idle"* structurally impossible; it does **not** make product gates bypass-proof at serve, **and that is correct for v0**. **THE FINDING THIS RESTS ON, measured at `92761e0`.** **Forty product-level gates across four products** — `cp-00` 8 (`IH-G01`…`IH-G08`), `cp-01` 9 (`CPR-G01`…`CPR-G09`), `cp-02` 9 (`FTS-G01`…`FTS-G09`), `cp-03` 14 live (`OFS-G01`…`OFS-G13` plus `OFS-G15`; `OFS-G14` retired with the Fluree design). **NONE has any SDK expression**: `grep -rnE "OFS-G|FTS-G|[A-Z]{2,4}-G[0-9]{2}" --include=*.py src/ runtime/` returns **0**, against a fabricated-prefix control that also returns 0 and non-zero populations in `examples/` (`OFS` 395, `FTS` 244, `CPR` 199, `IH` 90), so the zero comes from an instrument that fires. The lifecycle is: **declared** in spec prose and artifacts, **referenced in example code only as comments**, **executed** by hand-written pytest functions, with the link between declaration and execution carried by naming convention alone. Contrast the universal gates, which are genuinely defended — `run_gates` is guarded by `_GATE_TOKEN`, the `_ServableProductMeta` metaclass and `GateBypassError`, so a product that skipped them cannot be served. **The population with the most semantic weight had the least structural support.** **`cp-03`'s OWN RECORD OF THE FAILURE**, `tests/examples/test_cp_03_output.py` module docstring, verbatim: *"Before this module existed, none of the fourteen ran at all — every ``OFS-G`` in the example's four modules was a comment, ``artifacts/expected.yaml`` was read by nothing, and the example's only test answered census questions with SQL."* **COVERAGE AS MEASURED IS AN UPPER BOUND, AND THE CHECKER MUST NOT REPRODUCE THE INSTRUMENT THAT PRODUCED IT.** Two instruments were run and they disagree. The first keyed on **function name** (`def test_*<gate_id>*`) and reported `cp-00` 0/8, `cp-01` 0/9, `cp-02` 0/9, `cp-03` 14/15. **That instrument was WRONG** — `cp-01` and `cp-02` name their tests by behavior (`test_entitlement_discriminates_as_sets_with_a_negative_control`) and cite the gate id in the docstring; only `cp-03` puts the id in the function name. The second keyed on **id presence anywhere in the product's test file** and reported `cp-00` **1/8**, `cp-01` **8/9**, `cp-02` **9/9**, `cp-03` **15/15**. **Docstring presence is an UPPER BOUND, not proof of an executing assertion**; true coverage lies between the two numbers, and neither figure may be quoted as coverage. **Three products use three different linking conventions** — which is exactly why the link must be **declared data with closed keys** rather than inferred by grep. **The checker must require an EXECUTING test, never `id in file`.** That is the whole point of closed-key declaration. **DEBT RECORDED, NOT A REOPENED GATE.** `cp-00` carries **seven** declared gates with no test-file presence at all (`IH-G01`, `IH-G02`, `IH-G03`, `IH-G05`, `IH-G06`, `IH-G07`, `IH-G08`) and `cp-01` carries **one** (`CPR-G08`) — inside phases already closed by `D-GATE-24.1` and `D-GATE-24.2`. Dave, verbatim: *"Finding under 24.4. Do not reopen D-GATE-24.1. Seven missing test-file ids in a gated phase are debt, not a silent amendment of the gate."* **Same pattern as `D-IMPL-221`** and `cp-02`'s missing phase home: the shortfall is carried as a named finding under the next phase, never as a quiet amendment of an approved gate. **THE STANDARD'S EXTRA THREE GATES** — debt, suppression silence, classification containment — are **declared product gates plus CI tests**, **not** new members of `run_gates`. **PROTOCOL FOR REVISITING.** `cp-04` pressure-tests it. If ontology claims must refuse **at serve** rather than only in CI, that product writes the case for a `ProductGate` Protocol. Until such a product exists, day-one enforcement for domain gates is refused as *"exactly the accretion 24.3 just escaped."* **A CORRECTION TO THE RECORD, CITING MEASURED IDENTITIES RATHER THAN A PARAPHRASE.** The ROADMAP's Phase 24 entry states that the SDK ships **THREE** validation gates and that `D-IMPL-102` limb 3 affirmatively ruled that no fourth joins `run_gates`. Measured at `92761e0`, `src/ccf/products/gates.py` defines **FIVE gate identity tokens** — `GATE_EMPTY_OPERATOR = "empty-operator-guard"` (`:119`), `GATE_LINEAGE_EQUALITY = "lineage-strict-equality"` (`:120`), `GATE_LINEAGE_ATTRIBUTABILITY = "lineage-attributability"` (`:121`), `GATE_TTL_BOUNDS = "ttl-bounds"` (`:122`), `GATE_SOURCE_ATTESTATION = "source-attestation"` (`:123`) — across **TWO runners**: `run_gates` (`:426`) invokes the empty-operator guard, lineage **strict equality**, TTL bounds, and `refuse_attestation` (`:213`); `run_federated_gates` (`:507`) invokes the empty-operator guard, lineage **attributability**, and TTL bounds. `refuse_attestation` returns `None` when `attestation is None` (`:240`), so its enforcement is **conditional** on a source having attested. **`D-IMPL-102` limb 3 is quoted here in full rather than characterized, because its heading and its explanatory clause differ in scope:** *"(3) **No fourth gate is added to `run_gates`.** The three shipped validation gates — the empty-operator guard, lineage strict equality, TTL bounds — **stay structural and are not joined by a payload gate**, which keeps the whitepaper's three-validation-gate commitment intact rather than widening it."* The heading is general; the clause names a payload gate specifically. **THIS ENTRY DOES NOT DECIDE WHICH READING GOVERNS.** It records three measured facts: a fifth identity token and a second runner exist in the tree; `GATE_SOURCE_ATTESTATION` is reachable from `run_gates` conditionally; and the ROADMAP's flat *"three"* is not what the tree holds. **Whether `run_gates`'s current membership requires its own dated ruling is left OPEN and is not decided here** — if a ruling is wanted it is a new entry, not an amendment of this one.

**D-IMPL-225 — Gate 1 for `CP-SPEC-004` is APPROVED WITH THREE AMENDMENTS: the MCP door is a REGISTERED resource that REFUSES, the consume path is the direct-adapter `ProductClient` constructor over a single-store binding, and the product gates schema lives off the top-level `docs/schemas` glob.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-08-31. Approver: Dave, at Gate 1 of Phase 24.4, on the amended text. **The `D-IMPL-222` precedent was invoked by name and honored: the amendments landed in `ROADMAP.md` and in this log BEFORE Wave 3, and the specification's `Gate 1 status` row was not flipped to RULED until they had.** Until then `examples/cp-04-corporate-family-tree/` held exactly one file, the specification itself. **AMENDMENT 1 — CRITERION 37 WAS FALSE AGAINST THIS TREE AND IS AMENDED RATHER THAN ENGINEERED AROUND.** It read *"`CFT-G13` — the MCP door is TOOL-ONLY — is sabotaged by exposing a product resource and observed RED."* Measured: `runtime/ccf_runtime/mcp/egress.py:475` registers `@server.resource(PRODUCT_URI_TEMPLATE, …)` **UNCONDITIONALLY**, and only the tool at `:529` sits behind `if expose_product_tool:`. `build_egress_server` can be resource-only or resource-plus-tool; it **cannot be tool-only**. Dave, verbatim: *"A listing that includes the resource is the SDK. Criterion 37 as written ('no resource is exposed') is false against this tree."* **`runtime/` is NOT touched** — `D-04` of `24-CONTEXT.md` governs, a minor phase records gaps rather than closing them. `CFT-G13` now asserts three things together: the resource **IS** registered and enumerable in `resources/list`; a resolve or read of it returns `ProductNotServable` (`egress.py:221`) or the existing refusal type and **NEVER a tree**; and the **TOOL is the only path that serves**, taking a client-supplied `lei` and `max_depth`. **Sabotage: make the resolver return a payload and the gate must go RED.** **THE WEAKNESS WAS STATED BEFORE THE RULING, NOT DISCOVERED AFTER IT.** A registered-but-refusing resource still appears in `resources/list`, so this satisfies *"the resource cannot be used to obtain this product"* and NOT the literal *"no resource is exposed."* That distinction was put to Dave explicitly rather than smoothed over, and the criterion was amended to say what is true instead of being left asserting something false. **D-34 IS THE GAP THIS LEAVES**, recorded under the same `D-04` posture and the same class as `D-30` and `D-33`: *`build_egress_server` cannot omit a product resource from MCP `resources/list` without `runtime/` work, so a genuinely tool-only door is not expressible today.* Criterion 49 is extended to it. **AMENDMENT 2 — THE CONSUME PATH IS THE DIRECT-ADAPTER CONSTRUCTOR, AND THE BINDING STAYS SINGLE-STORE.** `src/ccf/client/adapters/binding_document.py:177` — `RULED_OUT_KEYS` — refuses a `resolver:` key **BY NAME**, and `inprocess.py` boots through `build_governed_resolver` against an already-populated graph with no L1 ingest. The `binding.yaml` path therefore **structurally cannot** express a two-store product; cp-04 could not have used `ProductClient.for_product` even had it wanted to. The form is `ProductClient(product_id=…, adapter=…)`, the documented public constructor at `src/ccf/client/client.py:100`. Dave, verbatim: *"Binding stays single-store. Two-store assembly happens inside the product, not via a forbidden `resolver:` key and not via a fixture that pre-opens both stores."* **`CFT-G10` therefore asserts that THE ASSEMBLY opened Fluree and Postgres, not that the RUNNER did** — criterion 34 is clarified to say so, because a fixture that pre-opens both stores and hands the product a populated graph would turn the gate into an assertion about a fixture loader. No HTTP path anywhere; nothing under `src/` changes. **A CONSISTENCY FINDING WITH THE CLIENT WORK, RECORDED BECAUSE IT IS EASY TO MISREAD LATER.** `cp-04` is the **FIRST `cp-*` rung to consume through the client seam at all** — `cp-00` through `cp-03` never import `ProductClient` and go straight through `ContextAssemblerProtocol`. The client work of Phases 17/18/20 lives in the `hw1-*` trees and proves a **different** property: `hw1-companies-over-revenue/consume.py` and `hw1-harness-clients/runner/drive.py` both call `for_product`, and that seam's own docstring states the claim as *"same `consume.py`, different `CCF_BINDING`, identical `Result`"* — transport swap as an ops action. **cp-04 supplies its adapter in code and therefore does NOT re-prove that.** Its portability claim is `D-21`'s: one standalone assembler, two thin callers — `run.py` in-process and `server/serve.py` over MCP. Both claims are legitimate and they are not the same claim; **no cp-04 document may imply cp-04 re-proves hw1's.** **AMENDMENT 3 — THE PRODUCT GATES SCHEMA LIVES IN A SUBDIRECTORY, DELIBERATELY.** `docs/schemas/product-gates/cp.product-gates.json`, with **CLOSED keys**, validated against by `examples/cp-04-corporate-family-tree/artifacts/gates.yaml`. `tools/dump_schemas.py:335` globs `docs/schemas/*.json` **TOP-LEVEL ONLY** against `SDK_ARTIFACT_CLASSES` in `src/`, and `:399` calls `orphan.unlink()` on any committed file that population does not emit — `tests/cli/test_schema_export.py:145::test_an_orphan_schema_is_drift` asserts exactly that. A hand-authored file at the top level would be **deleted**, so the subdirectory is what keeps criterion 43 and criterion 49 from contradicting each other. Verified before ruling: `docs/schemas/` holds **27** files and **ZERO** subdirectories, so the namespace is new and uncontested. It is correctly **not SDK-owned** — a per-product gate roster is the product's namespace, and making it an SDK artifact class is the surface `D-IMPL-224` declined. **ENFORCEMENT IS PHASE 24.5's CHECKER, not this phase** (`D-24`). **WHAT ELSE THE GATE 1 PASS PRODUCED.** Two defects in verification machinery, both found by RUNNING checks rather than reading them: the plan's own `<automated>` block **cannot run on this host** — `ugrep 7.8.4` rejects `\b` inside that alternation and fails identically against the known-good `CP-SPEC-003`, so it is the instrument and not the document, and the portable form `^## Section $s( |$)` replaces it for every later plan; and the reproducibility claim was **line-wrapped**, so `grep -F` reported it missing while the sentence sat plainly on the page. All seven spec checks were sabotaged and observed RED, including a reintroduced replay-pin claim and a dropped conflict. **Governs:** `CFT-G13`'s three-part assertion, the cp-04 consume path, the product-gates schema location, and criterion 34's subject. **Related:** `D-IMPL-222` (amend-before-execute precedent, invoked here), `D-IMPL-224` (no `ProductGate` Protocol; the CI-coverage posture), `D-30` and `D-33` and `D-34` (the recorded mechanism gaps), `D-21` (one assembler, two callers), `D-GATE-18` (hw1's transport portability, which cp-04 does not re-prove).

**D-IMPL-226 — PARTIALLY RETRACTED 2026-09-01. Its DECISION 2 half (one envelope per NODE, `relationship_rules: []`, `D-35`) is RULED and stands. Its DECISION 1 half (family-scoped Policy classification) was NEVER RULED BY DAVE and is RETRACTED — see `D-IMPL-227`.** Original title, preserved: *"cp-04's Policy classification is FAMILY-SCOPED, and its L1 ingest emits one envelope per NODE with each typed edge admitted directly; the declared resolution spec cannot carry a typed edge and that is recorded as `D-35`."* Date: 2026-09-01. **APPROVER, CORRECTED: Dave ruled DECISION 2 only.** The Decision-1 half was written as though approved on the strength of the word *"Unlock it"* and the phrase *"SMCI headline unchanged"*, neither of which selected a policy shape. **Do not cite this entry as authority for family-scoped classification.** **DECISION 1 — THE POLICY ENVELOPE WAS DELETING THE PRODUCT'S SUBJECT, AND THE ARTIFACT'S OWN CLAIM ABOUT ITSELF WAS FALSE.** `ccf_config.yaml` declared nine permitted classifications — `US`, `US-CA`, `US-DE`, `US-NY`, `NL`, `LU`, `DE`, `SG`, `KY` — and classified BOTH `family_anchor` and `family_member` on `entity_jurisdiction`. Its inline comment asserted the list was *"the jurisdiction set the family graph's LEI-bearing nodes resolve under."* **Measured against the estate and re-verified independently: that set is THIRTY-THREE values, not nine.** Distinct `legal_jurisdiction` across the 181 LEI-bearing family nodes: `US-DE, GB, IN, CA, CA-BC, US-MD, DE, NL, CN, AU, BE, US-FL, KR, US-NV, LU, SG, JP, US-TX, HK, SE, CH, US-NY, MO, AT, HU, NZ, US-WA, KY, US-OH, CA-NS, ES, US-MN, IT`. **606 of 748 family nodes carry no `ccf_v2.legal_entity` row at all**, so they classify as absent. **Through the shipped `PolicyFilter` and the shipped artifact, the SMCI subtree lost 20 of its 22 nodes** — only the anchor (`US-DE`) and `SuperMicroComputerBV` (`NL`) survived. **Those twenty are exactly the population criterion 33 and `CFT-G09` exist to protect** (*"a node carrying no LEI stays in the tree and in the roster"*), so the Policy step as configured deleted the thing the product is for. **[STRICKEN 2026-09-01, Dave — this sentence asserted a ruling that was never made.]** It read: *"RULED: family-scoped classification. Every member carries the ANCHOR's jurisdiction, so the envelope discriminates on the anchor rather than on each subsidiary independently."* **Family scope over the NINE declared jurisdictions was never ruled and is not the shipped shape.** The measurement of the problem in this section stands; only the disposition was invented. The actual ruling is `D-IMPL-228`. **This needs no artifact edit and keeps every member**, so criteria 12 and 33 both continue to hold: the subtree stays 22 nodes, 2 resolving in Postgres and 20 not. It implements spec §B.2's own sentence rather than inventing a reading — *"whether an edge to an entity in a restricted jurisdiction may be returned … is not the same question as whether that entity's attributes may be"* — and it is the credit semantic, since a borrowing group is the anchor's group. **THE TWO REJECTED OPTIONS, recorded so they are not re-proposed.** Widening the list to the 33 measured values plus a token for the 606 would make entitlement **non-discriminating**, which spec §B.2 already records as the unmeasured state and which the vault's own §F warns against — *"a floor nobody evaluates is documentation, not a gate."* Leaving the filter and amending criteria 12 and 33 would make `CFT-G09` **unsatisfiable**, which is the fourteen-idle-gates class arriving by a different road. **DECISION 2 — THE DECLARED RESOLUTION SPEC CANNOT EXPRESS A TYPED EDGE, AND THIS IS `D-35`.** Read in the source rather than taken on report: `src/ccf/assembly/worker.py:381` iterates `for rule in relationship_rules: for subject in by_class[rule.subject_entity_class]: for obj in by_class[rule.object_entity_class]:` and mints a claim for **every** such combination resolved from ONE envelope. **Minting is by CLASS CO-OCCURRENCE; nothing selects the relationship type from the payload.** Measured live through `booted.handle.worker`: one envelope carrying one `entity_uri` minted **2 entities** (the same node under both classes, identical identity hash) and **TWELVE relationships, SIX of them self-loops**, spanning all six declared types. **A member-to-member edge cannot be minted at all**, because one envelope resolves at most one `family_member`. Had the twelve `relationship_rules` been kept, the payload's `predicate` field would have been a lie and lineage strict equality would have been sealing a false document. **RULED: one envelope per NODE**, so no relationship rule ever fires; `resolution.relationship_rules: []`; and each normalized edge admitted through **`worker.admit_relationship_claim` (`:315`), a real public method**, carrying its true predicate. **The single-writer invariant is preserved** — admission still runs through L2's worker, and no second writer touches L3. **No `src/` change**, so criterion 49 holds. **`D-35` IS RECORDED, NOT CLOSED**, under `D-04`'s posture, beside `D-26`..`D-34`; criterion 49 is extended to it. **THIS IS THE FOURTH MECHANISM GAP THIS PHASE HAS SURFACED WITHOUT TOUCHING A LINE OF `src/` OR `runtime/`** — `D-33` (traversal types on edges only), `D-34` (a product resource cannot be omitted from `resources/list`), `D-30` (the resource URI cannot address a parameterized product) and now `D-35`. That is `D-03` of `24-CONTEXT.md` working as intended: examples exist to pressure-test the SDK, and the pressure is being recorded rather than absorbed. **A THIRD FINDING, FIXED IN PLACE RATHER THAN RULED.** `ccf_config.yaml` pointed at `artifacts/assembly-recipe.yaml` for the six predicates' full IRIs and **they were not there** — `grep -rn 'edmcouncil'` over the artifacts tree returned nothing, and the per-predicate direction lived only in `expected.yaml`, which is gate-side and off the serving path. Commit `75819fd` adds `artifacts/source-vocabulary.yaml`, validating against the same `ccf.declared-artifact` schema as the other five, so the serving path reads its vocabulary from a document instead of from a gate artifact. **Governs:** cp-04's Policy classification scope, its L1 envelope shape, and the `relationship_rules` posture. **Related:** `D-IMPL-225` (the Gate 1 amendments), `D-33`/`D-34` (the sibling mechanism gaps), `D-10` (cycle detection in the L2 assembler), `D-03` and `D-04` of `24-CONTEXT.md`.


**D-IMPL-227 — a ruling record asserted an approval that was never given, and the correction is a retraction rather than a rewrite.** RECORDED. Date: 2026-09-01. Raised by: Dave. **THE MISMATCH, IN ONE SENTENCE, IN DAVE'S FRAME.** `D-IMPL-226` and the wave-4 policy work assumed family-scope was ruled; **Dave only ruled (a) + `D-35`.** *"Unlock it"* and *"SMCI headline unchanged"* said: do not reopen census or cycles, keep going on `D-35`. **They did not pick a policy shape.** **WHY THIS IS THE SAME DEFECT AS THE STALE POINTER IT WAS FILED BESIDE.** Dave, verbatim: *"A pointer to the wrong file and a pointer to the wrong ruling are the same defect: a reader stops looking."* `ccf_config.yaml` named `assembly-recipe.yaml` as the home of six predicate IRIs that file does not contain; `D-IMPL-226` named Dave as the approver of a policy shape he did not choose. Both make a reader stop looking, and the second is worse because the log is the project's memory of who decided what. **WHAT WAS DONE, AND THE COST WAS MEASURED BEFORE IT WAS PAID.** Nothing had been committed on the false record — `git log aed9a2e..HEAD` was empty and the family-scope work was three modified files in the working tree. The executor was stopped mid-task, the diff was saved to the session scratchpad rather than discarded blind, and `examples/cp-04-corporate-family-tree/` was reverted to `aed9a2e`. **The one change Dave explicitly endorsed was re-applied on its own**: `ccf_config.yaml` now points at `artifacts/source-vocabulary.yaml`, which carries the seven IRI references, instead of at `assembly-recipe.yaml`, which carries zero. **THE FOUR CONDITIONS DAVE SET FOR CONFIRMING FAMILY SCOPE, MEASURED.** (1) *"The serve path still answers SMCI downward, 22 nodes, both cycles, default depth 3"* — 22 nodes and depth 3 hold, and cycle 1 is fully inside the subtree at 3/3; **cycle 2 is 0/3 and cannot be reached under any policy shape**, because it has zero external in-edges, which is criterion 16's own measured fact and predates this wave. The census reports two cycles over the whole graph (criterion 14); the SMCI payload carries one. **Recorded rather than scored as a pass.** (2) *"Policy does not resolve the other 83 roots into the payload"* — holds: exactly 1 of the 83 roots is reachable from the anchor at depth 3, and it is the anchor. This is a property of the walk being anchor-bounded, not of the policy shape, so it holds either way. (3) *"Jurisdictions / principals are the family's, not a nine-row fiction and not the whole 33-jurisdiction set dressed as 'the family'"* — **FALSE.** The family's actual jurisdiction set is **`{NL, US-DE}`, two values.** The declared nine carry **SEVEN the family never uses** — `DE`, `KY`, `LU`, `SG`, `US`, `US-CA`, `US-NY`. Family scope makes every member pass because the anchor is `US-DE`, but it passes for a reason unrelated to those seven, and the list remains false about what it is. (4) *"`CFT-G10` still means assembly opened both stores, not 'policy scanned the estate'"* — not reached; condition 3 already failed. **BY DAVE'S OWN PROTOCOL, ANY FALSE CONDITION MEANS REVERT THIS WAVE AND RE-POSE.** Done. **WHAT WAS EXPLICITLY NOT DONE, because Dave named it as the tempting wrong move:** the prose was not amended to match the code. *"Do not 'amend the prose to match the code' unless you actually choose that option."* **THE RULE THIS ENTRY EXISTS TO FIX.** Silence is not assent, a terse go-ahead selects only what it names, and an orchestrator that infers a ruling from adjacent approval has invented authority. Where a ruling is needed and absent, the phase stops and asks — it does not proceed on the most plausible reading and record it as decided. **Governs:** how a ruling reaches `docs/DECISIONS.md`. **Related:** `D-IMPL-226` (partially retracted here), `D-IMPL-222` (amend-before-execute, which this entry does not disturb), `D-GATE-19` (criteria are locked by the approval authority, never inferred), `D-65` (never verify a claim against the document asserting it).


**D-IMPL-228 — AMENDED 2026-09-01 by `D-IMPL-229`: `{NL, US-DE}` remains the family's observed set and stays CLOSED, but it is NOT `permitted_classifications` and is no longer the `_admits` input — it moves to the SERVED-AND-ASSERTED set. Every sentence below treating it as the policy admission key is superseded.** Original title: *"cp-04's declared jurisdictions ARE THE FAMILY'S OBSERVED SET, `{NL, US-DE}`, CLOSED, with an unknown key refused; the walk is family-scoped to one root and 22 nodes; and `CFT-G10` remains a claim about the assembly, not about Policy.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-09-01. Approver: Dave, ruling Decision 1 after retracting the record that had claimed it was already ruled (`D-IMPL-227`). **WHAT WAS RULED, in Dave's words.** *"Declared jurisdictions = the family's observed set, closed."* Spec, config and the policy envelope list **`{NL, US-DE}`** and **refuse an unknown key — the same closed-world pattern as `gates.yaml`.** *"Family-scope the walk (one root, 22 nodes). Do not 'family-scope' a superset of jurisdictions so the anchor happens to hit the list."* **WHY THE NINE FAILED, AND IT IS THE PHASE'S RECURRING DEFECT RATHER THAN A LOCAL SLIP.** The declared list was `US, US-CA, US-DE, US-NY, NL, LU, DE, SG, KY` and claimed inline to be *"the jurisdiction set the family graph's LEI-bearing nodes resolve under."* Measured: that set is **33 values**, and the set this payload actually touches is **TWO** — `NL` and `US-DE`. **Seven of the nine never touch this payload at all.** Family-scoping over the nine would have passed every member because the anchor is `US-DE`, for a reason unrelated to `DE`, `KY`, `LU`, `SG`, `US`, `US-CA` and `US-NY`. Dave, verbatim: **_"Nine-row 'coverage' is how idle gates look when the extra rows never fire."_** A row that cannot fire is the fourteen-idle-gates class wearing a jurisdiction's name, and the same defect as the pointer to a file lacking its subject and the ruling record naming an approver who never approved — **each makes a reader stop looking.** **THE TWO SABOTAGES, REQUIRED AND NAMED BY DAVE.** Dropping `NL` **or** `US-DE` from the declaration must go **RED**; adding `US-NY` *as if it were in-family* must also go **RED**. The second is the one that matters: it is the only control that can catch a list quietly re-widened, and without it the closed world is a convention rather than a gate. **WHAT DOES NOT MOVE.** **`CFT-G10` stays a claim that THE ASSEMBLY opened both stores** — *"Policy is not that proof."* The census (criteria 3–13), the two cycles, the SMCI headline at 22 nodes and default depth 3, the ceiling of 6, and the sixteen gates `CFT-G01`..`CFT-G16` are untouched. **A CORRECTION DAVE MADE TO HIS OWN TEST, recorded because it prevents a future misreading.** His first condition asked that the serve path answer *"SMCI downward, 22 nodes, both cycles, default depth 3."* **Cycle 2 has zero external in-edges (criterion 16) and is unreachable from any LEI-bearing anchor**, so *"both cycles"* is a **census** claim, never a payload claim, and must not be used as a policy pass/fail. The census reports two over the whole graph (criterion 14); the SMCI payload carries one. The orchestrator had declined to score that condition as a pass for the same reason before the correction arrived. **Governs:** cp-04's declared jurisdiction set and its closed-world discipline, the walk's scope, and what `CFT-G10` proves. **Related:** `D-IMPL-227` (the retraction that made room for this ruling), `D-IMPL-226` (which keeps its Decision-2 half — one envelope per node, `relationship_rules: []`, `D-35`), `D-IMPL-224` (declared artifacts with closed keys), criterion 33 and `CFT-G09` (the no-LEI population the old envelope deleted).


**D-IMPL-229 — Policy admits on FAMILY MEMBERSHIP THE WALK OBSERVED; jurisdiction is a SERVED FIELD, not the admission key; a member with no PostgreSQL row carries `null` and never the anchor's value.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-09-01. Approver: Dave. **THE MEASUREMENT THAT FORCED THE CHOICE, taken against the SDK rather than argued.** `src/ccf/operators/categories.py::PolicyFilter._admits` ends `return record.claim.attributes.get(attribute) in params.permitted_classifications`, and `PolicyFilter.apply` filters `view.entities` wholesale, so **every one of the 22 subtree nodes passes through it**. Exercised on the four cases: a stored `US-DE` admits, a stored `NL` admits, an explicit `None` is **refused**, and an absent key is **refused** — `.get()` returns `None` in both, and `None` is not in the permitted set. **FOUR THINGS COULD NOT ALL HOLD.** (1) `{NL, US-DE}` as `permitted_classifications` on `entity_jurisdiction`; (2) the 20 row-less members carrying `jurisdiction: null` and never a default; (3) all 22 served, per criteria 12 and 33 and `CFT-G09`; (4) `_admits` refusing null. Holding 1, 2 and 4 serves **2 of 22** — the original defect returning through the front door. **RULED: the policy axis changes; the jurisdiction list does not disappear, it MOVES.** **Policy admits on FAMILY MEMBERSHIP** — `family_id` / anchor LEI / *"in this walk"* — an attribute **minted when the node is admitted to the walk**, so it is **observed, not inferred from PostgreSQL**. Dave: *"If PolicyFilter can only key off a claim attribute, that attribute is membership, minted when the node is admitted to the walk."* **`{NL, US-DE}` becomes the SERVED-AND-ASSERTED set** — carried on the payload and in `expected.yaml`, still closed, still sabotaged in both directions — and is **struck as `_admits` input**. **WHAT THE PAYLOAD CARRIES.** A member with a `ccf_v2.legal_entity` row carries its **stored** jurisdiction, `NL` or `US-DE` as measured. A member with **no row carries `null`** (or the field is omitted) — **never SMCI's Delaware, and never a null token inside a permitted set.** Dave: *"A missing Postgres row is not `US-DE`."* And: *"Cycle members already have no LEI; they must not pick up SMCI's Delaware because the walk started there."* **THE SABOTAGE HE NAMED:** fill-from-anchor, so those 20 show `US-DE` → **RED**. **THE FINDING.** The 20 surface as an **`unresolved_jurisdiction` finding carrying the ROSTER of its members** — asserted as that roster, **never as `len(findings) > 0`**, the same discipline `D-13` fixed for cycles. **WHY INHERITANCE WAS REFUSED, and it is the phase's recurring defect for the third time.** Dave: *"Inheritance is the same class as the nine-row fiction: a value that was never observed, applied so a gate looks populated."* The nine-jurisdiction list had seven rows that could never fire; anchor-inheritance would have put a value on 20 nodes that no source ever asserted about them. Both make a check look populated while measuring nothing. **Family membership is admissible precisely because the walk DID observe it**, which is the distinction between (A) and the fiction. **WHAT THIS CORRECTS.** `examples/cp-04-corporate-family-tree/deployment.py::classify_family` currently reads *"a member carries its own jurisdiction where PostgreSQL holds a row, and the family's — the anchor's — where it does not."* **That rule is struck.** The correction lands with plan `24.4-07`; `deployment.py` is plan `24.4-06`'s file and is amended rather than re-planned. **WHAT DOES NOT MOVE:** the census (criteria 3–13), the 22-node SMCI subtree, the cycle-1 payload, the ceiling of 6 and default of 3, and the **SIXTEEN** gates `CFT-G01`..`CFT-G16` — no gate id is minted for the new finding without a further ruling. **Governs:** cp-04's policy admission axis, its served jurisdiction field, and the `unresolved_jurisdiction` finding. **Related:** `D-IMPL-228` (amended here), `D-IMPL-227` (the retraction that set the ask-don't-infer discipline this ruling was reached under), `D-13` (roster not cardinality), criteria 12, 33 and `CFT-G09`.

**D-IMPL-230 — `D-36` records that the L4 walk is an undirected NEIGHBORHOOD rather than a directed descendant walk; and cp-04 SERVES on context debt rather than calibrating `debt_tolerance` to rescue a number the whitepaper never produced.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-09-01. Approver: Dave. **PART 1 — `D-36`, THE FIFTH MECHANISM GAP.** `src/ccf/operators/categories.py::TraversalNeighborhood` builds its adjacency by adding **both** `subject→object` and `object→subject` for every traversable edge, so the walk expands over an undirected neighborhood. Dave, verbatim: *"Undirected L4 neighborhood, not a directed descendant walk… Traversal expands adjacency, not `owns` parent→child."* **THE LIE IS AT DEPTH 2, AND ONLY THERE.** Measured over the SMCI anchor: the operator serves **20 / 22 / 22** at depths 1 / 2 / 3 where the family tree gives **20 / 21 / 22**. The single divergent node is `CycThornburyCapitalLtd`, which arrives at depth 2 through **cycle 1's closing edge** — as a neighbor two undirected hops out, not as a child three directed hops down. **NO DECLARED FIGURE MOVES**, because every demonstration this phase makes sits at the declared default depth of **3**, where both shapes give 22. **NOT FIXED IN `src/`** — same `D-04` posture and the same class as `D-33`: recorded, not closed. **The remedy is documentary:** spec §C and §D state that L4 is a **neighborhood**, and that a directed tree is not what this SDK walk is. `FamilyScenario.depth_by_node` keeps the **corrected undirected figures** — wave 4 had written a directed claim into it that the measurement falsified, and the correction stands rather than the claim. **PART 2 — CONTEXT DEBT: SERVE.** Two numbers were on the table and they are **different things**, which is why neither could be quoted alone. **`0.909`** treats *"20 of 22 members lack a PostgreSQL row"* as a single lump of context debt; against the declared `debt_tolerance` of `0.25` that **409s and kills criteria 12 and 33** — the very population the phase exists to serve. **`0.0909`** is the **whitepaper factor path the scorer already runs**, and against `0.25` it **serves**. Dave: *"Do not calibrate `debt_tolerance` to rescue a 0.909… Don't raise tolerance to 0.95 and don't pretend 0.909 is the whitepaper number."* **§E.2's OWN `[TBC]` ALREADY POINTED THE RIGHT WAY** — it routes an absent attribute row to **`S`** and says *"serve"*. The arithmetic that appeared to contradict it was the lump reading, not the factor path. **WHAT SHIPS.** §E.2 is filled with the **measured factor table** — the one that produced `0.0909` — and `debt_tolerance: "0.25"`. The shortfall is served as the **`unresolved_jurisdiction` roster finding** (`D-IMPL-229`), not as a refusal. **HOW IT IS GATED, AND THIS IS THE LOAD-BEARING HALF.** The assertion is that **`D_c` MOVES WHEN THE BOUNDARY MOVES**, together with the **20-member roster** — **NOT `D_c == 0.0909` forever.** A frozen scalar is a constant that agrees with itself; a debt score that does not move when its inputs move is the idle-gate class arriving through a float. **NO NEW GATE ID IS MINTED** — the roster's home is `CFT-G09` and the movement assertion is a test; the roster stays **SIXTEEN**, `CFT-G01`..`CFT-G16`. **THE SPEC FILL IS A GATE-1 AMENDMENT** under the `D-IMPL-222` discipline: §E.2's `[TBC]` becomes measured values, which is substance rather than form, and the `Gate 1 status` row records it as such. **Governs:** what §D and §C say the L4 walk is, §E.2's factor table and tolerance, and how `D_c` is asserted. **Related:** `D-33` (traversal types hops on edges, the sibling mechanism gap), `D-IMPL-229` (the roster finding this serves through), `D-IMPL-222` (amend before execute), `D-13` (roster, never a cardinality — and now, never a frozen scalar either).

**D-IMPL-231 — `D_c` moves on IDENTITY DISPUTE, never on a missing PostgreSQL jurisdiction; the two twenties are different populations and §E.2 says so; and a flag with nothing measured behind it is dropped rather than shipped.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-09-01. Approver: Dave, confirming the executing agent's reading after it declined to implement a rider literally and said why. **PART 1 — THE DEBT AXIS.** `D_c`'s `S` counts members whose **identity** no finding disputes. It does **not** count members holding a `ccf_v2.legal_entity` row. Dave: *"`D_c` moves on identity dispute, not on 'missing Postgres jurisdiction.'"* **The attribute boundary is `S`-as-roster, and it was already ruled SERVE** (`D-IMPL-230`). **Wiring `D_c` to those 20 rows is precisely how `0.909` and a `409` are produced — the outcome §E.2 and criteria 12 and 33 forbid.** The agent's **sabotage 3** — folding attribute coverage into `S` — produced exactly `0.909090…`, and **that sabotage is the control**, not an anomaly. **THE THIRD TEST STAYS:** the attribute boundary moves the **roster** and does **not** move the **debt**. It goes red if anyone quietly reverses the SERVE ruling, which is the only assertion that can catch that reversal. **WHY THE AGENT WAS RIGHT TO DIVERGE AND TO SAY SO.** `D-IMPL-230`'s rider read *"`D_c` moves when the boundary moves"*, and there are two boundaries. Implemented literally against the attribute boundary it would have reintroduced the forbidden number; the agent gated the boundary `D_c` genuinely has, asserted the roster beside it, and **flagged the divergence rather than burying it**. That is the behavior `D-IMPL-227` asked for — where the instruction underdetermines the work, surface it instead of choosing silently. **PART 2 — THE TWO TWENTIES ARE DIFFERENT SETS, AND §E.2 MUST SAY SO IN ONE LINE.** `S`'s twenty and the roster's twenty **overlap in 19**, not 20: `SubSuperMicroComputerBV` is **roster-only**, the anchor is in **`S`'s numerator only**, and `SuperMicroComputerBV` is in **neither**. **`D_c ≈ 0.0909` is NOT "20 missing jurisdictions."** A reader meeting the two numbers together will assume it is, which is why the line is mandatory and why `test_the_two_twenties_are_different_populations` stays under that name. **PART 3 — `--principal` IS NOT SHIPPED, AND `--role` SURVIVES ONLY IF IT DOES SOMETHING.** `deployment.read` states in as many words that no per-principal discrimination over the family population has been measured. Dave: *"A flag that changes nothing is `D-IMPL-228` again."* — the nine-row fiction in argv form. **`--role` is kept only if a role change is ACTUALLY OBSERVED to change the served payload. If it is not, the flag is dropped too and the README says so.** An unmeasured switch is not a smaller version of a feature; it is a claim the product cannot support. **Governs:** which boundary `D_c` is gated on, §E.2's disclosure of the two populations, and the CLI's flag surface. **Related:** `D-IMPL-230` (the SERVE ruling and the movement rider this interprets), `D-IMPL-229` (the roster finding), `D-IMPL-228` (rows that cannot fire), `D-IMPL-227` (surface the underdetermined case, do not choose silently).

**D-IMPL-232 — the ELEVEN gaps Phase 24.4 found are RECORDED here and NONE of them is closed: `D-26`..`D-31` and `D-33`..`D-36` as SDK-surface gaps, `D-32` as an ESTATE gap that is not an SDK gap at all.** RECORDED. Date: 2026-09-01. Raised by: Claude Code, at plan `24.4-14`, discharging locked ROADMAP criterion 49. **This entry RECORDS; it rules nothing and it closes nothing.** **READ THIS FIRST — THE NUMBERS `D-26` THROUGH `D-36` ARE PHASE-LOCAL AND THEY COLLIDE WITH PHASE 17's.** Every gap below is `D-NN` **of `.planning/phases/24.4-corporate-family-tree-cp-04-first-multi-store-product-fluree/24.4-CONTEXT.md` and of ROADMAP criterion 49**, and it is a DIFFERENT decision from the `D-NN` of the same number in `17-CONTEXT.md`, which this log already cites repeatedly. Measured before writing, so the hazard is stated as a fact rather than as a worry: at the commit before this append, `` `D-27` `` occurs **35** times in this file and `` `D-32` `` **19**, and the ones a reader meets first are Phase 17's — `D-27` the condemned-tree decision and `D-32` the no-data-in-`examples/` rule. A bare `grep 'D-26' docs/DECISIONS.md` therefore CANNOT tell the two families apart, and the verify line in plan `24.4-14` does exactly that grep. Each gap below is consequently written as **`24.4 D-NN`** as well as by its bare number, so a reader who wants only this family has a token that finds only this family. Nothing is renumbered — `D-31` of the decisions discipline, ids are stable and append-only — and no alias is minted. **NUMBERING, MEASURED BEFORE APPENDING, BECAUSE GETTING IT WRONG COLLIDES WITH A RESERVED ID.** `D-IMPL-232` occurs **0** times in `docs/DECISIONS.md` and **0** times in `references/CCF_SDK_DE_REQUIREMENTS.md`, against positive controls of **1** occurrence of `D-IMPL-231` and **12** of `D-IMPL-201` in this file — so the zeros come from an instrument that fires rather than from a reader that found nothing. `D-IMPL-202`…`211` remain RESERVED as the ten DE-requirement candidates (`D-IMPL-212`, `D-IMPL-214`), so the free id after `231` is `232` and not `202`. Entry-opening lines rather than mentions were counted, the distinction `D-IMPL-200` and `D-IMPL-201` each had to make. **THE POSTURE, STATED ONCE AND GOVERNING ALL ELEVEN.** `D-04` of `24-CONTEXT.md`: **a minor phase RECORDS gaps and a separate phase closes them.** Criterion 49 makes that mechanical rather than a promise — *"no file under `src/` is modified by it"* — and it is asserted here as a pathspec diff between two pinned commits by `tests/examples/test_cp_04_phase_record.py::test_no_file_under_src_moved_across_the_phase`, with the instrument proven able to report a change and the pathspec proven to name a tracked subject. **Every entry below is RECORDED. None is RESOLVED.** `24.4 D-31`'s closure is Phase 24.5. `24.4 D-32` and `24.4 D-33` are closed by NEITHER this phase NOR `ccf_dataprep` this sitting. **`24.4 D-26` — THE FLUREE ADAPTER FLOORS BUT CANNOT PIN.** `Fluree-Min-T` sets a LOWER bound — *"do not answer me from older than this `t`"* — and leaves the upper bound open. No `@t:` and no `from: ledger@t:N` construction exists anywhere in `src/ccf/graph/backends/fluree.py::FlureeGraphStore.post_query`, which sends `"Fluree-Min-T": str(self._min_t)` as a header and nothing else about `t`; the module's own docstring says the header serves *"exactly one role — threading `Fluree-Min-T` for read-after-write"*. **On a quiet ledger a floor and a pin are indistinguishable**, which is why the reproducibility claim is bounded to a quiescent ledger FOR THAT RUN and to nothing wider. A floor presented as a pin would be a **vacant guarantee** rather than `EXAM-06`. **`24.4 D-27` — `graph_snapshot_at` IS A `datetime` AND STORE `t` IS AN `int`.** `src/ccf/products/contract.py::ProductLineage` declares `graph_snapshot_at: datetime` and documents it as *"The temporal anchor of the graph state read"*. A Fluree transaction number is an integer sequence. There is no type into which a transaction-snapshot pin could be written on the shipped contract, so transaction-snapshot pinning has no expression at L6 even if the adapter grew one. **`24.4 D-28` — FLUREE `@iso:` SEARCHES EVENT TIME, NOT TRANSACTION TIME.** It resolves nearest-at-or-before against `db:time` and is backdatable. That is legitimate for a CLOCK pin and wrong for a TRANSACTION pin, and **neither of the two is CCF `as_of`**, which is a cut over observations rather than over writes. `D-IMPL-88` stands unamended: Fluree's `t` must not implement `as_of`. Three axes, and the SDK has a name for one of them. **`24.4 D-29` — THE ADAPTER DOCSTRING COLLAPSES THREE TIME AXES INTO TWO.** The module docstring of `src/ccf/graph/backends/fluree.py` sets transaction time against CCF `as_of` and does not name event time as a third thing, which is the axis `24.4 D-28` is about. **Recorded, and deliberately NOT fixed:** `src/` is not edited in this phase, and a docstring correction is still an edit to `src/`. **`24.4 D-30` — THE MCP RESOURCE URI CANNOT ADDRESS A PARAMETERIZED PRODUCT, AND THE BUILDER CANNOT OMIT THE RESOURCE.** `runtime/ccf_runtime/mcp/egress.py::PRODUCT_URI_TEMPLATE` is `ccf-product://{tenant}/{product_class}/{version}` and has nowhere to put cp-04's anchor LEI or its `max_depth`, so a standing parameter-free answer is the only thing that address shape can name. **Every Tier 2 and later product hits this.** The MECHANISM face this phase measured is recorded beside it: `runtime/ccf_runtime/mcp/egress.py::build_egress_server` registers the product resource UNCONDITIONALLY and only the tool sits behind `expose_product_tool`, so a **tool-only door is not expressible through that builder** — which is `24.4 D-34` below, and which is why `CFT-G13` asserts a registered resource that REFUSES rather than an absent one. **`24.4 D-31` — DECLARED PRODUCT GATES HAVE NO SDK OR CI EXPRESSION.** Measured at the phase's context sitting: 40 product-level gate ids across four products, and `grep -rnE "OFS-G|FTS-G|[A-Z]{2,4}-G[0-9]{2}" --include=*.py src/ runtime/` returns **0**. Declaration lives in spec prose and artifact comments; execution lives in hand-written pytest; the link between them is naming convention. cp-04 narrows the gap by declaring its sixteen ids as DATA under a closed schema — `examples/cp-04-corporate-family-tree/artifacts/gates.yaml` against `docs/schemas/product-gates/cp.product-gates.json` — but **a declaration nothing checks is still unchecked**. This is a DIFFERENT SEAM from `24.4 D-26`..`D-28` (mechanism) and from `24.4 D-29` (a docstring defect). **Its closure is Phase 24.5's checker** (`D-24`, `D-IMPL-224`). **`24.4 D-32` — THE ESTATE GAP ONTOLOGY ROLE 1 BECAME. THIS IS NOT AN SDK-SURFACE GAP AND IS DELIBERATELY NOT FILED AS ONE.** Added to criterion 49 by Dave on 2026-08-31. The gap is about the DATA, not the machinery: *class-diverse populations — `Person` **46**, `SpecialPurposeVehicle` **50**, 5-class **123**, 4-class **68**, 3-class **29** — sit in components that no LEI-bearing anchor reaches downward.* **The measurement, recorded rather than the withdrawn claim restated:** over all **748** family nodes, no LEI-bearing anchor reaches a node outside the 7-class `LegalPerson` `Corporation` profile within depth 3; all **50** SPVs are owned by non-LEI `HLD-*` corporations; and a SECOND anchor was measured and REFUSED — Extreme Networks (**22** nodes) and Celanese (**53**) carry no SPV and no Bank, and their only class variation is `Guarantor` **added to the root**, an ADDITIVE class rather than an exclusion, and a guarantor belongs inside a credit family anyway. **What followed from it:** ontology role 1 was STRUCK from cp-04, `CFT-G17` was WITHDRAWN and must never be minted, and criterion 41 is **WITHDRAWN IN PLACE** — the number still exists and carries its own withdrawal record. **A positive-property restatement was refused BY NAME** — *"every admitted node's class is in the declared set"* is a tautology over a class-homogeneous population and would read as coverage while measuring nothing, which is the fourteen-idle-gates class. (3) **Fix-rows are CLUSTERED, not enumerated into sub-phases** — 24.4's nine SDK-shaped gaps already fall into **time** (`24.4-D-26` the adapter floors but cannot pin, `D-27` `datetime` vs int `t`, `D-28` `@iso:` is event time not `as_of`, `D-29` three axes collapsed to two), **traversal** (`D-33` edges only, `D-36` undirected neighborhood), **door/gates** (`D-30` unaddressable parameterized product, `D-34` no way to omit a resource, `D-31` declared gates have no SDK expression, plus 24.4 deferred row 9 — refusals reach clients as prose) and **ingest** (`D-35` claims by class co-occurrence); `24.4-D-32` and `D-37` are ESTATE gaps and are not SDK work. **D-IMPL-243 — Cross-revision replay after Phase 24.5 (CR-01): a new required-default field in the canonical form is a GENERATION change; a field is hash-transparent only when its sentinel means the old contract, marked at the field and OMITTED by `_normalize` when the value IS that sentinel; a non-sentinel value is rendered and moves the hash; a record whose canonical field set differs from the running canonicalizer on a NON-transparent field is refused by name; adopter stores from before 24.5 are not promised byte-identical replay.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-09-02. Ruled by: Dave, at the Phase 24.5 execution close, on `24.5-REVIEW.md` finding CR-01 after the orchestrator reproduced it (identical `TraversalNeighborhoodParameters` hash `5aab0c9f…` at `13bd250`, `ef583667…` at HEAD) and after the orchestrator wrote down, from the types, each field's sentinel, its pre-`13bd250` shape (every field absent), its owning plan's prose and a verdict — and Dave ticked the table below. **WRITTEN BEFORE THE EDIT** (`D-IMPL-222`). Nothing here is written that Dave did not state (`D-IMPL-227`). **THE FACT.** `src/ccf/contracts/canonical.py::_normalize` renders every field of every model, defaults included; each sentinel-defaulted field 24.5 added therefore moved the content hash of every model carrying it. `src/ccf/replay/engine.py::replay` compares exactly those hashes (`parameter_hash` per step via `src/ccf/operators/base.py::mint_provenance`, the `D-11` `graph_query_sequence` pins, `product_content_address`) and `src/ccf/controlplane/registry.py::register` versions every Control Plane document by `content_hash(artifact)`. `D-IMPL-240` (1) re-sealed the only content addresses IN THE TREE; persisted records and registered versions outside the tree are the scope this entry rules. **THE POSTURE, Dave's words:** *"Do not pretend additive defaults are hash-neutral. New required-default fields in the canonical form are a generation change. Pre-24.5 persisted records with a traversal step will not match."* Replay of a record whose canonical field set ≠ the running canonicalizer on a non-transparent field is refused by name — the token is `canonical_generation_mismatch` (none existed; measured) — *"not a quiet address drift and not a silent upgrade."* *"In-tree seals already rewritten under 240 stay. Adopter stores from before 24.5 are not promised byte-identical replay."* That sentence goes into `D-GATE-24.5`. **THE RULE, Dave's words:** *"A field is hash-transparent only when its sentinel means the old contract: the walk / table / request is observationally the same as a record written before the field existed. Mark that at the field (`ccf_hash_transparent`). `_normalize` omits it when the value is that sentinel. Any non-sentinel value is rendered and must move the hash. That is not 'defaults never count.' It is 'silence equals yesterday.'"* Option A of the review, narrowly — *"A, narrowly. Not B. B writes 'identity is revision-scoped' into the gate and walks past §7.10."* Re-register-everything-on-upgrade stays available as an OPS note for artifacts marked non-transparent; it is not the default posture for traversal hashes. *"Record bytes stay under D-IMPL-89 byte-first. Transparency is only `_normalize` for the hashes CR-01 named."* **THE TABLE — measured from the types by the orchestrator, TICKED by Dave:**
