**D-IMPL-256 — The three 24.6 delivery-boundary questions RULED BEFORE WAVE 1, and the DELIVERY-BOUNDARY REPLAY INVARIANT added to the criteria: every governed determination that crosses a CCF delivery boundary reaches the replay writer before the response is released; a boundary that cannot is unavailable, not partially governed; replay belongs to the determination, never to the transport.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-09-04. Ruled by: Dave, remotely, after the planning report; verbatim in `24.6-RULINGS.md` §7, which governs. He noted he could not yet inspect the files (the branch was unpushed; pushed to `origin/phase-24.6` at this sitting). **(1) MCP standing-resource denial — RECORD IT:** *"Mint the replay at the entitlement audit's instant. A standing-resource access is still a governed request to the CCF, even though it is not expressed through the same tool-call ProductRequest shape. … No fulfilled Context Product does not mean no Decision Replay."* The resource-request identity must answer *"what resource was requested, by whom/perspective, at what instant, under which policy, and why fulfillment was refused. Otherwise we would have just created a replay hole based on transport shape."* **(2) Entitling door with no recorder — UNAVAILABLE FOR ALL GOVERNED REQUESTS:** *"a door configured to make governed determinations without the ability to record them is not a valid governed door. … That would make auditability contingent on outcome. The correct invariant is: If a delivery boundary is required to mint replay and has no functioning recorder, it cannot make any governed determination."* *"Prefer fail-at-construction/boot where practical; otherwise fail closed uniformly."* This also removes the residual status channel the checker measured at a recorder-less door. **(3) Experience server — SAME TREATMENT IN 24.6, NARROWLY:** *"That is a delivery-boundary rule, not an egress-door-specific feature. … leaving them untouched means 24.6 would knowingly ship another delivery seam violating the very architecture the phase exists to establish."* Scope: *"only the three measured entitlement paths and whatever shared mechanism they require"* — `runtime/ccf_runtime/mcp/experience.py` `context_product` (:879), `get_context` (:1018), `get_lineage` (:1063); *"not a general experience-server rewrite."* **THE INVARIANT, HIS WORDS (criterion 36):** *"Every governed determination that crosses a CCF delivery boundary—fulfilled or refused, tool or resource, authorized or denied—must reach the replay writer before the response is released. A delivery boundary unable to satisfy that invariant is unavailable, not partially governed."* *"That would make the recorder seam on GovernedResolver more than an implementation convenience. It becomes a structural property of the delivery path."* **THE SEQUENCE PRINCIPLE, HIS WORDS:** *"request → identity/policy → determination → replay → disclosure shaping → transport encoding — not: request → determination → HTTP/MCP → transport notices refusal → writes replay. Replay belongs to the governed determination, not to HTTP or MCP. That matters because otherwise the standing-resource/tool asymmetry simply reappears somewhere else."* **WHY BEFORE WAVE 1:** *"The checker has found the same defect three times: a governed determination can occur without reaching the replay writer. That isn't implementation trivia."* **APPLIED:** CRITERIA-LOCK Amendment 2 (criteria 24, 25, 35 amended in the marked form; criterion 36 added; digest re-pinned), `24.6-CONTEXT.md` D-34..D-37, plans 07/09/10/13/15 revised and re-checked. **Next free decision id: `D-IMPL-257`.** **Related:** `D-IMPL-253`, `D-IMPL-254` (this is its delivery-path corollary), `D-IMPL-255`, `24.6-LEDGER.md` L-03, L-08, L-21.

**D-IMPL-257 — The 24.6 fence WIDENED NARROWLY for citation maintenance the phase's own SDK deletions caused (Dave, 2026-09-04 21:40 MST, during Wave 5, in reply to plan 03's open finding).** **CONTEXT:** plan 24.6-03 deleted the `effective_debt_ceiling` helper from `src/ccf/products/gates.py` as criterion 6 required; plan 24.6-05 deleted the `_refuse_empty_results` step and the `empty-result-refusal` kind with its coverage test as criteria 14/15 required. Each deletion stranded `path::Symbol` citations in dated pages, and `make lint` (`cite03-node-id`) went RED — six findings after plan 03, nine after plan 05. Plan 03 measured three options and picked none; the criteria fence (`examples/` open only for cp-04, hw1, cp-01's narrow publication correction) closed cp-01/02/03. **DAVE'S RULING, VERBATIM:** *"I would not leave lint red until close, and I would not defer known false references merely because the files sit outside the original example fence. The SDK symbol was deliberately removed by 24.6, so those citations have become mechanically stale because of this phase. That satisfies the same dependency principle we used earlier: an SDK change may open an example surface narrowly when the SDK change itself makes that surface false."* *"Narrowly widen the 24.6 fence to correct the four stranded `effective_debt_ceiling` citations in the CP-SPEC pages for cp-01 through cp-03. The edits are citation/prose maintenance caused directly by the 24.6 SDK deletion. They do not reopen those rungs for behavioral changes, assembler changes, version bumps, transcript rebuilding, or republishing."* *"I would make that a dated scope amendment and identify the four exact measured occurrences. Then rewrite each to cite the replacement SDK semantics/symbol that actually governs the statement now. Don't simply delete a citation if doing so leaves the surrounding assertion unsupported."* *"SDK-caused stale reference → fix now. Previously existing stale behavior/prose unrelated to the changed SDK surface → wait for that rung's return trip."* *"No reason to interrupt Plan 05. Record this ruling and schedule the four surgical corrections at the earliest dependency-safe point; then continue execution."* **THE FOUR MEASURED OCCURRENCES (the ruling's scope):** `examples/cp-01-counterparty-reference-snapshot/spec/CP-SPEC-001_Counterparty_Reference_Snapshot.md:1121`; `examples/cp-02-facility-terms-snapshot/spec/CP-SPEC-002_Facility_Terms_Snapshot.md:930` and `:1225`; `examples/cp-03-obligor-financial-spread/spec/CP-SPEC-003_Obligor_Financial_Spread.md:1409` — all four inside 2026-09-03 SUPERSEDED notes describing what `24.5-L-14` shipped. Each cite is recast in place as prose naming the deleted helper, with a dated parenthetical citing what governs now: `default_debt_tolerance` on `src/ccf/products/contract.py::ServeObligations` (a DEFAULT filling an omission only — `D-IMPL-251` C1=A), the one fold in `src/ccf/products/constraints.py::resolve_effective_request`, and the `tolerance-exceeded` shell from `src/ccf/products/gates.py::refuse_over_tolerance`; the debt half of `DeclaredObligationRefusal` and its 409 are retired, the new kind's HTTP status being plan 09's. No other line in those pages changes. **APPLIED BY THE ORCHESTRATOR UNDER THE STATED PRINCIPLE, BEYOND THE FOUR NAMED — flagged for Dave, reversible by a one-line revert each:** (a) `CP-SPEC-001…md:1266`, a `::_refuse_empty_results` cite stranded by plan 05 AFTER the ruling was written (same page, same class, same cause); (b) `docs/surface-changes/24.5-15-the-empty-operator-gate-s-two-halves-by-name.md:124`, a `::test_envelope_for_empty_result_refusal` cite in a prior phase's surface-change fragment (recast to prose with a dated retirement note; `docs/SURFACE-CHANGES.md` regenerated by `make surface-changes`, never hand-edited); (c) `CP-SPEC-004_Corporate_Family_Tree.md:291` and `:1148`, the two cp-04 cites of the same helper — cp-04's page was ALREADY inside the fence, so this is not a widening; plan 14 still owns that page's §B.4.1 supersession and depth/1.1.0 prose. **NOT DONE, DELIBERATELY (the second half of the principle):** the cp-01/02/03 `ccf_config.yaml` parameter descriptions and spec §D.7 notes that still say a tolerance breach "refuses with 409" are behavior prose whose truth changes when plan 09 assigns the new kind its status — not a stranded citation, lint-clean, and left for those rungs' return trip unless Dave rules otherwise. **RECORDED:** CRITERIA-LOCK Amendment 3 (the header's fence sentence and criterion 1 amended in the marked form on the line; digest re-pinned; before-text preserved in `24.6-CRITERIA-LOCK.md`). **Next free decision id: `D-IMPL-258`.** **Related:** `D-IMPL-214` (the widening-is-a-dated-D-IMPL rule criterion 1 cites), `D-IMPL-251`, `D-IMPL-255` (4), `D-IMPL-256`, plan summaries `24.6-03` F-1 and `24.6-05`.

**D-IMPL-258 — Five 24.6 execution findings RULED mid-phase (Dave, 2026-09-05 03:09 MST, during wave 10): absence is a governed fact, not a versionless artifact; the `policy_bindings` disclosure leak is CLOSED in 24.6 and BLOCKS the gate; the HTTP `403 → 404` shell change is intentional and kept; the three archived servers keep their minimal recorder bindings; a class default for an undeclared parameter is a configuration failure, never a caller refusal.** **CONTEXT:** plan SUMMARIES 04 F-1, 07 F-1, 08 F-1/F-2, 09 F-1, 10 F-1, 16 F-1 and the orchestrator's STATE.md roll-up carried five open items to Dave; he ruled all five in one message while plan 13 ran. **DAVE, VERBATIM — (1) absent-policy replay pin:** *"keep `policy=None`; do not weaken D-IMPL-26. 'No applicable policy artifact existed' is not a versioned artifact and should not be represented by a synthetic/versionless artifact pin. That would violate the same no fake artifacts principle we established for provenance."* Shape: *"replay Policy Bindings dimension: `policy=None`; preserve the consulted policy key / lookup identity / absence determination in the appropriate determination/provenance evidence; do not fabricate `ArtifactPin(key=..., version=None)`; do not relax the validator that requires real artifact pins to have versions. Replay must be able to distinguish 'no policy applied' from 'policy provenance was lost', but that distinction does not require pretending absence is an artifact."* Record: *"Absence is a governed fact, not a versionless artifact. Real policy pins remain `(id/version)`; no applicable policy is represented explicitly as absence plus the consulted lookup provenance."* **(2) `policy_bindings` disclosure leak:** *"fix it in 24.6. Do not allowlist it. This directly violates D-27/D-IMPL-254. If unauthorized and nonexistent subjects differ in `policy_bindings` by either key presence or value, then they are not consumer-observationally equivalent. The allowlist would merely teach the invariant test to accept the leak. The distinction we established was: internal truth ≠ permitted disclosure. Therefore: replay/internal determination may retain the actual policy bindings that produced the decision; the externally disclosed `RefusalEnvelope` must normalize/suppress that field so unauthorized and nonexistent cases have the same observable policy-binding shape at the same disclosure level; the control should prove equivalence at HTTP and MCP. Given your note that this would become a real A2A leak, I consider this blocking for the 24.6 gate."* **(3) HTTP `403 error-code → 404 envelope`:** *"keep the new behavior. This is an intentional wire change required by the suppression-silence ruling, not a regression to revert. A `403` for unauthorized and `404` for nonexistent would itself reveal the distinction D-27 requires us to suppress. The shared `404` plus the governed shell is the better external contract."* Record prominently as a breaking delivery-surface change: *"governed entitlement denial returns the same externally observable status family as unavailable/nonexistent; the body is the canonical refusal shell; internal/replay truth can still record `unauthorized`; no known governed outcome becomes `500`. I would not invent another compatibility shim that resurrects the `403`."* **(4) three archived servers:** *"keep the minimal recorder bindings. Since those archived servers are still executed by the repository's tests and invoke the current runtime builder, they are not actually isolated historical binaries; they remain compatibility consumers of the live SDK. … Keep the minimal recorder wiring required for archived executable fixtures to remain compatible with the current runtime. Do not otherwise modernize, rewrite, republish, or reinterpret the archived examples. If we later want `archive/` to be truly immutable historical evidence, that should be a separate decision to decouple its tests/runtime dependencies."* **(5) plan 04's class default for an unexposed parameter:** *"I would not treat that as a governed request refusal. Under Q2, a product default is part of the request contract. Therefore a default naming a parameter the contract does not expose is a malformed/internally inconsistent declaration. That should fail registration/configuration/boot validation, not produce a shell to a caller. The caller did nothing wrong, and the fabric cannot truthfully say the request violated a limit. The Control Plane contradicts itself. So the rule is: Default for undeclared parameter → configuration/invariant failure. Caller outside a valid declared constraint → governed shell. If Plan 04 merely uses a test to prove that a hidden default cannot silently constrain a request, fine. If it actually converts the malformed declaration into a runtime caller refusal, I would correct that before close."* On `restored_surfaces` (05) and the partial `CLNT-02` supersession (07): *"keep them recorded unless one contradicts the rulings above."* **REQUIRED BEFORE PLAN 14's PUBLICATION CHECKPOINT (his list):** the `policy_bindings` leak closed with a sabotage/control; absent-policy replay represented as explicit absence, not a fake pin; the 404 shell change documented as intentional; archive bindings retained as narrowly scoped compatibility edits; confirmation that plan 04 does not turn malformed defaults into caller-owned refusal semantics. **MEASURED AT THE RULING (orchestrator):** (1) plan 08 shipped exactly the ruled shape — `policy=None`, the consulted key in the internal envelope's `error_code`, `detail` and `resource.tenant_id`, validator untouched; nothing to change, recorded. (5) plan 04 did NOT ship a caller shell: `src/ccf/products/constraints.py` raises `ValueError` (an invariant failure, deviation 1) when a class default names a parameter the contract does not declare — but it raises at RESOLUTION time, per request, not at registration/boot; the correction moves the check to declaration validation so a self-contradicting Control Plane fails before it serves. (2) and (5) are applied by an orchestrator-dispatched fix on `phase-24.6` recorded in `24.6-D-IMPL-258-FIXES.md`; (3) documented in the `24.6-09` surface-change fragment's migration note; (4) recorded, no change. **APPLIED READING, FOR CONFIRMATION (orchestrator, not Dave):** "the same disclosure level" is realized as suppression of `policy_bindings` in the disclosed shell at every level BELOW `full`, where the existing D-27 control requires equivalence; at `full` the shipped permitted-difference table (`detail`, `fields.cause`, `fields.error_code`) governs and what crosses is measured and stated — if Dave meant `full` too, that is one more table row. **Next free decision id: `D-IMPL-259`.** **Related:** `D-IMPL-26`, `D-IMPL-251`, `D-IMPL-253` (Q2, Q18, Q27), `D-IMPL-254`, `D-IMPL-256`, `D-IMPL-257`.

**D-IMPL-259 — cp-04 `max_depth` has a declared request-contract MINIMUM of 1; the floor is the parameter's valid domain, held by the SDK's request validation, and neither a policy constraint nor an example-local bounds check (Dave, 2026-09-05 04:35 MST, at plan 24.6-14's publication checkpoint).** **CONTEXT:** plan 14's publication record (F-3) measured that `MAX_DEPTH=0` was SERVED as a one-node family (seal `d7180a0c…`) — plan 13 deleted the example-local `argument_bounds` block, which had carried the floor of 1 together with the bound of 6, and the floor went with it; the SDK ships no number and nothing re-declared one. Dave approved publication of both pages **conditional on correcting this first**, because the staged cp-04 build (`eb5ee562…`) represented zero as valid. **DAVE, VERBATIM:** *"declare a floor of `1` on the request contract. I would fix this before publication if the staged cp-04 page currently represents zero as valid. This follows the model we just established. A family-tree traversal depth of zero is not a useful product preference in this contract; `1` is the minimum meaningful supported request. More importantly, the SDK now has the correct place to express that fact: the request contract."* The ruling: *"cp-04 `max_depth` has a declared request-contract minimum of 1 and a technical maximum of 100. The default remains 6. Requests below 1 or above 100 are governed request-validity refusals returned as data; values 1–100 are valid and are never clamped."* The three-part definition: *"`default = 6` — product preference when omitted; `minimum = 1` — declared parameter validity boundary; `maximum = 100` — backend technical capability boundary."* The nuance: *"don't turn `1` into a Policy Constraint. It is simply the parameter's valid domain. And don't resurrect the old example-local bounds check; this should use the SDK request-contract validation surface established in 24.6."* On the sequence: *"Apply the floor through the request contract, add the boundary controls (`0` refuses, `1` serves), rebuild/re-pin cp-04, confirm the estate hasn't moved, re-resolve `f20ed519…` again, and then publish both pages."* On the other finding (F-1, the replay-carriage sentence on cp-01/02/03): *"leave cp-01/02/03 alone. The phase did not measure their replay wiring, so we should not generalize cp-04's result into those rungs. The cp-04-specific correction is sufficient. Carry the other three as measured/unresolved rather than guessing."* **ONE CORRECTION TO THE PREMISE, FLAGGED RATHER THAN SILENTLY APPLIED (orchestrator):** the declared default is **3**, not 6, and has been since Gate 1 — `ccf_config.yaml` `defaults: max_depth: 3`, measured as the smallest depth at which cycle 1 is visible (CP-SPEC-004 §B.4.1); 6 was the deleted ceiling. "Remains" reads as *no change*, so the default is left at 3 and no value moved; if Dave meant 6, that is a separate ruling. **APPLIED READING, FOR CONFIRMATION:** "above 100 … request-validity refusal" is realized as it already was under `D-IMPL-253` Q21 — a `constraint-refusal` with authority `technical`, returned as data — and the new domain mechanism carries only the floor for cp-04; both are governed refusals returned as data, in two vocabularies (`product-request-violation` / `below-minimum` and `constraint-refusal` / `bound-exceeded`), which is the three-part definition's own split. **MECHANISM SHIPPED (SDK, `src/ccf/products/request.py`):** `ArgumentDomain` (`minimum` / `maximum`, `Decimal | None`, inclusive, hash-transparent at `None`); the seventh declaration key `argument_domains` on `ProductRequestContract`, read by `from_declared` and held by a validator refusing a domain over an undeclared, magnitude-less or inert parameter and a declared default outside its own domain; reasons `below-minimum` / `above-maximum` APPENDED to `ProductRequestViolationReason`; `refuse_request`'s domain step LAST, so `resolve_effective_request` step 5 refuses a caller's out-of-domain value with no deployment code. **cp-04:** `argument_domains: {max_depth: {minimum: 1}}` on the request contract; boundary controls `tests/examples/test_cp_04_traversal.py` — a no-store control (the SDK's verdict over the declaration) and two live asks (`0` refused as `product-request-violation` / `below-minimum` with no tree; `1` served at `max_depth_applied == 1`). Lane unchanged at `1.1.0`: relative to the last published lane the floor is what it was. **Next free decision id: `D-IMPL-260`.** **Related:** `D-IMPL-251` C1=A/C5, `D-IMPL-253` Q2/Q21, `D-IMPL-258` (5), plan `24.6-13`, `24.6-PUBLICATION.md`.

**D-IMPL-260 — Phase 24.6 gate HELD for one correction pass: ten close findings ruled as implementation corrections under the 24.6 invariants already locked, no design sitting (Dave, 2026-09-05 09:56 MST, after the §3.1 panel and review).** **CONTEXT:** the close sequence ran whole — plan 15's evidence, Dave's build evaluation (cp-01 APPROVE with F-1 carried; cp-04 APPROVE; phase APPROVE TO CLOSE subject to gates), the cross-AI panel (`24.6-CLOSE-REVIEWS.md`) and the single-agent review (`24.6-REVIEW.md`) — and the orchestrator presented ten verified questions (P-A … P-J) plus the carried items rather than disposing them. **DAVE, VERBATIM:** *"I need you to do better than this. I would hold the gate for one more correction pass. The close evidence is strong, but several of these are not follow-on polish; they are direct consequences of the 24.6 invariants we locked."* His rulings, mapped to the ten: **(1) P-I / criterion 10 — fix now, do not carry.** *"An override attempt is part of the governed request and policy-resolution provenance whether the request ultimately fulfills or refuses. If refusal records drop it only because the current helper returns provenance on the success path, that is an implementation asymmetry in exactly the area 24.6 owns. Change the refusal path so the replay record preserves the attempted override and the authority/entitlement result that rejected it. Do not weaken criterion 10 and do not substitute corrected docstrings for missing replay evidence."* **(2) P-J / criterion 22 — fix now.** *"The resource key is another observable presence channel. My earlier allowance that 'request identity may legitimately differ' was never permission for authorization state to change whether an identity field exists. For the same disclosure level, unauthorized and nonexistent must be consumer-observationally equivalent. Normalize the resource-key shape below full; retain the real key internally/replay as permitted. Move the ~25 assertions rather than allowlist the leak."* **(3) P-A / criterion 36 — fix now, not next phase.** *"This is the most important remaining item. Construction-time checks and a good reference resolver are not sufficient if the delivery boundary will happily release an arbitrary resolver result with no proof that replay/disclosure happened. We explicitly ruled: A governed determination cannot escape the replay writer, and a transport cannot become the replay writer. The boundary therefore needs an enforceable contract on what it accepts from a governed resolver—some typed/provable governed result indicating determination, replay and disclosure have completed. A nonconforming resolver result must not cross the boundary. This is core 24.6 work."* **(4) P-B — fix now.** *"The experience product resource must not dereference the resolver result around the common delivery semantics. We deliberately opened the three experience paths into 24.6 for this exact reason. Route the resource path through the same governed-response translation."* **(5) P-C — fix now.** *"An unregistered product class is a governed request/fulfillment outcome and should reach the caller in the canonical shell shape, not as an unrelated bare 404. The HTTP status may still be 404 if that is the ruled suppression-safe mapping; the body semantics must be the common shell."* **(6) P-D / dimension-4 role on denial —** *"use the role that actually participated; never invent one. If role/perspective participated in the denial determination, Decision Replay must record it in Perspective Conditioning. If the determination occurred before any role was established, record explicit absence rather than substituting a deployment/default role. If current code records the wrong role, fix now. If it already carries true absence, no further work is required."* **(7) P-E / second clock read —** *"acceptable only as a separate audit timestamp. The governed question retains one asked_at/determination instant. An entitlement audit event may have its own audit_at obtained from a second clock read because it is a different event. That second read must not alter policy effectivity, request identity, replay identity, disclosure choice, or the determination itself. If it is purely audit-event time, carry/no blocker. If it influences the governed determination, fix it now."* **(8) `bound.source` at minimal — fix now.** *"Minimal disclosure must not reveal that a policy authority was the source of a bound when doing so distinguishes 'you may not' from 'does not exist.' Internal truth and replay retain the source; full may disclose it when authorized. Minimal/reasoned must normalize or suppress it consistently with the same equivalence rules used for policy_bindings."* **(9) unread `PolicyConstraint.reason` — do not leave it semantically dead.** *"We deliberately put reason in the v0 Policy Constraint artifact. At minimum, it should flow into the internal resolution provenance/replay when that constraint participates. Whether it crosses into the shell remains controlled by disclosure level. I do not require that it always be shown externally, but I would not close 24.6 with a governed artifact field that the resolver simply ignores."* **(10) cp-04 fulfilled replay without resolution — fix now.** *"Q1 was one of the strongest 24.6 rulings: effective parameter provenance is semantics, not audit decoration. Fulfilled replay needs the policy/default/caller/technical resolution outcome just as refusal replay does. cp-04 cannot be the rung demonstrating the new resolution model while its fulfilled replay omits that resolution."* **The carried items:** *"Unminted gate ID: mint CFT-G19 now. We explicitly ruled that identifier; don't close with the ruling recorded but the gate absent. Pre-phase gate-tools roster red: continue to carry it exactly as you described—proved present at phase base, same failure signature, untouched cause, named future owner. Do not call that suite fully green. D-IMPL-259 / D-IMPL-258 flagged readings: keep their existing dispositions unless the fixes above falsify one of their premises. Do not reopen them merely because they are flagged. Published cp-04 page behind on two inlined test modules: rebuild and replace cp-04 once more before gate. A published page that embeds source/tests should not close the phase already behind the shipped tree. Re-resolve the artifact ID again, prove the rebuild differs only by the post-publication close fixes, then replace in place. cp-01 does not need another publish unless its embedded content also changed."* **The disposition:** *"HOLD — not because the phase is architecturally unsettled, but because the final review found several places where the implementation still does not fully enforce the architecture we already ruled. … These are implementation corrections under existing rulings. The critical close conditions are P-I, P-J, P-A, P-B/P-C, P-F, P-G, P-H, CFT-G19, and the final cp-04 republish. P-D and P-E are conditional as stated above. Once those are green and the criteria digest remains properly amended/pinned where necessary, I would expect the gate to move to APPROVE / merge / push without reopening the architecture."* (Dave's P-F/P-G/P-H letters follow his own list — `bound.source`, `reason`, cp-04 — where the close record's letters were P-G/P-H/P-F; the record maps them by content.) **EXECUTION RECORD:** `.planning/phases/24.6-…/24.6-CORRECTION-PASS.md`, one section per item with its measurement, fix commit and control. **Next free decision id: `D-IMPL-261`.** **Related:** `D-IMPL-253` Q1/Q7/Q17/Q21/Q27, `D-IMPL-254`, `D-IMPL-256`, `D-IMPL-258` (2), `24.6-CLOSE-REVIEWS.md`, `24.6-REVIEW.md`.

**D-IMPL-261 — EXAMPLES ARE PROBES, NOT REPAIR TARGETS: the example lifecycle is reset; cp-00 through cp-04 are FROZEN as diagnostic evidence; no example republishing or transcript re-pinning inside an SDK remediation phase; the cp-04 SDK gap ledger is built from existing evidence only, with four dispositions, before the next SDK phase is scoped.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-09-05 (14:15 MST). Ruled by: Dave, at the `/gsd-resume-work` sitting that opened on the held `D-GATE-24.6`, after stating the process failure in his own words: *"The examples are designed to identify shortcomings in the SDK that we did not know about before the examples were created. What I see happening now is a process where you are perfecting the example or devising a hack around a fundamental gap in the SDK, spending a ton of money doing so and getting absolutely nowhere."* **THE DIAGNOSIS HE ACCEPTED (the orchestrator's, measured against the 24.6 tree):** the SDK work in 24.6 was real (25 `src/` files, 8 `runtime/` files changed against `main`); the time went into the loop around it — cp-04 republished three times in two days, each republish re-entering the panel, the review and a correction pass; five cp-04 tests rewritten to the new mechanism instead of frozen as evidence; the depth floor (`D-IMPL-259`) handled as a condition of publishing the page; the phase's planning records larger than its SDK change. The orchestrator was optimizing for closing the phase and keeping the published artifact current; the example had done its job by the end of 24.4. **THE RULE, DAVE'S TEXT VERBATIM:** *"**Examples are probes, not repair targets.** An example changes only when the example is objectively wrong, its test is wrong, or the SDK surface it legitimately consumes was deliberately changed. Every other failure is classified as an SDK gap or an estate/environment limitation, assigned an identifier, and preserved as visible evidence."* *"No example behavior, prose, test, configuration, expected output, or local workaround may be changed merely to make an example pass around an SDK deficiency."* *"The first question on every example failure is: **‘Is this evidence of an SDK deficiency?’** If yes, example editing stops. The finding is recorded and escalated into the SDK backlog/next applicable SDK phase."* *"A known SDK-gap test may be quarantined or explicitly marked as an expected failure so that it does not prevent unrelated SDK work from proceeding, but the evidence must remain executable and must not be converted into a passing assertion by weakening or changing the example."* *"**No example republishing or transcript re-pinning occurs inside an SDK remediation phase.** After the SDK remediation phase completes, affected examples are rerun against the resulting SDK as a separate validation step. Only then are their artifacts republished if necessary."* Dave on the last paragraph: *"That last paragraph is important. It breaks the feedback loop that consumed the last two days."* The scientific loop this restores, in the words he adopted: *specify example → run it → observe SDK shortcomings → fix SDK → rerun example*; never *specify example → run it → patch example → patch tests → patch prose → patch page → patch more example*. **THE FREEZE, BROADENED BY DAVE:** *"Freeze cp-00 through cp-04 as diagnostic evidence. We should not start ‘cleaning up’ cp-01 because we found its replay semantics differ from cp-04, for example. That difference is valuable. It tells us something about the evolution of the SDK. The examples are effectively **test specimens at different points on the capability ladder**. We shouldn't continually rewrite earlier specimens to look like the latest SDK. When an SDK phase deliberately changes something they consume, we can later run the affected examples and see what happens."* cp-01's F-1 (the replay-carriage difference, `24.6-CLOSE-PREP.md` A.4) is the named instance: it is evidence, not debt. **THE LEDGER CHARTER (the first work after `D-GATE-24.6` merges, never before):** *"build the cp-04 SDK gap ledger exactly as proposed"* with four dispositions — **OPEN** (cp-04 exposed an SDK deficiency that remains), **FIXED-24.6** (cp-04 exposed it and 24.6 changed the SDK to address it), **ESTATE-LIMITATION** (the limitation belongs to Fluree/data/environment rather than CCF), **NOT-A-GAP** (investigation established that the observed behavior was correct SDK behavior or an example/test defect) — one row per entry in the form `Gap ID | cp-04 requirement | observed behavior | why this is an SDK/estate issue | evidence | disposition | phase fixed / target phase`. *"Most importantly, **do not fix anything while constructing the ledger.** No agents rewriting code. No reruns intended to make something green. No cp-04 edits. No republishing. No ‘while I was here’ fixes. We're taking inventory."* The ledger goes to Dave BEFORE the next SDK phase is scoped: *"Some of those gaps may be fundamental architectural deficiencies; some may be convenience features; some may no longer exist after 24.6; and some may not deserve to be solved at all. That is the value the examples were supposed to give us in the first place."* **WHERE THE RULE LIVES:** the full ruling here; the short invariant in CLAUDE.md §9 (*Examples are probes, not repair targets*), per Dave: *"I would put the shorter invariant in `CLAUDE.md` and preserve the full ruling in D-IMPL-261."* **CONSEQUENCES:** (1) `D-GATE-24.5.1`'s sentence *"at which point it is rebuilt and republished"* and `D-IMPL-252` (2)'s *"examples/ open only where an SDK change makes a rung's behavior, prose, transcript or page stale"* are SUPERSEDED for every phase after 24.6: rerun-and-republish is a separate validation step after an SDK phase closes, never inside it. (2) The 24.5.1 discipline *"back-correct examples to the SDK that now exists"* is narrowed to the three allowed reasons above. (3) `D-IMPL-235` (5) (no product rung enters discussion while fix rows are open) now reads against the gap ledger's OPEN rows, and an OPEN row is allowed to stay open by Dave's disposition. (4) The phase-close machinery (§3.1) is unchanged; what changes is that an example red inside an SDK phase is a ledger row, not a close condition. **Next free decision id: `D-IMPL-262`.** **Related:** `D-GATE-24.6`, `D-IMPL-260`, `D-IMPL-259`, `D-IMPL-252`, `D-GATE-24.5.1`, `D-IMPL-235`, `D-IMPL-227`, CLAUDE.md §9.

**D-GATE-24.6 — Phase 24.6 (SDK Gap Phase: the delivery boundary realized) is APPROVED and CLOSED as-is; the final cp-04 publication is the last publication under the pre-`D-IMPL-261` process.** Date: 2026-09-05 (14:15 MST). Approved by: Dave, at the `/gsd-resume-work` sitting, after the gate had been HELD (`D-IMPL-260`, 09:56 MST) for one correction pass and every ruled item was fixed, measured and committed (`24.6-CORRECTION-PASS.md`, twelve items done, two carried by ruling; commits `635e8d3a`, `b08c4b4d`, `f4277b49`, `9d514646`, `b71bbbd8`, `118a1435`, `caa28d28`). **THE RULING, DAVE'S TEXT VERBATIM:** *"Approve 24.6 for close and merge as-is. The final cp-04 publication is accepted as the last publication performed under the pre-D-IMPL-261 process. No further cp-04 correction, republish, transcript regeneration, re-pinning, panel run, or example remediation is required as a condition of closing 24.6."* And: *"Do not make creation of the cp-04 gap ledger another condition for merging 119 commits. That would immediately violate the spirit of the rule we just established: we would once again be holding completed SDK work hostage to additional example bookkeeping."* *"Carry the known findings forward. **D-IMPL-262 — THE cp-04 SDK GAP LEDGER IS APPROVED FOR USE after one factual correction (G-14); its three OPEN rows are RULED — G-26 an SDK gap to fix (an enumerated request-contract domain), G-28 an SDK DEFECT for the next traversal-owning phase, G-33 an SDK gap under a conditional replay invariant; the next SDK work is scoped by SDK OWNERSHIP, not as a cp-04 cleanup, and cp-04 is neither edited nor rerun during it.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-09-05 (14:43 MST). Ruled by: Dave, after reading `.planning/phases/24.6-…/24.6-CP-04-SDK-GAP-LEDGER.md` end to end. His verdict on the artifact: *"This is much closer to the operating model you originally intended: it tells us what cp-04 taught us about the SDK, rather than trying to make cp-04 itself perfect."* *"The ledger is good enough to use for scoping, but I would make one factual correction before treating it as authoritative, and I would not put all three OPEN rows into one phase automatically."* **THE CORRECTION — G-14, HIS WORDS:** *"It currently says the cp-04 requirement was 'depth 6 as a default a caller may exceed.' That is not quite right. We established later that the declared product default was 3; 6 was the measured deepest tree / incorrectly promoted ceiling."* The requirement now reads, in his words: *"`max_depth` default 3 is a product default a caller may override; the measured depth 6 must not become a governance ceiling; the real technical maximum is 100."* *"That matters because this ledger is now supposed to become our reliable historical inventory."* Applied in the ledger row, marked as corrected. **G-26 — enumerated request-contract domains: REAL SDK GAP, FIX.** *"The distinction is sound: `intent ∈ {…}` is part of the valid request vocabulary. It is not a policy constraint. We now support numeric domains through `ArgumentDomain(minimum, maximum)`, but not a closed domain for strings/enums. That is a clean missing request-contract primitive. I would extend the contract domain model rather than use Policy `allowed_set` as a substitute."* Design bound: *"`ArgumentDomain` should be able to say either numeric bounds or an enumerated domain, perhaps ultimately more than that, but I would resist turning it into a generic validation language. The immediate requirement is simple: the contract can declare the legal values of a parameter."* **G-28 — staged versus pushed traversal disagreement: REAL SDK DEFECT, TRAVERSAL-OWNED.** *"This one is more serious technically than G-26 because two implementations of ostensibly the same traversal semantics can return different results on a dangling-edge graph. That is not an example deficiency and not merely a convenience feature. It is a semantic inconsistency in the SDK."* *"But I would not bundle it into a request-contract/replay phase just because cp-04 exposed it. D-IMPL-255 already got this right: open it explicitly in the next traversal-owning ledger. That phase should answer what a dangling endpoint means, then make the reference/in-process and pushed implementations conform to one ruled behavior."* **G-33 — fulfilled replay may omit request resolution: AN SDK GAP WITH A CONDITIONAL INVARIANT.** *"I don't think the right requirement is 'every replay record must always contain `request_resolution`,' because some products or requests may have no effective resolution step to record. But where the product request contract/default/policy/technical-capability machinery did resolve effective parameters, the replay record should not be valid if that resolution disappears."* **THE INVARIANT, HIS WORDS, TO BE CARRIED INTO THE PHASE THAT IMPLEMENTS IT:** *"If effective-request resolution participated in a governed determination, Decision Replay must carry that resolution and its authority provenance. A replay builder may represent genuine non-applicability explicitly, but it must not silently accept omission of resolution that actually occurred."* *"That would convert G-33 from 'question' to OPEN SDK gap."* **THE LESSON IN THE COUNTS, HIS WORDS:** *"cp-04 exposed 36 distinct things, but only 3 remain open; 24.5/24.6 actually fixed a large fraction of the SDK shortcomings the example discovered. That is evidence the examples are working. The waste came from continually rewriting and republishing the specimen after those fixes, not from the discovery process itself."* **THE SCOPING, BY SDK OWNERSHIP:** *"I would avoid a giant 'cp-04 cleanup' phase."* (1) *"Next request/replay hardening phase: G-26 and G-33."* (2) *"Next traversal phase: G-28, explicitly named from day one."* (3) *"No cp-04 edits or reruns during either implementation phase. After the applicable SDK phase lands, cp-04 can be rerun as validation evidence—not repaired while the SDK is being developed."* (4) *"I would also leave the four `ESTATE-LIMITATION` rows alone. They are doing exactly what the ledger should do: telling us that not every limitation discovered by an example warrants SDK engineering."* (5) *"I would not start another example modification cycle from this ledger. The ledger is the output of cp-04. That was the point."* **NOT RULED HERE:** the phase NUMBERS of the request/replay hardening phase and the traversal phase, and where cp-05 (`D-IMPL-252` (5), unnumbered) sits relative to them — Dave named none, and `D-IMPL-227` forbids writing one for him. No ROADMAP phase entry is written until he does. **Next free decision id: `D-IMPL-263`.** **Related:** `D-IMPL-261`, `D-GATE-24.6`, `D-IMPL-259`, `D-IMPL-255` (3), `D-IMPL-252` (5), `D-IMPL-253` Q1, `D-IMPL-227`, `24.6-CP-04-SDK-GAP-LEDGER.md`.

**D-IMPL-263 — THE TWO SDK PHASES THE cp-04 LEDGER OPENS ARE NUMBERED AND ORDERED: Phase 24.7 = Request/Replay Hardening (G-26 + G-33); Phase 24.8 = Traversal Semantics (G-28); cp-05 follows both; cp-04 stays FROZEN through both; the `tests/examples/` quarantine rule is stated; 24.7 is DESIGNED with Dave before any criterion is written.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-09-05 (15:21 MST; the record approved for writing at 15:51 MST). Ruled by: Dave, at the `/gsd-resume-work` sitting that followed `D-IMPL-262`, choosing Option 1 of the three orderings presented — his confirmation of the clause: *"I was presented three alternatives and explicitly chose Option 1. It is useful provenance for why the ordering was selected rather than merely recording the resulting numbers."* **THE RULING, HIS WORDS:** *"24.7 = Request/Replay Hardening — G-26 + G-33. 24.8 = Traversal Semantics — G-28. cp-05 follows both."* **WHY BOTH SDK PHASES BEFORE cp-05, HIS WORDS:** the reason is *"architectural rather than numerical … We should finish the SDK lessons from the rung before asking cp-05 to probe the next one. Otherwise we risk knowingly carrying G-28 into cp-05 and potentially having the next example rediscover or work around it—the exact behavior we just ruled against."* **WHY 24.7 FIRST though G-28 is the more serious defect, HIS WORDS:** *"G-26 and G-33 are tightly bounded extensions of machinery we just built in 24.6: request-contract validity and replay completeness. Closing those now preserves continuity and should make 24.7 relatively surgical. Then 24.8 can own traversal properly."* **THE FREEZE, VERBATIM, ATTACHED TO BOTH ROADMAP ENTRIES:** *"cp-04 remains frozen throughout 24.7 and 24.8. These phases repair SDK surfaces identified by the cp-04 probe; they do not repair, republish, re-pin, or otherwise modify cp-04. After the applicable SDK work lands, cp-04 may be rerun as validation evidence. Any red produced by the frozen example is evidence to classify, not an instruction to edit the example."* **THE FENCE FOR BOTH PHASES, INCLUDING THE QUARANTINE RULE (Dave, 15:51 MST):** `src/` and `runtime/` are open. `examples/` is closed. `tests/examples/` may be touched **only** to quarantine or mark expected-failure an existing example test that turns red because of the SDK work. *"Do not change the assertion, expected value, fixture, test data, or test semantics to accommodate the SDK."* And the constraint Dave made explicit: *"a quarantined/expected-failure test remains evidence and retains its original assertion. The quarantine must identify the SDK gap/decision that caused it and must not turn into a permanent way of making the suite green. When the applicable SDK gap is closed, the quarantine is removed and the original test is rerun unchanged."* His reason: *"otherwise we could recreate the same failure mode under a different name: instead of hacking cp-04, we start ‘maintaining’ its tests until they agree with whatever the SDK currently does."* **24.7 DIRECTION, VERBATIM:** *"Request/Replay Hardening: close the two remaining request/replay SDK gaps exposed by cp-04: contract-level enumerated domains for non-numeric request parameters (G-26), and fail-closed replay completeness when effective-request resolution participated in a governed determination (G-33). No cp-04 changes."* The semantics each gap must satisfy are already ruled in `D-IMPL-262` (G-26: `ArgumentDomain` states numeric bounds OR an enumerated domain, not Policy `allowed_set`, not a validation language; G-33: the conditional replay invariant, quoted there) and are not restated here. **24.8 DIRECTION:** Traversal Semantics — G-28, *"explicitly named from day one"* (`D-IMPL-262`): *"answer what a dangling endpoint means, then make the reference/in-process and pushed implementations conform to one ruled behavior."* **THE PROCESS RULE, HIS WORDS:** *"we should stop and design 24.7 before writing its criteria … I don't want Fable deriving a large implementation plan from a two-line roadmap entry without us first ruling the semantics."* **DIRECTION BANKED IS NOT PHASE DESIGNED — HIS WORDS:** *"D-IMPL-263 establishes why the phases exist, their order, their ownership boundaries, and their freeze. It does not decide the detailed design of G-26 or G-33."* On G-33 specifically: the phrase *"fail-closed replay completeness when effective-request resolution participated in a governed determination"* must not *"silently become an implementation design. We have ruled the invariant, not yet the representation, API shape, validation point, compatibility behavior, or what constitutes ‘participated.’ Those are precisely the things I want us to work through in the 24.7 design sitting."* Consequence: the ROADMAP entries carry DIRECTION ONLY; success criteria are written at the design sitting and locked before Wave 1 (`D-GATE-19`); no research or planning agent runs against 24.7 before that sitting — Dave: *"I want to design 24.7 with you before Fable researches, derives criteria, or plans anything."* **WHAT THIS ENTRY DOES NOT DO:** it writes no criteria, runs no code, edits no example, and does not assign cp-05 a number (cp-05 is the rung after 24.8; `D-IMPL-252` (5) stands). The four `ESTATE-LIMITATION` rows stay as they are (`D-IMPL-262` (4)). **HOUSEKEEPING RULED AT THE SAME SITTING:** the two stale `.continue-here.md` files in the closed 24.4 and 24.5 phase folders were to be deleted *"provided they are genuinely transient checkpoint artifacts and not cited as canonical evidence by a decision, gate, ledger, or close record. If either is cited, leave it."* Both are cited (24.4's by `D-IMPL-232`/`235`/`236` and the ROADMAP; 24.5's as a canonical ref in `24.5-CONTEXT.md` and by `24.5-CLOSE-PREP.md`, `24.5-VERIFICATION.md`, `24.5-DISCUSSION-LOG.md`), so both stay. **Next free decision id: `D-IMPL-264`.** **Related:** `D-IMPL-262`, `D-IMPL-261`, `D-GATE-24.6`, `D-IMPL-259`, `D-IMPL-255` (3), `D-IMPL-252` (5), `D-GATE-19`, `24.6-CP-04-SDK-GAP-LEDGER.md` rows `CP04-G-26`, `CP04-G-28`, `CP04-G-33`.

**D-IMPL-264 — THE 24.7 DESIGN SITTING: thirteen rulings on enumerated request-contract domains (G-26) and fail-closed replay completeness (G-33), and two architectural principles that connect them — declaration is not advertisement; absence is not omission. Criteria are still NOT written.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-09-05 (16:18 MST). Ruled by: Dave, at `/gsd-discuss-phase 24.7` on `main`, the design sitting `D-IMPL-263` required before any criterion (*"stop and design 24.7 before writing its criteria"*). The rulings are VERBATIM in `.planning/phases/24.7-request-replay-hardening-enumerated-request-contract-domains/24.7-RULINGS.md` (governs over this summary); the mapping to D-00..D-13 is `24.7-CONTEXT.md`; every option considered is `24.7-DISCUSSION-LOG.md`. Process: after one AskUserQuestion turn Dave ruled *"to save time ask me all questions at once and do not use a wizard. too slow"*; the remaining thirteen went as one numbered batch and he took every marked recommendation (*"Q1:a … Q13:a"*). **THE TWO PRINCIPLES, HIS TEXT:** (P-1) *"The request contract is the authority for legal values; schemas and discovery advertise that authority but never independently define it."* (P-2) *"`not applicable` is an explicit governed fact with a reason. Missing resolution information is an internal integrity failure."* — *"That second sentence is really the essence of G-33. It prevents us from ever again treating 'the caller didn't provide the replay input' as equivalent to 'resolution did not participate.'"* **G-26 — WHERE THE DOMAIN LIVES.** (D-00, wizard) *"Both, one declaration of record"*: `ArgumentDomain` (`src/ccf/products/request.py`) is the declaration of a closed value set; the argument-schema render derives the MCP `inputSchema` `enum` from it; no second declaration. (D-01) *"`intent` is a top-level request concept, not an ordinary argument. `ProductDiscovery.intents` is the declaration of what the class serves. A duplicate `arguments.properties.intent` is a shadow declaration and should fail contract construction. Leave cp-04 frozen as evidence of the gap."* (D-02) *"Always advertise the legal set. This is contract truth, not Policy. A caller should be able to know the valid vocabulary before making the request. … don't make request validity disclosure-dependent here."* **G-26 — SEMANTICS AND VOCABULARY.** (D-03) *"Exactly one domain shape: numeric bounds or enumerated values. Non-empty, duplicate-free, and any declared default must be inside the domain. Neither shape is also invalid if `ArgumentDomain` is present."* (D-04) *"Exact canonical match. No trimming, case folding, aliases, or silent substitution. Canonicalization, if ever wanted, should be an explicit mechanism upstream of domain validation."* (D-05) *"New `not-in-domain` reason. Wrong type and valid type/wrong value are materially different failures. The presented value can be named; disclosure controls whether the allowed set is exposed."* (D-06) *"Any supported primitive type, with homogeneous members matching the declared property type."* **G-33 — WHAT "PARTICIPATED" MEANS.** (D-07) *"Resolution participated whenever the resolution step actually ran. If it refuses halfway through, that partial work is still governed truth and belongs in replay. 'It failed before producing an effective request' must not erase what resolution already established."* The live SDK case measured at the sitting: the governed resolver (`src/ccf/products/resolver.py:1299-1308`) records a refusal returned BY `resolve_effective_request` with no resolution although defaults and constraints were resolved first. (D-08) *"Return the refusal paired with the partial resolution. Keep refusal vocabulary separate from resolution provenance rather than cloning resolution fields into multiple refusal classes. I would think of this as a common resolution outcome shape: completed request or governed refusal, both with the resolution evidence accumulated so far."* (D-09) *"Legitimate non-applicability. A path that never invokes resolution should say so explicitly. Do not redefine all direct validators as defective merely because the newer resolver exists. The frozen rungs are specimens of that earlier path."* **G-33 — WHERE FAIL-CLOSED BINDS.** (D-10) *"Make the builder require an explicit choice: effective/partial resolution, or a typed not-applicable marker with a reason. No implicit omission for new records. Keep the historical sentinel readable and hash-stable for old records."* (D-11) *"Enforce at construction and verify at replay. Construction prevents new incomplete records. Replay verification protects against a false `not-applicable` claim. The verification must use the pinned historical contract/constraint state, not today's configuration."* (D-12) *"Preserve old records exactly. The new invariant applies prospectively. Do not retroactively declare previously valid replay artifacts defective because the SDK acquired a stronger contract."* (D-13) *"Accept the reds. Under Q10, explicitness is the invariant; inferring non-applicability from missing arguments would reopen the ambiguity we are trying to close. cp-00–cp-03 therefore become quarantined evidence if their existing calls fail under the new builder. Do not edit them."* **WHAT THIS ENTRY DOES NOT DO:** it writes no success criteria (they are authored at the planning sitting after research and locked before Wave 1, `D-GATE-19`), names no field or type (Claude's discretion per `24.7-CONTEXT.md`), and touches no example. **REJECTED AT THE SITTING (recorded so they are not re-derived):** Q9 (b) deprecating direct validators; Q12 (b) retroactive flagging of legacy-sentinel records; Q13 (b) inferring non-applicability from a missing request. **Next free decision id: `D-IMPL-265`.** **Related:** `D-IMPL-263`, `D-IMPL-262`, `D-IMPL-261`, `D-IMPL-259`, `D-IMPL-260` (10), `D-IMPL-254`, `D-IMPL-253` Q1/Q6, `D-IMPL-243`, `D-GATE-24.6`, `D-GATE-19`, ledger rows `CP04-G-26`, `CP04-G-33`.

**D-IMPL-264 — AMENDMENT 1 (after research): the four stop-and-return findings of `24.7-RESEARCH.md` (`b0150cf9`) RULED — F-1 the intent invariant (absence of a discovery declaration is non-applicability; presence makes the set authoritative, an explicit empty set serves none); F-2 four frozen rungs quarantined, not one; F-3 the explicitness invariant crosses the recorder seam; F-5 D-02 refined to representation-without-delivery with a named carry row `24.7-C-01`; the paired-outcome red on cp-04 accepted as evidence.** Date: 2026-09-05 (17:44 MST). Ruled by: Dave, on the research's `## RESEARCH BLOCKED`, each finding verified against the tree by the orchestrator before presentation (F-1: 0 `intents`/`discovery` keys in 8 example configs, `NOT_DISCOVERABLE` at `src/ccf/controlplane/artifacts.py::ProductClassDeclaration.discovery`, `ProductRequest.intent` required; F-2: YAML parse — cp-01, cp-02, cp-03, cp-04 declare `intent` under `arguments.properties`; F-3: both `record()` signatures default `resolution=None`; F-5: `to_input_schema` has one caller, `src/ccf/skills/toolsurface.py`, for skill entries). Verbatim in `24.7-RULINGS.md` §6; mapped in `24.7-CONTEXT.md` `<amendments>`. **F-1 (a), HIS WORDS:** *"The default not-discoverable state means 'no discovery declaration exists,' not 'this class serves zero intents.' An explicitly declared empty set means 'serves none.'"* **THE INVARIANT:** *"Absence of a discovery declaration is non-applicability. Presence of a discovery declaration makes its intent set authoritative, including an explicitly empty set."* *"absence is not the same thing as omission or an empty declaration."* **F-2, HIS WORDS:** *"cp-01 through cp-04 may go red for this reason and those tests are quarantined under D-IMPL-261 with their assertions unchanged. Do not rewrite those contracts during 24.7."* *"their construction failures are specimen evidence, not an instruction to repair the examples."* **F-3 (a), HIS WORDS:** *"If the builder is fail-closed but the recorder still accepts `resolution=None`, then the API permits exactly the omission we are trying to prohibit and merely delays the failure by one call frame."* **THE INVARIANT:** *"Any API that constructs or delegates construction of a replay record must require an explicit resolution state: effective/partial resolution or explicit not-applicable marker. Do not distort the new SDK return type to preserve an old example `isinstance` check. That is exactly what D-IMPL-261 was written to prevent."* **THE GATE HE SET:** *"With those amendments, I would allow the criteria to be authored and brought back for lock. I would not do another design expansion unless criteria research uncovers another genuine architectural ambiguity."* **Next free decision id: `D-IMPL-265`** (unchanged; this is an amendment). **Related:** `D-IMPL-264`, `D-IMPL-263`, `D-IMPL-261`, `D-IMPL-22`, `D-IMPL-23`, `24.7-RESEARCH.md` F-1..F-5.

**D-IMPL-267 — THE 24.8 DESIGN SITTING: eight rulings on what a dangling endpoint means in CCF traversal (G-28) and two principles — persisted graph state and traversal membership are not the same universe; traversal semantics are execution-path invariant. Criteria are still NOT written.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-09-06 (11:29 MST). Ruled by: Dave, at `/gsd-discuss-phase 24.8` on `main` after `D-GATE-24.7`, as the design sitting `D-IMPL-263` required (*"stop and design … before writing its criteria"*). Verbatim in `.planning/phases/24.8-traversal-semantics-one-ruled-meaning-for-a-dangling-endpoin/24.8-RULINGS.md` (governs); mapped D-01..D-08 in `24.8-CONTEXT.md`; alternatives in `24.8-DISCUSSION-LOG.md`. Process: one batch of his own eight questions with options and recommendations (his 24.7 rule); he took every recommendation and sharpened four. **THE MEASURED SHAPE PUT TO HIM:** the query tier (`src/ccf/graph/fallback.py::answer` → `_endpoint_closure` → `_walk`; the five pushed adapters held to it byte-identically) endpoint-closes before walking, so a claim-less endpoint is never a hop; the operator tier (`src/ccf/operators/categories.py::_bounded_walk`, both traversal operators, over the as-of view that keeps dangling edges as state) does not, and with `admitted_entity_classes=None` steps onto the claim-less URI (`:168`), spends depth on it and reaches the claimed nodes beyond it; `docs/GRAPH_QUERY_SEMANTICS.md` 1.2.0 is silent on the operator tier; no test covers the shape (`D-GATE-24.5` R1; ledger row `CP04-G-28`). **THE RULINGS, HIS WORDS:** (Q1 b) a dangling endpoint is *"an unresolved reference: legal persisted graph state, but not a traversal member until an entity claim exists for it."* (Q2 a) *"Traversal membership requires an entity claim … Edges may reference unresolved entities, but traversal operates over claimed entities."* (Q3) *"not admitted; no placeholder … would manufacture context the source never asserted."* (Q4 a, with a carry) *"Exclusion is a traversal semantic, not an invariant failure … Traversal silently excludes the unresolved endpoint from path formation. Whether the existence/count of excluded unresolved references should later become execution/completeness evidence is explicitly deferred"* — carry row `24.8-C-01`, *"not part of G-28 and not a requirement for 24.8."* (Q5 b, defined) *"byte-identical canonical traversal results, not raw implementation/internal bytes … Equivalent traversal questions over equivalent pinned state must yield the same canonical traversal result regardless of execution path."* (Q6 a) *"A claim-less URI is neither a valid walk start nor an intermediate hop."* (Q7 a) *"An excluded endpoint consumes no depth and participates in no path or cycle. Depth counts admitted traversal hops."* (Q8 a) *"Generic traversal-family semantics, not an adapter capability … A capability flag would institutionalize the divergence"*; the rule: *"Construct the admitted entity universe first; endpoint-close edges against that universe; then walk"*; the operator conforms; *"the new differential should compare operator-tier results against the query-tier/reference semantics."* **THE TWO PRINCIPLES, HIS TEXT:** (P-1) *"Persisted graph state and traversal membership are not the same universe. An edge may legally name an unresolved endpoint; that does not make the endpoint traversable."* (P-2) *"Traversal semantics are execution-path invariant. In-process, fallback, and pushed implementations may execute differently, but the same question over the same pinned state must produce the same canonical traversal result."* **FENCE AND FREEZE (restated by him):** *"cp-04 stays frozen. G-28 is fixed in the SDK traversal machinery. cp-04 is not modified, re-pinned, republished, or used as the repair target during 24.8."* `src/`+`runtime/` OPEN, `examples/` CLOSED, `tests/examples/` quarantine-only (`D-IMPL-263`); `archive/` non-gating (`D-IMPL-265`). CLAUDE.md §9 cleanup stays deferred (*"Mixing the cleanup into the traversal phase would blur ownership again"*). **WHAT THIS ENTRY DOES NOT DO:** no criteria (authored and locked at the planning sitting after research, `D-GATE-19`); no mechanism, version number, or test shape (Claude's discretion per `24.8-CONTEXT.md`); no example touched. **REJECTED AT THE SITTING:** Q1 (a)/(c), Q2 (b), a placeholder record (Q3), a refusing invariant (Q4 c), set-equivalence only (Q5 a), a hop-counting phantom (Q7 b), an adapter capability flag (Q8 b). **Next free decision id: `D-IMPL-268`.** **Related:** `D-IMPL-263`, `D-IMPL-262`, `D-IMPL-261`, `D-IMPL-265`, `D-IMPL-255` (3), `D-GATE-24.5` R1, `D-GATE-24.7`, `D-GATE-19`, ledger row `CP04-G-28`, `24.8-C-01`.

**D-IMPL-268 — PHASE 24.8 CRITERIA LOCKED (23, as drafted) and the criterion-4 MECHANISM RULED: (i) close-then-walk inside `_bounded_walk` — shared semantics, not a shared helper; no new public surface to share the predicate; the differential must prove depth and cycle consequences, not only membership.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-09-06 (12:34 MST). Ruled by: Dave, at the planning sitting on `phase-24.8` (`cfa21a55`), after research (`604c6554`), `24.8-VALIDATION.md` (`529ed440`) and the pattern map, and BEFORE any plan and BEFORE Wave 1 (`D-GATE-19`). Verbatim in `.planning/phases/24.8-traversal-semantics-one-ruled-meaning-for-a-dangling-endpoin/24.8-RULINGS.md` §5 (governs); the pinned digest and its controls in `24.8-CRITERIA-LOCK.md`. **Decision 1 — the lock, his words:** *"LOCK the 23 criteria as currently drafted. Pin the digest and record the lock before the planner runs."* Grounds: *"the divergence is now measured across the operator tier, fallback, and all six pushed adapters; the affected cases are bounded; and the pattern-map corrections were made before pinning rather than after."* **Decision 2 — the mechanism, his text for the record:** *"The in-process operator conforms by endpoint-closing its working edge set against the claimed/admitted entity universe before `_bounded_walk` traverses it. The semantic rule is shared across tiers; implementation reuse is not required. No new public helper or SDK surface is introduced solely to share the predicate."* Why (i) over (iii): *"The architectural invariant is shared semantics, not necessarily a shared helper function … Promoting the fallback predicate to a public SDK surface just to make the code literally share one symbol would create unnecessary surface area and coupling between the query and operator tiers"* — reserved for the case *"research shows the two implementations cannot be kept equivalent without duplication drift"*, which the 42/42 measurement of all three candidates (`24.8-RESEARCH.md` § Priority 7) says is not the case. **Carried into planning (a requirement on the planner, not an amendment to the locked text):** *"The new differential must prove depth and cycle consequences, not only final entity membership. A phantom endpoint must not consume depth, create a path, or participate in a cycle even if the eventual returned entity set would coincidentally match."* Follows from `D-IMPL-267` Q7; criteria 6, 12 and 14 already bind the G2-cycle and G3-bypass shapes at both tiers by bytes. **What research established before the lock (`604c6554`):** no stop-and-return findings; 10 of 42 (graph, question) pairs diverge at the operator tier, all `depth ≥ 2` with `admitted=None` on a path through the unresolved endpoint; 252/252 pushed rows byte-identical to the fallback across sqlite, postgres, neo4j, mongo, fluree and memory; no per-node depth emitted by any implementation; `canonical_bytes(GraphView)` the one rendering; no frozen-example test expected to change color; three disclosures inside discretion (F-1 the corpus has no G-28 case, F-2 the existing operator oracle is bare `_walk`, F-3 the shipped walk is not idempotent on a dangling graph). **REJECTED:** (iii) shared private predicate / public promotion (surface and coupling cost with no measured need); (ii) claimed-adjacency guard (moves two sabotage-control pins); amending the locked text for the carried requirement (it is a planning instruction). **Next free decision id: `D-IMPL-269`.** **Related:** `D-IMPL-267`, `D-IMPL-263`, `D-IMPL-262`, `D-IMPL-261`, `D-GATE-19`, `D-IMPL-264` am.2 (the 24.7 lock, the form followed), ledger row `CP04-G-28`, `24.8-C-01`.

**D-IMPL-269 — Phase 24.8 BUILD EVALUATION: APPROVED; the §3.1 cross-AI panel is SKIPPED BY BUILD-EVALUATION RULING as disproportionate to residual risk; the three carries dispositioned; two general lessons preserved as design guidance.** RESOLVED. Dave, 2026-09-06 (20:34 MST), on the build at `d6c4d0ad` (`phase-24.8`, 7/7 plans, tree clean, local equal to remote at evaluation time).

*The evaluation, verbatim:* "I approve the 24.8 build. The result is exactly what this phase was supposed to do: one ruled traversal semantic, one function changed, red-before/green-after proof on the same cases, agreement across all seven backends, and no movement in the surrounding contracts, replay, adapters, examples, or other operator families. I see no reason to reopen the mechanism."

**(1) The panel is SKIPPED BY RULING, and the ruling is a proportionality decision, not a rejection of panels.** Dave, verbatim: *"Do not run the §3.1 panel for 24.8. … The mechanism was ruled before implementation; the source change is exceptionally narrow; the AST comparison shows one changed definition out of 29; the behavioral differential is demonstrated on both sides of the phase boundary; all seven backends agree; and the full surrounding surface is proven unmoved. Meanwhile, the phase itself taught us that essentially every defect discovered during execution was in newly invented proof machinery, not in the mechanism. Running another six-bundle panel now is more likely to generate another proof-of-proof tail than to materially increase confidence in a two-file, one-function semantic correction. That is not a general rejection of panels. It is a proportionality decision: **Review effort should scale with unresolved architectural uncertainty and implementation breadth, not run automatically because a phase reached its end.** For 24.8, both are low."* The staged packet in `24.8-PANEL/` REMAINS in the tree as evidence that the review was available and deliberately not invoked. This is the second consecutive phase whose panel was skipped by ruling (`D-IMPL-266` for 24.7); each skip is a per-phase judgment on that phase's evidence and neither establishes a default.

**(2) `24.8-C-03` (NEW ID, assigned at this ruling) — the `CLAUDE.md` `PHASE_BASE` pin: CARRIED BY ID to the next proof/tooling cleanup sitting, and EXPLICITLY NOT accepted as a permanent standing red.** `tests/invariants/test_determination_authority_disclosure_delivery.py`'s `test_the_document_is_unchanged_since_the_phase_base` on the `CLAUDE.md` parametrization is RED and PRE-EXISTING — proven by RUNNING the test at the phase fork `8567d683`, where it fails identically. It pins `CLAUDE.md` against `1022ad59` while the file last moved at `4683f245`, the 24.6 close: **a constant was pinned and then invalidated by that same phase's later edit.** Dave, verbatim: *"defer to the cleanup sitting. Do not repoint it inside 24.8, because criterion 20 explicitly fenced CLAUDE.md, and the red is proven identical at the phase fork. But I also do not want this accepted as a permanent standing red. It is a defect in proof machinery created by 24.6 … Carry it by ID into the next appropriate proof/tooling cleanup sitting and fix the pin there."* **The general lesson, recorded at Dave's instruction:** *"if the thing being pinned is legitimately mutable project governance, a raw constant may be the wrong proof mechanism."*

**(3) `24.8-C-02` — the stale `protocols.py` module-docstring version claim: CARRIED as a documentation / API-surface item, out of the phase fence.** The `src/ccf/graph/protocols.py` module docstring claims the query contracts render the vocabulary at "semantics version 1.0.0" — a CURRENT-RENDERING claim, three amendments stale. It is not among the nine sites in `24.8-RESEARCH.md` § Priority 6 item 4 (that roster names `protocols.py::TraversalSpec`'s docstring, an ARRIVAL note that stays true), so criterion 17 does not reach it; criterion 19 requires `protocols.py` to carry an EMPTY diff, so fixing it in-phase would have VIOLATED a locked criterion. Plan 05 surfaced it rather than fixing it. Dave, verbatim: *"carry it. Do not violate criterion 19 to fix prose after the fact. This is not a traversal-mechanism defect and it did not affect behavior. Record 24.8-C-02 as a documentation/API-surface carry for the next phase that owns that file or the next cleanup sitting. When fixed, it should describe the actual current semantics/version rather than simply bumping a number mechanically."*

**(4) `24.8-C-01` — unresolved-reference observability: REMAINS DEFERRED EXACTLY AS DESIGNED.** Deferred at the design sitting (`D-IMPL-267`); criterion 9 requires exclusion be SILENT and criterion 20 forbids a partial implementation. Untouched. Dave: *"No change."*

**(5) THE PHASE-LEVEL LESSON, preserved at Dave's instruction because it is valuable beyond G-28.** Across five waves roughly ten defects surfaced and EVERY ONE was in proof machinery; NONE was in the mechanism. Plan 01 found its own plan's `<action>` and `<acceptance_criteria>` contradicting each other and followed the stronger instrument. Plan 02 found criterion 15's `_walk` grep UNSATISFIABLE (it matched a function *name*, so `= 0` could never be reached). Plan 03 reported three research-vs-measured differences and adopted none. Plan 05 caught its own lint sabotage MASKING 91 failures because the inserted line contained the very token being searched for, and caught § Baseline being measured on a different tree. Plan 06 self-reported FOUR defects in its own verification code. Plan 07 self-reported TWO. The orchestrator reddened a CI citation gate TWICE while writing prose about the fix, and briefed one wrong number (a citation delta correct for one tree, passed on without its "which tree" qualifier). Dave, verbatim: ***"When semantics are ruled before coding, mechanism risk collapses; verification machinery becomes the higher-risk surface."*** And the design consequence, verbatim: *"That should influence how we design the next phases. **D-IMPL-277 — OPEN, AWAITING DAVE: the SDK has no acquisition boundary for an EXTERNAL graph store, and two Context Products have now hand-rolled SPARQL around its absence.** OPEN. Raised 2026-09-08 while building cp-05 (`credit-risk.exposure-rollup.v1`). Not resolved here; recorded so a third product does not work around it silently.

**THE MEASUREMENT.** `src/ccf/graph/backends/` ships Fluree, Neo4j, Mongo, Postgres, SQLite and memory adapters, and every one of them is an **L3 substrate** — `FlureeGraphStore`'s own docstring says *"The CCF-owned ledger (D-03). Bootstrapped idempotently at construction."* They are stores the fabric OWNS and WRITES. **There is no SDK surface for reading a graph store the fabric does NOT own, as a SOURCE.** Consequence, measured: `examples/cp-04-corporate-family-tree/deployment.py` carries **16** hand-written SPARQL/SELECT sites against the source Fluree estate, and `examples/cp-05-credit-exposure-rollup/deployment.py` independently carries its own. Both products reached for the same missing thing and both built it themselves.

**WHAT IS *NOT* THE GAP.** Everything downstream of acquisition is supported and cp-04 uses it: normalized edges are admitted through L2's single writer (`worker.admit_relationship_claim`), land in L3, and are traversed by the registered `traversal.typed-neighborhood` operator over a `GraphView`. The fabric is not missing a traversal, a projection or a gate. It is missing the step that gets someone else's graph *in*.

**WHY IT NEEDS A RULING RATHER THAN A PATCH.** Dave, verbatim: *"If the only supported graph abstraction assumes CCF-owned graph state, while real products need to read an external graph as a source, then the SDK is missing an acquisition boundary. That one deserves a ruling before more hand-coded SPARQL proliferates."* The question is architectural: is external-graph acquisition an **L1 Signal Layer** concern (a graph-shaped ingress adapter beside CDC and MCP-ingress, per whitepaper §8.3 Pattern 1/3), an **L4 operator** concern (content acquisition at decision time, `CLAUDE.md` §7.1), or deliberately the deployment's own business? The three answers imply different homes, different Protocols and different replay obligations, and picking one silently would be exactly the kind of unruled surface decision this project stops for.

**RELATED BUT DIFFERENT — NOT this entry.** `resolve_effective_request` was bypassed by cp-05's first draft in favor of a hand-rolled `pick()` helper. Dave classified that separately and correctly: *"The capability exists; the problem is that the happy path is not obvious enough to keep competent authors from bypassing it. I would classify that as an adoption/API ergonomics defect, not a missing semantic capability."* It needs no ruling — it needs the obvious path to be obvious.

**ALSO DEFERRED, DELIBERATELY.** Whether the governed MCP door is disproportionately expensive (cp-04: 801 lines of door against a 458-line assembler) is **not judged yet**. Dave: *"I would defer judgment until cp-05 is using the correct internal path. If the MCP door is still hundreds of lines after the product is properly assembled through CCF, then we have strong evidence the delivery abstraction is too expensive."* cp-05's door is not built and must not be built until the product crosses L2–L5, because a governed door around a hand-rolled query *"would give us a beautifully governed delivery path around a hand-rolled query ... the appearance of a complete Context Product without answering the real question."*

**Next free decision id: `D-IMPL-279`.** **Related:** `D-IMPL-278` (cp-05's findings dispositioned), `D-IMPL-276` (the course correction that put examples back at the center), `D-IMPL-261` (examples are probes, not repair targets), `CLAUDE.md` §7.1 (MCP as bidirectional ingress), whitepaper §8.3 Patterns 1 and 3, `examples/cp-04-corporate-family-tree/produce.py::_ingest` (`D-35`, the class-co-occurrence behavior that forces `relationship_rules: []`).

### D-IMPL-278 — cp-05's findings DISPOSITIONED: one architecture gap, one adoption-surface gap, one delivery-ergonomics gap, two extension points, one deferral — and ONE RETRACTED CORRECTNESS CLAIM

**D-IMPL-278 — cp-05 (`credit-risk.exposure-rollup.v1`) HAS DONE ITS JOB. Its findings collapse into a small number of real SDK issues rather than example-specific annoyances, and Dave dispositions each one. The next SDK work is the SMALLEST changes that make the governed spine the obvious safe path — NOT another generalized hardening phase.** RESOLVED as a disposition; the remedial work is NOT yet scoped, planned or authorized. Date: 2026-09-08. Ruled by: Dave, on the six-step cp-05 rebuild (`1fc91903` … `f0cbccff`) executed under `D-IMPL-276`.

**THE ONE ARCHITECTURAL STATEMENT, in Dave's words:**

> *"CCF has a governed execution spine, but it does not make that spine the canonical path, nor does it verify that the product being delivered is the product that spine actually governed."*

> *"Findings 8, 12, 14, and 17 are manifestations of the same architectural problem. Acquisition, policy, debt/fulfillment, and finally the entire governed resolver were all available, but an author could construct something beside them that looked conforming. The individual components behaved correctly; composition was optional."*

On the delivery boundary, promoting the provisional issue to a genuine gap:

> *"The delivery boundary already proves something useful — this product crossed gates and has a replay record. But … that is a shape proof. It does not prove: the bytes about to leave are the governed determination represented by that replay record. That is the reconciliation CCF is currently missing."*

On `GovernedResolver`:

> *"The GovernedResolver discovery is probably the most consequential finding in the entire example. You effectively rediscovered the intended CCF programming model by hand. That tells us the architecture is substantially there, but the product surface is wrong. … That is beyond documentation friction. I would classify it as an adoption-surface/design gap: the safest governed path is not the path of least resistance."*

On MCP, answering the question the door was built to answer:

> *"The MCP measurement also answers our question: 204 executable lines is still another application, not configuration and binding. The 22% reduction from cp-04 confirms that having the governed product already built helps, but nowhere near enough. The 72 lines of resolver/refusal application logic and the requirement to understand three MCP auth internals are the clearest evidence. The 60 lines of genuine binding are much closer to what should remain."*

**THE DISPOSITION TABLE, verbatim:**

| Finding | Disposition |
|---|---|
| Declared execution vs replay/delivered product not reconciled | **SDK architecture gap** |
| `GovernedResolver` exists but is not the canonical author path | **SDK adoption/API design gap** |
| ~~`GovernedResolver` omits request/bound-payload refusal obligations~~ **→ RECLASSIFIED: `refuse_bound_payload` is not part of the shipped governed path** | **Delivery/adoption gap with LATENT CORRECTNESS RISK — not an observed correctness defect in the current product path.** The request-boundary half was measured false and is retracted; see below |
| MCP requires resolver/refusal application code + auth internals | **SDK delivery ergonomics/API gap** |
| Product-specific debt scorer | **Expected extension point** |
| Product-specific reconciliation guard lacks a home | **Candidate SDK extension-point gap** |
| Acquisition before `GovernedResolver` | **Hold for `D-IMPL-277` architectural ruling** |

**THE ARCHITECTURAL TARGET, verbatim:**

> *"A Context Product author supplies acquisition, product-specific assembly/projection logic, product-specific scoring where needed, and declarations. CCF owns the governed spine. MCP should bind that already-governed product to transport—not require the author to reconstruct governance again."*

> *"CCF should refuse to emit a product when the replayed governed determination and the product presented for delivery cannot be shown to correspond."*

And the fence on how it is done:

> *"I would not launch another generalized hardening phase around this. cp-05 has given us concrete product evidence. The next SDK work should be the smallest changes that make the governed spine the obvious safe path and close the actual request-boundary defect."*
