**D-IMPL-311 — s1-00's canonical adoption. `ProductRequestViolation` is an INTERNAL producer/contract representation; `RefusalEnvelope` is the canonical CONSUMER-FACING governed refusal. And s1-00 changed architectural category: it no longer authors an operator set, the SDK supplies it, so it leaves the one-document exemption for the SDK-supplied roster.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-09-09. Ruled by: Dave, at the `/gsd-resume-work` sitting, on `MOD-07` and `MOD-08`.

**`MOD-07` — THE REFUSAL CARRIER.** Dave: *"`ProductRequestViolation` is an internal producer/contract representation. `RefusalEnvelope` is the canonical consumer-facing governed refusal."* Before canonical adoption s1-00 performed the door's comparison itself and had nothing else to hand back; it now returns what the SDK returns. **Explicitly forbidden and not done:** *"do not make `GovernedResolver` return `ProductRequestViolation` just to preserve the old `isinstance`"*, and *"no exception-based refusal handling."* No SDK code changed.

The two carriers hold the same three facts the test asserts, and the envelope holds one more:

| | fields |
| --- | --- |
| `ProductRequestViolation` | `reason` `key` `detail` + `declared_keys` `declared_type` `presented_keys` `presented_type` `overrides` |
| `RefusalEnvelope` | `reason` `key` `detail` + `kind` **`replay_reference`** `policy_bindings` `disclosure` `request` `pre_assembly_lineage` `evidence` `provenance` `resource` `fields` |

Three sites changed and one gained an assertion: `produce.py`'s declared return type and its docstring's argument; `consume.py`'s branch, which now also prints the record's address; and `test_a_missing_threshold_is_refused_not_defaulted`, which keeps `reason`, `key` and *no product released* verbatim and **adds** `replay_reference != NO_REPLAY_REFERENCE`. The docstring's original argument survives intact — *"a verdict returned as a value cannot be swallowed by a bare `except`"* — because an envelope is still a value.

**The `ccf.client` surface was considered and is not the target.** `Result`/`Refusal` is the **transport** client's API, reached through `ProductClient`; s1-00's `consume.py` calls `produce.assemble_and_serve` in-process. Routing it through `ProductClient` would change what the example teaches, so the envelope is the right carrier here.

**Two sabotages, both RED:** serve a product for the missing-required-parameter question (the door's refusal neutralized in `ccf.products.constraints`) → RED; drop the refusal's replay reference (`resolver.py:1028`) → RED.

**`MOD-08` — THE ARCHITECTURAL CATEGORY.** Dave: *"The reason is architectural, not administrative: s1-00 no longer authors an operator set; the SDK supplies it."* Removed from `RULED_ONE_DOCUMENT_DEPLOYMENTS` and added to `RULED_SDK_SUPPLIED_DEPLOYMENTS` **in one commit**, with the removal site carrying a dated comment naming the migration — the `cp-05`/`D-IMPL-301` shape, *"a classification update, not an exemption swap."* **No new exemption class and no raised ceiling.**

**THE ROSTER EDIT ALONE WAS NOT ENOUGH, AND THAT IS THE INTERESTING PART.** `sdk_supplied` is **measured from the tree**, not read from the roster, and the predicate did not see s1-00. The cause: `_sdk_supplied_operator_set` requires `isinstance(scope, ast.FunctionDef | ast.AsyncFunctionDef)`, and the migrated `plan_factory` was written as a **lambda**, which no static check can read. The fix was **not** to widen the predicate — `cp-05`, the ladder's reference authoring example, uses a named `def plan_factory`, and a named factory whose only operator source is the `required` parameter makes `D-IMPL-137`'s demand *provable* rather than merely true. s1-00 now matches the reference shape. The roster was not edited to paper over an instrument that could not see a tree that plainly delegates.

**TWO CONTROLS WERE RE-POINTED, ON MY OWN JUDGMENT, AND THIS ENTRY FLAGS IT.** `test_hw1_claims_the_exemption_for_the_stated_reason` and `test_a_second_operator_set_outside_the_control_plane_is_refused` used **s1-00 as their row-B specimen** — the first asserting that its body reads one document, the second mutating its plan construction to prove row C is refused. The ruling made the first false and deleted the second's mutation target. Both now point at `examples/cp-00-institutional-holders`, which is row B on the same reading and constructs its plan from the **identical expression**, so the mutation string is unchanged and each control keeps exactly the property it had. The first was also renamed: it had said `hw1` while pointing at s1-00 for some time. **This was not in the brief; if the row-B specimen should be a different deployment, the choice is one line in each.**

**EIGHT QUARANTINED TESTS WERE UN-QUARANTINED AND PASS UNCHANGED.** All eight carried one reason — *"frozen s1-00 produce.py calls `build_replay_record` with no resolution state — quarantined evidence … un-quarantine and rerun unchanged after `D-GATE-24.7`"*. That gate has passed and the migration deletes the call that caused the quarantine, so all eight `XPASS(strict)`-ed. The markers were removed and **no test body was touched**: the ruled un-quarantine, not a re-pin.

**D-IMPL-316 — `CP04C-F-01` REPAIRED as a bounded SDK fix. A POSITION IS NOT AN IDENTITY: an entity rule may declare which payload field supplies a declared identity key, and the DECLARED key is still what is hashed. The global content-hash and identity model is untouched.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-09-10. Ruled by: Dave, on the successor sitting's first unclassified miss.

**THE RULING, AND ITS BOUNDARY.** Dave: *"Fix `CP04C-F-01` now as a bounded SDK repair. Position/source field names are not entity identity. Endpoint selection should bind a payload field to the entity class's declared identity key, and the canonical identity key/value pair is what gets hashed. Do not change global hashing semantics."* Four constraints held exactly: the global entity hash model is unchanged; canonical identity key names remain in the hash; only endpoint resolution's *source* of a value moved; and `admit_relationship_claim` was **not** used as a fallback. The stop condition Dave attached — *"Only stop if it turns out the repair requires changing the global content-hash/identity model across all entities"* — was not reached: nothing outside `SpecDrivenEntityResolution.resolve` and the rule contract changed.

**THE DEFECT.** A URI is `entity_class://content_hash(identity)` where `identity` was `{payload_key: value}`, so the payload key's NAME was inside the identity. Endpoint selection (`24.5-L-21`) requires the two endpoints to come from two entity rules reading two different payload fields, so **the same company hashed differently in each position**: measured live, three real nodes became five entities, and two companies in a mutual pair became four. The condition is not exotic — the cp-04 family fixture carries **22 mutual pairs**, so the ordinary case was the broken one, and it failed silently because both URIs were well-formed.

**THE REPAIR.** `EntityResolutionRule.identity_sources` — declared identity key → the payload field that supplies its value. Defaulted empty, **hash-transparent** (`D-IMPL-243`), so every rule written before it keeps its canonical form and its URIs; verified by canonical bytes, and by the marked-field roster in `tests/contracts/test_hash_transparency.py` being updated deliberately rather than drifting. A remap naming a key the rule does not identify by is **refused at construction**, because ignoring it would silently fall back to the same-named payload field, mint a different URI, and report nothing.

**PROVED, AND THE CONTROLS ARE THE POINT.** Dave's five cases, each a committed test in `tests/assembly/test_worker.py` except case 5: (1) one LEI in both endpoint positions is ONE entity; (2) an A→B same-class edge still mints, so the repair did not cost the feature it repairs; (3) a mutual pair is 2 entities and 2 edges; (4) **the negative control** — reintroducing payload-key-name identity reproduces the duplicate-entity defect at 4; (5) cp-00's different-class co-occurrence is **byte-for-byte unchanged**, measured by running identical inputs against a detached worktree at the pre-fix commit `fbfcce2d` and diffing the resolved URIs, attributes and classes.

**TWO THINGS THE PROOF MACHINERY GOT WRONG FIRST, RECORDED BECAUSE THEY ARE THE RECURRING CLASS.** The negative control initially ingested ONE envelope carrying two distinct values and asserted four entities; it fails at two, because one envelope with two different companies duplicates nothing. The defect needs the SAME company in both positions, which is TWO envelopes — the shape a mutual pair actually arrives in. The control caught its own error. Then the repair was **sabotaged in `src/`** and the three positive tests observed RED while the negative control and the validator test stayed green, which is what distinguishes tests that depend on the repair from tests that merely coexist with it.

**WHAT THIS SAYS ABOUT `24.4-D-35`.** It is genuinely closed — `24.5-L-21`'s endpoint selection does mint typed same-class edges, measured live. What was underneath it is this entry. The successor found it only because it was authored forward against the current surface; copying cp-04's `admit_relationship_claim` shape would have sidestepped the defect and left it live for the next adopter.

**Next free decision id: `D-IMPL-317`.** **Governs:** the identity/position separation, the `identity_sources` construct and its refusal, the hash-transparency obligation, and the five proof cases. **Related:** `D-IMPL-315` (the adjudication obligation this finding was decided under), `D-IMPL-314`/`D-IMPL-313` (the successor's charter and its stop-on-first-miss rule), `D-IMPL-243` (hash transparency), `24.5-L-21` and `24.4-D-35` (endpoint selection and the gap it closed), `D-IMPL-293` (pre-v0, correctness beats compatibility).

**D-IMPL-317 — The remaining example test modules move to the read-only live estate on their OWN branch, AFTER cp-04-canonical closes. Not now, and not inside the successor's branch.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-09-10. Ruled by: Dave, on the tension surfaced when the read-only posture was written into CLAUDE.md §9.

**THE COMMITMENT.** Dave: *"We will need to update them once we are done with cp-04 we can open a new branch and address them."* The `.76` read-only, seed-nothing posture (CLAUDE.md §9) is the standing rule for every example's tests. `tests/examples/test_cp_04_canonical_output.py` already meets it. The rest — the cp-00 through cp-05 modules and their `cp_0N_seed.py` helpers — do not, and converting them is **a separate branch off `main` after `cp-04-canonical` closes**, never work folded into the successor.

**WHY THE SEPARATION IS THE RULING RATHER THAN THE SCHEDULING.** The successor's branch exists to prove one thing: that a canonical rung-4 example can be authored against the current surface. Converting six other modules' estate posture in the same branch would put two unrelated claims behind one review and one gate, and a reviewer could no longer tell which change produced which result. It is the same discipline that kept cp-04 frozen while its successor was built.

**THE TENSION THE NEXT BRANCH HAS TO RESOLVE, NAMED NOW SO IT IS NOT REDISCOVERED.** `D-IMPL-261` freezes cp-00 through cp-04 as specimens and forbids changing an example's *test* to make it pass around an SDK deficiency. Converting a frozen specimen's test from a seeded fixture to the live estate is **not** that — it changes where the data comes from, not what is asserted — but it is still an edit to a frozen specimen's test surface, and it needs an explicit ruling rather than an inference from this entry. Two things that branch must establish per module before converting it: that no assertion pins an estate count (a pinned count has made the estate a fixture again, and is rewritten rather than re-pinned), and that nothing in it requires estate **perturbation**, which is the one case that still needs a private seeded namespace.

**THE MEASURED REASON THE WORK IS WORTH DOING.** 27 `cp04-examples-*` ledgers sit on `.76` as branches of the `ccf` ledger, left by prior seeded runs. They do **not** contaminate `fibo-v2` — measured 2026-09-10, `fibo-v2` reads exactly one clean copy of its data, 636 `owns` edges rather than 27× that — but Fluree is append-only and none of them can ever be removed. Every seeded run adds one more. And the fixtures they seed go stale silently: the committed cp-04 fixture carried 142 attribute rows while the live estate held 156.

**Next free decision id: `D-IMPL-318`.** **Governs:** when and where the remaining example test modules convert; the separation from the successor's branch; the `D-IMPL-261` question that conversion raises. **Related:** `D-IMPL-261` (examples are probes, and the specimen freeze), CLAUDE.md §9 (the estate rule and the read-only test posture), `D-IMPL-315` (the successor sitting's constraints), `D-IMPL-313` (the specimen/successor separation this mirrors).

**D-IMPL-318 — Converting frozen cp-04's TEST SURFACE to read-only `.76` validation is AUTHORIZED, behind a hard fence: only `tests/examples/test_cp_04_*.py` and `tests/examples/cp_04_seed.py` may change. The specimen tree itself is untouched, and a count assertion is REPLACED BY A BEHAVIORAL INVARIANT rather than re-pinned to estate numbers.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-09-10. Ruled by: Dave, opening the estate-conversion sitting.

**WHY THIS NEEDED A RULING AT ALL.** `D-IMPL-261` freezes cp-00 through cp-04 as specimens and forbids changing an example's *test* to make it pass around an SDK deficiency. Converting a test from a seeded fixture to the live estate changes **where the data comes from, not what is asserted**, so it is not the thing the freeze forbids — but it is still an edit to a frozen specimen's test surface, and inferring permission from that distinction is exactly the kind of reasoning that erodes a freeze. Dave ruled it explicitly instead.

**THE HARD FENCE, AND IT IS THE LOAD-BEARING HALF.** Dave: *"Only `tests/examples/test_cp_04_*.py` and `cp_04_seed.py` may change for cp-04 estate conversion. That makes the ruling much safer. It guarantees we are changing how the frozen specimen is tested, not changing the specimen itself."* **Nothing under `examples/cp-04-corporate-family-tree/` may be touched — not a line, not a comment, not a whitespace.** The first commit of this conversion carries the zero-diff proof for that directory beside this entry, so the fence is evidenced at the moment it is granted rather than asserted at the end.

**COUNT ASSERTIONS ARE REPLACED, NEVER RE-PINNED.** Dave: *"do not re-pin cp-04 to `.76` counts."* A test asserting *"there must be N entities"* does not become *"there must be M entities"* against the estate — that would make the estate a fixture again, and would go red on the next legitimate data change for no reason anyone could act on. It becomes a **behavioral invariant** that holds at any roster size. The named examples: depth changes the result and `D_c`; a technical bound of 99 refuses; replay retains the store pin; traversal relationships are coherent.

**A TEST THAT CANNOT WORK WITHOUT WRITING IS LEFT AS IT IS AND REPORTED.** Dave: *"if a cp-04 test truly cannot work without writing, leave it as-is and report it rather than inventing another private namespace. The whole point is to stop creating more irreversible Fluree debris."* Perturbation tests — those that must mutate data to prove a guard fires — are the expected members of that set. **Inventing a fresh private namespace to keep such a test converted is refused by name**: it would trade one irreversible ledger for another while appearing to solve the problem.

**THE MEASUREMENT THAT SIZED THE SITTING**, taken 2026-09-10 before any edit: **all 27** `ccf:cp04-*` debris ledgers on `.76` came from these modules, and **no other example creates a Fluree ledger at all** — so this fence covers the entire irreversible-write surface in `tests/examples/`. Alongside them sit 22 `cp04_*` and 9 `s1_00_*` PostgreSQL schemas, which unlike ledgers **can** be dropped.

**s1-00 IS NOT CONVERTED, and its own fixture says why.** `examples/s1-00-companies-over-revenue/scenario/companies.sql` opens *"THIS IS NOT CCF. These rows fabricate the demonstration; you delete them."* Ten companies with a deliberately built `last_updated` spread are what make its `D_c` a measured number against the declared half-life; pointing it at the curated estate would destroy the demonstration. Dave: **keep the synthetic dataset, redirect it to local Postgres / a test container, never `.76`.** Its defect is *where* it seeds, not *that* it seeds.

**THE SCHEMA CLEANUP IS A MANUAL OPS ACTION, NOT PYTEST TEARDOWN.** Dave: snapshot the exact schema names first, then drop **only** `cp04_*` and `s1_00_*`; **never** `public`, `ccf_v2`, or any `fibo*` namespace. Teardown logic that dropped schemas would put an unattended `DROP` on a path that runs on every developer's machine against whatever DSN happens to be exported.

**THE EXECUTION ORDER, as ruled.** (1) This entry, with the zero-diff proof, as the first commit. (2) Convert the eight cp-04 test modules to read `.76` read-only. (3) Redirect s1-00's synthetic seeding to local Postgres. (4) The schema cleanup afterward, separately and by hand.

**Next free decision id: `D-IMPL-320`.** **Governs:** the fence around cp-04's test conversion; the replacement of count assertions with invariants; the disposition of tests that cannot convert; s1-00's posture; and the manual, scoped shape of the schema cleanup. **Related:** `D-IMPL-261` (the specimen freeze this operates inside), `D-IMPL-317` (which scheduled this sitting and reserved this id), `D-IMPL-319` (the successor's close, whose read-only posture this generalizes), CLAUDE.md §9 (the estate rule and the read-only test posture).

**D-IMPL-320 — The `.76` schema cleanup is DONE, fail-closed, entirely outside pytest. And `D-IMPL-318` is DISCHARGED FOR THE TEST-SURFACE / DATA-SOURCE CHANGE ONLY — it is not standing permission to edit the frozen cp-04 specimen.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-09-10. Ruled by: Dave, closing the estate-conversion sitting.

**THE SCOPING, AND IT IS THE HALF THAT OUTLIVES THE SITTING.** Dave: *"`D-IMPL-318` should be considered discharged only for the test-surface/data-source change; it does not become a standing permission to edit the frozen cp-04 specimen later."* The authorization was spent on moving where cp-04's tests read their data. **Anything else under `examples/cp-04-corporate-family-tree/` — or any further edit to its test surface for any other purpose — needs its own ruling.** `D-IMPL-261` is undisturbed. As it happens this branch changed **no example tree at all**: `git diff --stat main -- examples/` is empty, which is stronger than the fence required.

**THE CLEANUP, AS RULED, AND IT WAS FAIL-CLOSED RATHER THAN EYEBALLED.** Dave's strengthening: *"Abort cleanup if the snapshot contains anything outside `cp04_%` or `s1_00_%` — especially `public`, `ccf_v2`, `ccf`, or anything `fibo%`. That makes the cleanup fail-closed instead of relying on someone visually spotting a bad name."* Executed in that order: the matching names were queried and written to a snapshot **file**; the exact list was printed **before any `DROP`**; every line was validated against `^(cp04_|s1_00_)` and against a forbidden set, **twice** — once at selection and again per line, read back from the file rather than from the query that produced it; then one explicit `DROP SCHEMA … CASCADE` per reviewed name.

**MEASURED BEFORE AND AFTER.** 31 schemas dropped — 22 `cp04_examples_*`, 9 `s1_00_*`. After: no `cp04_%`, no `s1_00_%`; `ccf_v2`, `public`, `information_schema` and `pg_catalog` all present; `ccf_v2.legal_entity` still reads **156** rows; Fluree still **30** ledger entries under names `ccf`, `fibo`, `fibo-v2`, and `fibo-v2` still answers **636** `owns` edges. **Nothing curated moved.**

**COMPLETELY OUTSIDE PYTEST**, as ruled. Teardown logic that dropped schemas would put an unattended `DROP` on a path that runs on every developer's machine against whatever DSN happens to be exported. The cleanup is an ops action a human authorized once, with its snapshot preserved.

**WHAT THE SITTING LEAVES BEHIND.** The 27 `ccf:cp04-*` Fluree ledgers **remain and always will** — the store is append-only and nothing can remove them. What changed is that nothing can add to them: `tests/examples/estate_guard.py::refuse_to_write_the_curated_estate` refuses a seed against a curated host on either leg, and the four cp-04 modules that read rather than write now read the curated estate directly. The division is settled: **the curated estate is read-only; whatever must write, writes to a local disposable store.**

**TWO DEFECTS THIS SITTING PRODUCED IN ITS OWN GUARD, both in the message rather than the mechanism, both found by reading the guard's own output rather than by review.** The first refusal printed the estate's PostgreSQL password once per erroring test into output CI keeps; DSNs are now redacted to `user:***@host`. The second asserted *"Fluree is append-only, so every seeded ledger there is permanent"* on a PostgreSQL-only refusal where no Fluree was involved; the message now distinguishes a permanent ledger from a removable-but-accumulating schema. A guard that refuses correctly while teaching a wrong fact is still teaching a wrong fact.

**D-IMPL-321 — For cp-06, lien priority is an AUTHORITATIVE INPUT on the reified pledge. The product does NOT determine legal UCC priority from filing records. Coverage under `allocation=priority` is coverage under those assertions.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-09-10. Ruled by: Dave, on `CP-SPEC-006` §F.2 row 6 before the gate.

**THE RULING, VERBATIM.** Dave: *"For cp-06, lien priority is an **authoritative input** on the reified pledge. The product **does not** determine legal UCC priority from filing records. Coverage under `allocation=priority` is coverage under **those assertions**."*

**WHY DERIVING IT WAS REFUSED, and the reasoning is about evidence rather than effort.** `CP-SPEC-006` §C.4 trap 1 surfaced that priority is *asserted* by the reified `ex:CollateralPledge` and not *derived* from a filing date, while UCC Article 9 makes the filing date what establishes priority between competing secured parties. The obvious next move is to join them. Dave refused it on two measured grounds: **the register holds Florida only — 8 of 50 anchors** — and **the register does not carry the facility link**, because it names a debtor rather than a facility. Dave: *"A Π that 'computes UCC priority from filing date' would be a legal claim the estate cannot support."* A coverage figure presented as legally-ordered priority, computed from a 16%-of-cast register that cannot say which facility a lien secures, would be exactly the confident-and-wrong answer this ladder exists to refute.

**THE EXAMPLE'S JOB IS ALREADY DONE.** Dave: *"same graph, different questions, coverage moves."* The product demonstrates that coverage is a graph question rather than a column, and that six caller parameters change the conclusion rather than the decimals. It does not need to adjudicate lien law to make that point, and adding an adjudication it cannot evidence would weaken the claim it can.

**WHERE THE SENTENCE GOES, so a reader cannot miss it:** `CP-SPEC-006` §F.2 row 6, the example README, and **the served payload's own basis block** — the product states its own footing rather than leaving it in documentation a consumer may not read.

**THE BOUNDED SCOPE OF THE CHANGE, as ruled.** *"Do not add operators, filing joins, or new tests beyond a docstring/spec assertion that the field is `asserted`, not `derived`."* No new operator is registered, no filing is joined to a facility, and the existing eighteen tests stand. The disclosure is a field and three sentences.

**WHAT IS NOT BEING HELD FOR THIS.** Dave: *"Do not hold the gate for Florida-complete UCC derivation. That is a different product when the register can name the facility."* Deriving priority from filed records is a future product with its own decision frame, not a completion criterion for this one.

**AND cp-07 RETURNS TO GATE 1 FIRST.** The spec-after-build inversion recorded at `CP-SPEC-006` §0.1 is **disclosed, not a template**. The next rung is specified, ruled, and only then built.

**Next free decision id: `D-IMPL-322`.** **Governs:** cp-06's treatment of lien priority, the refusal to derive it, where the disclosure appears, the bounded scope of the change, and cp-07's return to Gate 1. **Related:** `CP-SPEC-006` §C.4/§F.2/§G.3, `D-IMPL-315` (adjudicate rather than edit), `D-IMPL-316` (a position is not an identity — the pledge reification this rests on), CLAUDE.md §9.

**D-IMPL-322 — `CP06-F-01` corrected: a BARE ledger name resolves its store watermark. The fix is the branch default and nothing else.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-09-10. Ruled by: Dave, immediately after `D-GATE-cp-06`.

**THE DEFECT.** `examples/cp-04-canonical-corporate-family-tree` read the ledger's transaction index by matching the server's listing on **name and branch**, which Fluree keys separately, via `self._ledger.partition(":")`. A ledger named `ccf:cp04-<uuid>` partitions correctly. A ledger named **`fibo-v2`** — the curated estate, and the value that example's own README tells a reader to export — partitions to `name="fibo-v2"`, `branch=""`, matches no listing entry, and returns the honest fallback `"unreported"`.

**WHY IT SHIPPED.** The example's tests and its development runs used *seeded* ledgers, whose names carry an explicit `name:branch`. The bug appears only against a bare name, which is exactly the curated estate and exactly what merged. The fallback is well-behaved and reports rather than raising, so nothing failed — a provenance field was simply empty where it should have carried `5545`.

**SEVERITY: MISSING, NOT WRONG.** The watermark is execution provenance recorded in replay (`D-IMPL-309`) and does not enter the product's content address. No determination was wrong and no address moved. What was lost is the ability to say which store state a decision read, for every run against the estate the example documents.

**FOUND BY BUILDING SOMETHING ELSE.** It surfaced while writing cp-06's graph leg, which inherited the same code shape. Recorded as `CP06-F-01` in cp-06's `FINDINGS.md`, fixed in cp-06, and **deliberately not fixed on cp-06's branch** — mixing an unrelated repair into a rung's branch puts two claims behind one review, which is the separation `D-IMPL-317` was written to preserve.

**THE SCOPE, AS RULED.** Dave: *"Touch only the watermark behavior for the bare ledger-name case. No cp-06 files, no docs expansion, no new feature work."* Two files: the two-line branch default, and three regressions. `git diff --name-only` against `ecc9ecff` returns exactly those two.

**THE THREE PROOFS, as specified.** (1) A bare ledger name resolves a **real** index — asserted as *a number was resolved*, never as a pinned value, because `t` advances. (2) An unknown ledger — in both the `name:branch` and bare shapes — still reports `unreported`. (3) The watermark is **never invented**: the returned value is compared against the server's own listing rather than against a constant, because a test carrying its own expected `t` would restate the estate and go red on the next write.

**SABOTAGE-VERIFIED.** Reverting the two-line fix reds exactly proofs (1) and (3) and leaves the negative control green — which is what distinguishes a regression that depends on the repair from one that merely coexists with it.

**Next free decision id: `D-IMPL-323`.** **Governs:** the watermark's branch default and the scope of the correction. **Related:** `CP06-F-01` (`examples/cp-06-collateral-and-setoff-coverage/FINDINGS.md`), `D-IMPL-309` (the store pin is execution provenance recorded in replay), `D-IMPL-317` (one claim per branch), `D-GATE-cp-06`.

**D-IMPL-323 — An ILLUSTRATIVE calibration is allowed where a frozen estate would otherwise make a control unobservable. It is allowed only to make the mechanism visible, never to tune a demonstration until it looks good, and it must be disclosed at every site that carries it.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-09-10. Ruled by: Dave, during cp-07's build, on a measurement that forced the question.

**THE MEASUREMENT THAT FORCED IT.** `CP-SPEC-007` §E declared `λ_c` for interaction records at **~7 days**, written at Gate 1 before the product existed. Built and measured against the curated estate, every anchor read `D_c ≈ 0.96`, signal `fail_closed` — a product that permanently refuses demonstrates nothing. The cause is not the SDK: the estate's newest interaction anywhere is **2026-08-18** and the spread of last-contact dates across every client is **27 days**, so at a 7-day half-life the entire population sits three to seven half-lives out and the term carries no information about any particular client.

**THE SHARPER DEFECT UNDERNEATH, found by sabotaging back to 7 days after the change.** That calibration did not merely score every anchor badly — **it inverted their order**: the anchor nobody had contacted since 2026-07-22 scored `F = 0.0633` against a current anchor's `0.0409`. At that decay every party's contribution is within rounding of zero, so the mean reported party-count structure rather than recency. **A term that ranks the staler relationship as fresher has stopped measuring its own subject**, which is why this could not be disposed of as *"the estate is stale and `fail_closed` is the correct answer."*

**THE RULING, verbatim.** Dave: *"For these examples, the estate is a historical snapshot, not a continuously refreshed production environment. We should not let stale fixture dates make otherwise useful Context Products permanently `fail_closed`."* And: *"Choose illustrative parameter values that make the scenario work against the available snapshot, and disclose where those values are demonstration-specific rather than production recommendations."* And, on scope: *"That principle should apply to the other examples too whenever static estate data forces an illustrative threshold."*

**THE FOUR CONDITIONS, conjunctive.** (1) **Choose a value that makes the mechanism observable** — a control that never fires and a signal that reads the same for every subject demonstrate nothing. (2) **Keep the calculation real** — no faked timestamp, and `asked_at` is never moved to reach an answer; only the *declared* threshold is a demonstration value, while the observations, the decay curve and the decision instant stay the SDK's and the estate's. (3) **Prove the term moves**, with a directional test asserting the **ordering** and the **signal** and never the number — pinning the number turns a documented demonstration value back into a fixture. (4) **Disclose it where a reader will hit it** — the artifact that declares it, the README, and the spec — in the standing wording recorded in CLAUDE.md §9.

**WHAT IT DOES NOT LICENSE.** It is not permission to tune a number until an example looks good. Dave: *"The purpose of the examples is to demonstrate how CCF behaves when parameters change, not to establish Wells Fargo's production policy values."* Production calibration is domain and policy work and is out of scope for the SDK (CLAUDE.md §13, *"Not the SDK's problem at all"*). A calibration changed silently is the thing this entry exists to prevent: the value is labeled at every site, and the measurement that forced the change is recorded as a finding.

**APPLIED, in cp-07.** `interaction_record` and `relationship_strength` move from ~7 days to **90 days**, labeled in `ccf_config.yaml`, `README.md`, `spec/CP-SPEC-007_Client_360_Coverage_Graph.md` §E and `FINDINGS.md` (`CP07-F-01`). What the calibration buys is a `D_c` that moves and a threshold that is actually crossed: Caesars Entertainment (last contact 2026-07-22) reads `F 0.3437 / D_c 0.6563 / forced_llm`, against Suburban Propane's `F 0.5279 / D_c 0.4721 / ok` and Container Store's `F 0.4774 / D_c 0.5226 / ok`. **A threshold nothing ever crosses is a threshold nobody has tested.**

**COMPLETENESS IS RULED SEPARATELY AND NOT CHANGED.** Dave: *"Keep completeness as an admission/checkability property rather than manufacturing a ratio."* `C = 1` on every anchor is not a broken metric — it reads *every party this graph walked was admitted and named, and the fabric is structurally unable to serve one that was not*, because `deployment.ingest` fails closed on exactly the condition the metric would score. Inventing a denominator so the number moves would manufacture a ratio to make a term look alive. The reading that WOULD move if a future estate carries the gap is recorded in `CP07-F-02` as the path not taken.

**TRUNCATION IS UNCHANGED BY THIS ENTRY** and stays out of `D_c`: a bounded read is a deliberate act with a known edge, disclosed as its own product fact rather than scored.

**Next free decision id: `D-IMPL-324`.** **Governs:** when an example may choose an illustrative threshold, the four conditions on doing so, and the disclosure wording; cp-07's λ_c values; the completeness reading. **Related:** CLAUDE.md §9 (where the principle is written for every example), `CP07-F-01` and `CP07-F-02`, `CP-SPEC-007` §E (superseded in place), `D-IMPL-261` (examples are probes — this is a calibration ruling and not an example repaired around an SDK deficiency).

**D-GATE-cp-07 — `examples/cp-07-client-360-coverage-graph` is APPROVED. Rung 7 of the ladder ships.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-09-10. Ruled by: Dave.

**THE GATE, as given:** *"Gate cp-07, merge `--no-ff`, push, and close the rung."* No further work was required of the build.

**WHAT DAVE SETTLED FOR THIS MERGE, in his own enumeration:** 90-day `λ_c` is explicitly illustrative; the tests prove the freshness term moves in the right direction and do not pin `D_c`; `C = 1` is an admission/checkability invariant rather than a fake completeness ratio; truncation is disclosed separately and stays out of Debt; the 7-day sabotage proved the old setting had stopped measuring recency meaningfully; and CLAUDE.md §9 says an illustrative calibration is allowed only to make the mechanism observable, not to tune the demo until it looks good.

**WHAT THE RUNG TEACHES.** Two things, and the second is why the first matters. **Coverage is a path, not a field** — a CRM answers *"who covers this client?"* in one column and cannot answer *"whom has nobody met?"*, which is a walk over an interaction graph joined to an officer roster. **And a bounded acquisition can MANUFACTURE a coverage gap that does not exist**: same client, same instant, same estate, `limit=200` finds 0 gaps and `limit=20` finds 3, two in material roles. The bound did not discover that nobody met the CFO — it hid the meeting. The finding is not wrong about the graph it was given; it is wrong about the world, and nothing inside the payload distinguishes the two except `evidence_boundary`.

**THE FOURTH VALIDATION GATE IS THE RUNG'S SUBJECT.** `cp-07.truncation-disclosure@1.0.0`, supplied as a `product_gate` and executed by the SDK at the ruled point (`D-IMPL-282`: the gate's identity is the Control Plane's, its implementation the deployment's). **It refuses SILENCE, never truncation** — a bounded read is legitimate; a payload cut by its bound that does not say so is refused before a consumer sees it. Sabotaged by suppressing only the `truncated` flag while leaving the counts intact, and watched refuse.

**CANONICAL SHAPE, PROVED BEFORE IT WAS ROSTERED.** `boot`/`acquire`/`govern`, one `build_governed_resolver`, a NAMED `plan_factory` whose only operator source is the resolver's `required`. Measured before the roster line was written: `shape_of` reads `canonical`, `resolver_ownership` finds the one call, `governed_seam_calls` and `legacy_governance_regions` are empty, and `_sdk_supplied_operator_set` answers True with plan sources `(('required',),)`. `RULED_SDK_SUPPLIED_DEPLOYMENTS` records that answer; it does not cause it. A duplicate cp-06 literal in that frozenset was removed in passing.

**GATES:** 23 directional tests plus 6 MCP door tests, all against the curated estate, none pinning an estate figure. Four sabotage-verified: the truncation gate disarmed (red), the ingestion order reversed (`226 of 250 admitted nodes carry no kind`), a node's kind prefix dropped (`200 of 450`), and the λ_c reverted to 7 days (the freshness ordering inverts). `make lint` rc 0. `.76` unchanged — read-only on both legs, no ledger created, no schema written.

**TWO DEFECTS IN A MERGED EXAMPLE, found by driving this rung's door.** `CP07-F-08`: cp-06's shipped MCP door never creates its assembly root, so its first call answers `unable to open database file` — it ships a test that the door *declares* an entry point, and nothing ever booted it. `CP07-F-09`: the same door's hand-rolled `RefusalEnvelope` cannot be constructed (it passes `reason`/`key`/`detail` against a contract requiring `kind`/`fields`/`request`/`pre_assembly_lineage`), turning a governed "no" into `ccf-runtime-failure` — which the SDK reserves for *"CCF or its runtime failed"*. **Neither is fixed here**, on the `CP06-F-01` precedent: one claim per branch. cp-07 resolved its own instance by DELETING the compensating code (`D-IMPL-289`) — the door refuses nothing of its own and the Control Plane returns `product-request-violation` with a replay reference — and a second compensating path went with it, so a question governance refuses is no longer read at all.

**THE THREE CARRIES, ruled out of this merge and ordered.** (1) **cp-06's MCP door** — `CP07-F-08` and `CP07-F-09`, small and concrete, and Dave's stated next piece of work. (2) **Relative `since` defaults** — `CP07-F-03`, a real SDK gap: a class default holds a literal, so a `−365 days` window becomes an absolute date that ages silently. (3) **`product-gates` / ROADMAP-number tooling** — `CP07-F-10`: the checker requires a locked ROADMAP criterion per gate, and no rung built since cp-04 has one, so four trees cannot be made green without inventing numbers that bind to nothing.

**Next free decision id: `D-IMPL-324`.** **Governs:** the approval of rung 7 and what it ships with; the ordering of the three carries. **Related:** `D-IMPL-323` (the illustrative calibration), `D-IMPL-282` (declared product gate), `D-IMPL-289` (compensating code is deleted, not relocated), `D-IMPL-315` (adjudicate rather than edit), `D-IMPL-317` (one claim per branch), `CP-SPEC-007`, `D-GATE-cp-06`.

**D-IMPL-324 — cp-06's door repair is ACCEPTED at `b85cf524`. `declaration ≠ door` is the load-bearing line: the driven-door test is the fix, and deleting the hand-rolled envelope is the refusal path becoming honest. The one-branch / two-commit shape is a RECORDED EXCEPTION, not a new rule.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-09-10. Ruled by: Dave, on the report of the merge.

**THE ACCEPTANCE, as given:** *"Accept `b85cf524`. Close the sitting."*

**THE LOAD-BEARING LINE, verbatim and stated as still standing:** *"The load-bearing line is still: **declaration ≠ door**. `test_cp_06_mcp_door.py` is the actual fix; deleting the hand-rolled envelope is the refusal path becoming honest."*

Which names the causal order correctly and inverts the intuitive one. The two defects (`CP07-F-08`, `CP07-F-09`) are consequences; **the absence of a driven door is the cause.** cp-06 shipped `server/door.yaml`, `server/serve.py` and `test_the_door_declares_its_entrypoint_rather_than_a_script_path` — a correct test of a real property, reading the YAML and asserting an entry point is *declared*. It could not see either defect and nothing was wrong with it. **A door that has never been opened passes every test written about its declaration.** So the repair that matters is the opening, not the two lines it exposed.

**AND THE SECOND HALF IS A CLASSIFICATION, not a description.** Deleting the hand-rolled `RefusalEnvelope` is *the refusal path becoming honest* rather than a bug fix: the door had been fabricating a refusal it could not construct, and what replaced it is the Control Plane's own governed determination — `product-request-violation`, the declared and presented key sets, a replay reference, and `isError: false`, because a governed refusal is a successful response. This is `D-IMPL-289` again (compensating code dies with the declaration), and it is the same move cp-07 made on the same shape hours earlier.

**THE EXTRA EVIDENCE DAVE RULED IS KEPT, verbatim:** *"Keep the extra evidence: both sabotages replayed the shipped failures; in-process numbers unchanged; `acquire_for` does not touch a store after a contract no."* Each is recorded because each answers a different doubt: the sabotages establish the guards are load-bearing **and** that they reproduce the failures as shipped rather than approximations of them (`unable to open database file`; `ccf-runtime-failure:<id>`); the unchanged in-process figures (`COVERAGE 1.0890`, `D_c 0.376895431605010680`) establish the repair reached the door and nothing else; and the acquisition behavior establishes that a question the contract refused costs no source read on either leg, so the refusal is not paid for twice.

**THE PROCESS EXCEPTION, ruled narrowly:** *"One-branch / two-commits is a recorded exception, not a new rule."* `D-IMPL-317`'s one-claim-per-branch discipline stands unchanged. `cp-06-door-and-spec` carried two claims — the door repair and the `§D.2` step-table correction — as two separate commits on one branch, and Dave accepted that shape for this sitting **without** generalizing it. A later sitting citing this entry as precedent for bundling is misreading it: the exception is recorded so the departure is visible, which is the opposite of making it a default.

**THE `§D.2` CORRECTION RIDING WITH IT.** cp-06's step table named `traversal.typed-neighborhood` on all three Fluree acquisition rows and omitted `policy.principal-subgraph` entirely — the identical defect Dave found by reading `CP-SPEC-007` §D.2, and it was in cp-06 first. Both tables are rebuilt on the layer split they were blurring (source access / L2 admission / the two L4 operators over L3 / Π / the SDK's) and both now carry the guard that holds three witnesses to one set: the table, the class declaration, and the served `operators_invoked`. **The defect was in the documents only** — both shipped products always invoked both operators, and `D-GATE-cp-06` and `D-GATE-cp-07` both stand.

**WHAT IS LEFT, and it is deliberately left:** *"Leave `F-03` and `F-10`. Next sitting picks one of them."* `CP07-F-03` — a class default holds a literal, so a relative window (`−365 days`) becomes an absolute date that ages silently; a real SDK gap. `CP07-F-10` — `tools/check_product_gates.py` requires a locked ROADMAP criterion per gate and no rung built since cp-04 has one, so four trees cannot be made green without inventing numbers that bind to nothing. Neither is started; the next sitting chooses.

**D-IMPL-325 — A request default may be declared RELATIVE to the request's own `asked_at`, in a separate `relative_defaults` field. `defaults` stays literal-only. What replay records is the RESOLVED LITERAL with `authority="default"`, never the rule.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-09-10. Ruled by: Dave, on `CP07-F-03` and four presented options, with one addition of his own and one constraint from Grok.

**THE GAP, as measured in cp-07.** `CP-SPEC-007` §B.2 declares the `since` default as **`−365 days`**. `ProductRequestContract.defaults` holds literal values, so the artifact could only carry the absolute `"2024-09-01"`. **That value ages silently**: written it meant two years of history, a year on it means three, the fan-out grows and nothing anywhere says the default drifted. Computing it in `deployment.request` is strictly worse — it puts a governance value back in code and gives the deployment a second authority for one bound, which is the shape `D-IMPL-315` exists to keep out.

**THE FOUR RULINGS, as given.** (1) **Separate field: yes.** *"Keep `defaults` literal-only and add `relative_defaults`. Do not overload `defaults` with marker objects."* (2) **`offset_seconds`: yes.** *"Reuse the SDK's existing duration vocabulary. No `days` convenience field and no ISO-duration parser."* — the vocabulary already in `HalfLifeEntry.half_life_seconds`. (3) **Explicit `render`: yes.** *"Use something like `date | timestamp`. Do not infer semantics from JSON Schema `type: string`."* (4) **cp-07 afterward: yes.** *"First land and test the SDK capability by itself. Then, as a separate validation/adoption step, change cp-07 from its aging absolute date to the relative default and rerun it. Don't mix example republishing into the SDK repair."*

**THE DOMAIN QUESTION, ruled by Dave against the option offered.** The presented design asked whether to refuse a relative default outright when an `argument_domains` entry exists, because its value is not knowable at declaration. Dave declined the refusal and split the validation instead: *"Do not forbid `relative_defaults` when an `argument_domain` exists."* At declaration time — the parameter exists, is not inert, has **one** default authority, and its declared type can hold the requested render. At request time — compute, render, then run the normal domain and conformity checks on the resulting value. And the reasoning, which is the part worth keeping: *"a dynamic default can legitimately be refused at request time if the computed date falls outside its governed domain. That is not weaker governance; **the value simply does not exist until `asked_at` exists**."*

**THE REPLAY INVARIANT, stated by Dave as the important one.** *"Replay records the resolved absolute value and `authority=default`, not a rule that gets recomputed later."* Worked: `asked_at = 2026-09-10` plus `-31536000` seconds under `render: date` resolves to `"2025-09-10"`, and **replay preserves `"2025-09-10"` permanently**. A rule re-evaluated at replay time would make one decision answer differently on two days, which is the determinism the five-dimension record exists to hold.

**THE HASH CONSTRAINT (Grok, adopted).** `relative_defaults={}` is hash-transparent, so every contract written before this field keeps its content address. **Any populated `relative_defaults` must change the contract hash** — otherwise two products with different relative-window rules would share one contract identity. *"That distinction needs a direct regression test."*

**THE DECLARED RULES, in full.** `offset_seconds: int`, `render: Literal["date", "timestamp"]`. `offset_seconds` must be negative; `0` refuses **by name**, directing the author to an ordinary literal default. A parameter appears in exactly one of `defaults` or `relative_defaults`. The parameter must exist and must not be inert. `render` must be compatible with the parameter's declared type. Relative defaults resolve from `request.asked_at` **before** the caller overlay, and an explicit caller value still wins. After resolution, the normal domain and conformity checks run.

**SCOPE, ruled narrow.** *"Implementation should be small: `D-IMPL-325` → new typed sub-contract → field on `ProductRequestContract` → one resolution branch → direct tests."* **No cp-07 files in the SDK commit.**

**AMENDMENT 1 (Dave, 2026-09-10, on a measurement taken before the value was chosen): cp-07 adopts a TWO-YEAR offset, not the `−365 days` the ruling's worked example used.** The adoption brief said both *"use `offset_seconds: -31536000`"* and *"existing cp-07 truncation, freshness, Debt, and coverage behavior remain valid"*. Measured against the curated estate at `asked_at` 2026-09-11 on `JJAX4X60DE65EYFOTY73` with the class `limit` of 200, those two cannot both hold:

| offset | resolved `since` | available | NTK withheld | admitted | truncated |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| −31536000 (1 yr) | 2025-09-11 | **179** | **0** | 179 | **False** |
| −47304000 (1.5 yr) | 2025-03-12 | 218 | 1 | 200 | True |
| **−63072000 (2 yr)** | 2024-09-11 | **240** | **1** | 200 | **True** |
| −78840000 (3 yr) | 2023-09-12 | 240 | 1 | 200 | True |

At one year **two of the rung's demonstrations stop firing**: truncation (179 is under the `limit`) and need-to-know withholding (the single classified interaction is older than a year). **This is `CP07-F-04` arriving from the other direction** — that finding had already established that §B.2's `−365 days` cell and its truncation claim cannot coexist, and resolved it in favor of truncation. Presented as three options with the measurement; Dave chose option 1, **−63072000**, which reproduces the retired absolute default's behavior exactly while no longer aging. Labeled an **illustrative calibration** under `D-IMPL-323` in `ccf_config.yaml`, the README and `CP-SPEC-007` §B.2, whose `−365 days` cell is superseded. `test_the_declared_window_still_exceeds_the_class_limit` asserts both demonstrations still fire, so a later narrowing is caught at the point of the change rather than left to prose.

**One cp-07 test changed, under the allowed clause.** `D-IMPL-261` permits an example change when *"the SDK surface it legitimately consumes was deliberately changed"*. `test_the_class_default_resolves_for_a_caller_who_sent_no_bound` read `config()["request_contract"]["defaults"]["since"]` — an authority location that no longer holds the window. Its stated intent (read the declaration, never a literal) is preserved: it reads the declared offset and derives the date from the instant the door was driven at. Nothing was weakened to make it pass, and six new tests were added for the semantics.

**Next free decision id: `D-IMPL-326`.** **Governs:** how a relative request default is declared, validated, resolved and hashed; what replay records for one; the ordering of the SDK repair against cp-07's adoption. **Related:** `CP07-F-03` (`examples/cp-07-client-360-coverage-graph/FINDINGS.md`), `D-IMPL-253` Q2 (product defaults belong on the request contract — *"they define what omission means for that product"*), `D-IMPL-259` (argument domains), `D-IMPL-261` (examples are probes — this is the SDK repair the probe earned), `D-IMPL-264` D-08 (the resolution outcome), `D-IMPL-315` (one authority per bound), `D-IMPL-243` (hash transparency), `CINV-01` (no governance value in the spine).

**D-IMPL-326 — `product-gates` accepts the acceptance authority that ACTUALLY governed the product: a numbered ROADMAP criterion, or a cited clause of the product's own `CP-SPEC`. Exactly one per gate. Fabricating a criterion number to satisfy the tool is forbidden.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-09-10. Ruled by: Dave, on `CP07-F-10`, as a **tooling-model fix and not an SDK fix**.

**THE RULING, as given.** *"`product-gates` must accept the authority that actually governed the Context Product. A product may be gated by either a numbered ROADMAP/phase criterion, or a cited clause / definition-of-done in its `CP-SPEC`. Do not fabricate ROADMAP criterion numbers for cp-04 through cp-07 merely to satisfy the tool."* And the reason, which is the part that generalizes: *"The goal is not to make the gate easier. It is to make it ask the right question: **What approved acceptance authority says this product is done?**"* An invented integer answers that falsely; a citation answers it checkably.

**THE STANDING RULE Dave restated here, and it governs beyond this entry:** *"Every example has its own specification. Every gate traces to that specification. Every declared gate is exercised by a real test."*

**THE SCOPE, ruled narrow and kept narrow.** No new planning framework; no invented phase numbers; existing ROADMAP behavior stays valid; add the CP-spec form; prove an invalid or missing spec reference still fails; then bring the affected active rungs onto it. Frozen cp-04 is untouched — and was already passing, since its roster predates the problem.

**WHAT WAS BUILT.** `spec_clause: {document, clause}` on the gate item of `docs/schemas/product-gates/cp.product-gates.json`, with `criterion` leaving `required` and a `oneOf` making the two forms mutually exclusive per gate. `tools/check_product_gates.py::spec_clause_problems` walks all three links — the document exists (tree-relative, because a product's authority is its OWN specification), the clause exists as a heading, and the gate's own id appears inside that clause's body, which runs to the next heading of the same level or higher. Link 3 is the one a coarser check would skip and is what stops a roster citing any real heading and reading as governed.

**A CORRECTION TO `CP07-F-10`'s OWN WORDING, measured.** The finding says the *checker* requires a locked ROADMAP criterion. It does not — the word ROADMAP appears nowhere in `tools/check_product_gates.py`. The requirement was in the **schema**, where `criterion` sat in the gate item's `required` list. The fix is therefore mostly a schema edit, which is narrower than the finding implied.

**THE ID PATTERN WAS WIDENED, and the reason is the ruling applied to itself.** `^[A-Z]{2,4}-G[0-9]{2}$` cannot express cp-07's own `C36-G01`..`C36-G08`, because `C36` carries a digit. The two available moves were renaming a shipped specification's gate ids to suit the checker, or widening the pattern to `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]{1,3}-G[0-9]{2}$`. The first is the inversion this ruling exists to prevent — the tool accepts the authority that governed the product, not the reverse — so the pattern was widened, in the schema and in the checker's `GATE_ID_TOKEN` together, with `test_the_token_and_the_schema_pattern_agree_on_what_an_id_is` holding the two readers to one vocabulary. Every id written before the widening still matches.

**ADOPTION, and it is partial by measurement rather than by choice.** cp-06 declares **twelve** gates, all twelve mapping to existing tests — pure id-wiring, exactly as the brief anticipated. cp-07 declares **six of the eight** its §G.1 table names: `C36-G02` had no test and one was written (four lines, no new instrumentation); `C36-G06` needs a query-counting seam that does not exist and is recorded rather than declared against a test that does not assert it; `C36-G08` states two claims proved by two different tests and a gate carries one `test:`. Both absences are `CP07-F-11` in cp-07's `FINDINGS.md`.

**WHAT IS STILL RED, and it is the next sitting's by ruling.** `make product-gates` goes from four failing trees to two. `cp-04-canonical-corporate-family-tree` has **no `spec/` directory at all** and so has neither authority form; `cp-05-credit-exposure-rollup` has a specification whose §G.2 is numbered prose criteria carrying no gate ids. Dave: *"I disagree with leaving cp-04-canonical permanently without a spec ... Recommended path: take the narrow 326 now, then normalize cp-04-canonical and cp-05 in the next small sitting."* That sitting creates cp-04-canonical's own `CP-SPEC-004C` — **never citing frozen cp-04's spec** — adds stable ids to cp-05's existing §G.2 without inventing new criteria, and verifies every active example has its own spec → gates → executing tests chain.

**A VACUOUS TEST WAS FOUND AND FIXED BY SABOTAGE, and is recorded because the class keeps recurring.** `test_the_clause_body_ends_at_the_next_heading` cited the fixture's LAST clause, where running to end-of-file adds nothing — so removing the body bound left the test green. Three of four sabotages went red; that one did not, and the fixture now carries a clause with something after it. The guard was proved load-bearing only after the fixture could express the defect.

**ACCEPTED (Dave, 2026-09-10, on the report of the merge at `4820531d`).** *"I'd accept `D-IMPL-326` as landed correctly."* Recorded as an amendment rather than a new entry **deliberately**: `D-IMPL-327` is reserved for the normalization sitting below, and spending it on an acceptance note would push that work's id and break the reference Dave has already made to it.

**THE OUTCOME HE NAMES AS THE IMPORTANT ONE, verbatim:** *"the gate checker now governs acceptance authority, not just file presence: each gate points to exactly one authoritative source — either a ROADMAP criterion or a product-spec clause — and that clause must itself name the gate id. That is the right shape."* The third clause is the load-bearing half — a citation that resolves to a real heading saying nothing about the gate is not authority for it, and without that link the model would be presence-checking one layer up.

**THE THREE DISPOSITIONS, agreed as landed:** cp-06 clean at 12/12; cp-07 **correctly partial at 6/8**, with `CP07-F-11` carrying the two unsupported cases *"instead of faking coverage"*; cp-04-canonical and cp-05 deferred, *"not work to pull into 326"*.

**TWO PROCESS FINDINGS DAVE RULED WORTH PRESERVING, in his words:** *"a test target that never executes because an earlier make leg is red is not coverage"* — `make gate-tools` runs three pytest legs sequentially and stops at the first failure, so `tools/lints/tests`'s standing reds meant `tools/product_gates_tests` was never reached by that target. And *"collection failure can masquerade as 'no failures reported' if you only read summarized output"* — a broken test module makes the gate checker print no line for that tree, which reads exactly like a clean tree. Both were hit in this sitting, not hypothesized.

**THE NEXT SITTING'S SCOPE, ruled here so it is not re-derived.** `D-IMPL-327` starts the cp-04-canonical + cp-05 gate normalization, and its four points are fixed: (1) cp-04-canonical authors **its own `CP-SPEC-004C`** — *"do not cite frozen cp-04"*; (2) cp-05 gets stable ids on its **existing** §G.2 and its roster wired against them, inventing no new criteria; (3) cp-06 and cp-07 are **not touched** unless the new checker behavior exposes a regression; (4) `CP07-F-11` stays a **carry** unless the query-counting seam and the multi-test gate representation are explicitly taken on.

**Next free decision id: `D-IMPL-327`.** **Governs:** what counts as a gate's acceptance authority and how a citation is resolved; the id pattern; cp-06 and cp-07's rosters; the scope boundary against the normalization sitting. **Related:** `CP07-F-10` and `CP07-F-11` (`examples/cp-07-client-360-coverage-graph/FINDINGS.md`), `D-IMPL-224` (gates are a declared artifact plus CI coverage), `D-IMPL-225` amendment 3 (the closed schema), `D-IMPL-261` (examples are probes), `D-IMPL-319` (cp-04-canonical is the pattern to copy), `D-22` (a prose table is the machine source for nothing).

**THE STANDING RULE THIS DISCHARGES, restated by Dave at `D-IMPL-326`:** *"Every example has its own specification. Every gate traces to that specification. Every declared gate is exercised by a real test."*

**`CP-SPEC-004C`, and why it is lean.** 314 lines, cp-07-shaped, against a ladder whose earlier specs run 1,395–2,275. Do not re-derive cp-04's full domain treatment."* The document is **retrospective and says so in §0**: the implementation existed first under `D-IMPL-313`/`D-IMPL-319`, so every gate describes a test that already ran and none was written to the document. It cites `CP-SPEC-004` nowhere — a successor whose acceptance authority lived in its predecessor's document would be governed by a document nobody may edit. Thirteen gates, `CFC-G01`..`CFC-G13`, one per executing test, **no hole**. The `CFC-` prefix rather than `CFT-` because the specimen's ids are claimed and two trees answering one question need two vocabularies.

**A TOOL DEFECT THE NORMALIZATION SURFACED, and it had to be fixed to finish.** `test_modules_for` globbed `tests/examples/test_cp_NN_*.py` by rung, and **rung 4 carries two trees**. Each was handed the other's modules: the canonical roster was reported as failing to declare the specimen's `CFT-G19` and `CFT-G99`. The two had never both carried a roster before, so nothing had exercised the collision. `test_modules_for` now partitions by the discriminator token after `cp-NN-`: a tree with modules of its own takes exactly those, a tree without takes the rung's minus every module another same-rung tree claims. Measured after: canonical 1 module, specimen 10 and none lost. Two tests hold it, one over a scratch pair and one over the real repository, both asserting **in both directions** — a partition that starved the base tree would otherwise pass.

**cp-05: four gates declared, four carried, and the count is a CORRECTION.** The sitting was planned at five-and-three on a probe that searched the test tree for each criterion's distinguishing term. Reading the assertions instead, `CER-G05` requires the reconciliation guard to be *observed firing* and its test asserts only that `reconciliation` **is present** — a different claim. **Token presence is not token force.** `CER-G04`, `CER-G05`, `CER-G06` and `CER-G07` are `CP05-F-01`; none was declared against a test that does not prove it. §G.2 itself is unchanged apart from an id per criterion: *"Do not invent new criteria."*

**`CP05-F-02` — THE FINDING OF THIS SITTING, and the gate wiring is what produced it.** `produce_governed` returns three values; `test_cp_05_output.py`'s fixture unpacked two. **Every test in that module errored at fixture setup — cp-05 has had no output-level test coverage** — and it is pre-existing, measured identically at the branch base. It went unnoticed because **an erroring test is still a COLLECTED test**: `pytest --collect-only` lists all eight node ids, and an instrument that asks *"did pytest collect this?"* — which is what `tools/check_product_gates.py` asks, by design — reports the module healthy. Without the gate wiring nobody would have run those tests directly and looked.

Dave ruled the repair and the boundary together: *"Fix the 2-line unpack. It is an objectively stale test, not a change to make the product pass ... Do not redesign the gate checker in this sitting. Its collection-only limitation is now known; direct pytest execution proves these four gates here."* The fix names `_record` rather than `*rest`, so a fourth return value fails loudly instead of being swallowed by the same silence. **No assertion was added, removed or weakened**; all eight now execute and pass.

**D-IMPL-328 — a relative default's offset of `0` is ADMITTED and means the request's own instant, unchanged. It is an ordinary relative default in every respect: same branch, same authority, same pin, same recorded literal. A positive offset is still refused.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-09-11. Ruled by: Dave, on `CP08-F-01`, before cp-08's spec may be completed.

**WHAT `D-IMPL-325` SAID, and why it was wrong from the other side.** That ruling required a negative offset, and its reasoning was that *"`0` is not a relative default at all but `asked_at` itself, which `defaults` already expresses without a rule."* The first clause is right and the second is not. `CP-SPEC-008`'s bitemporal surface defaults `as_of` to *today* and `known_as_of` to *now* — **the request's own instant, unchanged** — and `ProductRequestContract.defaults` **cannot** express that. Any date written into the literal surface is a date that ages, which is precisely the defect `CP07-F-03` measured and `D-IMPL-325` exists to close. The rule closed one hole and left the same hole one value over.

**THE TWO AVAILABLE MOVES, and why this one.** Either the mechanism admits `0`, or the deployment injects `asked_at` in code. The second puts a governance value back in the spine and gives the deployment a second authority for one bound, which is the shape `D-IMPL-315` exists to keep out — and it would do so for the one parameter whose whole subject is *which instant governed this decision*. Dave: *"do not inject `asked_at` in deployment/example code."*

**ZERO IS ORDINARY, and that is the load-bearing half of the ruling.** It is not a special case with its own path. It resolves in the same branch of `resolve_effective_request` against the same `request.asked_at`, at the same point in the resolution; it records authority `default` with the same contract pin; and what lands in replay is the **resolved literal**, never the offset. Dave: *"authority and replay behavior are identical to any other relative offset."* The only thing special about it is that the arithmetic is an identity.

**WHAT IS STILL REFUSED.** A positive offset, and for the reason that always applied: a default in the future describes no window a caller could have observed. The refusal message and the field's documentation now say that and only that — the module no longer explains a rule it does not have.

**EVIDENCE.** Six direct regressions in `tests/products/test_relative_defaults.py`: the identity resolution under both renders; authority and pin identical to any other offset; the value still MOVING with the question across two instants (which is what makes it relative rather than a literal); the resolved literal recorded with the offset absent — **and a positive control that the instant IS present, so the absence is a claim about the offset rather than about an empty record**; a caller's value still winning; and zero and a negative offset hashing to two contract identities. Sabotage-verified four ways, each restored: re-refusing zero (6 red), admitting positive offsets (3), silently treating zero as one day back (3), and flipping the recorded authority to `caller` (2).

**Next free decision id: `D-IMPL-329`.** **Governs:** what `offset_seconds` admits and what it refuses; the identity offset's authority, provenance and replay treatment. **Related:** `D-IMPL-325` (amended here, not superseded — the relative-default mechanism is unchanged), `CP08-F-01` (`examples/cp-08-covenant-in-force-as-of/spec/CP-SPEC-008_Covenant_In_Force_As_Of.md` §B.2), `CP07-F-03` (the aging literal this keeps closed), `D-IMPL-315` (one authority per bound).

**D-IMPL-329 — cp-08 ships as OPTION B. Two clocks are demonstrated on AMENDMENTS, not on covenants; the supersession claim is WITHDRAWN because covenant thresholds never change.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-09-11. Ruled by: Dave, at cp-08's Gate 1, on measurement taken before the spec was revised.

**THE DURABLE CONCLUSION, in Dave's words, and it is the whole entry:**

> **Booking lag proves two clocks. It does not prove covenant supersession.**

**OPTION B.** The vault frames rung 08 as a flagship demonstrating *"ledger time-travel with supersession preserved rather than overwritten."* The supersession half is withdrawn. What ships is smaller and honest: two clocks over the amendment booking lag, `as_of` against `known_as_of`, historical replay at a recorded ledger `t`, and current covenant terms **labelled unversioned** with `CIF-G12` holding the label as a payload field so no consumer mistakes them for historical covenant state.

**TWO CLOCKS — ON AMENDMENTS, NOT COVENANTS.** `ex:assertedAt` appears on **0 of 180 covenants**, on all three booking-lag facilities and across the whole ledger at every point sampled; it lives on the amendment nodes. Nothing on a covenant can be filtered by `known_as_of`, so the covenant set is identical either side of a booking gap. One level up it is real: `AMD-01BB3F-2` (`validFrom` 2025-08-14, `assertedAt` 2025-10-05, 52 days, drawdown `DRW-01BB3F-0000` inside the gap) is excluded at `known_as_of=2025-09-09` and admitted after.

**SUPERSESSION — WITHDRAWN BECAUSE THE THRESHOLDS NEVER CHANGE.** Covenant thresholds are unchanged across the entire ledger: **180 at `t:1500` through head `t:5591`, zero changed and zero added at every point.** No interval is ever closed (`validTo` constant at 2) and no covenant ever gains a marker (`supersededBy` 0 at every point). The ledger's 1,107 supersession markers belong to `WarningSignal`, `OpportunitySignal`, `CreditRating`, `IssuanceEvent`, `PriorObservation`, `BreachOfCovenant` and `PolicyVersion` — **not to the covenant slice cp-08 reads**, and per the instruction they do not count. There is no row for time-travel to reconstruct, so the claim is removed from the title, the gates and the teaching text rather than softened, and two gates were **deleted** rather than weakened.

**WHERE THE EVIDENCE LIVES.** `examples/cp-08-covenant-in-force-as-of/spec/CP-SPEC-008_Covenant_In_Force_As_Of.md` **§0.5** (what Gate 1 measured and what it withdrew) and `examples/cp-08-covenant-in-force-as-of/spec/MEASUREMENT-NOTE.md` (both claims measured apart, with the ledger figures and the near-miss the control disproved). The note ships beside the spec by ruling and stays there.

**WHAT GATE 2 INHERITS, and these are constraints rather than notes.** `CP08-F-03` — `assertedAt` lives on **amendment rows**, so implementation may filter amendments by `known_as_of` and **must not pretend covenants carry an `assertedAt` field**. `CP08-F-04` — there is **no covenant supersession to implement**, so supersession semantics may not be reintroduced. Gate 1 is complete at `260ff4aa`; Gate 2 starts fresh.

**Next free decision id: `D-IMPL-330`.** **Governs:** cp-08's shipped scope and the two constraints Gate 2 inherits. **Related:** `D-IMPL-328` (the identity offset `CP08-F-01` needed), `D-IMPL-325` (relative defaults), `D-IMPL-240` (2) (`t` is transaction time and is not `as_of`), `D-IMPL-309` (the store pin is execution provenance), `D-IMPL-261` (examples are probes), `CP-SPEC-007` §B.2 (where `as_of` was declared inert at Tier 2).

**THE GATE, as given:** *"I approve D-GATE-cp-08. … The rung is gated. No further cp-08 work is required for this close."* The approval was withheld until the documentation and finding-reference gaps were discharged, on Dave's instruction: *"Do not gate cp-08 with required documentation and broken finding references knowingly outstanding."*

**WHAT DAVE SETTLED FOR THIS CLOSE, in his own enumeration.** cp-08 is accepted as the Tier-3 two-clock product; the README and FINDINGS requirements are discharged; `CP08-F-01` is resolved; `CP08-F-02` is closed by scope/refusal; `CP08-F-03` remains an explicit constraint — assertion time belongs to amendments, not covenants; `CP08-F-04` remains open — historical covenant-term reconstruction is not supported by this product; `CIF-G07`, `CIF-G13` and `CIF-G14` remain named gaps and `CIF-G15` remains specified but unimplemented; 18 live-estate tests pass; 105/105 declared product gates execute; `.76` remains read-only; and the product carries **no supersession claim and no product-specific Debt metric**.

**WHAT THE RUNG TEACHES, and the second half is why it was allowed to ship smaller than it was framed.** A question with **two independent time axes**, where moving either alone changes the answer on real estate data: at `as_of=2025-09-09` the amendment set is one member at `known_as_of=2025-09-09` and two at `known_as_of=2025-12-31`. `AMD-01BB3F-2` took effect 2025-08-14 and was booked 2025-10-05, so on the drawdown date it **was in force and was not known**. A `SELECT` against current state answers neither question and gives no signal that it answered a different one. **And the supersession half of the original framing was WITHDRAWN on measurement before any code was written** — 0 of 180 covenants carry `supersededBy`, thresholds are unchanged from `t:1500` to head, no interval is ever closed, and the ledger's 1,107 supersession markers belong to other classes entirely. **Booking lag proves two clocks. It does not prove covenant supersession.** A product may not teach a property its data does not have.

**THE DECLARED INVARIANT.** `cp-08.temporal-coherence@1.0.0`, supplied as a `product_gate` and executed by the SDK at the ruled point (`D-IMPL-282`: the gate's identity is the Control Plane's, its implementation the deployment's). Every admitted amendment must satisfy **both** filters; the gate is sabotaged in-test on each limb independently, because a sabotage as coarse as the whole guard proves only that SOME test mentions it.

**GATES:** 12 declared, each with an executing test and a named sabotage; 18 tests against the curated estate, none pinning an estate figure. `CIF-G16` replaced `CIF-G13` under a **new id** after the original was measured vacuous — it read its left-hand set from `policy_bindings`, an attribute `ProductLineage` does not have, so `cited <= recorded` was trivially true and the gate proved only that a decision record existed. **A gate that once reported coverage it did not provide does not keep its name.** `.76` unchanged: read-only on both legs, no ledger created, no schema written.

**FOUR DEFECTS THIS RUNG FOUND IN ITS OWN WORK, all in proof machinery rather than mechanism.** (1) **A count is only as good as the population it ranged over** — the Gate-1 `CP08-F-03` claimed 112 of 137 amendments lacked a booking date; 137 counts every `ex:amends` edge in the ledger and this product reads the **25** pointing at a credit facility, **all of which carry both clocks**. The finding, the `D_c` metric built on it, and two gates were withdrawn together. (2) **A one-sided subset check cannot fail on omission** — `CIF-G13`, above. (3) **A withdrawn claim survives in the code that cited it** — both the population figure and the debt metric were struck from the specification and still doing load-bearing work in five modules and the resolver wiring. (4) **Configuration that nobody reads is documentation, not control** (Dave's phrase) — removing the deployment's own scorer exposed that the λ_c table had never been read by anything, because it was keyed `amendment_structure`/`covenant_terms`/`facility_reference` while the SDK's reference scorer looks each observation up **by type**. Re-keyed `amendment`/`covenant`/`facility`.

**`D_c` IS 0 ON EVERY ANSWER, AND IT IS STATED RATHER THAN DRESSED UP.** The product declares no Debt metric of its own and the platform's reference assessment applies. Measured across three `as_of` instants: freshness, completeness and semantic consistency all read 1 — freshness because every observation is minted from a live read inside the run, the other two declared against a measured estate in `artifacts/debt-declaration.yaml`. **The withdrawal cost no working signal; it removed a per-run ratio dressed as one.**

**THE IDS WERE RECONCILED BEFORE THE GATE, not after.** `CP08-F-NN` was minted at Gate 1 in the specification's §F.3, which the engineer-voice rewrite removed without relocating it, while `D-IMPL-329` numbered the inherited constraints against content the Gate-1 spec had carried under different numbers. The facts were identical in both records and nothing false was published, but for one sitting the same id named two claims and two citations resolved nowhere. `examples/cp-08-covenant-in-force-as-of/FINDINGS.md` is now the authoritative record and its §0 states exactly what moved. **`CP08-F-02` was investigated before being defined rather than defined to save the id** — Dave: *"Do not invent a definition to save the id."* It is real and distinct from `CP08-F-04`: F-02 governs a **refused request parameter**, F-04 how **served covenants are labelled**.

**WHAT IS CARRIED OUT OF THIS GATE.** `CIF-G15` — the dual TTL — is specified and deliberately unimplemented, because where *closed* ends and *live* begins is an operator's policy decision rather than one this deployment may take; **its behavior must not be invented**. `CIF-G07`, `CIF-G13` and `CIF-G14` are gaps in the numbering and are not reused. `CP08-F-03` and `CP08-F-04` stand as constraints on any successor: an implementation may filter amendments by `known_as_of` and **must not pretend covenants carry an `assertedAt` field**, and **no supersession semantics may be reintroduced**.
