**D-IMPL-336 — AMENDMENT 5 (2026-09-13, Dave, SIMPLIFICATION GO after he challenged the design). The composite is a CONSUMER of Context Products, not a second Control Plane. Skill-driven acquisition becomes the supported path; the parallel local attestation layer is REMOVED; verification stays at the boundary that owns it.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-09-13. Ruled by: Dave, after asking *"I'm wondering why this is so difficult… I feel you are overcomplicating this somewhat simple structural architecture."* **Implementation GO on `d-impl-336-composite`. No merge. CP-14 acquisition remains HOLD.**

**DAVE'S ARCHITECTURE, IN HIS OWN WORDS.** *"A complex context product can be made up of several other context products. It does not have to necessarily be responsible for assembling the atomic context products. They very well may be registered elsewhere servicing other use cases. The composite context product needs to be able to call the atomic context product whose definition exists either in-process, via an MCP, A2A or by calling another agent. The skill that the composite agent has knows how to acquire the atomic context product and roll it in."*

**WHAT WAS MEASURED BEFORE THE RULING, and what it showed.** `src/ccf/products/composite.py` stood at **1,910 lines**. By section: `compose_children` and its helpers **478 lines (25%)** — the pre-ruled content (`D-IMPL-31`'s four laws, `D-IMPL-104`'s per-factor debt); the trust apparatus — eligibility policy and evidence (90), provenance types, attestor and peer carry (280), invocation and producer tokens (124) — plus most of `CompositeAdmissionGate` (358), together **~40%**. A deployment acquiring ONE local child wrote **45 lines of non-comment code** and constructed **five intermediate typed objects** (`ResolvedProducer`, `ChildInvocation`, `LocalProvenance`, `ChildCandidate`, `AdmittedChild`). The eligibility-evidence machinery was verified **peered-only** by reading `_establish_eligibility`: a local child takes the invalidation-register check and returns.

**THE ROOT CAUSE, admitted by the orchestrator and accepted by Dave.** The outcomes map was treated as a **hostile input** — as though arbitrary code could hand the composite a fabricated child — so a second authorization layer was built on top of the one that already existed. **The grant is the authorization.** A skill is granted to produce class X; the composite declares it requires X; the skill runs. Asking a second time inside composition whether that was authorized asks the Control Plane a question it has already answered. Every panel finding that drove the token layer was real *given that design*; the design choice that made them real was making acquisition a loose seam rather than a granted skill dispatch.

**DAVE'S CORRECTION TO THE ORCHESTRATOR'S PROPOSAL, recorded because it was wrong in one respect.** The proposal offered to "move cross-fabric eligibility out to sit with peering". Dave: ***"MCP is not automatically peering. `D-IMPL-59` explicitly separates them. Apply the existing controls for the actual provider relationship; do not require a new signed envelope merely because acquisition uses MCP. A genuinely peered product must still pass peering verification, regardless of how the skill retrieves it."*** The axis is the **provider relationship**, never the transport the skill happened to use.

**THE RULING, in six parts, verbatim in substance.**

**(1) Skill-driven acquisition is the supported path.** The local path is **effective grant → actual skill dispatch → the child's governed delivery → fit checks → compose**. `GrantBoundChildResolver` ships **in `src/`** — which also settles the question the orchestrator raised at checkpoint 1 about whether CLAUDE.md §7.3/§8.1 or §11 governs: **§11, a reference implementation ships alongside the Protocol**, because acquisition through a granted skill is not an agent loop. Deployment code **binds** the resolver; it does not construct a chain of provenance objects. **`LocalFabricAttestor` and the additional local attestation/token machinery are REMOVED.** Invocation attribution comes **directly from the existing grant and dispatch execution records** — never caller-written grant hashes or identity strings. *"The grant authorizes invoking the skill. The provider's existing authorization still governs what that invocation may return. Do not duplicate either decision inside composition."*

**(2) The composite consumes products; it does not own their assembly.** `requires` names **product contracts**. `produces` means **the skill returns that product class**, not that it builds the product from raw data. An atomic Context Product **may already be registered elsewhere and serve other use cases**, and **its provider decides** whether to return a valid existing instance or assemble one on demand. **The composite must not need the atomic provider's assembler, source credentials, database handles, or boot context.** In-process, MCP, A2A and another-agent acquisition all belong **behind the skill's acquisition interface**. **No new identity axis, no scheduler, no swarm loop.**

**(3) Verification stays at the boundary that owns it.** **Local** — use actual dispatch and governed delivery evidence; where local dependency eligibility is checked, take touched entities from **the child's persisted execution/replay record**, never a caller-supplied list, and **do not require access to a remote provider's internal replay store**. **Peering/A2A** — signature, trust, policy and eligibility verification stay **in the peering layer**; composition consumes the verified result or the refusal. **Remove the duplicated verification machinery from `composite.py`, not the verification itself.** **MCP** — retain its existing authenticated/authorized access and typed-result handling; **do not automatically reclassify it as peering**, and **a local skill fetching a remote product must not relabel that product as locally produced to bypass its applicable checks**. **`R1` REMAINS BLOCKING**: fix the header-cap failure in peering using the already-authorized bounded configuration, and **prove an honest signed envelope reaches `peer_provenance_from_admitted` and composition**, retaining oversized-envelope and signature-tampering controls. ***"Moving the code does not close the finding."***

**(4) The composition contract is preserved.** `requires` stays authorable, registered and read by `GovernedResolver`. Fit checks are retained for class/version, subject/request, tenant, shared `asked_at`, content address, validity and assessable debt, **and so is slot-to-child reconciliation** — *"a child obtained for another requirement or request is not interchangeable."* The four existing composition rules apply: **factor-wise debt, lineage union, expiry floor, mixing refusal**. **`R4` is KEPT**: parent-declared operators are checked against parent execution **before** unioning admitted child operators; Gate 2 stays strict; inherited lineage is recorded **without claiming the parent engine executed the child's operators**. **`F1` is KEPT**: an optional declared absence takes its configured treatment, and an invoked child's refusal or admission failure **refuses the composite** — *"never turn rejection into a healthy omission."*

**(5) Replay is finished and provider independence is demonstrated.** **`CMP-R-01`** for persisted refused-composite records and **`R5`/`CMP-R-02`** for actual composite reconstruction — and **replay uses retained child artifacts and recorded composition evidence, not fresh calls to the atomic providers.** Then **`INT-01b`**, a small nested chain through the shipped acquisition path. **The demonstration must also show an independently registered atomic product serving ANOTHER consumer and the composite, and must change its acquisition binding from in-process to a supported remote route WITHOUT changing the composite's requirements or roll-up logic.** It exercises real dispatch, the relevant boundary verification, refusal handling, inherited expiry and persisted replay. **The full estate tour remains CP-14 work.**

**(6) One completion package.** The finding register distinguishes **removed duplicate mechanism**, **retained control**, **relocated responsibility** and **remaining defect**. **Tests of retired attestor classes are REPLACED by tests of the actual supported path — not merely deleted**, because *"do not merely delete the controls they represented."* Returned together: the **simplified deployment example**, the **candidate hash**, **exact regression and sabotage results**, **remaining limitations**, and **independent cross-AI reviews of the same immutable candidate**. ***"Stop before merge. The objective is a simple consumer-facing composition path backed by existing controls — not another Control Plane."***

**WHAT THIS SUPERSEDES AND WHAT IT DOES NOT.** It supersedes **the separate local-attestor requirement** — Amendment 4's `O1` as a composite-module obligation, and the `LocalFabricAttestor` shipped at `bd66f1f0`. **It does not supersede the existing authorization, product-validation, or replay obligations**, which stand unchanged. `O2` (the grant binding) and `O3` (the admission clock) stand. `R4`, `F1`, the four composition laws, the fit checks and slot reconciliation stand.

**Next free decision id: `D-IMPL-337`** — unchanged; an amendment spends none. **Governs:** the simplification on `d-impl-336-composite` through to the completion package. **Related:** Amendment 4 (the checkpoints this replaces the O1 half of), Amendment 3, `D-IMPL-59` (MCP is a Peering transport, not the concept — the separation Dave's correction rests on), `D-IMPL-31`, `D-IMPL-104`, `D-IMPL-334`/`D-IMPL-335`, `D-IMPL-308`, `D-IMPL-324`, `D-IMPL-222`, CLAUDE.md §7.3/§8.1/§11, INV-CH7-47.

**D-IMPL-337 — TOKEN-GUARDED VALUES MUST BE REVALIDATED AT EVERY PUBLICLY REACHABLE CONSUMER.** **OPEN — DESIGN REQUIRED.** Raised: 2026-09-14. Raised by: Dave, ruling on a measurement surfaced during `D-IMPL-336`'s close panels. **This is a cross-cutting SDK invariant gap that `D-IMPL-336` happened to expose. It is NOT a `D-IMPL-336` defect and it is not `D-IMPL-336`'s to remediate.**

**THE INVARIANT, PROPOSED — and it is the INVARIANT that is canonized here, never an implementation.** Dave's wording: *"If a type derives its authority or validity from a guarded construction path, every publicly reachable consumer that relies on that authority must positively verify the guarded runtime type before using it. Structural compatibility or duck typing is insufficient."* It applies whether the guarded value represents admission, authorization, single-writer authority, replay integrity, or another capability.

Stated as the property: **guarded authority cannot be recovered through structural typing.** Dave's refinement, recorded because the distinction is the whole point: *"`isinstance` may be the enforcement form, but that distinction matters… Canonize the invariant first: a consumer may not infer guarded authority from shape alone. Then let the 337 design prove whether `isinstance` is the correct universal enforcement mechanism or merely the correct mechanism for the six sites currently observed."* **A lint is the enforcement-mechanism CANDIDATE, not a silently adopted implementation detail.**

**HOW IT WAS FOUND, and why the finding is a class rather than six bugs.** Two close panels on `D-IMPL-336` (30 agents, then 15) each found one instance of the same shape, and each instance was repaired individually. Dave: *"I simplified the architecture yet we still can't get it right. What seems to be the core problem? You are just repeating the same loop but not moving forward."* An AST census of `src/` then measured the population the panels had been sampling:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| token-guarded capability types | **7** |
| consumer sites annotated to take one | **15** |
| sites that positively verify the type at runtime | **1** — added under `D-IMPL-336` close panel 2 |
| sites publicly reachable by an adopter | **6** |

**Minting is guarded; consumption is not.** The token is a *static* guarantee — mypy enforces it for conforming callers — presented in docstrings as a runtime one. `ccf.products.gates.ServableProduct`'s own docstring says *"holding one of these is the evidence that the gates ran."* That sentence is false at the consumer.

**MEASURED, not argued** (public imports, no reflection, no private names): a duck-typed `ServableProduct` reaches `DeliveryCapability.deliver`, which does `ServedProduct(product=product.product, …)` with no type check, and a `ServedProduct` is returned. `isinstance(duck, ServableProduct)` is `False`. **The three validation gates never ran.** Dave's endorsed reading of the diagnosis: *"My three mechanism defects weren't three mistakes. They were three samples from a population."*

**THE INITIAL CENSUS — six sites, recorded BEFORE any of them is modified, and deliberately NOT flattened into one severity.** Dave: *"Do not flatten these into one severity merely because one lint finds them."*

*Group A — guarded product / gate bypass.* The guarded type is `ServableProduct`, whose possession is meant to be the evidence that the three validation gates (empty-operator guard, lineage strict equality, TTL bounds) ran.
- `ccf.replay.serve.serve(product)` — **exported**.
- `ccf.replay.serve.DeliveryCapability.deliver(product)` — public name, reachable.
- `ccf.products.gates.refuse_over_tolerance(product)` — **exported**.

*Group B — a product crossing the Peering / L3 boundary without its admission proof.* The guarded type is `ccf.peering.admission.AdmittedProduct`, whose possession is meant to be the evidence that signature verification, peer entitlement and policy-binding checks ran. A bypass here puts an unverified federated product on the path to L3, against the single-writer invariant (CLAUDE.md §10) and `D-IMPL-59`'s admission commitment.
- `ccf.graph.product_source.mount_product_source(admitted)` — **exported**.
- `ccf.assembly.worker.ingest_admitted(admitted)` — public name, reachable.

*Group C — Control Plane state mutation on a structurally similar but unauthorized value.* The guarded type is `ccf.controlplane.state.StateWriteToken`.
- `ccf.controlplane.state.AuditedStateWriter.put(token)` — public name, reachable.

**Nine further sites are module-private** — the minter and the consumer share a module, so no caller can reach them without crossing the module boundary — and are therefore **not governed by the invariant as proposed**. Whether that exemption is correct is one of the design questions below, not a settled fact.

**WHAT THE 337 DESIGN PACKAGE MUST CONTAIN**, per Dave, before any fix:
1. the exact definition of a **token-guarded type**;
2. what counts as a **publicly reachable consumer**;
3. the six measured sites, and **why each is or is not actually governed** by the invariant;
4. the proposed static lint and its **false-positive / false-negative boundary**;
5. how **Protocol-typed consumers** interact with the rule;
6. whether an explicit **validator or helper** can satisfy the rule in lieu of a literal `isinstance`;
7. **negative controls** showing the lint catches a duck-typed substitute;
8. **positive controls** showing legitimate abstraction seams are **not** accidentally outlawed.

**WHAT IS FORBIDDEN, in Dave's words:** *"Do not run another broad sabotage sweep and patch whatever falls out. Do not fix all six sites opportunistically on the 336 branch. Do not record the finding and leave it indefinite. Do not call the lint complete merely because it finds the six known examples. Do not weaken Protocol usage generally; structural typing remains valid where no guarded authority is being asserted."*

**WHY IT IS SEPARATE, and this is the load-bearing reason.** A four-subsystem correction inside `d-impl-336-composite` would destroy the ability to answer the basic review question *"did `D-IMPL-336` correctly implement composite Context Products?"* — the branch would become inseparable from unrelated replay, peering, assembly and Control Plane repairs. Dave: *"That is exactly the scope-accretion pattern we have been trying to eliminate."*

**`D-IMPL-336`'s OWN POSITION, measured.** Dave requires that 336's own guarded-consumer site be correct and that the branch introduce no new bypass. Audited at `64d4ae4a`: `invocation_from_dispatch` is exported and **verifies** (`ProvenanceForgeryError` on a non-`ResolvedProducer`, closed at close panel 2); `compose_children` — the composition entry point, whose `outcomes` is typed `object` deliberately so mypy cannot prove its guard unreachable — **verifies** with `isinstance(outcome, AdmittedChild)`; `_admit`, `_rebinding_failure` and `_row_for_admitted` are module-private. **No publicly reachable consumer of a guarded type in `ccf/products/composite.py` or `ccf/products/child_resolver.py` trusts structure alone.** 336 carries `D-IMPL-337` as a **discovered dependency**, not as remediation scope.

**SEQUENCING.** `D-IMPL-337` is recorded now as OPEN with the census above. `D-IMPL-336` then finishes on its own terms and reaches its stop-for-review checkpoint. The 337 design cycle runs **separately, afterwards**.

**Next free decision id: `D-IMPL-338`.** **Governs:** the guarded-type consumer invariant across the SDK. **Related:** `D-IMPL-336` (which exposed it, and whose close-panel record at `docs/D-IMPL-336-CLOSE-PANEL.md` carries the two sampled instances), `D-IMPL-59` (Peering admission), `D-IMPL-57` (attributable vs verifiable), CLAUDE.md §10 (single-writer), §11 (invariants are CI-enforced, not aspirational), INV-CH7-46/47/52 (the three validation gates `ServableProduct` attests to).

**D-IMPL-336 — `R4` RULED: GO AS IMPLEMENTED. The engine-resolved operand widens for a composite, and the parent's own declaration is held strictly BEFORE the union.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-09-14. Ruled by: Dave, at the Amendment 5 §6 checkpoint. This converts the PROPOSED reading carried since `7d18004d` into the ruled one; **no code changes under this entry** — the implementation already matches the ruling, and the entry exists so the reading is ruled rather than inherited from an implementation.

**THE RULED SEMANTICS, in Dave's numbering:**

1. **`run_gates` remains unchanged.** Gate 2 is not edited; only the operand handed to it.
2. **Non-composite behavior remains byte-identical.** `composed` is `None`, the union is with `frozenset()`, and the operand is the value it has always been.
3. **For composites, FIRST require** `parent_declared_operators == parent_executed_operators`.
4. **Only after that succeeds**, form `parent_executed_operators ∪ admitted_child_operators`.
5. **Compare the composite lineage against that union with strict equality.**
6. **Child operators may never mask parent drift.**
7. **Keep the parent-drift sabotage.** Codex finding no masking case is **corroboration only**.

**WHY A RULING WAS NEEDED RATHER THAN A REPAIR.** INV-CH7-47 requires a candidate's declared operators to equal what this fabric's engine resolved, strictly, in both directions. `D-IMPL-31` requires a composite's lineage to be the N-way union over its constituents'. A composite satisfies both only if the operand widens: its engine never ran its children's operators, because the children did. **The two obvious alternatives each break a standing ruling** — a subset check abandons INV-CH7-47's strictness; declaring only the parent's own operators abandons `D-IMPL-31`'s union. Measured twice independently before the question was put: a real child of another class refused with `lineage-mismatch-refusal` before it could serve.

**WHAT LIMB 3 BUYS, and it is the whole reason the widening is safe.** A naive union masks parent drift: if the engine runs operator X while the class declares only Y, and a child happens to invoke X, then X sits on both sides of the comparison and the parent's own divergence disappears. So the parent's declared set is held to the parent's executed set **first and strictly**, as the same refusal type with the same gate identifier. Proven by sabotage that perturbs the **engine** rather than `run_gates` — the guard reads `execution.operators_invoked` and runs before the gate, so perturbing the gate's argument would leave the guard looking at the honest set and prove nothing.

**EVIDENCE.** `tests/products/test_resolver_seam.py::test_r4_a_composite_serves_with_a_child_that_ran_ITS_OWN_operators` (which asserted the DEFECT first and went red on the line that fixed it), `::test_r4_the_positive_control_a_child_WITHIN_the_parents_operators_serves`, and `::test_r4_the_union_CANNOT_mask_the_parents_own_declaration_drifting` — the limb-6 sabotage, which found the masking hole before the guard existed and which limb 7 preserves. Close panel 2 recorded a **negative result** from codex — *"I did not find an R4 masking case in the checked-out resolver path"* — which this ruling accepts as corroboration and not as clearance.

**`D-IMPL-336`'s GUARDED-TYPE OBLIGATION IS ALSO DISCHARGED** (Dave, same ruling). `compose_children` positively verifies `isinstance(outcome, AdmittedChild)`, and `invocation_from_dispatch` — the branch's other exported consumer of a guarded type — raises `ProvenanceForgeryError` on a non-`ResolvedProducer`. **This does NOT close `D-IMPL-337`**, which remains OPEN at `13d7e8ec` with its six-site census and its eight design questions intact.

**Next free decision id: `D-IMPL-338`** — unchanged; a ruling on an existing entry spends none. **Governs:** Gate 2's operand for composite products. **Related:** `D-IMPL-336` Amendments 3–5, INV-CH7-47, `D-IMPL-31`, `D-IMPL-104`, `docs/D-IMPL-336-CLOSE-PANEL.md`, `D-IMPL-337` (raised by the same checkpoint, explicitly not closed by it).

**D-IMPL-336 — `INT-01b` CLOSED. Nested dependency propagation is proven through historical reconstruction.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-09-14. Ruled by: Dave, on the measured proof at candidate `29d1885a`. This was the last outstanding pre-merge deliverable.

**THE RULING, in Dave's words:**

> `INT-01b` proves nested dependency propagation through historical reconstruction. After a real L2 supersession at `T_WORLD > T0`, the same child question asked again at `T0` is refused by the child's own governed delivery path. The middle and higher composites refuse because the governed child they acquire refuses. No parent invalidation boundary is separately written or synthesized.

**THE FAILED FIRST PROOF, recorded because it is the more useful half — also in Dave's words:**

> The original cached-child test was invalid as evidence for `D-IMPL-334`/`D-IMPL-335` because `F15`'s one-`as_of` rule produced `as-of-mismatch` before dependency invalidation could be exercised. **Sabotage 2 remaining green exposed the false proof.**

The first version pinned the leaf to an instance built at `T0` and re-served the composite at a later instant, expecting the stale child to be refused as invalidated. It was refused — for the wrong reason. The prescribed sabotage (cutting the child's dependency evidence) left the test **green**, which is what surfaced it; the actual refusal reason was then obtained by instrumenting `CompositeAdmissionGate.admit` rather than by re-reading the source.

**THE MEASURED FACTS, kept:**

- **real boot-bound L2 ingest** — one `SignalEnvelope` through `worker.ingest`; the writer `ccf.boot.boot` bound the sink to publishes the boundary itself;
- **invalidation boundary = 13:00 world time, not the June ingestion time** (`D-IMPL-335`, `_boundary_instant` taking `valid_from`);
- **no direct register write**;
- **no direct sink invocation**;
- **no manual dependency copying into the composites**;
- **all three targeted sabotages RED and restored byte-identically** — writer publishes no boundary; execution reports no entities; boundary reverted to ingestion time. `git diff --stat src/` empty after each;
- **post-change re-derivation serves again through the nested chain**, at all three levels.

**WHAT `INT-01b` DOES NOT PROVE, corrected by Dave against the orchestrator's own write-up.** The single-entity fixture **cannot** express an *"equally old unrelated product still serves"* control, and describing it as doing so was wrong: re-derivation and dependency **selectivity** are different claims. **Selectivity remains covered by the existing `D-IMPL-334`/`D-IMPL-335` regression** at `tests/products/test_dependency_invalidation.py`, which has the entities to express it. `INT-01b` proves **nested propagation and re-derivation**, and nothing wider. The test's own prose has been corrected to say so.

**EVIDENCE.** `tests/products/test_composite_integration.py::test_int01b_a_real_L2_change_invalidates_the_NESTED_composite_chain` and `::test_int01b_the_inherited_composition_state_survives_on_the_nested_chain` (child lineage reaching the top two levels down; parent expiry bounded by its child; the persisted row identifying the contributing governed product by class, address and grant; replay re-deriving the union and the floor from the rows alone without calling a child skill).

**D-IMPL-336 — the MISATTRIBUTED replay-reference defect, FIXED at `23c296af`.** RESOLVED. Date: 2026-09-14. Found by the final cross-AI review against `29d1885a`; verified by the orchestrator against `35cec2c6` before it entered the register, per Dave's ruling that reviewer assertions are not evidence.

**THE DEFECT.** `ccf.products.child_resolver.GrantBoundChildResolver._touched_entities` declared a ``contract`` parameter and **never read it**. A composite child's dependency evidence — which entities the child's execution touched — was taken from whatever replay record the producing skill **named**, with no check that the record described the product being admitted. Measured:

```
my own record    -> ('entity://the-one-that-matters',)
a FOREIGN record -> ()
```

A producer serving an honest contract **and** an honest content address, while pointing ``replay_ref`` at an unrelated resolvable record, had the invalidation register asked about the wrong product's reads — and the composite's replay row still recorded ``local-register`` as the authority that cleared it.

**THE ASYMMETRY THAT MADE IT FINDABLE.** The admission gate already refuses to trust the producer on the content address, recomputing ``content_hash(contract)`` itself; ``DoorOutcome`` already binds ``replay_ref`` on the **refused** path. Only the served path left it free — and ``product_content_address`` was already a **required** field on the record, so the evidence needed to close it was present and simply unused.

**`F3` closed the ABSENT-evidence case on this leg. This is the MISATTRIBUTED case**, which reads as present and passes.

**THE RULED BINDING, and the repair matches it verbatim** (Dave): *"the binding is between the referenced record's product identity and the **RECOMPUTED** child content address, established **BEFORE** reading its dependency evidence."* The shipped code computes ``address = content_hash(contract)`` — never the producer-reported value — compares it against ``record.content_generation_path.product_content_address``, and does so before ``record.context_fabric_snapshot.touched_entities`` is read.

**RAISED, NOT REFUSED, and the distinction is deliberate.** A governed refusal says *this child may not be composed*. ``ChildRecordMismatch`` says *the evidence offered is not about this child at all* — a producer defect or a substitution attempt, neither of which is a fact about the child's eligibility. Reporting it as one would let a misattribution be read as a governed answer.

**PROOF, and all three halves Dave required are preserved.** `tests/products/test_composite_integration.py::test_a_child_naming_ANOTHER_products_replay_record_is_refused` drives the **shipped** resolver with a door that serves an honest product and swaps **only** the record reference — a real, resolvable record of a different product (the **valid-foreign-record rejection**). The **honest-record positive control** asserts the unswapped pairing still serves, so the check is a differential rather than a method that refuses everything. The **binding-removal sabotage** turns it RED, restored byte-identically.

**Next free decision id: `D-IMPL-338`** — unchanged. **Governs:** the record-to-product binding on the composite's local acquisition leg. **Related:** `D-IMPL-336` Amendment 5 §3 (the ruled contract it satisfies), `F3` (the absent-evidence case on the same leg), `D-IMPL-334`/`D-IMPL-335`, `docs/D-IMPL-336-CLOSE-PANEL.md`.

**D-GATE-336 — `D-IMPL-336` IMPLEMENTED / CLOSED. Composite Context Products are approved for merge.** APPROVED. Date: 2026-09-14. Approved by: Dave. **Merge candidate: `513d5712120f6354dc9343da5e43ea93e1718266`.**

**WHAT SHIPS.** A composite Context Product declares the child product **classes** it requires; a granted skill acquires each child — in-process, over MCP, over A2A/peering — and the composite rolls them up under `D-IMPL-31`'s four laws and `D-IMPL-104`'s per-factor debt. **The composite does not assemble its atomics.** They may be registered elsewhere serving other consumers, and their provider decides whether to return an existing valid instance or assemble on demand. Dave's architecture, in his words: *"The skill that the composite agent has knows how to acquire the atomic context product and roll it in."*

**THE EVIDENCE DAVE RULED SUFFICIENT:**

| Item | Status | Closed by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `R1` — the peering path | closed | `ccf.peering.identity.MAX_PROTECTED_HEADER_BYTES`; `tests/peering/test_peered_child_envelope.py` (5) |
| `CMP-R-01` — refused-composite child evidence | closed | `RefusalRecorderProtocol.record(child_resolutions=…)`; 2 tests, surface recorded first |
| `GrantBoundChildResolver` in `src/` | closed | `ccf.products.child_resolver`; `INT-01a` + negative controls; fragment `336-05` |
| `R4` — Gate 2's operand for composites | **ruled GO** | parent declared == parent executed FIRST, then the union; children may never mask parent drift |
| composite replay (`R5`/`CMP-R-02`) | closed | `child_operators_invoked`, `child_expires_at`, `child_admitted_at`; reconstruction from the rows alone |
| `INT-01b` | closed | historical reconstruction → governed child-refusal propagation through the nested chain |
| misattributed `replay_ref` | fixed | the record-to-product binding, with regression **and** sabotage |
| MCP leakage from `ChildRecordMismatch` | fixed | through the **existing** opaque-door exception posture, not a new one |
| full verification on the exact candidate | green | baseline failure roster **unchanged** |

**HOW IT GOT HERE, recorded because the process is the lesson.** Four review rounds. The design panel found 19 defects; the R-series 6; close panel 1 nine; close panel 2 six; the final review one, plus a follow-on the repair itself introduced. **Mechanism defects fell 19 → 6 → 2 → 1** while the later rounds shifted almost entirely to *proof machinery* — tests that did not hold the mechanism they named. Dave's intervention at the midpoint — *"I simplified the architecture yet we still can't get it right… you are just repeating the same loop"* — produced Amendment 5, which **removed ~40% of the module** (a parallel authorization layer) on the ground that **the grant is the authorization**. Deployment code to acquire one child went from **45 lines and five hand-built evidence objects to 16 and none**.

**TWO PROOFS THAT PASSED FOR THE WRONG REASON, and both were caught by prescribed sabotage rather than by review.** The first `R2` test was tautological under its own fix. The first `INT-01b` test measured `as-of-mismatch` rather than dependency invalidation, because `F15` fires first — *sabotage 2 remaining green* is what exposed it. Neither was found by reading.

**CARRIED FORWARD AS LIMITATIONS — explicitly not hidden debt inside this close, and not to be fixed in the merge commit:**

1. an over-bound peering header reports as `SignatureInvalid` (`ExceededSizeError` is a `JoseError`; nothing is admitted, but the operator is told the wrong thing);
2. a remote-proxying `local_callable` is **structurally invisible** — the entry genuinely is local and the dispatch genuinely ran locally;
3. multiple peered products matching one class are not disambiguated;
4. `CP-F-06` — a content address in a field that elsewhere holds a class name;
5. **`AmbiguousProducerError` can escape the same MCP opaque-failure posture.** Dave: *"should receive its own follow-on decision/finding if we decide to repair the runtime door. It is not a reason to reopen `D-IMPL-336`."*

**`D-IMPL-337` STAYS SEPARATE AND OPEN.** Its census and design questions are untouched, and **merging 336 is not authorization to begin it**. No CP-14 acquisition work before Dave's sequencing decision between 337's design and CP-14 Gate 1.

**D-IMPL-337 — DESIGN RULED GO. The governing mechanism is GUARDED-PATH PROVENANCE VERIFICATION, with mint verification as the reference pattern.** DESIGN RESOLVED; **implementation scope NOT yet ruled.** Date: 2026-09-14. Ruled by: Dave, on the measured evidence in `docs/D-IMPL-337-DESIGN.md` at `f62b8a25`.

**THE DISTINCTION THAT SETTLES IT:** *the invariant is about **provenance from the guarded construction path**, not nominal type identity.* The design therefore **canonizes the property, not a syntax**.

**THE ELEVEN RULED CONCLUSIONS:**

1. **`isinstance` is explicitly NOT sufficient.** It proves nominal type membership, not that the guarded construction/admission path ran. Measured: a subclass that skips `super().__init__` and `object.__new__` both pass `isinstance` on `ServableProduct` and `StateWriteToken`, and the subclass reaches a real `ServedProduct` with the three validation gates never run.
2. **The governing rule.** *A consumer that relies on authority established by a guarded construction path must positively verify evidence that the supplied value actually passed through that guarded path. Nominal type identity, structural compatibility, annotations, Protocol conformance, pattern matching, or duck typing alone are insufficient.*
3. **The reference implementation pattern is the existing `StateWriteToken` design**: the guarded path establishes a mint/provenance marker; the externally substitutable trust boundary verifies it; internal helpers inherit the verified value and do not repeatedly re-check. Already pinned by `tests/invariants/test_state_seam_closure.py::test_a_token_subclass_skipping_init_cannot_succeed` — *"isinstance is not the gate — the mint is verified at the write."*
4. **Do not canonize one concrete sentinel for every type.** Equivalent construction-path proofs are permitted where they establish the same property: a private mint sentinel, a capability/token, a verified admission wrapper, a signed/verified proof object, or another construction-path proof.
5. **The governed unit is `entry point × authority-bearing value × external substitutability`.** A function is governed when an externally substitutable value can reach it **and** it relies on authority only the guarded path establishes. Function visibility alone is insufficient.
6. **Module-private status is not an exemption.** Reachability and substitutability determine governance, never naming convention.
7. **The census is discovery evidence only and must not become the semantic rule.** Proven by its own failures: v1 under-counted verification, v2 over-credited it, v3 misfiled `ProductSource.__init__` as private on the strength of a leading underscore.
8. **Introduce a declared guarded-type registry** so future guarded types cannot depend on heuristic discovery.
9. **Drift enforcement verifies that every declared guarded type states**: the authority carried; the mint/construction mechanism; the verifier; and the externally substitutable boundary consumers.
10. **Runtime negative controls must include**: a structural impostor; a subclass bypassing guarded construction; a constructor-bypass / `object.__new__` specimen where applicable; and an honest minted **positive control**.
11. **`__init_subclass__` refusal is allowed as defense-in-depth but must not replace boundary provenance verification.** The boundary check remains load-bearing.

**STARTING IMPLEMENTATION POPULATION: the seven measured governed sites**, including the `ProductSource.__init__` correction found by review rather than by the instrument.

**STANDING CONSTRAINTS.** Frozen example specimens are **not** edited merely to satisfy a lint signature (CLAUDE.md §9, `D-IMPL-261`); the five shipped examples verify with `case ServableProduct() as gated:` and are not reached by a provenance rule at declared boundaries. **The third-party store Protocol seam remains a recorded residual** if the SDK cannot establish guarded-path provenance across that external implementation boundary — `ccf.controlplane.state.ControlPlaneStateStore` is the only Protocol of 50 in `src/ccf/` carrying a guarded type.

**NOT YET RULED, and the next question:** *how much of the seven-site population is repaired in one implementation phase.* **No `D-IMPL-337` implementation before that ruling. No CP-14 acquisition.**

**Next free decision id: `D-IMPL-338`** — unchanged. **Governs:** the mechanism for the guarded-type consumer invariant. **Related:** `D-IMPL-337` (raised OPEN at `13d7e8ec`), `docs/D-IMPL-337-DESIGN.md`, `.planning/censuses/guarded_type_census_v3.py`, `D-IMPL-336` (which exposed the class), `D-IMPL-261` and CLAUDE.md §9 (frozen specimens), `D-IMPL-253` Q20.

**D-GATE-337 — `D-IMPL-337` IMPLEMENTED / CLOSED. Guarded-path provenance is verified at every governed boundary.** APPROVED. Date: 2026-09-14. Approved by: Dave. **Merge candidate: `1df12c6aa8d00db7418e5f71c98bd682107db6a4`.**

**WHAT SHIPS, and the distinction it rests on:** *authority comes from the guarded construction/admission path, and governed externally substitutable boundaries verify that **provenance** rather than nominal type identity.*

**THE MEASUREMENT THAT RULED OUT THE OBVIOUS ANSWER.** `isinstance` proves class membership and **not** that the guarded path ran:

```
ServableProduct   subclass skipping __init__ -> isinstance: True
                  object.__new__             -> isinstance: True
```

and the subclass reached a real `ServedProduct` with the three validation gates never run — strictly worse than a duck type, because it inherits the real attribute surface and satisfies any `isinstance`-shaped rule. **The project had already settled this** at its one considered site: `ccf.controlplane.state._verify` checks the mint, and `tests/invariants/test_state_seam_closure.py` pins it — *"isinstance is not the gate — the mint is verified at the write."* Canonizing `isinstance` would have reported that single correct implementation as a violation and replaced it with a weaker check.

**CANONICAL ACCOUNTING: 7 declared guarded types / 9 governed boundaries.** The earlier "seven sites" figure was the *design-phase census* population quoted against an implementation whose registry had grown; the roster and the implementation status now describe the same population.

| Guarded type | Provenance | Boundaries |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ServableProduct` | `verify_gate_provenance` | `serve`, `DeliveryCapability.deliver`, `refuse_over_tolerance` |
| `AdmittedProduct` | `verify_admission_provenance` | `mount_product_source`, `ProductSource.__init__`, `ingest_admitted` |
| `StateWriteToken` | `_verify` — **pre-existing, retained** | `InMemoryStateStore.put` |
| `ResolvedProducer` | `verify_resolved_producer_provenance` | `invocation_from_dispatch` |
| `AdmittedChild` | `verify_child_admission_provenance`, via the mint-backed `TypeGuard` | `compose_children` |
| `ChildInvocation` | — | **no externally substitutable governed boundary** |
| `DeliveryCapability` | — | **no externally substitutable governed boundary** |

**`D-IMPL-336`'s SEMANTICS ARE UNCHANGED.** This is provenance hardening, not a 336 reopen: composition, grant resolution, acquisition, replay, `R4` and the child-admission rules are untouched. `compose_children` keeps `outcomes: Mapping[str, object]` **deliberately** — `F13`'s reasoning is why the guard is reachable at all — and the `TypeGuard` does the narrowing, so satisfying mypy did not reintroduce `isinstance` where no reviewer would look. The four branches and their **order** are preserved: a genuine child composes, a `ChildAdmissionRefusal` propagates, `None` takes absence handling, and **a forgery falls to `unsupported-outcome`** — never an honest absence, which would price it at the declared absence cost, and never a governed refusal, which would report a forgery as a decision the fabric made.

**THE REGISTRY IS THE SOURCE OF TRUTH, NOT THE CENSUS** — and that ordering was paid for. The AST census was wrong three times in three ways: it under-counted verification, then over-credited it, then filed the constructor of an exported class as module-private **because the function name begins with an underscore**, missing a governed site. It also discovers guarded types by a heuristic that all existing types happen to share. `ccf.contracts.guarded` declares each type's authority, mint, verifier, boundaries, propagation model and residual, entirely in **strings** — a registry importing what it names would pull five subsystems into one leaf module. `tools/lints/guarded_provenance` reports drift in both directions and **keys on none of the forbidden signals**: not annotations, not name visibility, not literal `isinstance` syntax, not Protocol presence, not PEP 634 patterns; and it does not scan `examples/`, because frozen specimens are not authority checks.

**THE SABOTAGE RECORD, ACCEPTED INCLUDING ITS FAILURE.** Eight sabotages, each restored and verified **by marker** rather than by a clean `git status`. **S7 did not bite on the first attempt**: reverting the invocation *boundary* to `isinstance` left all 24 controls green, because every one exercised the *verifier* directly. **A boundary is only pinned by a test that drives the boundary**, and `test_the_INVOCATION_BOUNDARY_refuses_a_nominal_forgery` was added because of it. The drift lint separately caught a real declaration/code mismatch on its first use, repaired by declaring both verifier spellings rather than relaxing the check.

**RESIDUALS CARRIED FORWARD, declared rather than hidden:**

1. **The third-party `ControlPlaneStateStore` Protocol.** The SDK invites a conforming external store and **cannot compel it** to verify the token. Not closed by strengthening a contract the SDK cannot enforce.
2. **`AmbiguousProducerError` escapes the MCP opaque-failure posture** — unrelated to this work, carried from `D-GATE-336`, and still owed its own decision if that runtime door is repaired.

**Next free decision id: `D-IMPL-338`** — unchanged; a gate entry spends none. **Governs:** the approval and merge of guarded-path provenance verification. **Related:** `D-IMPL-337` (raised at `13d7e8ec`, design at `f62b8a25`), `D-GATE-336`, `D-IMPL-253` Q20, `D-IMPL-261` and CLAUDE.md §9 (frozen specimens), `D-IMPL-16`, `D-IMPL-59`, CLAUDE.md §10 (single-writer), §11 (CI-enforced invariants).

**D-IMPL-338 — A COMPOSITE'S CHILD-RESOLUTION EVIDENCE SURVIVES EVERY DOWNSTREAM REFUSAL.** APPROVED, SCOPED. Date: 2026-09-14. Ruled by: Dave, in the consolidated `D-IMPL-338` / `D-IMPL-339` ruling on `CP-SPEC-014` Gate 1 (candidate `e759dad5`). **Exclusively scoped to `CP14-F-09`.** Baseline: the approved `main` this entry lands on. **No merge without review.**

**The finding (`CP14-F-09`, measured 2026-09-14).** `compose_children` builds one `ChildResolution` row per declared requirement, refused or not, and the rows reach the persisted record on the served path (`resolver.py:2343`) and on a *composition* refusal (`:2217`, `CMP-R-01`). They do **not** reach it on the three refusals that can follow a successful composition — the universal-gate path (`:2224`), the declared-product-gate path (`:2260`) and the **tolerance** path (`:2300`) — each of which calls `_record_refusal` without `child_resolutions`. A tolerance refusal is CP-14's headline behavior, so the rows are absent in exactly the case whose cause they explain.

**The ruling.**

1. **Implement the targeted repair through the existing refusal-recording mechanism.** `RefusalRecorderProtocol.record` already accepts `child_resolutions` (`D-IMPL-336` `CMP-R-01`); no protocol changes.
2. **Every applicable refusal after child acquisition preserves the available child-resolution evidence** — composition, universal-gate, declared-product-gate and tolerance refusals alike. **Enumerate the actual exits; do not fix only the first omitted argument found.**
3. **Before acquisition, invent no child outcomes.** A refusal reached before the composite block records `()` — the true claim that no child was considered — never a synthesized row.
4. **After acquisition, retain what actually happened**, including known child identities, grant mappings and original refusal evidence, exactly as the rows carry them.
5. **Test against reloaded persisted records**, never the in-memory value. **Keep protected audit evidence separate from caller disclosure**: the rows are dimension-5 record content and are never part of the disclosed shell.
6. **`D-IMPL-338` must be reviewed and merged before CP-14 Gate 2.** It is not optional merely because a successful serve would work without it.

**Sabotage obligation.** Dropping the rows from any downstream refusal must make the corresponding persisted-record test fail.

**Next free decision id: `D-IMPL-339`** — spent by the entry below. **Governs:** the completeness of child evidence on refused composites. **Related:** `D-IMPL-336` (`CMP-R-01`, the served-path and composition-refusal halves), `D-IMPL-253` Q13 / `D-IMPL-256` (a refusal is a first-class decision with a full record), `D-IMPL-254` (record the internal truth, disclose the shell), `CP-SPEC-014` §D.4 / §F.2 (`CP14-F-09`).

**D-IMPL-339 — ACQUIRE ONCE AND EXPOSE THE ADMITTED CHILD CONTRACTS TO THE PARENT'S COMPUTATION.** DIRECTION APPROVED. Date: 2026-09-14. Ruled by: Dave, in the same consolidated ruling. **Its own SDK phase and branch, baselined on the approved `main`, independent of `D-IMPL-338` and of the CP-14 example. No merge without review. CP-14 Gate 2 remains HOLD.**

**The requirement it serves, restated so it cannot be narrowed.** CP-14 consumes the five required child products' **content and governing evidence**. *"Govern, not fill"* is **not** an approved narrowing. CP-14 must not independently reconstruct financial spread, family structure, exposure, collateral or covenant material its children supply. **The atomic providers own their assembly; skills acquire those independently provided products; the composite owns the roll-up.** Do not expand `ProductSource`, remount structured payloads as graphs, or introduce another `GraphReader`.

**The gap, measured.** On the shipped surface the projection plan is built at `resolver.py:1878` and executed at `:1889`; composition begins at `:1983`; the `outcomes` mapping holding the `AdmittedChild` values is built inline and never bound. Every downstream use of the composition outcome is governance. No existing interface carries admitted child content to the parent's computation — `ProductSource` takes only the peering gate's `AdmittedProduct`, requires a `graph_state` payload, must mount before the plan, and has zero consumers; `plan_factory` takes only `(required, request)`; `CompositionOutcome` has no child field; there is no second projection pass.

**The approved split.**

```
existing child-independent request / policy / declaration checks
    -> acquire and admit children ONCE
    -> establish the read-only child-contract view
    -> construct and execute the parent's plan
    -> assess the parent's own evidence
    -> compose using the SAME acquired outcomes
    -> existing gates, tolerance, delivery / refusal, and replay
```

- **The plan receives child contracts, not raw admission machinery.** A read-only mapping keyed by the declared requirement, derived from the acquired `AdmittedChild` values **after** their existing provenance and request/slot bindings have been established.
- **Retain those original outcomes for `compose_children`.** Content and governance refer to the same admitted products — not a second acquisition, a fresh lookup, or a separately reconstructed contract.
- The SDK exposes the contracts; **CP-14 performs the product-specific mapping into memo sections.**
- **No scheduler, new authorization layer, local attestor stack, or new composition algebra.**

**The three ordering questions, settled.**

1. **View to the plan:** the admitted children's read-only contracts. No invented graph view.
2. **Known blocking outcome before projection:** do **not** run child-dependent computation when a required child is absent or an invoked child has refused or failed admission. Preserve the existing distinction between optional absence and optional refusal.
3. **Later composition or parent refusal:** any payload already computed is **provisional and must not be served**. Record the refusal and the child evidence; do not substitute another child or fall back to raw source queries.

Keep child-independent request/schema/policy checks above acquisition where their inputs are already available; checks requiring child state remain below admission. **Correction to the proposal's own claim:** the hoist crosses nothing that *returns or refuses in the enclosing block*, but **called functions can fail even where the block contains no literal `raise`** — the claim "crosses nothing that can raise" is withdrawn. **Keep the declaration-versus-plan binder (`refuse_operator_set_divergence`) after plan construction and before execution.** Acknowledge and test the changed order rather than building a dummy plan or acquiring twice.

**Compatibility.** For non-composites, retain the existing call exactly: `plan_factory(required=required, request=effective_request)`. **Adding a defaulted parameter to a Protocol does not make existing implementations accept that keyword.** Composite-capable factories must explicitly support the child input. **Do not catch `TypeError` and retry without it.**

**Replay, wired explicitly.** Retain the exact child content the parent consumed, using existing immutable artifact references where sufficient. Reconstruct the child-contract view **before** rebuilding the child-dependent plan. No current provider calls, latest-version lookup, source re-query, or reliance on a live closure holding the original objects. **Test with a fresh replay environment.** The composition laws, `R4`, the gates and the tolerance semantics remain unchanged; replay's overall position may stay unchanged, but its child-input reconstruction must be connected and proven. Also demonstrate how the parent's own child-dependent `C`/`S` measurements reach its assessment per request — moving acquisition does not by itself prove that scoring reads those inputs.

**The proof, as a small SDK fixture.** `CMC-G28` / `CMC-G29` stay UNRUNNABLE on the shipped SDK until the connection exists and are never discharged with raw source legs. The fixture must establish:

| Proof | Required result |
| --- | --- |
| Child-content dependence | Two valid child instances differ in a business value; other parent inputs fixed; the corresponding parent payload value changes |
| Same acquisition | Each child acquired once; computation and governance use the same admitted result |
| No source substitute | Disable the child provider/source after acquisition; the parent still computes from the retained child contract |
| Early failure | A known blocking child outcome prevents child-dependent projection |
| Late refusal | A later governing failure produces no served parent and retains the acquired child evidence |
| Replay | A fresh environment reconstructs identical parent bytes/address with provider calls disabled |
| Compatibility | Existing non-composite factories retain their signatures, behavior and identities |

Keep the child's relevant governance factors equivalent in the content-differential test, so a debt or expiry change cannot masquerade as evidence that the parent read its business content. **Severing the child-content input must make that test fail.**

**Execution order.** `D-IMPL-338` first, returned for targeted review; `D-IMPL-339` as its own branch. Each candidate returns its exact interface changes, regression commands and results, targeted sabotage evidence and baseline comparison. **After both are reviewed and merged, CP-14 Gate 1 is re-presented as a brief reconciliation** — the child-content path, refusal evidence, affected `F`/`C`/`S` inputs and `G28`/`G29` readiness — without rewriting the whole spec. No CP-14 `run.py`, acquisition implementation or Gate 2 until that separate ruling.

**The 2026-09-14 hold release, scoped.** It authorized **Gate-1 measurement and reconciliation only**; Gate 2 remains unapproved.

**Next free decision id: `D-IMPL-340`.** **Governs:** the child-content connection for composite Context Products. **Related:** `D-IMPL-336` (composition, and Amendment 5's *"the composite is a consumer, not a second Control Plane"*), `D-IMPL-337` (the provenance the view is derived after), `D-IMPL-338` (refusal evidence, independent and prior), `D-IMPL-31` / `D-IMPL-104` (the unchanged composition laws), `D-IMPL-86` / `D-IMPL-300` (the binder stays between plan construction and execution), `D-IMPL-137` row C (named plan factories), `CP-SPEC-014` §0.0 / §B.8 / §H.1.

**D-GATE-339 — `D-IMPL-339` IMPLEMENTED / CLOSED. Acquire once, and expose the admitted child contracts to the parent's computation.** APPROVED. Date: 2026-09-14. Approved by: Dave, on the integrated candidate. **Merge candidate: `197cd63d`** on `d-impl-339-child-contract-view` — the independent candidate `d8020a2e` (baselined on `57d045c9`) reconciled onto post-`D-GATE-338` `main` (`4c77cc60`) by the merge `31de41d2` and the reconciliation commit `197cd63d`. **D-IMPL-340 — COMPOSITE ACQUISITION OF A PARAMETERIZED CHILD PRODUCED BY ANOTHER DEPLOYMENT.** OPEN. Date: 2026-09-14. Raised by: CP-14 Gate 2, on a measured blocker, before any Gate-2 artifact was written. **CP-14 Gate 2 is HOLD on this entry.** Rung 14 (`credit-memo-context`, Tier 4) is the first composite whose five required children are **five separately deployed products**, and the shipped composite path cannot admit any of them.

**THE MEASUREMENT.** The ruled pattern-to-copy, `examples/cp-04-canonical-corporate-family-tree`, was run for real against the curated estate (reads only), put behind a real `local_callable` door emitting `door_answer` bytes, and offered to a real `GrantBoundChildResolver` + `CompositeAdmissionGate` — the fixture wiring of `tests/products/composite_fixture.py::build_composite`, with the deployment's tenant set to a CP-14 tenant. **Refused at check 1:** `ChildAdmissionRefusal(reason='tenant-mismatch')` — *"the child claims tenant 'cp-04-canonical-demo' and this gate admits for 'cp-14-probe'; trust is per tenant, and a child that merely claims another tenant would otherwise escape this fabric's invalidation register entirely."* **Positive control 1** (gate tenant set to the child's own, requirement as the approved spec wrote it): refused at check 2, `class-mismatch` — the child serves `reference.corporate-family`, not the spec's `credit-risk.corporate-family-tree` (a Gate-1 spec defect, corrected at `CP14-F-18`). **Positive control 2** (gate tenant = child's, requirement `reference.corporate-family` from `2.0.0`, the composite's `FileArtifactStore` rooted at the child's `<root>/artifact-store`): **`AdmittedChild`**, eligibility basis `local-register`. So the wiring is sound, the refusal is the tenant check and nothing else, and the local-dispatch legs (shared on-disk store index, `_touched_entities`, the local register) all work — **for a child of the same tenant.**

**THE POPULATION.** Five children, five tenants, read off their own `ccf_config.yaml`: `cp-03-demo`, `cp-04-canonical-demo`, `cp-05-demo`, `cp-06-demo`, `cp-13-crossref-demo`. `CompositeAdmissionGate` holds **one** `tenant_id`; the peering gate applies the same rule (`src/ccf/peering/admission.py::_check_policy_bindings`, *"trust is per tenant"*). No child exposes a tenant override, and `src/ccf/deployment/manifest.py::_resolve_tenant` refuses a conflicting supplied tenant. The frozen-specimen rule (`D-IMPL-261`) forbids editing the five trees. And one of the five, `cp-03`, **does not serve on the current SDK at all** — 13 of its 17 output tests are a `strict` xfail quarantine, refused at `ProductRequestContract` (`D-IMPL-264`); the rung-3 rerun that quarantine deferred to after `D-GATE-24.7` was never done, so under either reading below the spread slot has no producer until it is (`CP14-F-22`). **Three transports, and none carries a question to a producer that is not this fabric:** `_invoke_local_callable` passes the arguments — and presumes this fabric's store and invalidation register; `_invoke_mcp` reads the **fixed** URI the binding was registered with (`McpSkillRegistry.register(resources={name: uri})`) and only *records* the arguments; `_invoke_peering` drains `transport.receive()` and only records them. All five children are parameterized (an LEI or a facility or an anchor set, plus the reconstruction instant), and the egress side already serves an addressed question (`ccf-product://{tenant}/{class}/{version}/q/{q}` and the `request_context_product` tool) that the composite side cannot ask. **And the composite's own request never reaches the child mapping:** `GovernedResolver` calls the child resolver with `requirements, asked_at, admitted_at, composition_invocation, consumer_lineage` — no request, no subject — and `ChildArguments` is `Callable[[ChildRequirement, datetime], Mapping[str, str]]`. A per-request anchor (CP-14's LEI) can reach a child only if the deployment closes over per-request state outside the SDK's declared mapping — a resolver rebuilt per request, or a mutable cell, which is what the `D-IMPL-339` proofs had to do. Door (1) below is therefore *the composite's effective request reaching the child as a question*, on whichever transport.

**WHY THIS IS NOT ONLY AN ESTATE LIMITATION.** The demo tenant strings are arbitrary, and one could call the mismatch an accident of five standalone demos. But the shipped model behind the check is *composition happens inside one trust domain; a foreign producer produces FOR the consumer's tenant*. Under that model the only shipped way for CP-14 to consume the five products is to run their code **in its own process, its own store and its own register** — which is what positive control 2 did, and which is not what a Tier-4 *"multi-agent handoff"* rung exists to demonstrate: the whitepaper's Data and Context pillar names *"content produced by other agents"* and third-party data, and `D-IMPL-336` Amendment 5 anticipates a child that *"may already be registered elsewhere and serve other consumers."* Neither of the SDK's two cross-process transports can ask such a producer a question, and the gate cannot admit its answer.

**THE READINGS, for Dave.**

- **(A) Estate-side: re-home the five children under one ladder tenant.** A `D-IMPL-261` exception editing five frozen `ccf_config.yaml` files — and every test, page and transcript that pins `cp-0N-demo` in a URI. Consequence: local dispatch then admits all five (control 2), but CP-14 must run five foreign fabrics in-process (module-name isolation per child, five SQLite fabrics writing into one scratch root, two different store directory names — `artifact-store` for three children, `artifacts-store` for `cp-03`/`cp-05` — that a single `FileArtifactStore` cannot serve without a filesystem alias), and the admission row would claim `local-register` for entities CP-14's register never saw. It demonstrates in-process composition of one tenant's products, not a handoff between producers.
- **(B) SDK-side: two doors, both small and both symmetric with what egress already serves.** (1) **A question-bearing acquisition** — the child mapping receives the composite's effective request (subject and parameters, not only the instant), and the `mcp` skill dispatch derives the resource address from it in the egress address form instead of reading one fixed URI. (2) **Admission of a child from a declared producer tenant** — the requirement (or the grant) declares the tenant the producer serves under; the gate checks the child's tenant against that declaration rather than against the consumer's, records it on the admission row, and eligibility stays `provider-controls` for that leg. Consequence: CP-14 acquires five producers over doors, per request, at one instant, with no child code in its process; the frozen trees stay frozen (cp-05 and cp-06 already ship MCP doors; the other three need one, which is example work on their own rungs, not a CP-14 workaround). `"trust is per tenant"` becomes *"trust is per declared producer"* for composite admission — a design change Dave must rule, not a repair.
- **(C) Hybrid: (B)(2) only, with local dispatch.** Admits foreign-tenant children without the MCP door, at the cost of every in-process consequence listed under (A). Not recommended: it spends a ruling to keep the shape (A) has.

**RECOMMENDATION: (B)**, as its own SDK phase off `main`, decision-first, no CP-14 code until it merges. It is the reading under which rung 14 demonstrates what Tier 4 is for.

**TWO INSTANTS, noted for whichever reading is taken.** The SDK already separates the decision instant from the temporal boundary: `decision_instant_parameter` moves `decided_at` (the TTL anchor and the gate instant) while `temporal_boundary` stays `request.asked_at`. cp-05 pins its boundary at `2026-09-07T12:00:00+00:00`, so the composite's `asked_at` must be that instant on any transport, while CP-14's `as_of` (policy-version selection, `CP-SPEC-014` §B.4 clock 1) must be declared as the decision-instant parameter rather than conflated with `asked_at` (`CP14-F-25`). And by the expiry-floor law (`D-IMPL-31`) a memo composed over cp-05's four-hour TTL expires at `2026-09-07T16:00:00+00:00` — in the past at any real wall clock; it serves only because the TTL gate's *now* is `decided_at`.

**WHAT CP-14 DID NOT DO.** No Gate-2 artifact, resolver, factory, scorer or door was written; no example-local workaround (no config copy with a swapped tenant, no store alias, no tenant-per-child gate) was tried. The spec's `§B.7` rows were corrected to the measured classes and lanes, and the measured findings were recorded (`CP14-F-16` .. `CP14-F-21`). The probe is not committed: it holds a literal LEI and estate wiring; the reproduction is the fixture's `build_composite` shape over `cp-04-canonical`'s `assemble_and_serve` with `FileArtifactStore(root=<child root>/"artifact-store")`, gate tenant `cp-14-probe`, then `cp-04-canonical-demo`.

**D-IMPL-340 — RULED (2026-09-14, Dave): DIRECTION B WITH ONE IDENTITY REFINEMENT. DESIGN ONLY, as its own SDK phase off `main`; implementation NOT authorized until the design package is ruled. CP-14 Gate 2 is HOLD.** Reading A is **rejected** — the five frozen products are independently deployed and `D-IMPL-261` stands. Reading C is **rejected** as the architectural answer — one store and one register demonstrate nothing about cross-deployment composition. **Two capabilities:** (A) parameterized cross-deployment acquisition — a granted skill asks a *registered* remote producer a question through the producer's existing `request_context_product` surface; arguments actually reach the producer; nothing is interpolated into a network address; the logical MCP server registry and its SSRF posture stay in force; no producer assembler enters the consumer process. (B) cross-deployment child admission — the rule is *not* `composite tenant != child tenant`; admission distinguishes the consumer tenant, the **expected producer identity**, the **tenant the child was governed under**, the class/version, and the provider relationship; the expectations derive from governed deployment/grant/binding state, never solely from the returned child; a payload cannot authorize itself by claiming them; for a remote MCP producer eligibility stays `provider-controls`, the local register is neither consulted nor credited, and replay records the producer and its tenant/governance context. Same-fabric/local-dispatch semantics unchanged; peering not rewritten unless the design proves a concrete inconsistency. **`requires:` stays about the product** — the exact class/version, never an implementation, a skill, a business label or a family of similar products; `produces:` and the granted binding decide how it is obtained; **no producer identity on `ChildRequirement`**. Related rulings recorded in the same message: `CP14-F-20` resolved for CP-14 by an explicit `facility_id` in the request; `CP14-F-22` is a blocking prerequisite (run cp-03 independently, determine whether the quarantine is stale, repair in its own phase or supply another real producer of the exact class); `CP14-F-19` estate limitation, kept visible; `CP14-F-21` a separate behavioral finding, population to be determined, not folded into 340.

**The design package is `docs/D-IMPL-340-DESIGN.md`** — producer identity model, the `ccf.mcp-producer` registration artifact, the `mcp_product` skill type and `McpProductBinding`, the `call_tool_text` client primitive, the `ChildQuestions` mapping reached through a capability Protocol (`RequestAwareChildResolverProtocol`, on the `D-IMPL-339` precedent), the producer admission leg with five new refusal reasons, the replay fields, peering compatibility (one recorded semantic divergence, not a rewrite), the thirteen proofs with their sabotages, and five questions for Dave (§12). Measured in the same sitting and recorded there: cp-03 refuses on the current SDK at `ProductRequestContract.from_declared` (the `intent` shadow, `D-IMPL-264` D-01) — the quarantine is real, not stale; and 16 of 19 shipped trees raise for an unresolvable anchor instead of refusing (`CP14-F-21`'s population).

**D-IMPL-340 — IMPLEMENTATION GO (2026-09-14, Dave). The five §12 questions RULED before code; branch `d-impl-340-cross-deployment` only; no F-22, F-21 or CP-14 implementation on it.** (1) **Producer failure semantics.** A correctly registered and governed remote producer that cannot answer produces a governed **`producer-unavailable`** outcome that preserves the child-resolution evidence available at that point and follows the `D-IMPL-338` refusal-record discipline. Distinguished from deployment/configuration defects: a timeout or an uncompletable governed request → `producer-unavailable`; a logical producer not registered at boot → a deployment/binding **error**; a malformed producer artifact → a configuration **error**. *"Do not collapse 'we could not reach the governed producer' and 'this deployment was never correctly wired' into one outcome."* (2) **Ship `DoorOutcome.producer`**, additive, so wrong producer, wrong producer tenant and wrong class/version stay independently testable; its value originates from the governed registration / verified door path; a payload cannot authorize itself by claiming the expected producer. (3) **Tenant semantics.** Peering unchanged. Recorded explicitly: peering `tenant_id` = the *admissible-to* tenant under the existing peering contract; `mcp_product` child `tenant_id` = the tenant under which the remote product was governed. No follow-up merely because the meanings differ — they belong to different provider relationships. For `mcp_product`, admission holds the returned child's producer-side tenant against the expected producer registration; ordinary local-dispatch admission is not weakened; the composite tenant is never set equal to the producer tenant to pass the gate. (4) **One governed registration per producer, with an `offers` list** — logical server name, producer identity, producer tenant, offered classes/version lanes, endpoint/credential references as environment-variable names; never one artifact per (producer, class). *"The registration is the authority for expected producer identity and producer tenant. The answer is evidence held against that authority; it is not the authority itself."* (5) **`mcp_product` ships as its own skill type**; fixed-resource `mcp`, `local_callable`, `tool` and `peering` behavior unchanged. *"`mcp_product` means: invoke a registered remote Context Product producer with a governed parameterized product question."*

**Also ruled in the same message.** (6) Question-bearing acquisition uses the producer-side `request_context_product` operation; `/q/{q}` is not used in v1; no subject, tenant, LEI, facility, anchor or other child argument is interpolated into a URL or resource address; the logical server is selected through deployment-controlled registration; `ChildQuestions` derives its values from the composite's **effective** request; sources stay explicit — producer tenant → registration, class/version → granted binding, `asked_at` → composite request, subject/intent/freshness/parameters → effective request through `ChildQuestions`; no caller-authored network address. (7) Product selection stays separate from producer selection: `ChildRequirement` names class + compatible lane and never a producer, skill, tenant or transport; two producers may implement one class and the existing ambiguity rules apply; no hidden producer preference on `requires:`. (8) Admission for `mcp_product` establishes independently: class/version, reconstruction instant, content address, assessable debt, expected producer identity, expected producer-side tenant, question/answer binding, provider relationship; eligibility basis `provider-controls`; the local register is never consulted nor recorded as the authority; wrong producer and wrong producer tenant are distinct reasons; equality is a necessary binding check, never authorization. (9) Replay retains the producing registration, producer identity, producer tenant, registration content address, question identity/address, exact admitted child content address and eligibility basis; reuses `D-IMPL-339` retention; makes no second producer call; persists no credential or resolved endpoint URL. (10) Security posture preserved: one shared MCP client, logical registration names, existing deadlines and bearer/credential factory, no second networking stack, no argument interpolation into addresses, no producer endpoint accepted from a returned product; artifacts carry environment-variable names, never secret values; **the address boundary is sabotaged explicitly.** (11) The proof package: fourteen proofs — the design's thirteen plus *question echo/binding mismatch refuses* — each load-bearing proof with a sabotage that turns it red; a sabotage that stays green stops the work until the proof is repaired. (12) `F-22` is not part of 340: frozen cp-03 is not modified, its quarantine is confirmed real and stays; after 340, a separate small phase builds a **canonical governed producer of `credit-risk.spread`** on the `cp-04-canonical` precedent, implementing the same required class. (13) `F-20` stands (facility grain, explicit `facility_id`, no implicit N-dispatch, no "first facility"). (14) `F-21` stays separate; if a required CP-14 scenario reaches a producer that raises where its contract requires a refusal, CP-14 **stops** on that named producer finding — no local catch-and-manufacture. (15) `F-19` stands untuned. (16) Stop point: candidate SHA, exact public/API changes, the registration / binding / `ChildQuestions` / `DoorOutcome.producer` shapes, the admission and refusal vocabulary, replay evidence, the fourteen proof results, the fourteen sabotage results, compatibility results for the existing skill types, lint/typecheck/product-gates, the exact baseline failure-roster comparison, remaining limitations — then STOP for `D-IMPL-340` review; no merge. CP-14 Gate 2 remains HOLD until 340 is merged and a real governed `credit-risk.spread` producer serves.

**D-IMPL-340 — IMPLEMENTED; candidate `25e4e1cb` on `d-impl-340-cross-deployment`, STOPPED for review.** Date: 2026-09-14. Not merged. CP-14 Gate 2 remains HOLD. Baseline `main` @ `c635037f`; the code candidate is `25e4e1cb` and this entry rides on the docs-only commit that references it.

**WHAT SHIPS (the public surface, `docs/surface-changes/340-01`, 30 entries).** *Capability A:* the sixth skill type `mcp_product` with `McpProductBinding(server, product_class, product_version)` (`produces` must equal the class); the `ccf.mcp-producer` Control Plane artifact (`McpProducerRegistration`: `server`, `producer_id`, `producer_tenant`, `endpoint_from_env`, `credential_from_env` — environment-variable **names**, a literal refused at parse — and an `offers` list; one registration per producer by ruling 4) with a `producers:` config section derived per label and validated at derivation; `McpSkillRegistry.register_producer` / `resolve_producer` beside the unchanged fixed-resource pair; `ProductQuestion` (subject, intent, freshness, aware `asked_at`, parameters, canonical `request_json`) whose `address` is `question_identity(...)` over **every** axis; the minted `McpProductInvocation` and `McpProductFailure` (producer members copied from the registration the registry resolved, verified at every boundary, both in `ccf.contracts.guarded`); `_invoke_mcp_product` calling the producer's existing `request_context_product` tool through the one shared `McpResourceClient.call_tool_text` — tenant ← registration, class/version ← binding, `asked_at` ← composite, the four axes and parameters ← `ChildQuestions` over the composite's **effective** request; `/q/{q}` unused; no code path from a question member to an address; `ccf.skills.producers.register_declared_producer` as the only place a URL or credential is resolved. *Capability B:* `QuestionBoundChildResolver` implementing `RequestAwareChildResolverProtocol.resolve_for` (a capability Protocol on the `D-IMPL-339` precedent; `GovernedResolver` branches on structural `isinstance`; `GrantBoundChildResolver` untouched); `DoorOutcome.producer` (`ProducerAssertion`) and `DoorOutcome.answered` (`AnsweredQuestion`, a naive instant refused), both additive and hash-transparent at `None`, stamped by `door_answer` on both branches and by `build_egress_server(producer_id, producer_tenant)`; the producer admission leg — `CompositeAdmissionGate.hold_producer_claims`, run on the served path in place of check 1 and on the **refused** path before an `ineligible` row: the child's tenant and its replay reference's tenant to the registration's `producer_tenant`, the door's assertion to the registration's `producer_id` and tenant, the echoed wire request plus the four answered axes to the question sent; checks 2–7 unchanged; eligibility `provider-controls`, the local register never consulted nor recorded. Five refusal reasons, each on exactly the paths the census pins: `producer-tenant-mismatch` (three claims, one reason by ruling), `producer-mismatch`, `producer-unasserted`, `question-mismatch` (no wire echo; no answered axes; another question), `producer-unavailable` (could not answer; answered with no door outcome) — and `CHILD_OUTCOME_STATUSES` gains `producer-unavailable`. Replay rows carry `producer_id`, `producer_tenant`, `producer_registration_address`, `producer_server`, `child_question_address`, `child_replay_ref` (transparent at `None`; `D-IMPL-243` table ticked); `D-IMPL-339` retention reused; replay makes no producer call; no credential or endpoint reaches a record. **D-GATE-340 — `D-IMPL-340` IMPLEMENTED / CLOSED. Parameterized cross-deployment child acquisition and admission.** APPROVED FOR MERGE. Date: 2026-09-14. Approved by: Dave, on the code candidate **`25e4e1cb`**, with the decision record at the branch tip **`6648ec95`** — both pushed and remotely resolvable before the merge. Merged `--no-ff` to `main` at the commit that references this entry. No behavioral change was made during the merge close. CP-14 Gate 2 remains HOLD.

**THE ACCEPTED CONTRACT, closed.** Producer identity comes from governed registration, not from the answer; the returned identity and tenant claims are held against that registration; equality is a binding check, never authorization by itself; `mcp_product` is distinct from fixed-resource `mcp`; parameterized questions use the producer's `request_context_product`; `ChildQuestions` derives from the composite's effective request; no `/q/{q}` construction; no question value becomes an endpoint or address; one producer registration carries an `offers` list; endpoint and credential configuration carries environment-variable names only; `DoorOutcome.producer` and the answered-question evidence are additive; served and refused doors are both held to the producer and question bindings; `producer-unavailable` is a governed refusal after a valid registered remote acquisition attempt; remote MCP eligibility is `provider-controls`; the consumer's local-register silence does not authorize a remote child; replay retains producer, question and child identity and makes no second producer call; existing local dispatch, fixed-resource MCP and peering semantics are unchanged. The cross-process proof is accepted. **The S3/S18 corrections are part of the evidence:** one assertion hiding two independent checks was not accepted as proof, and the repaired tests and sabotages now isolate the mechanisms.

**ACCEPTED RESIDUALS — recorded, not fixed, and none blocks 340.** (1) The door's producer assertion is unsigned; the governed registration remains the authority. (2) Peering carries no producer-side tenant under its existing contract. (3) `load_config_and_boot` derives producer artifacts but does not construct the MCP client; the composition root calls `register_declared_producer`. (4) No separate YAML lint rejects literal URLs, while the actual validator rejects them at parse and at derivation. (5) Producers that have not adopted the new parameterized door refuse by design.

**EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE at this close:** `CP14-F-22` / cp-03; `CP14-F-21` / the sixteen-tree raise-vs-refuse population; CP-14 artifacts or `run.py`; the frozen example tenants; peering semantics.
